quotes.quote: I didn't want to be back at the field, but as I said before the race, Middle Earth is a bit of a slow starter. He travelled on and finished very well. He ran home the last three furlongs in, I'd imagine, the quickest time of the race, so you have to be grateful for that. He's probably run up to his rating. quotes.race: Churchill Tyres Handicap
quotes.quote: Jimmy [Sullivan] gave Rousing Encore a lovely ride. We thought we were maybe drawn on the wrong side, he likes some cover but we didn't want to be too far back because it's hard to make up ground on a fast track on fast ground. Jimmy edged over onto the rail and the horse put his head down and battled well for him. There are plenty of decent six-furlong races for us to go at - Ruth Carr, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won at York and Ayr last year, both over 6f. He's going to run in a 6f handicap at Newmarket on Wednesday. He ran really well first time out at Newcastle when he was beaten only by William Haggas's Power Fizz, who's probably going to be a Group horse. He's my trainer's pick seeing as he's my ride at home and is a good old horse. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Unbeaten; the only one open to improvement back from seven months off; market informative
runners.spotlight: Impressive on her Kempton AW debut last September and easily defied a penalty from the front on Tapeta (both 6f) a fortnight later; dam won a French Group 3 over this trip and she's the only one open to improvement back from seven months off; market informative.

runners.comment: Solid comeback behind Akkadian Thunder over C&D; fair chance of turning things round
runners.spotlight: Yard going well and won this in 2023 and 2024; solid comeback behind Akkadian Thunder over C&D five weeks ago, when picked off late by four who'd sat in the rear, and is 3lb better off with that one; player.

runners.comment: Kept to 5f last year, when winning three times; undergone wind surgery; needs to settle
runners.spotlight: Often inclined to pull hard over this trip in the past and was kept to 5f last year, when winning three times; undergone wind surgery since last seen six months ago and will need to settle in tonight's small field if he's to have a chance off this mark.

quotes.race: Always Trying Racing Syndicate Handicap
quotes.quote: Brummell is a very genuine horse. The plan was to get a lead but when he travelled so well and you get such an easy time in front here, I don't think we were ever going to get beat and I probably held onto him a bit longer than I needed to. The second has come to him and he's battled on again - Ryan Sexton, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He made his debut last month at Thirsk where he showed some very good speed for a long way before getting tired. He'll have learned plenty there and I'm sure there is much more to come from him. 06-09-23

runners.comment: Returns to turf 10lb higher than when last running on it; not improving at his age
runners.spotlight: C&D win last summer came off 18lb lower and he returns to turf 10lb higher than when last running on grass, thanks to a consistent spell on Tapeta; will need something close to a career-best to take this and he's not improving at his age.

stable_tour.quote: I think he is a very nice colt with a bright future. His work had been encouraging this spring and we started him off over 7f late last month at Yarmouth in what looked a particularly hot maiden, with several of the big yards represented and many trainers liking their charges. He ran a cracker to be third behind New Science, where he was rather green but ran on well. It was the perfect start to his career as he will have learned plenty and mentally handled things well. There are a few 7f maidens around Royal Ascot time later this month and we will pick our spot to make him a winner and take it from there. He runs in the colours of owner Khalifa Dasmal, who is a great man to train for. His patronage is largely thanks to my former guv'nor David Simcock giving him a nod in my direction. David has been a huge help to me in my career and I am very hopeful that I have a potentially nice horse here for Mr Dasmal. 10-06-21

racecards.verdict: Kevin Ryan is looking to win this for a third time in four years and his runner TERRITORIAL KNIGHT is preferred to Rose Of Honour.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Akkadian Thunder,  Rose Of Honour, 4/1 Territorial Knight, 8/1 Rousing Encore, 10/1 Papa Cocktail, 16/1 Brummell

racecards.race_name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap

runners.comment: Winning comeback at Redcar and he holds obvious claims off 4lb higher
runners.spotlight: Took advantage of a drop in class and a career-low mark when making it 2-3 at Redcar on his recent comeback; tonight's extra distance and similarly long home straight won't hurt and he holds obvious claims off 4lb higher.

quotes.race: Watch Irish Racing On Racing TV Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mafting still felt a little bit green in front. He was sort of all over the place and had a bit of a wobble a furlong out, but he got the job done which is grand. He's done nothing wrong up to now and there's a chance he might handle a little bit more ease in the ground - David O'Meara, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

prev_owners.owner: Any Excuse For A Holiday Syndicate

runners.comment: Inconsistent ex-Irish gelding but solid comeback off this mark three weeks ago; player
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent ex-Irish gelding who's never run on ground faster than good; didn't take to hurdles in one try last autumn but solid comeback off this mark three weeks ago and this does seem to be his time of year; no surprise to see him take this.

quotes.race: Racing Again Here On June 10th Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought the step up in trip would be a big help to Sixpack. It was a bit of a messy race here last time, they didn't go quick and didn't the gaps when he needed. Everything went to plan today, we went a nice even gallop and I was able to get the gap turning in. I thought he stayed on well to the line and the more racing the better he'll get - Ben Coen, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour.quote: I bought him from Johnny Murtagh. He's having a break but I really like him and I think he can compete in the nice Saturday staying races for new owners in the yard. I was keen to go jumping with him but we'll probably do that next year. 01-01-25

runners.comment: Not run on turf in almost two years; plenty of chances off a sliding mark on the AW lately
runners.spotlight: Hasn't run on turf in getting on for two years and has had plenty of chances off a sliding mark on the AW lately; said to have hung right when again a beaten favourite last time and that leaves him with a bit to prove.

quotes.race: Follow @AtTheRaces On Twitter Handicap
quotes.quote: Adam Kirby gave Pleasant Man a great ride and rode exactly to instructions. He is quite a lazy type and I don't think any other jockey would have won on him - Grant Pritchard-Gordon, representing owners Brook Farm Bloodstock.

stable_tour.quote: Formerly a good staying handicapper on the Flat, he was found to have bled when pulled up in the Adonis Hurdle at Kempton and had a breathing operation straight afterwards. He's a good horse and will leave that form well behind when resuming over hurdles in five or six weeks. 31-10-22

runners.comment: Most wins in second half of the year; may need this at his age after five months off
runners.spotlight: Serial winner in his younger days but been dry in almost three years; does have a comeback spring victory to his name but all other wins came in the second half of the year and he may need this at his age back from five months off.

quotes.race: Rangers Riding Ranch Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
quotes.quote: We thought as a youngster Saratoga Gold wanted softer ground, being by Mayson, but he seems to like it quick and Kayleigh gave him a cool ride. We had another in here but she said she wanted to ride him so credit to her - Charles Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Goodwoof 28th & 29th May Handicap
quotes.quote: The ground was the only question mark for Saratoga Gold, but they've done a wonderful job here. Kieran came in and said he'd stay two miles, but he does travel well. There are no plans yet, but he could improve again, especially over further and if he gets his toe in - Charlie Hills, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was gelded before the start of last season and the results were impressive with four wins, including a hat-trick in the late summer months, all over 1m4f, with two at Epsom. He really thrives on those undulating tracks, as the first of his wins last year was at Goodwood. He has had one run this season when a decent third at Newmarket last month over 1m6f, his first try at the trip. There are plenty of options coming up for him and he seems in good order. 21-06-23

runners.comment: Two wins last summer came at a lesser level, latterly over 2m1f; returns from a layoff
runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer came at a lesser level, latterly over 2m1f off 3lb lower, and he wants a good test at this trip; doesn't boast the greatest reappearance record down the years and, like stablemate Saratoga Gold, may need this after seven months off.

runners.comment: Inconsistent hurdler; nothing to suggest he's best caught fresh; tough to find positives
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent hurdler who's been off for five months since a poor effort here in the winter; nothing to suggest he's best caught fresh and it's tough to find any positives.

racecards.verdict: Sixpack ran well off this mark on his comeback but MAFTING (nap) is preferred after his Redcar win.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Mafting, 7/4 Sixpack, 7/1 Saratoga Gold, 8/1 Pleasant Man, 12/1 Tazaman, 20/1 Dreams Fled Away

racecards.race_name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap

runners.comment: Last of 13 on return at Newcastle; has something to prove in a first-time hood now
runners.spotlight: Made the frame three times over 6f last season but she came in last of 13 in a 6f Newcastle handicap on her return so has something to prove in a first-time hood.

runners.comment: Close third at Southwell (7f) last month; merits serious consideration off unchanged mark
runners.spotlight: Has made a positive start for his new yard, coming home strongly on his handicap debut when a close third of seven at Southwell (7f) last month; merits serious consideration off an unchanged mark.

runners.comment: Last of eight at Newcastle 19 days ago; needs switch to handicaps to spark major progress
runners.spotlight: Shaped encouragingly when a debut third in 1m Newcastle novice in March but has twice failed to build on it, last of eight back there 19 days ago; needs this switch to handicaps to spark major progress.

runners.comment: Good Chelmsford fourth in February; not out of things on his handicap debut after a break
runners.spotlight: Took a step forward when fourth of ten in 7f Chelmsford novice in February; that form has worked out well so he's not out of things on his handicap debut after a break.

runners.comment: Cut little ice in three novices last autumn but could do better now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Cut little ice in a trio of novices last autumn, only eighth of ten at Carlisle (6f) on final one, but she could still do better now venturing into handicaps.

runners.comment: Seventh on h'cap debut at Newcastle; tongue tied for turf debut with more required
runners.spotlight: Only modest form shown thus far, finishing seventh of 13 on her handicap debut at Newcastle (6f) 19 days ago; tongue tied for her turf debut with more required.

runners.comment: Did well from wide draw when sixth at Pontefract latest; very much one to consider here
runners.spotlight: In good form on the AW before acquitting herself well from a wide draw when sixth of 14 in 6f Pontefract handicap last month; eased 1lb so she's a player in her bid for a breakthrough success.

runners.comment: Beat one rival in a trio of runs last summer for Michael Keady; lots to prove for new yard
runners.spotlight: Beat just one rival in a trio of runs last summer for Michael Keady, last of nine in 5f Wolverhampton maiden ten months ago; tongue tied now; has lots to prove for her new yard.

runners.comment: Little promise shown in three outings thus far; cheekpieces on for his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Little promise shown in his three outings thus far, beating one in 6f novice at Pontefract recently; cheekpieces on for handicap debut.

racecards.verdict: In-form maiden TRUCIAL PEARL was done no favours by the draw when sixth at Pontefract last time and is taken to gain a deserved success.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Tekitoff, 7/2 Grey Force,  Trucial Pearl, 8/1 Vega's Virtue,  Forever Twenty, 10/1 Too Darn Spicy, 12/1 Thornaby Annie, 33/1 Caitlin G,  Go Teejay

racecards.race_name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners.comment: Failed to fire in two 6f Newcastle handicaps at start of year; needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 in good form on the AW but this veteran failed to fire in a pair of 6f Newcastle handicaps at the start of the year; needs to bounce back after a break.

quotes.race: bet365 Superlative Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Maxi Boy is definitely Group class, we'll just have to box clever - Michael Bell, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Maxi Boy has a great attitude and it was nice to see him win like that. Hopefully he can now go to the Coventry - Nick Bell.

runners.comment: Back on track when runner-up in 7f Kempton handicap; needs to back it up on return to turf
runners.spotlight: A dual 6f scorer in first half of 2025 who was back on track when runner-up in 7f Kempton handicap in March; needs to back it up now returned to turf.

runners.comment: Shaped well on return from eight months off with Lingfield third; holds very good claims
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who shaped well on his return from eight months off when third of 11 in 7f AW Lingfield handicap 18 days ago; holds very good claims off an unchanged mark for yard among the winners.

runners.comment: On a losing sequence but he arrives in decent nick; possibilities
runners.spotlight: On a losing sequence but he arrives in decent nick, finishing fourth of six in 7f Kempton handicap 33 days ago; possibilities.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Straight A is such a baby. It's nice because he's not had a hard race and he's learnt a lot. Hopefully he'll take a step forward for that. He's been showing a lot at home and he really improved from his debut at Leicester - Hayley Turner, rider.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late J P Carrington

runners.comment: Set a lot to do when solid sixth at Lingfield 18 days ago; considered from an easing mark
runners.spotlight: Dual 7f Wolverhampton winner over the winter; not discredited, given he was set a lot to do, when sixth of 11 in 7f Lingfield handicap 18 days ago; considered from an easing mark.

runners.comment: Landed pair of 7f handicaps at Catterick; up 3lb but not taken lightly in current mood
runners.spotlight: Veteran who has been back in fine form of late, landing a pair of 7f handicaps at Catterick; up another 3lb but he's not taken lightly in his current mood.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
quotes.quote: Things worked out for Evocative Spark. He'd been waiting for that ground, which suits him well, and the course suited him too, as he likes those sharp bends. He's a brilliant horse to train and has been knocking on the door for a while. Last time at Redcar, he just didn't get out in time, but Sean knows how to ride him - John David Riches, trainer.

quotes.race: Alan McGuiness And Robin Lunness Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Evocative Spark is a progressive colt and the draw beat him last time, he'd have been a good winner otherwise. He's one to look forward to. The Britannia would have to come into the reckoning, he'll get a mile and he likes fast ground. And there's a £75,000 seven-furlong handicap at Goodwood in late-May - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won over 7½f for Hugo Palmer last year and I was delighted with his stable debut this month when second of 14 at Beverley, as it brought him on nicely. I found a lovely opportunity at Beverley last week and he ran out an impressive winner. He is a well-bred son of Frankel and we can now look to some nice handicaps like the Britannia or a 7f handicap at Newmarket on July Cup day. He is still a colt and there is more improvement to come from him. 27-04-22

runners.comment: Back on track when second in 6f Pontefract handicap last week; well in the mix eased 1lb
runners.spotlight: It's now 13 starts since his last success but he was back on track when finishing second in 6f Pontefract handicap 11 days ago; well in the mix eased 1lb.

quotes.race: Happy 40th Birthday Gary Sivills EBF Novice Stakes (Horses With No More Than 3 Runs) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Valentine Catcher showed enough at home but first-time-out in those conditions, you'd think it wouldn't be ideal. He was a bit slow away and a bit green but he travelled nicely and got there quite easily. There's obviously plenty of potential there and I was quite impressed - David Allan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's done really well and could be another for the Macmillan race at York. He's done all his racing on soft or heavy, because there was nothing else around, but I think he'll be better on good ground. 23-04-24

runners.owner: Ursa Major Racing Ltd & Julie Camacho
runners.comment: C&D winner in July; largely in good form after so not discounted after six-month absence
runners.spotlight: Scored over C&D last July and in good form after until finishing only eighth in 7f Redcar handicap on his final run; this reliable sort can't be discounted despite a six-month absence.

stable_tour.quote: He's consistent and has been running well this season. He finished in the places in his first three starts after a short break and then got his head back in front at Doncaster last Saturday. It was soft ground - we were unsure about that but you've got to give these things a go and he reacted really well to it. That's good to know and we were really pleased with him; he showed a good attitude. He's just a fun horse to have around. He tries hard and I'm sure he can win again. 23-07-25

runners.comment: Lightly raced but failed to beat a rival in 6f Leicester h'cap on reappearance last month
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who failed to beat a rival in 6f Leicester handicap on her reappearance last month; hard to warm to.

runners.comment: Without a win since 2022; has gone well fresh so can't be totally dismissed on return
runners.spotlight: Without a win since 2022 but she has gone well fresh so can't be totally dismissed on her seasonal return; yard also runs Lumenbourg.

stable_tour.quote: She won at Haydock over 7f as a juvenile but we've not seen the best of her this year. She's the sort who could pop up at a price one day. She's very capable and can definitely win off her mark. 06-09-23

racecards.verdict: George Scott's string is in fine form and his ZUBARU is taken to build on a promising Lingfield third and gain a breakthrough success.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Zubaru,  Evocative Spark, 5/1 Mr Cool, 8/1 Straight A,  Valentine Catcher, 10/1 Lumenbourg, 12/1 Maxi Boy, 16/1 Chifa,  Oscar's Sister, 33/1 Magic Music

racecards.race_name: Elston Supports UK Financial Advisers Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB)

runners.comment: Well held in two 1m maidens last month, with a best RPR of 53
runners.spotlight: Well held in 1m maidens at Kempton (AW) and Bath (good to soft) last month, with a best RPR of 53; remains best watched for now.

runners.comment: Promising third at Chelmsford in December and could be dangerous if he can build on that
runners.spotlight: 25-1 on Chelmsford debut (1m2f, AW) in December but he came from off the pace to finish third of eight and was beaten less than 2l; needs to build on that on this drop in trip but that was a promising start and he should know more this time.

runners.comment: 50-1 and he finished a remote eighth of ten on Newmarket debut (1m, good) last month
runners.spotlight: 50-1 and he finished a remote eighth of ten in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket (1m, good) last month; half-brother to a 1m2f winner and he's probably one for longer trips later on.

runners.comment: Always behind and was well held at a big price on Newbury debut last month
runners.spotlight: The product of extremes, being by Dream Ahead and first foal of 1m6f winner (RPR 78); started off over 1m at Newbury (good) last month but he was always behind and finished well held at 80-1; others preferred.

runners.comment: Half-brother to five winners; yard won this last year and he needs a close look on debut
runners.spotlight: 15,000euros yearling; gelded half-brother to five winners including Abadan (1m2f-2m including German Listed; RPR 98), Agent Empire (French 1m5f; 75) and Alika Breeze (1m; 70); dam German/Belgian 1m-11.5f winner; tongue-tie is applied on debut but yard won this with a newcomer last year and he needs a close look.

runners.comment: Sets good standard on his best 2yo form and he's a big player on his return
runners.spotlight: Sent off 100-1 for Curragh debut (7f, good) last August but he wasn't beaten far in sixth of 14 and recorded an RPR of 81; made his stable debut at Brighton (1m, good to soft) two months later and he went close behind his main market rival and was 6l clear of the third; sets a good standard on his return and he should have more to offer as a 3yo; key player.

runners.owner: Gee Gee's Racing & Hold My Beer
runners.comment: 20,000gns yearling; has good target to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners.spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-sister to winners All Go (6f-1m) and Dea Giulia (Italian 9.5f); dam 2m winner (RPR 64) and very well related; has good target to aim at on debut and she's best watched unless market is persuasive.

runners.comment: Went close when upped to 1m at Kempton on her reappearance last month; respected
runners.spotlight: Backed in from 20-1 to 9-2 when fourth of 14 on her Newbury debut (6f, good to firm) last June; that was her only 2yo run but she returned after a lengthy absence with a close call over 1m at Kempton (AW) last month; this is a tougher assignment but she looks promising and is bred to be useful.

runners.comment: Has form claims but she flopped at Chelmsford last time and needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on Kempton debut (1m, AW) in October and she ran to a similar level when third at Southwell in January; that form puts her firmly in the picture but she flopped at Chelmsford in March and needs to bounce back after another break.

runners.comment: Promising fourth at Lingfield (7f) last month but she needs another major step forward
runners.spotlight: Left her Salisbury debut form behind when a promising fourth on her reappearance at Lingfield (7f, AW) last month; could continue to improve with experience but she needs another major step forward at this new trip.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for CIARRAI ABU who sets a good standard on his return and should have more to offer as a 3yo.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Ciarrai Abu, 7/2 Doodling, 9/2 Adalo, 11/2 Shebara, 8/1 Cold Fish, 10/1 Crimson Sunset, 16/1 West Byfleet, 20/1 Arc At Her, 33/1 Cosmo Brown, 66/1 Ocean Force

racecards.race_name: Fitzdares Chelmer Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.comment: Second in Molecomb here; back with good fourth in Chantilly Group 3; enters calculations
runners.spotlight: Scored three times at 2yrs (including in 6f Listed event at Newmarket in June) and also runner-up in the Molecomb here; returned with a good fourth of 13 in Group 3 at Chantilly (5.5f, good) 18 days ago so must enter calculations.

quotes.race: HKJC World Pool Molecomb Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Argentine Tango just keeps finding a bit more every time we run her. She's had plenty of runs so she looks more exposed than the rest but she keeps finding a bit more improvement. I thought the five [furlongs] here might catch her out but she's that tough she just dug in again at the finish to get up for second - David Allan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I couldn't believe Argentine Tango was 9-1 as she was second to Karl Burke's Royal Ascot winner Venetian Sun at Carlisle the time before last giving her 6lb. Somehow she was rated only 84 and Venetian Sun is now 20lb higher. I would say that Tim, as a Yorkshireman, would want to have a crack at the Lowther at York instead [of the Empress Fillies' Stakes]- Terry Holdcroft, owner-breeder.

quotes.race: Hilary Needler Trophy EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was brilliant. Argentine Tango is really tough and genuine, she tries like hell.  We don't know about Ascot. It depends what the ground is like, if it was sparking fast ground we probably wouldn't go - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Argentine Tango is as hard as nails and was very hard to break in. But she's tough and she'll improve masses. When the other horse came to her she went again. We might take her to York for the Marygate Stakes - Tim Easterby, trainer.

runners.comment: Ascot Group 3 winner; fifth in Nell Gwyn at Newmarket on return; big player back at 6f
runners.spotlight: Likeable front-runner who made up into a useful juvenile, winning Group 3 Princess Margaret Stakes at Ascot and signing off with a good fifth in Newmarket's Cheveley Park Stakes; shaped encouragingly when fifth of 12 in Nell Gwyn Stakes back at Newmarket (7f) on her recent return, leading long way; this drop back to 6f promises to suit, so she's a big player.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix du Calvados (Group 2) (2yo Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Fitzella's run a massive race and it's always the 'what if' question when you're second. If Andre had decided against it this morning she would have won a Group 2 in devastatingly impressive fashion and she'd probably be favourite for next year's 1,000 Guineas. But that's not what happened. Luckily the remarkable filly she finished second to is trained a thousand miles away from where my horse is trained and we might find it rather easier to avoid her than if she were with Karl Burke. Oisin said it was definitely a career-best and she's got options; she's in the Moyglare, she's in the Cheveley Park and the Rockfel, while the Breeders' Cup remains an option as well. We were going further clear of the third with every stride so she stayed really well, we were just beaten by a better filly. She's every chance of staying a mile, probably not this year though unless we go to the Breeders' Cup - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.race: Sodexo Live! Princess Margaret Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Oisin [Murphy, jockey] was upset when he came in after the Albany because he felt he sat too close to a very strong pace. He did realise and took back, but the damage was done by then and we felt on reflection that it was Fitzella's class which allowed her to finish fourth. The plan today was to hold her up and race more patiently, and to use her finish, but she absolutely pinged the lids and Oisin went to plan b. It worked very nicely and he didn't go hard - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred 'Supporting Macmillan' EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fitzella has done it with the minimum of fuss. We've loved her from day one, I think she was our most expensive yearling last year. Everything we've done with her at home, she's learned and done it so much better the next time, which is exactly what she's done today. She's going to go up massively in grade and I think we'll go for the Albany over six as eventually she's potentially a miler. She's gorgeous and beautifully bred - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A gorgeous filly who has been a star for us. She rushed the gates in the Cheveley Park and crashed her head into them. It's hard to say she completely didn't run her race, but we were expecting more. Because she didn't get into a rhythm after that, she didn't handle the Dip. We were thinking about the Breeders' Cup if she had been right there in the mix, but that will be it for this year. We don't really know what her trip will be as a three-year-old. I think we'll enter her in the 1,000 Guineas and run in a trial. If we come back after the Nell Gwyn and find she doesn't handle the Dip, we could maybe go to the French Guineas. She might be a sprinter as she's fast, but I thought she stayed 7f well in the Prix du Calvados. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Not disgraced when eighth in 5f Listed race at Bath last month but this requires more
runners.spotlight: A fairly useful 5f winner at 2yrs; not disgraced after six months off when a close eighth of 14 in 5f Listed race at Bath last month but this requires more.

quotes.race: Queen Mary Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: You come into every race wanting to win but at 100/1 you have to check reality and see what's possible but we always liked Flowerhead at home. We're only a very small team so to see her run such a big race like that it's huge for us and to have the support of Amo and the team there has just made a complete change to the start of my career. We came in here hopeful but not expecting too much and she's very gutsy and tried very hard so we can think about the bigger picture now - Charlie Clover, trainer.

runners.comment: Comfortably landed odds in 7f maiden at Newmarket 16 days ago; has fair bit more to offer
runners.spotlight: Built on debut promise when comfortably landing the odds in 7f maiden at Newmarket 16 days ago; this is much tougher but this Night Of Thunder filly looks to have a fair bit more to offer; very much one to consider.

runners.comment: Landed Newbury Listed event in August but seventh in Group 3 at Longchamp final run
runners.spotlight: Landed 5f maiden (for Raphael Freire) last spring before showing much improved form to follow up for her new yard in 5f Newbury Listed event in August; only seventh of ten in Group 3 at Longchamp (5f) final run and faces no easy task on her return.

quotes.race: Sequoia Hair & Spirit St Hugh's Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Hollywood Treasure has only had the one start ? she had a bit of a setback ? and she'll get a lot of confidence from that because she won well. When the gap opened up she picked up well and she was strong at the line. She could get six, she's got a lot of natural speed so there are options for her - Rowan Scott, jockey.

runners.comment: Sweet Solera runner-up at Newmarket at 2yrs; beat one in Fred Darling at Newbury on return
runners.spotlight: Stylish winner of 6f Ascot novice in July and bettered that form when runner-up in the Sweet Solera at Newmarket (7f) and fourth in a Longchamp Group 2 (1m) in the autumn; hooded for her reappearance but she beat only one home in Fred Darling Stakes at Newbury; headgear quickly dispensed with.

quotes.race: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was really smart. Princess Petrol had a lovely intro at Newbury with George Downing, who gave her a lovely educational ride, and learned a lot there. She's reaped the rewards here. There was a moment of worry in the stalls but she does that, even going to the stables sometimes. She likes to make everyone think she's in charge. We'll go 7f next time. Her dam won the Oh So Sharp Stakes and those kind of races would be good for her, but the Sweet Solera might come too soon. We'll definitely step up in class now - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She did very well last year and was unlucky not to win the Sweet Solera Stakes at Newmarket. She hasn't progressed a great deal physically, but she's been training well and she was coming with a bit of a run on the toughest part of the track in the Fred Darling until she got knocked sideways. She was a bit gassy but hopefully that run has blown the cobwebs away. We'll probably go for a Listed race next and try to get that all-important stakes win. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Landed Newcastle novice but ninth in Group 3 at Chantilly since; plenty to find on form
runners.spotlight: Starman filly who went 2-2 when impressively landing 6f Newcastle novice in March; only ninth of 13 in Group 3 at Chantilly 18 days ago though so has plenty to find on form.

stable_tour.quote: A quick filly who's going for the Prix Sigy on April 7 for a first run on grass. We've won that race before with the likes of Quiet Reflection and I think she's a sprinter. 31-03-26

runners.breeder: Mrs Liz Barry & Mr Luke Barry
runners.owner: Mrs Frank Barry & Mrs Luke Barry

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Frank Barry & Mrs Luke Barry

runners.comment: Won Southwell maiden; improved when sixth in 7f AW Listed event at Lingfield; more needed
runners.spotlight: Last on her debut (for Jessica Harrington) at the Curragh in August but she comfortably landed a 6f Southwell maiden in January before improving again when a close sixth of eight in 7f AW Listed event at Lingfield the following month; this demands another sizeable step forward though.

runners.comment: Good fifth in Fred Darling at Newbury on return; back in trip but capable of better
runners.spotlight: Promising filly who has improved with each of her three runs; ready winner of a 7f Newmarket novice in November and reappeared with a good fifth of 14 in the Fred Darling Stakes at Newbury (7f) two weeks ago; drops back in trip but capable of better still and firmly in the picture.

racecards.verdict: Hugo Palmer's FITZELLA (nap) is taken to build on an encouraging reappearance fifth in the Nell Gwyn now she is dropped back in trip.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Fitzella, 7/2 Hassaleh,  Zooming, 8/1 Argentine Tango, 10/1 Flowerhead, 12/1 Princess Petrol, 14/1 Hollywood Treasure, 16/1 Soul Love, 50/1 Starfinch

racecards.race_name: Fitzdares Conqueror Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.comment: Reliable mare who should go well again back in a Listed event but her last win was in 2024
runners.spotlight: Talented mare who ran well in Listed and Group events last season and was runner-up in a Class 2 handicap at Newmarket (1m, good) on her reappearance last month; should go well again but she has a bit to find on these figures and her last win was in July 2024.

stable_tour.quote: She's very talented but needs to be ridden with restraint. I thought she was a little bit unlucky on her comeback, but she hasn't stayed in training to win handicaps at Newmarket, so it was a great reappearance. She'll likely go to the Listed Conqueror Stakes at Goodwood next, which she probably should have won last season but for traffic problems. She likes fast ground and, if we can get the big black type secured, then we may well become more ambitious and take a shot at Group 2s or even Group 1s. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Fair effort on her Kempton reappearance but this looks a tough task on the figures
runners.spotlight: Won a Listed race at York (5f, good) as a 2yo but she's 0-12 since and has had some major blips along the way; reappeared with fair fifth in Listed event at Kempton (1m) in March but Never Let Go was ahead of her in that race and the market leaders were well below form; only beaten a nose in the corresponding race 12 months ago but even that will need bettering today.

quotes.race: Clipper EBF Marygate Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I bred Betty Clover her and I'm so wildly excited, I just can't believe it. I thought she had a chance of a place and I thought she had a chance of turning the form round with Running Queen, who got first run on us last time. Georgia gave her the most beautiful ride. I'm very proud of my jockey, she doesn't get many chances and bloody hell she's good. She should be saluted for that.   We have to look at Ascot. I don't know which race. It's a very fast five furlongs at York and she travelled all right into it but we'll have a think - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She was second, beaten only a nose, by last week's Duke of Cambridge winner Crimson Advocate in a Listed fillies' race at Goodwood and was then third in a Group 2 in France. She ran in the Sandringham at Royal Ascot on Friday and I was expecting her to go very well as a Group horse in a handicap but she was pulled up. I think she must have whacked a joint and I'm really happy that William Buick pulled her up as it's better to be safe than sorry. She appears to be fine but we'll make further checks just in case to make sure there's no problem. I think she's very underrated and I've got her in the Falmouth at the Newmarket July meeting. That may be a step too far, but all being well it'll be Group races over a mile for her. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Listed winner who was runner-up in a Group 1 in her final 3yo run; strong claims on return
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced and progressive filly who completed a hat-trick in a Listed race at Sandown (1m, good to firm) last July; held in second in her final two runs last season but the first was a Group 3 and latest was in the Group 1 Sun Chariot Stakes at Newmarket; sets the standard on this big drop back in class and she's a strong contender on her return.

quotes.race: BetMGM Sun Chariot Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Blue Bolt has run a career best, no doubt about it, and Andrew Balding was very confident beforehand as she's been working well. She didn't enjoy the very soft ground at Sandown last time but this was better for her and she was in the right place sat on the heels of the winner. She hasn't many miles on the clock and could make up into a smart four-year-old next year - Barry Mahon, oiwners' racing manager.

quotes.race: Coral Distaff (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Blue Bolt is a lovely filly. We couldn't really train her last year as she had a few niggles. She's improved with her racing and her work this year and seems to be getting better and better. She's smart - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Blue Bolt is a nice filly. She won well the last day and she seems to have stepped forward again. She's very uncomplicated and gallops on anything. The first half felt very easy and she got a bit lonely when they quickened, but she's a filly with a nice future - Colin Keane, jockey.

runners.comment: Lost unbeaten record in a Group 1 last June but she's still unexposed; respected on return
runners.spotlight: Made it 3-3 when landing a Listed race at York (1m, good to firm) last May but she found things tough in the Group 1 Coronation Stakes at Ascot (never-dangerous seventh) the following month; has been on the sidelines since but she's still unexposed and could resume her progress back in calmer waters on her return.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (Registered As The Michael Seely Memorial Fillies' Stakes)
quotes.quote: I'm thrilled. Kon Tiki trained well all winter and I had her in the Guineas but we decided to come here because it was first time on turf, coming off the all-weather and I thought this was a nice start for her and allowed her to come in her coat.  Mr Harris likes them to go gradually up the staircase, there's no rush. So we'll head for the Sandringham, a Group 2 at Chantilly in June.  Then for me it would be the Falmouth - Jane Chapple-Hyam, trainer.

quotes.race: Free Bet With Unibet's Betbuilder Rebound Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This was a competitive novice but we felt coming here gave us an extra week up our sleeve for the Guineas rather than running in the Nell Gwyn. I'm thrilled with the way Kon Tiki did and how she quickened up. As long as she comes out of this okay she will go for the Guineas - Jane Chapple-Hyam, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Runner-up in Listed race at Kempton latest but this is a much tougher test; down the list
runners.spotlight: Won the Sandringham Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer; runner-up in Listed events in two of her three runs since but she chased home a rival with a BHA rating of 94 at Kempton last month and this is a much tougher test; down the list.

quotes.race: Sandringham Stakes (Fillies' Handicap)
quotes.quote: Kieran's [Shoemark] given Never Let Go a peach. She's a filly we've always believed in and thought this race would be ideal for, and we were not getting in the race at one stage because she didn't win at Wetherby, she didn't win at Haydock, and I thought, 'crikey, we're not going to get in' and I was desperate to run her here, so we ran her in a Listed race, Hollie gave her an absolute peach, she nicked some black type and went up enough to get in, which I was thrilled about. I think she can go on. The family get better with time, she's still very raw still and unfurnished and leggy. She's a homebred of the Keswicks who have supported me for a few years now, and we had a really good year for them last year with Celandine being the highlight - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was good to see her placed in a Listed race at Goodwood the other day, beaten less than a length. She went up 12lb but I still think she's well handicapped for the Sandringham. 10-06-25

She ran a big race when second in the Snowdrop Stakes at Kempton at 25-1 and should have a good year. We could run her in the Nottinghamshire Oaks on Sunday or the Conqueror Stakes at Goodwood on Guineas weekend and, if we can make her a stakes winner, her big target would be the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot, where she won the Sandringham last year. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Demoted to second in French 1,000 Guineas last season; respected back in trip on return
runners.spotlight: Won a Haydock maiden (7f, good to firm) as a 2yo; all three runs last season were in France and she suffered a heartbreaking demotion for connections when placed second in the French 1,000 Guineas at Longchamp (1m, good); well held at Chantilly in her final run last term but that was the French Oaks and she may have had stamina issues over an extended 1m2f; returns after 11 months off but she's still lightly raced and needs a close look on this drop back in trip and class.

quotes.race: Prix de Diane Longines (Group 1) (3yo Fillies) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Kieran felt they went a good pace and Shes Perfect never quite dropped it. She always looked like she was just in a gear too many. He felt coming into the straight he had plenty in the tank but she emptied very quickly. I think we'll come back to a mile after that. It was always the big question mark and she's got lots of speed. I think very simply she didn't quite get home. I thought getting a lead would help us but she never really switched off and the last furlong and a half looked a very long way - Charlie Fellowes, trainer.

quotes.race: Emirates Poule d'Essai des Pouliches (Group 1) (3yo Fillies) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: We've been invited into the stewards' room and they are going to explain and let us know the process from here. I thought [the interference] was minimal and a long way out and I was very surprised. In England that would not be overturned but we're not in England and I don''t know the rules over here. I'd need to speak to some people and get some advice on the situation and decide whether it's worth it [appealing the decision] - Charlie Fellowes, trainer of Shes Perfect.I'm gutted for the connections but we've got a wonderful filly. Shes Perfect is really exciting going forward and I'm sorry for the connections that it didn't happen today. We'll get over it and I'm sure we'll see her at Ascot, she's a wonderful filly - Kieren Shoemark, jockey.

quotes.race: Prix de la Grotte (Group 3) (3yo Fillies) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Shes Perfect pinged the lids from out wide and Shoey [Kieran Shoemark] had no choice but to slide across and just let her bowl along. She'll come on for this, she's not rock-hard fit and she'll improve, so I'm delighted with that, she's run a cracker - Charlie Fellowes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won nicely at Haydock and had working well at home so that wasn't a massive surprise. She could go to the Rockfel and there's also a £100,000 restricted final at Goodwood on September 25 that she's eligible for but I don't want to overrace her. 11-09-24

racecards.verdict: The leading contender is the progressive BLUE BOLT who was runner-up in a Group 1 in October and sets the standard on her return.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Blue Bolt, 9/4 Shes Perfect, 6/1 Arisaig, 7/1 Kon Tiki, 12/1 Never Let Go, 25/1 Betty Clover

racecards.race_name: Munro UK Equity Income Fund Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

prev_owners.owner: John Johnstone, Capt Adrian Pratt & Lord Clinton

runners.comment: Has done well since switched to hurdling and he's respected back on the Flat
runners.spotlight: Made good start to hurdling career in the autumn, including when going close in a Cheltenham novice (2m4f, good to soft; has won on good ground); reappeared with a creditable third at Plumpton last month and he's feasibly treated on his best Flat form last year, including a sequence of runner-up efforts over staying trips; respected back in this sphere.

stable_tour.quote: I like this horse. He was rated 85 on the Flat and won nicely on his debut over hurdles at Uttoxeter before walking over at Ludlow. He runs in the 2m4f novice hurdle at Cheltenham on Friday and he should go well. 24-10-25

runners.comment: C&D winner and he's in the mix off a workable mark back on the Flat
runners.spotlight: Acts on good and heavy ground; won off 2lb lower over C&D for Charlie Johnston last autumn and he ran well over hurdles last month, on his second run for current yard; seems tactically versatile and he's in the mix off a workable mark back on the Flat.

quotes.race: Royal Sussex Regiment Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: That was a good performance. The three-year-olds over this sort of distance get a good weight allowance and we thought that would really matter in this kind of ground. Novelista is a big, immature horse who stays every inch of the trip and he deserved a win - Mark Johnston, trainer's assistant. Novelista deserved that today. He's probably still a bit weak and is probably better on a flatter track but that should do his confidence the world of good - Hollie Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Michel Sardou
runners.comment: Triple C&D winner and he needs watching in market back on the Flat
runners.spotlight: Well held over hurdles in last three runs but he's won plenty under both codes including three over C&D; still 3lb higher than for his win here last June but he needs watching in market back on the Flat; effective on good/good to firm but most of his wins have come on slow ground.

quotes.race: cavani.co.uk Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: All credit for this goes to Josh (Moore), he was adamant we should come up here with Aggagio today. He gave me my instructions, to pop him out and be very positive on him, and it's worked - Caoilin Quinn, rider.

quotes.race: Royal Sussex Regiment Handicap
quotes.quote: I don't know if there's another race back here for Aggagio. If there was he might come back, but the ground would have to be soft enough. Otherwise, he'll go jumping because his handicap mark is what it is now. He wouldn't want it bottomless over jumps - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Sussex Roof Garden Bar Handicap
quotes.quote: Aggagio is a lovely horse. We didn't know he'd get the trip, but he's done really well. I was a bit worried about the ground if it was soft, which Goshen wants and we don't really. Gary Moore will place him where he wants and Aidan said he might get slightly further - Gary Robinson, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He did a bit of damage when he fell over fences at Plumpton in April. He's had a couple of runs back, including a spin on the Flat, and shaped okay at Wincanton over hurdles a couple of weeks ago. We'll stick over hurdles and, providing we can get his confidence back, he should do okay on slow ground. 29-10-24

runners.comment: Won over 2m in final two runs last season and he's open to more progress as a 4yo
runners.spotlight: Improved form upped to 2m when winning at Kempton (AW) and Nottingham (good) in his final two runs last season; up another 5lb but he still looks feasibly treated and could continue on an upward curve as a 4yo; interesting contender on his return.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Colwick Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: We are thrilled to bits with that. We enjoyed winning last time out at Kempton Park, but we didn't quite know what would happen this time back on turf, however. I thought it was a good performance and St Mawes battled well. We thought there was talent with him, but it has been unlocking that ability and it now seems to have clicked at last. The feedback after his last win was that he had come on again. The original thought after Kempton Park was to see if he could do it again and then have a break and give him some time off over the winter before bringing him back next year, but we will chat to Emma and see what we will do - Julian Reed, owner.

runners.comment: Ten-time winner but he flopped at Lingfield latest and his last turf win was in 2022
runners.spotlight: Recorded his tenth win when scoring at Wolverhampton (2m, Tapeta) in January; held his form with creditable efforts in next three starts but his good spell came to a halt at Lingfield last month; has bit to prove again after that heavy defeat and his last turf win was in 2022.

runners.comment: Dual AW winner but has mixed record in handicaps and she's untried at 2m; new headgear
runners.spotlight: Both wins have been on AW and latest was on her Southwell reappearance (1m4f) in March; only 3lb higher than for that win but she faded at Wolverhampton (1m6f) last time and is untried at this trip; comes with risks attached and she's not been easy to predict in handicaps; first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Hat-trick seeker who has won four times on AW since December; respected back on turf
runners.spotlight: Four AW wins since December and she completed a double in good style at Lingfield (2m) last month; 7lb higher back on turf but that was a clear personal best last time and she's unexposed in this sphere; respected.

quotes.race: Midnite All-Weather Vase Marathon Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Arc Zoosve has recently got two new owners into racing in Iain Francis and his wife Ingrid and I sold him to them before he won at Southwell last time ? so what a fantastic start they have had. He's improving and pretty exciting. With his pedigree, it gives you hope he can keep improving. He's a good-ground horse so when we were heading into the depths of winter it made more sense to run him on the all-weather than stick to jumping. I'm keen to target the two-and-a-half-mile handicap at Glorious Goodwood that we won with Lil Rockerfeller -  Neil King, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The two who appeal most are the hat-trick seekers Arc Zoosve and ST MAWES, with slight preference for the latter.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Arc Zoosve, 100/30 St Mawes, 9/2 Percy Shelley,  Novelista, 5/1 Solar Pass, 8/1 Aggagio, 10/1 Appier

racecards.race_name: Highclere Castle Gin Handicap

runners.comment: Has patchy profile and was well held when last seen in December; work to do back on grass
runners.spotlight: Winning start on turf as 2yo and later won on handicap debut on AW (both 5f); lightly raced and kept to AW since, some way below best at Southwell in December (first-time cheekpieces, retained); work to do back on grass.

runners.comment: 0-16 on turf but he was only beaten a nose at Bath on Monday; leading claims off same mark
runners.spotlight: All seven wins have been on AW; record of 0-16 on turf but he was only beaten a nose off this mark at Bath (5f, firm) on Monday; has leading claims if he can repeat that form and he's versatile ground-wise; regular hood is removed and cheekpieces return.

quotes.race: It's Never Ordinary At bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: The Thames Boatman needs pace in his races and looking at this race beforehand I knew he'd get that today, so that was an advantage. He's at his best when he has something to aim at, but he made life harder for himself by hanging in the last half a furlong. We do think he's a smart horse, especially on the all-weather - Finley Marsh, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He was brilliant at Lingfield on Saturday, taking his record at the track to 3-3. He just got there over 5f and we might see an ounce of improvement if we go to 6f. He loves Lingfield, so we'll probably stick to there for now. 18-09-24

runners.comment: Ended last season with a second at Newmarket (5f) and she needs a close look on return
runners.spotlight: All three wins have been at 6f but she ended last season with a creditable second over this trip at Newmarket (good); has gone close when fresh in the past and she's a player if she can pick up where she left off.

quotes.race: At The Races App Market Movers Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands C-D 3 Runs Or Fewer) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Everything went smoothly. Tiger Tulip was away nicely and we just took a tow into the race off the favourite. She's still very inexperienced so I thought I'd squeeze her in between two (rivals) in the home straight and she picked up nicely - Cieren Fallon, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Turf winner who was only just caught over 6f on Polytrack last time; respected up 2lb
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-12 but his win was on turf (5f, good) last summer and he had a near-miss on Polytrack at Lingfield (6f) in March; nudged up 2lb but that was a bold bid from a tough draw last time and he's respected back in trip.

runners.comment: Triple winner but all over longer trips and he's untried at 5f; others preferred
runners.spotlight: His three wins have come over 6f/7f including at Goodwood (good to soft) last summer and at Kempton (off 3lb lower) in January; made some late gains when a creditable third at Kempton last month but this is a different test and his tactical speed will be tested on this first try at 5f.

runners.comment: Dual AW winner who was disappointing in final run last season; bit to prove on return
runners.spotlight: Two 5f wins on AW last year but she's been absent since a disappointing run at Southwell (tenth of 12) in September; has bit to prove on her return and this is competitive back on turf.

runners.breeder: J A Knox And Mrs M A Knox
runners.comment: His last two wins were over 6f in 2024; well-beaten sixth in the 4.25 here on Friday
runners.spotlight: Won twice at Newmarket (6f, good) in 2024 but he's drawn a blank since; finished runner-up on stable debut at Leicester last month but he was 6l behind the winner and and is only 1lb lower on this drop back in trip; well-beaten sixth in the 4.25 here on Friday.

runners.comment: Well handicapped on his Newbury win last summer but he's been disappointing since
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer who has won five times on turf including at Newbury (5f, good to firm) last July; well handicapped on that form but he's been disappointing since and has plenty to prove after 108 days off.

runners.comment: Made the breakthrough at Kempton (6f) and has possibilities if he can back that up
runners.spotlight: 4yo who made the breakthrough when scoring off a reduced mark at Kempton (6f, Polytrack; 18-1) in March; has claims if he can back that up but he can miss the break and will need a good pace on this drop back to 5f.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to THE THAMES BOATMAN who had a near-miss at Bath on Monday and is on the same mark here.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 The Thames Boatman, 5/1 Rory Rocket, 6/1 Solvency,  Sandscreendeliverd, 7/1 Tiger Tulip, 8/1 Serenity Dream, 9/1 Spring Bloom, 12/1 Tanjen,  Faustus

racecards.race_name: Listen To Track Radio Next Week Handicap

runners.comment: Last of 11 in Lingfield h'cap in February; needs to take a big step forward after a break
runners.spotlight: A very useful 1m2f/1m4f winner at his best but lightly raced in recent seasons and came in last of 11 in 1m2f AW Lingfield handicap in February; needs to take a big step forward after a break.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet November Handicap
quotes.quote: Jack gave Lord Melbourne a lovely ride. He's a push-button ride and didn't really travel with Jack, but he kept him in the hunt and kept on finding - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

quotes.race: Queen Mother's Cup Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys)
quotes.quote: I spoke to Tyler Heard who rode Lord Melbourne at Epsom and he said sit handy with a bit of cover. He was sure he'd stay, he had form at Pontefract over 1m4f on heavy ground. He saw it out really well. He's a really nice, straightforward, uncomplicated horse. He travelled throughout and quickened nicely - Serena Brotherton, jockey.

runners.comment: Enjoyed a very good 2025 when a three-time winner; can't be ruled out on his return
runners.spotlight: Enjoyed a very good 2025 (three-time 9.5f to 1m4f winner) and he signed off with a good sixth in 1m6f Ascot listed race in October when set a lot to do; hood goes on and can't be ruled out on his seasonal return.

prev_owners.owner: Fal Stud Sas, Gl Racing Et Al

runners.comment: Failed to shine in Meydan for Fawzi Nass in February; gelded and starts out for a new yard
runners.spotlight: A useful ex-French 9.5f scorer who failed to shine in a couple of 9f handicaps at Meydan for Fawzi Nass in February; since gelded and starts out for another new yard here.

runners.comment: Good third here in August but below par on softer ground subsequently; not dismissed
runners.spotlight: Very useful winner at his best; posted a good third over 1m4f here in August but below par on softer ground subsequently; not dismissed off a reduced mark on his return.

quotes.race: bet365 Cambridgeshire Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: It is his distance and he stays every inch off that. Okay Majestic had luck in running but he has had an easy life so far as four months ago he was an unraced four-year-old. That's probably it now and we will call it a day for the season - Nick Hitchins, owner/breeder.

stable_tour.quote: Last time he came 12th in the Cambridgeshire, which he won in 2022 and was fourth in last year. He may be out again on turf before the end of the season but if the ground stays really soft we might look at the all-weather with him. 10-10-24

runners.comment: Three-time course winner; good fifth in Lincoln at Doncaster so must enter calculations
runners.spotlight: A three-time course winner who returned from five months off with a good fifth of 21 in the Lincoln at Doncaster; he's proven over this longer trip so must enter calculations eased 1lb.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 firmly on the up with Newmarket win; more to offer in 2026 so well in the mix
runners.spotlight: Ended last season firmly on the up with gutsy success in 1m4f Newmarket handicap in October; this low-mileage son of Sea The Stars has more to offer in 2026 and is well in the mix despite dropping in trip and up 6lb for his return.

quotes.race: bet365 Old Rowley Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Yabher nearly fell over at Goodwood last time and has had a long time to recuperate. He travelled like the winner throughout and he could be a good Saturday horse - Phillip Robinson, racing manager.

runners.breeder: G H S Bloodstock & J C Bloodstock
runners.comment: Impressive reappearance win at Nottingham; showed a good turn of foot there so big shout
runners.spotlight: Progressive son of New Bay who returned with an impressive victory in 1m2f Nottingham handicap last month; hiked up 8lb but showed a good turn of foot there so big shout.

runners.comment: Winless since 2024; not given a hard time of it when well held on Doncaster return
runners.spotlight: Winless since 2024 but largely in good nick last season and not given a hard time of it when well held on his return in 1m2f Doncaster handicap in March; can take a step forward now.

runners.owner: All For One Racing III & I Bandres
runners.comment: C&D winner who  comes here in good nick after a spell in Meydan; not discounted
runners.spotlight: Dual winner last spring (including over C&D) and comes here in good nick after a spell in Meydan; he's not discounted.

quotes.race: Lilley Plummer Risks City & Suburban Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't sure City Of Delight handled the track until he hit the rising ground in the last 50 metres. He looked like getting swamped but then he flew and ran on well. I'm proud of him. He did it the hard way but he's so consistent. He's so easy to train and has all the traits of a good horse. I think it would make sense to come back here for a handicap on Oaks day or to step him up to a mile and a half. I think he's craving a step up in trip but he keeps winning over this one so I'm happy to take my time - David Menuisier, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Top Price Guarantee Races Handicap
quotes.quote: City Of Delight stays this trip really well and has a big heart. What stuck out to me was his will to win, he is admirable really - Kieran Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: Nothing went right last time at Haydock. He didn't lie up with the pace and burned out his energy in the back straight. He just didn't perform, so we'll go back to basics and to a trip he has won over before. We looked at the Chesterfield Cup at Goodwood on Tuesday but he didn't get in. He goes on any ground. 30-07-25

prev_owners.owner: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith

runners.comment: Offered little in handful of runs for current yard, beating two at Newbury on his return
runners.spotlight: Useful ex-Irish winner but he's offered little in a handful of runs for his current yard, beating just two in 1m Newbury handicap on his recent return; others are much preferred.

quotes.race: SP Or Better Guaranteed With Tote Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Samuel Colt is a lovely colt. He wasn't in love with the ground but his class got him through it. He could be an exciting colt for next year all being well - Chris Armstrong, assistant trainer.

runners.comment: Looked on the up when twice second last spring; off since July but remains with potential
runners.spotlight: Looked on the up when twice runner-up in 1m2f handicaps at Sandown and York last spring; not seen out after posting just a fair fourth at Newmarket in July but subsequently gelded and remains with potential for yard among the winners.

racecards.verdict: There was a lot to like about the Nottingham reappearance win of LOVE BEACH, so he is taken to make light of a 6lb rise.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Yabher, 100/30 Love Beach, 11/2 Alpha Crucis,  Urban Glimpse, 6/1 Circus Of Rome, 8/1 City Of Delight, 20/1 Too Soon, 25/1 Lord Melbourne,  Al Aali,  Majestic, 66/1 Samuel Colt

racecards.race_name: Fitzdares Offers Bespoke Bets Handicap

runners.comment: Still early days but he needs to resume his progress back up in trip and down in grade
runners.spotlight: Had form figures of 421 in novice events (7f/1m) during the winter; started his handicap career with a heavy defeat at Newcastle last month but that was over 6f in a valuable event on Good Friday; this is more suitable but he needs to resume his progress back up in trip and down in grade.

stable_tour.quote: I think I got it wrong by running him over 6f at Newcastle. He was outpaced from a long way out, up against a better grade of sprinter, and I'll step him back up to 7f or even a mile. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Flopped on handicap debut at Nottingham in October and has bit to prove for new yard
runners.spotlight: Justified support with front-running win in Ayr novice (1m, good to soft) in September but he flopped when favourite on handicap debut at Nottingham (1m2f) the following month; left Adrian Keatley since; may have had stamina issues last time but that was a heavy defeat and he has bit to prove on return for new yard.

quotes.race: Almins Vantage/Lallemand Magniva Classic EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've thought a bit about Sea The Power for a long time. The plan was always to make the running. York just probably didn't suit him on the day, he was just run off his feet a little bit early on and he'll go a mile and a quarter or a mile and a half no problem - Adrian Keatley, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He has a big future. Things didn't go well for him at Beverley last week. They crawled down the hill and he pulled hard. He'll come on a ton for that introduction and I'm now looking at the Convivial Maiden at York. He needs 7f or a mile at this stage. 07-08-25

runners.owner: Jastar Capital, K Lawrence & P Merritt
runners.comment: Kempton winner who is unexposed and looks interesting on his handicap/turf debut
runners.spotlight: Promising fourth on Wolverhampton debut in November and he ran to a similar level when landing the odds at Kempton (1m) in February; returns after another break but this unexposed gelding has a striking pedigree and he's an interesting contender on handicap/turf debut.

runners.comment: Twice-raced colt but opening mark looks on the high side and he needs major improvement
runners.spotlight: 16-1 winner on Lingfield debut (7f, AW) in November but he failed to match that when a well-held fifth on his Leicester reappearance last month; still early days but opening mark looks on the high side and he needs major improvement upped in trip.

runners.comment: Went close in a Wolverhampton novice last month; respected upped in trip on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Reached the frame in all three qualifying runs including a close call on his reappearance over 7f at Wolverhampton (13-8 favourite) last month; out of a useful 9.5f winner and he's open to more progress upped in trip on handicap debut; shortlisted.

runners.breeder: Bermart Bloodstock, Equinow Srl, Valle F
runners.comment: Reappeared with a laboured effort at Newmarket (1m) and others are preferred
runners.spotlight: Won a Salisbury novice (7f, good) in his final 2yo run but he was only eighth of 12 on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m; first run since gelded) last month; has bit to prove after that laboured effort and he needs more progress to defy this mark; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Handicap newcomer and he's a possible improver on this step up to 1m
runners.spotlight: Had only two runs as a 2yo and the second was a daunting task in the Chesham at Royal Ascot; never involved back in a novice on Doncaster reappearance (7f, good to soft) last month but this is more realistic and he's a possible improver upped in trip on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Clearcut win in Pontefract handicap in October; respected off 6lb higher on his return
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the sixth attempt when forging clear to justify favouritism in Pontefract handicap (1m, soft) in October; 6lb higher on his return but he should have more to offer at this trip and he seems versatile ground-wise; respected.

runners.owner: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
runners.comment: Won on AW in final two runs last season and he's respected back on turf on his return
runners.spotlight: Made his breakthrough when landing a Kempton nursery (1m, AW) in September and he followed up with another comfortable success at Wolverhampton (9.4f) five days later; 7lb higher in this deeper race on his return but he's still lightly raced and is out of a useful turf winner; respected.

runners.comment: Win and close third in two nurseries last autumn; been gelded before this return to action
runners.spotlight: Won on nursery debut at Salisbury (7f, heavy) in September and he was a close third of four in similar conditions at Doncaster the following month; still has low mileage but he needs more progress back on quicker ground after 189 days off; been gelded since his last run.

runners.owner: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
runners.comment: Won at Chester on the second of his two 2yo runs; needs close look on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Made a low-key start at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) last June but he left that form behind when justifying support over 7f at Chester (good) the following month; been gelded since and he needs a close look now upped to 1m on his handicap/seasonal debut.

runners.comment: Well held in two AW handicaps this season and he needs a transformation back on turf
runners.spotlight: Won a 7f Musselburgh maiden (good) last August but he's been held in two handicaps at Wolverhampton (8.6f/7f) this season; has something to prove and he needs a transformation back on turf.

runners.breeder: New England Stud & Mount Coote Stud
runners.comment: Handicap debutant but this is competitive and he has lots to prove on return; been gelded
runners.spotlight: Finished in rear in his three 2yo runs including a tailed-off effort at Kempton (1m) last time; now goes handicapping after a gelding operation but this is a competitive and he has plenty to prove after 199 days off.

runners.breeder: R F And S D Knipe
runners.comment: Unexposed as a handicapper but she needs to find more at this new trip on her return
runners.spotlight: Won a Lingfield maiden (7f, AW) last summer but she didn't go on from that in three subsequent runs last season; still unexposed as a handicapper but she needs to find more at this new trip on her return.

stable_tour.quote: She was placed in her first three starts and then hosed up at Lingfield on Monday. At the moment she's chasing the Great British Bonus - she was only a 1,200gns buy, so can go in the D Class bonus races. That's the big aim this season. 27-08-25

racecards.verdict: This looks wide open but Pontefract winner OHARA could continue on an upward curve this season and he gets the vote on his return.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Law Court, 5/1 Berkshire Boom, 11/2 Mohaaraj, 15/2 Chapter, 8/1 Midnight Rodeo, 10/1 Dumuji,  Ohara, 14/1 Northern Empire,  Akho Mezzna, 20/1 Sea The Power,  Brave Hunter,  Lyra Lea, 25/1 Born A Star,  Celestarak

racecards.race_name: Fitzdares Telephone And Text Betting Service Handicap

runners.comment: Still has potential but he was tailed off latest and needs more progress at this new trip
runners.spotlight: Record of 2-5 on AW and he had a near-miss at Haydock (6f, good to soft) in his only previous turf start; had tough assignment in a valuable handicap at Newcastle (6f; cheekpieces added) on Good Friday but he finished tailed off and needs to resume his progress at this new trip.

runners.comment: Highly tried in final three 2yo runs; been gelded and now goes handicapping on his return
runners.spotlight: Won on Ayr debut (6f, good) last June and was highly tried when down the field in Listed events and the Group 1 Phoenix Stakes in his final three runs as a 2yo; opening mark looks on the high side on the balance of his form but he's still unexposed and needs watching in market on his return; been gelded since his last run.

runners.comment: May have needed the run on stable debut and he's not ruled out on this drop back in grade
runners.spotlight: Easy win on Leicester debut (5f, good to firm) last May and he finished runner-up in two of his three handicaps for Richard Hughes, including over 6f at this track and over 7f at Newbury; well held on stable debut two weeks ago but he may have needed that run and he's not ruled out on this drop back in grade.

stable_tour.quote: He's nice and won really well on his debut at Leicester. He should run a good race in thew Windsor Castle. 10-06-25

runners.comment: Handicap newcomer and he needs a close look on his first run after being gelded
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt when landing the odds with an all-the-way win at Kempton (7f, AW) in October; struggled in his final run last season but that was a hot conditions event and he was always on the back foot after missing the break; been gelded since and he needs a close look back up in trip on his handicap/seasonal debut.

runners.comment: Unexposed filly and she's in the mix back in calmer waters on her handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Big improvement when going close in a Newmarket novice (7f, good to soft) in the third of her three 2yo runs; found things tough in the Nell Gwyn (Group 3) on her reappearance but this is more realistic and she's still unexposed; in the mix on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Has mixed record in five starts and others are more persuasive; blinkers added
runners.spotlight: Won a Newmarket novice (7f, good) in October but has a mixed record in his five starts and was beaten 10l on recent handicap/seasonal debut at Newmarket (1m, good); now drops back in trip with blinkers added but others are more persuasive.

quotes.race: Safer Gambling With CopyBet Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Major Neigh Sayer is a horse we've always liked and he has improved for the step up in trip. We may chuck him into a trial next spring and see where we are and if not we could work back from a Britannia - George Scott, trainer.

runners.comment: Won 7f maiden on his return and he's open to more progress back in a handicap; respected
runners.spotlight: Returned after a gelding operation with comfortable win in Catterick maiden (7f, good; 7-4 favourite) last month; this is tougher off a revised mark back in a handicap but that was a personal best last time and he's open to more progress; respected.

stable_tour.quote: It was great he got his head in front finally at Catterick as he'd become quite frustrating last year. I hope he'll improve as he steps up in trip and become a progressive miler. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Overall record of 1-9 and was well below form on her stable debut in March; opposable
runners.spotlight: Her eight 2yo runs for Eve Johnston Houghton yielded one win, a 7f maiden at Epsom last summer; looked exposed as the season went on and she failed to beat a rival on her stable debut at Kempton (1m) in March; now drops back in trip and class but others are preferred.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lovely filly who has been second on both her starts over 6f. I think she probably needs 7f and I entered her over that distance at Newbury on Tuesday. She led the time before at Goodwood but was outpaced two furlongs out before staying on really strongly behind the winner, Game Striker. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Has record of 34131 in handicaps and is only 2lb higher than for his last win; big player
runners.spotlight: Progressive gelding who has form figures of 34131 since switched to handicaps and that last win was a brave effort at Newmarket (7f, good) 18 days ago; 2lb higher on this step back up in grade but he's unexposed at this trip and is a big player again.

runners.comment: Went close on handicap debut at Wolverhampton last month and he's respected back on turf
runners.spotlight: Won a Wolverhampton maiden last autumn and he returned after six months off with a strong-finishing second on his handicap debut there (7f) last month; up 3lb but he's still lightly raced and has possibilities if he can transfer his form back to turf.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is STARTLED who has a record of 34131 in handicaps and is only 2lb higher than for his win at Newmarket last month.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Startled, 4/1 Jeddaal, 5/1 Deluded, 6/1 Shaman Champion, 7/1 Siren Suit, 10/1 Monarch's Gold, 14/1 Do Bronxs,  Harlequin Breeze, 16/1 Major Neigh Sayer, 25/1 Mystic Moment

racecards.race_name: mybettingsites.com/ie Everything New On Irish Bookies Selling Hurdle

prev_owners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.comment: Out of sorts for this yard and has masses to find at the weights
runners.spotlight: Has won over hurdles for three different yards, most recently at Worcester (2m7f, good) last July, but he's been pulled up in three starts for this stable and drops into a seller with masses to find at the weights.

quotes.race: Scottish Racing Academy Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Palm Beach felt like he was going half-speed the whole way round and he did that well. He's been working very well and I was hopeful of a big run - John Dixon, rider.

runners.comment: Four hurdle wins at 2m-2m4f; running well last autumn; favourably treated on these terms
runners.spotlight: Four hurdle wins at trips ranging from 2m-2m4f; was running well in handicaps in the autumn after chancing her arm over fences last September and this is a very winnable race given the favourable terms; strong claims for top yard that's 4-5 here.

quotes.race: Visit Irish Store Sales With ITM Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Seeyouinmydreams is a fair horse and she'll go to Aintree now for the mares' bumper there. Harry had never sat on her, but said he thought she'd win going to the start because she felt so good. We haven't pushed many buttons and we thought she was nice, but you never know until you run them. She's already won a point-to-point, so will be a lovely hurdler next season after a summer of strengthening - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lovely prospect and I've been delighted with her, but we're in it for the long game with fillies like her and I'm in no rush. She was very impressive when hacking up by 15 lengths in a Irish mares' maiden point-to-point at Largy in April, after which she was bought at the Tattersalls May NH Sale. She didn't come cheap but all the right faces were trying to buy her. She's from a great family, being related to three winners, notably the smart hurdler Songe. Two or three runs in bumpers will suffice for this season, but without doubt she's a name to remember for the future. 31-10-22

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.comment: Encouraging handicap debut last March but very modest form since; no realistic chance here
runners.spotlight: Encouraging handicap debut when third at Ayr (2m, soft) last March but soundly beaten or pulled up in the meantime and no improvement for cheekpieces at Ayr last time out; visored this time; all uphill on these terms.

runners.comment: Winless after 26 hurdle starts; has a mountain to claim at these unfavourable weights
runners.spotlight: Winless after 26 hurdle starts and although he often runs respectably at the right level, he has no realistic chance against rivals who mostly would be giving him plenty of weight in a handicap.

runners.breeder: Dr V Roger-Yves Simon Et Al

prev_owners.owner: Exors of the Late Michael Ronayne

runners.comment: Three hurdle wins in Ireland; one good chase run for this yard but basically under a cloud
runners.spotlight: Three hurdle wins in Ireland during 2023 but a close second over fences at Catterick (about 1m7f, good) in January came from out of the blue and hasn't been repeated since; returns to hurdles with a cloud hanging over him.

quotes.race: Parkway Shopping Centre Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Starman is a bridle horse and finds nothing but he's won three races - Anthony McCann, trainer.

runners.breeder: E A R L De Cordelles Et Al
