runners.comment: Four hurdle/chase wins in 2025; below par now but still a viable option in a weak race
runners.spotlight: Four wins over hurdles and fences in 2025 (about 2m2f; ground ranging from good to soft); not in the same form since returning from a layoff in January, including in a Stratford seller in March, but this is easier and she's a viable option.

quotes.race: Coming Soon betvickers.com Sports Betting Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Demoiselle Kap was pretty good on the whole even though the ground may have been a bit quick for her - Luke Scott, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Arabian Horse Bahrain Equine Products UK Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Demoiselle Kap jumped a lot better than I thought she would. She was very good at the ditch down the back then at the last down the back she came out of my hands and I knew she had loads left. We'll have to go up in grade now so we'll find out a lot more - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

racecards.verdict: Demoiselle Kap looks the only realistic alternative to SEEYOUINMYDREAMS, who has plenty going for her now down in class.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/5 Seeyouinmydreams, 2/1 Demoiselle Kap, 14/1 Starman, 50/1 Mr Globalist, 66/1 Bray Dale, 100/1 Palm Beach

racecards.race_name: Bobby Roberts Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)

prev_owners.owner: D Fish And Mrs J Aldridge

runners.comment: 1-25 on Flat, tailed off last time, but not ruled out if taking well to hurdling
runners.spotlight: 1-25 on Flat, tailed off when last seen at Southwell in January; bit to prove on hurdling debut but this is not a strong contest and he would have a squeak if taking well to the new discipline.

runners.comment: Third in an Irish point but beaten at least 25l in two runs under rules
runners.spotlight: Third in an Irish point but beaten at least 25l in two runs under rules; improvement required.

runners.comment: Recent point runs have been underwhelming; new stable today; probably best watched
runners.spotlight: Won a point in April 2024 (soft/heavy) but recent runs in that sphere have been underwhelming; perhaps he'll be revived by a switch to Phil Kirby's stable but he's probably best watched unless strong in the market.

runners.comment: Third in two hurdle races, although latest effort was a step in the wrong direction
runners.spotlight: Won two points in Ireland; third in two hurdle races, although the latest effort at Sedgefield was a step in the wrong direction; needs to bounce back and may prove ideally suited by longer distances.

runners.comment: Well held in two runs over hurdles, jumping none too fluently; major improvement required
runners.spotlight: Placed in a heavy-ground Irish point in March 2024; well held in two runs over hurdles, jumping none too fluently; major improvement required.

runners.comment: 1m4f winner on Flat; satisfactory hurdling debut when third at Fakenham; high on the list
runners.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who won over 1m4f on Polytrack last autumn; satisfactory start over hurdles when 6l third of four at Fakenham (2m, good) last month, jumping soundly in the main; open to improvement and high on the list.

runners.comment: Pulled up last time but previously seventh in Listed bumper; worth another chance
runners.spotlight: Seemed to go wrong and was pulled up early when favourite for bumper at Taunton (tongue tied) six weeks ago, but he'd previously shaped quite well when seventh of 16 in a Listed event at Cheltenham (good ground) on New Year's Day; now goes hurdling (is bred for the job) and worth another chance.

runners.comment: Some promise in Irish points but hasn't achieved much over hurdles; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Some promise in Irish points but hasn't achieved much in two runs over hurdles, always behind at Stratford (50-1) two weeks ago; others appeal more.

runners.comment: Point winner; pleasing fourth at Perth on hurdles debut; leading claims despite drop to 2m
runners.spotlight: Won mares' maiden point in Ireland (yielding to soft) last November, and she made a pleasing hurdling debut when fourth of eight at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) ten days ago; dropping down to 2m may not be a positive but she could get away with it on this stiff track; leading claims.

runners.comment: Usually runs some sort of race; third at Newcastle last time; each-way possibilities
runners.spotlight: Usually runs some sort of race and she was third of eight at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) at the end of March, fading; will be fine back at around 2m; each-way possibilities.

racecards.verdict: Point winner EXPENSIVE EMOTION shaped nicely on her rules debut at Perth and can get off the mark.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Crest Of Arms,  Crackalackin, 7/2 Expensive Emotion, 5/1 Passing Diamond, 8/1 Lipstick Traces, 20/1 Jet Noir, 25/1 Cloud Free,  Mickthesoldier,  The Brave Guy,  After The Ball

racecards.race_name: Bobby Roberts Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)

runners.comment: 1-10 in Irish points; pulled up both starts in maiden hurdles; opposable
runners.spotlight: 1-10 in Irish points; pulled up both starts in maiden hurdles; opposable.

runners.comment: Second when last seen on Flat in October; going hurdling rather late but not without hope
runners.spotlight: On a long losing run on the Flat but he ran creditably when last seen, finishing second at Redcar (1m2f, good; final outing for Tim Easterby) in October; changed hands for £5,000 soon after; going hurdling rather late but not without hope.

quotes.race: Denford Stakes (Listed Race) (formerly The Washington Singer Stakes)
quotes.quote: Masekela has a couple of entries in the Champagne Stakes and the Royal Lodge and I need to talk to Andrew, but my view is that a mile is the right distance. William said he's a nice horse and there would be more to come. He said he'd make a nice 3yo, which we always felt as he's a big horse - Mick Mariscotti, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He won't run until later in the season, I gave him a good break when I got him from the sales last autumn. He'll be out from midsummer and I'm looking forward to him, we like him a lot. We bought him to run him at the big meetings and we gave him the winter off as he needed a break. He looks well handicapped and a mile and a half seems to be his trip. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Weak in market and tailed off in Sedgefield bumper last month; difficult to recommend
runners.spotlight: Weak in the market and tailed off in Sedgefield bumper (25-1) last month; difficult to recommend.

runners.breeder: Woodpark Bs, V Dubois & N Baudron
runners.comment: Third in point looks solid form; has joined fine yard; commands respect on rules debut
runners.spotlight: Third in Irish point (good/yielding) last April and that form looks solid, with the runner-up easily landing a bumper next time and the fourth winning a point; has joined an excellent yard and commands respect on rules debut.

runners.comment: Perfectly satisfactory start over hurdles when third at Carlisle; open to improvement
runners.spotlight: 0-6 on Flat for the Gosdens; perfectly satisfactory start over hurdles when third at Carlisle (2m1f, good to soft) six weeks ago, keeping on from midfield; open to improvement and high on the list.

runners.comment: Modest Flat maiden; no obvious promise in two runs over hurdles; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Modest Flat maiden; no obvious promise in two runs over hurdles; others preferred.

runners.owner: Mrs K Elliott & Mrs E J Quinlan
runners.comment: Well held in bumpers; related to winning jumpers but may require time and more of a test
runners.spotlight: Well held in bumpers seven months apart; related to winning jumpers but may require time and more of a test of stamina.

runners.owner: DL Adams, JA Adams & G McPherson
runners.comment: 2-3 so far; won bumper here three weeks ago; leading claims now tackling obstacles
runners.spotlight: From a good jumping family and she's quite a promising type; won a point bumper in March 2025 and she wasn't hard pressed to account for six rivals in bumper here (good ground) three weeks ago; leading claims now tackling obstacles.

runners.comment: More encouragement when sixth at Kelso last month and may improve further
runners.spotlight: Didn't show much on her first two starts but there was more encouragement in a close sixth of ten in novice at Kelso (2m, good to soft; 300-1) last month; may improve further.

stable_tour.quote: She probably didn't look anything special on her debut at Wetherby but she's a nice mare for the future. She's perhaps not a bumper mare, but she'll have a couple more runs in them. She's very much one for hurdles next season. 22-01-25

racecards.verdict: Terrano's point form has worked out well. Just preferred is BLUE SKIES AHEAD who won a course bumper with plenty in hand.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Blue Skies Ahead, 2/1 Terrano, 100/30 Earnest Belief, 9/1 Just A Poet, 10/1 Masekela, 33/1 Just Keeps Rolling,  Autumn Getaway, 40/1 Karthala, 50/1 Scopic

racecards.race_name: Max And Naomi Are Getting Married Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Sir A Ferguson, G Mason, L Hales, The Late J Hales

prev_owners.owner: Sir A Ferguson G Mason J Hales & L Hales

runners.comment: Useful hurdler; beat sole other finisher 16l on chase debut; should go well again
runners.spotlight: Useful hurdler with 6-22 strike-rate; beat sole other finisher by 16l on chasing debut at Fakenham (2m5f, good) four weeks ago; that form is not easy to read but he jumped soundly and should go well again.

quotes.race: Boylesports Extra Place Races Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sonigino wants a trip now and is getting much more relaxed. We were toying about going chasing, but I want to hang on hurdling with him and I dare say we'll head off for the Lanzarote now, find something in the spring and go chasing in the autumn. Then he will be an exciting horse - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Winvic Construction Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Whatever Sonigino does over hurdles is a stepping stone to fences. It's quite hard to make the running around here but I wanted to be up there and he toughed it out - Harry Cobden, jockey.

quotes.race: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm pleased with that. Sonigino showed plenty of promise last season but he was a big baby and had to carry two penalties in a lot of races. He still ran well but struggled with his breathing which we've sorted out now. This was much better and he did it nicely - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's back from a season off following a couple of setbacks. Now rising nine, he's getting on a bit for chasing but I've always been keen to see what he can do over a fence. He's got plenty of scope for chasing and as he was a 140-rated hurdler let's hope he can transfer some of that ability to fences. He's looking in great shape at the minute. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Best hurdles effort when winning well at Newbury in February; should make a chaser
runners.spotlight: Not at his best in competitive handicap hurdles at Sandown in March and Aintree in April, but he'd previously won well at Newbury (2m, good to soft; probably stays 2m4f); began his career in points (1-1) and has a jumps pedigree so there's a reasonable chance he'll make a chaser; respected in first-time headgear.

quotes.race: BetVictor Favourite Things, Bet Boosts Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: This week, I couldn't see Rubber Ball being beaten. He's in better form at home now, and we've tried various trips that have been wrong, so we wanted to bring him back. Coming here, I thought that if he won nicely, we could go to the Imperial Cup next week. He'll have an entry because I don't think he'll get into the Cheltenham races off his mark - Neil King, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Proper Prices Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was probably asking too much of Rubber Ball today - it was only two weeks since Uttoxeter and he ran on the 2nd of January as well - but I wanted to come here. It's a big, galloping track and I thought it was made for him. I'd see no harm in stepping him up in trip if the ground was quick. This is the softest he's run on before, so perhaps stamina has won it for him - Neil King, trainer.

runners.comment: 3-7 over hurdles; bred for chasing and may not be fully exposed
runners.spotlight: Has had less racing than his rivals and his record is 3-7; gained second win over hurdles at Sandown (2m, heavy) in January and ran just as well when second at Fontwell next time; bred for chasing; may encounter quicker ground than he's used to, but otherwise he has plenty in his favour.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Crackerjacque is a chaser for next season really. He looked like a big weak horse coming up the straight but he's seen it out nicely enough. He handles soft and heavy ground very well, which bodes well for when he goes chasing - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

runners.comment: Two below-par runs have followed Sedgefield hurdles win; others may have more potential
runners.spotlight: Won over hurdles in a first-time tongue-strap (retained since) at Sedgefield (2m4f, good to soft) in December; however, two below-par runs have followed and he now goes over fences; others may have more potential.

stable_tour.quote: His form over a trip on the Flat in France was good and he'll probably want further than 2m over hurdles in time. He was a very pleasing second in a novice hurdle at Sedgefield last week and looked to love the soft ground. I'm looking forward to him. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Third at Kempton in February; 6lb out of the weights but has plenty of chasing experience
runners.spotlight: Already placed three times over fences, third of ten at Kempton (3m, good to soft) when last seen in February; faces a stiffer assignment here from 6lb out of the weights but his experience should stand him in good stead and he's not ruled out.

racecards.verdict: Fakenham winner Sonigino is respected but CRACKERJACQUE, three years his junior, can make a successful start over fences.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Sonigino, 11/4 Crackerjacque, 3/1 Rubber Ball, 6/1 Moonshine Man, 10/1 Kingston Narcissus

racecards.race_name: mybettingsites.com Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: C&D win in 2024; modest runs over further last term; may fare better at 2m with headgear
runners.spotlight: Won a Wetherby novice hurdle (2m) and a C&D handicap, both on good to soft, two seasons ago; ordinary efforts on both outings last term (2m3f/2m4f) but drops back in trip with headgear tried; quite interesting.

quotes.race: William Hill More Top Prices Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Lawrenny is a nice horse. I don't know what happened at Leicester but it was barely raceable and the better ground here helped him. He learned a lot from his first run too - Alan O'Keeffe, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: A really nice prospect. He won his bumper at Newcastle in March and has been given plenty of time afterwards. He'll be going for a 2m4f novice hurdle next week, provided there's plenty of ease in the ground. He's a proper mudlark. 05-12-24

runners.comment: Back to form to win on good ground at Newcastle last time and chance off 4lb higher mark
runners.spotlight: Back to form in first-time tongue-tie when winning at Newcastle last time (2m1f, good; third has since won on the Flat); up 4lb; chance.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well at Bangor on his reappearance. He jumped great and just had a blow from the second-last. He'll run in another novice hurdle in a fortnight before he loses his novice status on December 1. I think he can make into a decent horse and might be a Challenger Series Final horse for Haydock in the spring. I don't think we've seen the best of him and he can be progressive. 19-11-25

runners.comment: Won a maiden last time (soft; form sound); chance on h'cap debut; first run on good
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner (2m, soft) who has run well all three starts over hurdles, last time getting off the mark in a maiden at Chepstow (2m, soft) when beating a subsequent dual winner who is now rated 16lb higher; interesting on handicap debut although unproven on this better ground.

prev_owners.owner: Oti Racing, Ballylinch Stud And Partner

runners.comment: Maiden hurdle/Flat h'cap winner last summer; off for 218 days; may improve for the run
runners.spotlight: Won a Southwell maiden hurdle (2m4f, good; first-time tongue-tie) and a Carlisle Flat handicap (2m1f, soft) last summer; off since September; likely to be better for the run.

quotes.race: Boodles Darley Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Banderas is a nice stayer for the future. He has a great temperament and a nice pedigree. There's a lot to like about him. He wants cut in the ground. We wouldn't run him on good to firm - Michael Bell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's won twice on the Flat and once over hurdles for us but we need to factor in a break for him as he's been on the go for a while and I'm not sure if we should be doing that now, because he wants soft ground. I don't think he's an all-weather horse and it was very much a shock the day he won in the fog at Wolverhampton. He stays well on the Flat, so he should get a trip over hurdles. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Three wins last summer and may have needed the run when pulled up at Perth last week
runners.spotlight: Won a Cartmel seller and two handicap hurdles (one over this C&D) last summer; may have needed the run when pulled up at Perth last week; bit to prove.

quotes.race: Burlington Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Pro/Am Race)
quotes.quote: We knew there was going to be plenty of pace on and that set the race up perfectly for her, because Winds Of Winter travels away really well and just needs something to aim at - Thomasina Eyston, winning jockey talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Last win was a chase, but better treated over hurdles; closely matched with Filibustering
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdles winner whose latest success was a handicap chase at Sedgefield in February (2m, good to soft); better handicapped over hurdles; over 8l behind Filibustering at Newcastle last time but meets the winner on 7lb better terms.

runners.owner: J Monkhouse R De Robeck A Miller
runners.comment: Two hurdle wins in 2022-23; three stable changes since; perhaps best watched on yard debut
runners.spotlight: Won twice over hurdles in 2022-23; has changed stables three times since and perhaps best watched after a break on debut for latest new trainer, although is well handicapped now.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Chatteris Fen Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Perseus Way is a very nice horse and I'm pleased that he has done it well today. His jumping is getting better all the time, but it needs to. He is getting slicker and quicker and he is starting to enjoy his racing. It was a good run in defeat at Chepstow last time and I felt that Chepstow was probably soft enough for him. We rode him too far back that day and that is why we rode him handier today. I don't think he is good enough to run in the Triumph but I think he could have a strong chance in the handicap - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Dreweatts Handicap
quotes.quote: Perseus Way has not run for months because we've been waiting for the ground. Jim said he'd get as far as you'd want. There is talk Gary Moore could have him for jumping at some stage. We were waiting to see what he'd do today because if he was well beaten, he might have gone to Gary's sooner! We just got away with the trip today as he's a grinder who will appreciate more give in the ground - Owen Burrows, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Reference Point Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was very pleased with Perseus Way. I hadn't sat on him at home and it was a proper slog on this ground, but he was quite fit and was able to keep going. He coped with conditions well. He's definitely a nice type for next year, he's big and raw and should furnish away over the winter - James Doyle, jockey.

racecards.verdict: The unexposed MARHABA PRINCE, whose maiden win has worked out well, can make a winning handicap debut by beating Filibustering.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Marhaba Prince, 9/4 Filibustering, 11/2 Double Digits, 8/1 Lawrenny, 10/1 Banderas, 12/1 Perseus Way, 14/1 Winds Of Winter

racecards.race_name: Elizabeth Elliott Birthday Celebration Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Off the mark on chase debut at Sedgefield last time; up 4lb; should go well again
runners.spotlight: Maiden hurdler; got off the mark when overcoming some trouble in running to make a winning chase debut at Sedgefield last time (2m5f, good); up 4lb; should go well again.

runners.comment: Novice handicap hurdle winner; modest run in headgear (retained) latest; chase debut
runners.spotlight: Won a novice handicap hurdle at Carlisle in February (2m3f, soft); creditable second over 3m at Doncaster next time but was disappointing with cheekpieces tried at Musselburgh last time (3m, good to soft; reportedly never travelled); headgear retained for chase debut.

runners.comment: Irish point third in October; rules form modest; worth a market check on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Creditable third in an Irish point in October (3m, good to yielding; second has won twice since) but previous rules form only modest; worth a market check on stable debut.

runners.comment: C&D winer in August; in decent form over fences and on the Flat last four starts; chance
runners.spotlight: C&D winner in May and August (good) last year; has been in good form both over fences and on the Flat (second over 2m5f at Pontefract 11 days ago) on last four starts; conditions suit and he's a contender.

stable_tour.quote: He was placed nearly every run over hurdles last season, he's strengthened over the summer and, although I was rather disappointed with him at Plumpton two runs ago he did run much better at Warwick on Tuesday. His trip is 2m, to start with at least. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Completed the course for first time over fences when 2nd last time; could go well again
runners.spotlight: Failed to complete on first two starts over fences, but shaped better when second of five at Newcastle last time (2m4f, good); could go well.

runners.comment: Irish point winner; 4th in h'cap hurdle latest and improvement likely now going chasing
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner in November (3m, yielding); fair form over hurdles, including when fourth on handicap debut at Newcastle last time (2m4f, good); likely to improve again now going chasing.

runners.comment: Best hurdles form when fourth at Wetherby in February; more needed on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Best form over hurdles when fourth in a 2m novice handicap at Wetherby (soft) in February; needs to improve for the switch to fences.

runners.comment: Disappointing since Sedgefield win in December and has a bit to prove at present
runners.spotlight: Has been a bit disappointing since winning a novice handicap chase off this mark in first-time cheekpieces at Sedgefield in December (2m5f, soft) and has a bit to prove at present.

quotes.race: The Prodrive Shopfitting Ltd Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: All Uncle Al has done is improve since we switched him to fences, and it's really helped his concentration too. After being hampered he had plenty of time to get back into it, and Aaron [Anderson] gave him such a patient ride. He battled so well to the line and we're all really happy with him - Jessica Bedi, trainer.

runners.comment: Has won at Hereford and Newton Abbot on last two starts; up 9lb but should go well again
runners.spotlight: Has come right back to form on last two starts, winning at Hereford (2m5f, good) and Newton Abbot (2m5f, good to soft); has gone up 9lb but should go well again.

quotes.race: Watch On Racing TV Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Jack Doyen has been fairly consistent since going handicapping and he stays this trip really well, which was key on this ground. He's a fun horse in this grade and a great horse for a syndicate - Ben Case, trainer.

runners.comment: C&D winner in March 2025; good third at Kelso last time and has an each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Won over C&D off this mark in March last year (good to soft); plenty of decent efforts since, including when third at Kelso last time (2m5f, good); each-way chance.

runners.comment: 0-9; two fair runs since 395-day break, notably last time; new headgear; a possible
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden; two fair efforts since returning from a 395-day break, notably when fourth over 3m at Carlisle last time (good; second-time cheekpieces); visor now tried and he's a possible.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Patricia O'Rourke & Mrs J S Bolger
Mrs J S Bolger & Mrs Patricia O'Rourke

runners.comment: Fair fifth after long break on stable debut last time; improvement likely; contender
runners.spotlight: Ex-Nigel Hawke; fair fifth after a long break on stable debut at Newcastle last time (2m4f, good to soft; 3-1); should come on for that; one with a chance.

runners.comment: Won this race off 3lb higher last year; well beaten last few starts and needs to improve
runners.spotlight: Returned to form to win this race off a 3lb higher mark last year; has been rather disappointing on his last couple of starts and more is needed for a repeat win.

runners.comment: Two fair runs at Wetherby in December, but well beaten since; 5lb out of the handicap
runners.spotlight: !6-race maiden; two fair runs at Wetherby in December (2m3f, soft); well beaten since (tried over hurdles last time); no easy task from 5lb out of the handicap.

racecards.verdict: The pick is ROYAL DEESIDE (nap), who won twice over C&D last year and warmed up for this with a good second on the Flat 11 days ago.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Jack Doyen, 5/1 Play By The Rules, 6/1 Maggies Boy, 13/2 Royal Deeside, 8/1 Quickasican,  Valtteri Its James, 10/1 Scairp Dubh,  Divas Doyen, 12/1 Kingofthegame, 20/1 Yapper Hill,  Cave Hill, 25/1 Tell Me Again, 33/1 Uncle Al,  Mademewhatiam

racecards.race_name: drainrat.co.uk Rat Entry Diagnosis Specialist Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Two wins last term, the second over C&D; not so good in 2026, but back after a break
runners.spotlight: Two wins last season, the second off 3lb lower over C&D in October (good); hasn't been in quite such good form in 2026, but has had a break and can't be rule out.

runners.comment: Dual hurdle winner in October and mainly creditable runs since; interesting on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Two wins over hurdles last October (first over 3m) and creditable runs since; quite interesting on her chase debut.

runners.comment: Catterick winner in 2024; some fair form since but pulled up last 2 runs; tongue-tie tried
runners.spotlight: Won a 3m1f handicap chase at Catterick in December 2024 (good); some fair runs since, but plenty to prove having been pulled up on last two starts; tongue-tie now tried.

runners.comment: Three C&D wins, including this race, last year; won over 1m7f here last time; contender
runners.spotlight: Three wins over C&D on good ground last season, including in this race, his mark going up 14lb as a result; won over 1m7f off his new mark here last time; up another 4lb but should again be competitive.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Margaret Coppola & Mrs Dianne Sayer

runners.comment: Two wins in November 2024; below par after 404-day break last twice; plenty to prove
runners.spotlight: Won twice in November 2024 (2m7f/3m, good/good to soft) but mainly disappointing since including on both runs since a 404-day break; plenty to prove at present.

quotes.race: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Go North Red Rum Qual')
quotes.quote: Cardamon Hill is a good-ground horse and we might as well keep him going. There's a 0-125 over three miles for him on November 28 at Musselburgh, which is his owners' local track - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in a few points for Colin McKeever and will run in a bumper sooner rather than later. 18-10-22

runners.comment: Point winner; best of three chase runs was C&D second last August; below par since
runners.spotlight: Point winner; yet to win under rules, best of her three runs over fences when second to an in-form rival over C&D last August (good; Ribeye back in third); chance on that form but below par both runs since.

runners.comment: Maiden; fair run over 2m4f on chase debut; chance in first-time tongue-tie back at 3m
runners.spotlight: Maiden; fine second to a subsequent three-time winner in a handicap hurdle at Carlisle in April 2025 (3m1f, good); hasn't done as well since, although not disgraced when sixth on chase debut at Newcastle last time (2m4f, good to soft); tongue-tie now tried; chance back up in trip.

stable_tour.quote: I've placed him terribly! He's been second three times over hurdles, including being beaten at Southwell by Almuhit, who was runner-up at the Punchestown festival, and at Carlisle by I'm A Starman, who won his next three races. He's a little behind the others as he was in a bit later, but he's definitely shown enough to win races. He'll stay well and he'll jump a fence - he's not big but he's really efficient. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Four fair chase runs with cheekpieces this year, including over 4m here; worth considering
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner on debut (2m1f, heavy); four fair runs with cheekpieces at up to 4m this year, all with give in the ground; worth considering.

stable_tour.quote: He's a Walk In The Park and has not been the easiest to train. We've never worked him too hard at home as we were worried we might just blow his head a bit. It's been about getting him on a racecourse and his bumper form looks good. He won first time at Carlisle and shouldn't really have gone to Hexham after that as the course didn't really suit him. I was desperate to get another run into him because of his temperament. He pulled hard on his hurdle debut at Kelso but he jumped really well and we were delighted with his performance. Two miles will be a bit sharp for him but we might stay there to get him to settle. We won't be in a great hurry, he might have another run before Christmas and we'll see where we are in the new year. His bumper form was very good and he is exciting. 15-11-23

runners.comment: Ran his best race since 2024 when a close fourth over C&D last time; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Ran his best race for nearly two years when a close fourth over C&D last time (good) on his third start over fences; each-way chance on that form.

runners.comment: Four chase wins including over C&D in May 2024; below par here last time; bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Has won four chases, including over C&D in May 2024 (good); best recent form has been at Musselburgh and he was below par over C&D last time (good).

runners.comment: Point winner; well beaten in 4 runs over hurdles; now goes chasing with cheekpieces tried
runners.spotlight: Point winner; well beaten in four runs over hurdles, including on handicap debut at Perth last time; now goes chasing with cheekpieces tried.

runners.comment: Point/hurdle winner; 0-18 over fences; 2nd of four in February but pulled up last time
runners.spotlight: Point/hurdle winner but 0-18 over fences; good second in a four-runner mares' handicap chase at Catterick in February (3m1f, soft) but pulled up last time.

runners.comment: Three chase wins (one over C&D) for Maurice Barnes; well beaten in 2026; 5lb wrong
runners.spotlight: Three chase wins for Maurice Barnes including over C&D in March 2025 (good to soft); well beaten last three starts; 5lb out of the handicap for stable debut.

runners.comment: Two fair runs at Market Rasen last season; stiff task from 5lb out of the handicap
runners.spotlight: Runner-up twice at Market Rasen last season, but failed to finish on her other three starts; no easy task from 5lb out of the handicap.

racecards.verdict: Kicksaftersix is in good form but slight preference is for PASSENGERONTHESHIP, who should appreciate this step back up in trip.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Kicksaftersix, 6/1 Rob Roy Macgregor, 13/2 Princesse Milania, 7/1 Rightbackatyou, 8/1 Passengerontheship, 10/1 Killybegs Jet Lady, 12/1 West Lawn, 14/1 Ribeye,  Dr Shirocco, 16/1 Halfway House Lad,  Worth The Walk, 20/1 Cardamon Hill,  Millford Hill, 25/1 Poetry Man

racecards.race_name: Winchcombe Working Mens FC Tour 2026 Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Hat-trick of chase wins in 2024; has struggled to finish since; visor tried back hurdling
runners.spotlight: Won three handicap chases on the trot in 2024; has struggled to finish since; may fare better back over hurdles with visor tried.

quotes.race: Mark Nield Wealth Management Go North Monet's Garden Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We always fancied William Of York as a chaser and just hope he gets three miles in time. He's not Third Time Lucki or Captain Chaos, but he's going the right way - you haven't seen the best of him yet and will improve. He'll come back to us for a good summer holiday too - Mike Newbould, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He got a lot stronger last season and continued to improve as a chaser, ending up by winning the Monet's Garden Go North final at Carlisle. He jumps very well - he's bold and quick but very rarely gets one wrong - and will be entered for the Grand Sefton at Aintree. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Ex-Irish; 2m4f win here on stable debut; fair since; interesting on first run at 2m7f
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; won over 2m4f here on stable debut in August; mainly fair form since; interesting on first try at this trip (has run well over 2m6f).

runners.comment: Three sound efforts on last three starts last summer; off 252 days and may need the run
runners.spotlight: Three sound efforts on last three starts last summer (good/soft), winning over 2m1f at Cartmel and finishing creditable second over 3m there on final start; off for 252 days and likely to be better for the run.

stable_tour.quote: He is an interesting horse in that he has only had one run to date, when winning a bumper at Stratford last May. He is a cracking individual who is a full-brother to the ill-fated Fontsanta, who was a smart stayer. Dusky Days won his bumper nicely and his schooling over hurdles has been very encouraging ahead of his return over 2m, although I expect him to get further later on. I would suggest he is one to follow for the season ahead. 28-09-21

runners.comment: 1-16 (C&D winner in November); sound runs last twice; good going suits; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: 1-16 over hurdles (sole win was over C&D in November); creditable second to Dillarchie over 3m3f at Sedgefield on last two starts; suited by good ground; each-way chance.

runners.comment: C&D winner on heavy in December; pulled up on three starts since; tongue-tie now tried
runners.spotlight: C&D winner on heavy ground in December; has pulled up on his three starts since; tongue-tie now tried; others stronger.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Best Odds Daily Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: It's Adveram's first win. He's a bit stronger this season and has improved - Ian Duncan, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: 5-19 over hurdles, latest win a four-runner mares' h'cap in April; stiffer task here
runners.spotlight: Has won five of her 19 races over hurdles, the latest a four-runner mares' handicap for today's claimer at Newcastle in April (2m7f, good); up 4lb in a tougher race.

quotes.race: Racingtv.com Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: It's Maisy is a typical of one of the trainer's horses, they jump and they gallop - Nick Scholfield, rider.

runners.comment: Has won her last three races, last twice at Sedgefield; stiffer task; could go well again
runners.spotlight: In fine form having won her last three races, one at Catterick (3m1f, good to soft) and the others over 3m3f on good at Sedgefield (Wee Alki second on both occasions); up 7lb for latest win, but a possible.

quotes.race: 100% Racing TV Profits Back To Racing Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: She has deserved that for a while. You don't want to be overdoing her because you can take too much out of the tank. We knew Dillarchie was well, but we were a little bit disappointed when it started raining because she would've maybe won easier if it hadn't - Jo Foster, trainer.

runners.comment: 2-16; two wins have been on good/good to firm; fair form last term; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Two wins have come on good/good to firm; some fair form on soft/heavy last season; has a place chance, but is not a regular winner.

stable_tour.quote: He unseated at Sandown on Sunday but he's fine. He's entered up at Cheltenham on Saturday but whether we run I don't know. 08-11-22

runners.owner: Mrs Janet Cooper & M E Sowersby
runners.comment: Two wins last term, latest by 9l at Stratford 13 days ago; 8lb higher; could go well
runners.spotlight: Two wins on good ground last season, the latest 13 days ago when scoring by 9l at Stratford; stiffer task off this 8lb higher mark, but these conditions suit.

runners.comment: Dropped to a good mark and won over 2m4f here last time; 2m7f may suit; interesting
runners.spotlight: Took advantage of his reduced mark and some better ground to win off 3lb lower mark over 2m4f here last time (good); may fare even better up to this trip (3m Irish point winner).

stable_tour.quote: He won a novice hurdle at Hexham nicely in the summer and then didn't back it up at Carlisle, but we later found a problem. It's been sorted now and he'll go back over fences, probably on a flat track. We're looking forward to him. 22-01-25

runners.owner: Miss E Emmerton & Major P H K Steveney

prev_owners.owner: Miss E Emmerton & Major P H K Steveney

runners.comment: Ex-Dan Skelton; several good runs for this yard last term; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Ex-Dan Skelton; several good runs for Rebecca Menzies last season, including when third at Kelso on latest start in November (3m, soft); just as effective on this better ground; each-way chance.

runners.comment: All 3 wins have been over C&D, including this race in 2025; on last winning mark; chance
runners.spotlight: All three wins have been over C&D, including in this race last season; shaped as though returning to form when sixth at Bangor last time; back on his last winning mark; one to consider.

runners.comment: C&D winner in June 2025; gained a second success at Southwell last time and should go well
runners.spotlight: C&D winner in June 2025; gained a second success at Southwell last time (3m, good); conditions suit; should go well again despite 5lb rise.

quotes.race: Greenhead Hotel Novices' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Belladinotte is quite a quirky mare and we've just made her happy. She gets treated like the princess she is and we've just given her TLC. She's blossomed. From our last five jumpers we've had a winner, three seconds and then another winner. They're absolutely flying - Sara Ender, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Best on good ground and, following a good second last time, could be in the mix again
runners.spotlight: Only win came in a Southwell novice handicap in May 2024 (2m4f, good); good run when second at Sedgefield last time (2m4f, good); stamina to prove, but could be in the mix.

runners.comment: Ex-Irsh; career best when second over 2m4f here last time; 3m should suit; could go well
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; unexposed hurdler who put up a career best when runner-up in a 2m4f handicap here last time (good); this longer trip should suit; a possible.

runners.breeder: E A R L Equi-Michel 6 & T Leboucher
runners.comment: 0-10; no improvement over fences this year and pulled up back hurdling last time
runners.spotlight: Ten-race maiden; tried chasing without success this year and, having been pulled up Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) when returned to hurdling last time, is perhaps best watched for now.

racecards.verdict: In an open race, the vote goes to last year's winner ROBERT D'ORES, who looked to be coming back to form when sixth at Bangor last time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/1 Stylish Recruit,  It's Maisy, 7/1 Wee Alki,  Dillarchie,  East Eagle, 10/1 Divilabother,  Victory Club,  Belladinotte, 12/1 Dusky Days,  Knacker Trapper,  My Boy Christy, 14/1 Robert d'Ores, 16/1 William Of York, 33/1 Adveram,  Lord De Vinci

racecards.race_name: Oddschecker Ellen Chaloner Stakes (Listed Race) (Formerly The Kilvington Stakes) (Fillies & Mares)

runners.comment: Seasonal debutante; good third to Sayidah Dariyan in York Group 3 on 2025 reappearance
runners.spotlight: Disappointing in similar event over C&D when last seen and is 0-5 since winning the Lowther as a 2yo; however, this seasonal debut may be the time to catch her; good third to Sayidah Dariyan in Group 3 at York (6f) on 2025 reappearance.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Celandine is very tough. We were scratching our heads at Goodwood as she didn't look so tough that day. Today she was great and I'm buzzing. It's all about the Cheveley Park for her now and hopefully the Breeders' Cup - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.race: Maureen Brittain Memorial Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Celandine has got loads of boot and is very tough and Tom thinks she is not done yet. I don't think we'll be going up in trip even though she's in the Moyglare Stud Stakes, and we may have to supplement her for something nice - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a star and the Cheveley Park is the obvious next step having won the Lowther. She's had ten days out in the paddock to freshen her up, which is what we did after Goodwood and before York, and she looks fantastic. She's back cantering and hopefully will be spot on for Newmarket. 11-09-24

As some sprinters can do, she rather missed out in her three-year-old season but she's back and we hope she can make up for that at four. She still ran a great race in the Nunthorpe last August and she's a bigger, stronger filly this year. With a good crack at it, she should be competitive at the top end. She'll probably start in the Kilvington Stakes at Newmarket. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Group 3 winner who has made the frame in several Group 1 events; leading contender
runners.spotlight: Group 3 winner in July 2024; campaigned mostly at Group 1 level since, making the frame on several occasions, most recently in the 2025 Sprint Cup at Haydock (6f, good) where she did well having met trouble; leading player back down in class.

quotes.race: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: I am absolutely delighted. Flora Of Bermuda is such a superstar. We just hope one day she'll get one of these but to be third in another Group One is magnificent - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: 1895 Duke Of York Clipper Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Flora Of Bermuda ran a hell of a race. She's been off the track for a long time (207 days) and for her to come back and run like that, with the right horse beating her, I think that means she's a really exciting filly. She's always shown a lot at home, Andrew has always liked her and mentally and physically she's developed. We were hoping for a big run and she hasn't disappointed us. I think so (run at Royal Ascot), why not? As PJ (McDonald) said when he got off her, she's got a heart like a lion and you can't ever take that away from her - Anna-Lisa Balding.

quotes.race: William Hill Summer Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Andrew (Balding) was confident Flora Of Bermuda would run a big race and get the trip and I talked to Oisin (Murphy), who thought she was better than her mark. She's starting to mature and behave better now and the race was very smooth for me - PJ McDonald, jockey.

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/(IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: We think a lot of Flora Of Bemuda. It was a bit of a punt on the ground, but we felt we would learn something if it didn't work. She's got a lot of talent, enjoyed the ground and would have no problem staying six if we put her up. I think that as long as she stays in one piece, black type will not be a problem.  She's in the Lowther and that was always the plan - Andrew Balding, trainer.

runners.comment: Placed four times in Listed grade, including over C&D; below par on seasonal debut
runners.spotlight: Novice winner as a 2yo; placed four times in Listed grade, most recently runner-up over C&D (good to firm) on final start in 2025; ran below market expectations at Bath on reappearance but consistent on the whole and may rebound.

stable_tour.quote: She's a very nice filly who won at Yarmouth last September. She's done well over the winter and is working well, although, as I've mentioned, the fillies have taken a while to come to hand. I hope she can build on that win last autumn. 17-04-25

runners.comment: Ended last season in a consistent vein of form but she's 0-9 since her debut success
runners.spotlight: Ended last season in a consistent vein of form at Listed level, creditable third at Doncaster (6f) the final time; may continue to give her running but that won't be enough to belatedly double her tally; 0-9 since 2yo debut success.

quotes.race: Racing TV EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: It wasn't too much of a shock. Kevin was pretty hopeful. He said to just take a lead on Magic Basma and see how we get on, and just make sure she enjoys her first day at school ? and she seems to have done that. There was a lot of unraced horses in there, but the Roger Varian horse was coming in with a nice bit of form and I was very happy with my filly - Jockey Oisin McSweeney, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.breeder: Al Shaqab Racing & S N C Ecurie De Cast
runners.comment: Ex-French filly who faces a stiff task in this second British start
runners.spotlight: Gained her French wins in maiden/handicap races; faded late over 7f on the AW finals card at Newcastle on British debut; may prove suited by this drop back in distance but the opposite is true of the step back up in class; stiff task.

runners.comment: Low-mileage filly who could go well in the retained hood; stable/seasonal debut
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage filly whose form wearing hood comprises a success in 6f novice event and two good efforts in Listed grade, third at Ayr when last seen (final outing for Mark Usher; remains with same owner); could go well in the retained headgear.

runners.comment: Progressive; ended her 2025 campaign with an August double (Listed/Group 3); respected
runners.spotlight: Record is 5-13; ended her 2025 campaign with an August double that comprised a Listed race at Pontefract (good to firm) and Group 3 at Deauville (soft), both over 6f; progressive and tactically versatile mare who warrants respect on reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: She performed much better in the second half of last year and we toyed with the idea of the Al Quoz Sprint in Dubai but decided to be patient. It was no surprise when she won a Group 3 in August and she's going to work back from midsummer targets. We'd love to get her to Royal Ascot and I'd imagine she'll start in a Listed race. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Best to forgive last two efforts; progressive otherwise and may still have more to offer
runners.spotlight: Had excuses (trip/draw) returned to Group 1 level in last two appearances; progressive otherwise and ran well in the Commonwealth Cup prior to Group 3 win at York (6f, good) last summer; may still have more to offer; major contender.

quotes.race: William Hill Summer Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Richard [Hughes, trainer] told me to be as confident as I can. Sayidah Dariyan relaxes brilliantly when she's in behind and conserves plenty of energy. She's got an electric turn of foot when you let her down. I'll leave that [possible future targets] to Richard and his team, but she's in great nick and is definitely a filly on the up. She's got the best mind. She yawns in the stalls, but as soon as the gates open, she's all business - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: bet365 Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wouldn't normally take on horses rated 110 when you're 92 but Sayidah Dariyan was working really well at home. She could come back here in two weeks [Chelmer Fillies' Stakes], but I wouldn't be mad about that, or go for the Carnarvon which would be spot on - Richard Hughes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was thrilled with her run in the Carnarvon at Newbury. The winner Symbol Of Honour can't run in the Commonwealth Cup as he's a gelding, so you can discount him, and it was only her second run on grass. She can only improve and she'll go there with a little squeak. 10-06-25

We really fancied her at Windsor at the start of the month, but she stumbled over every one of those ridges and it was hard to get her on an even keel. I backed her up just over a week later because it was the ideal race over 6f at Lingfield on the all-weather. I didn't think she'd win like she did and she's gone up in her estimation at home. We might go to Dundalk on October 4 for a Listed race over 5f. 18-09-24

runners.comment: Record when racing below Group 1 level on turf is unblemished (5-5); strong claims
runners.spotlight: Has come up short in Group 1 attempts, including last two appearances; record when racing below that level on turf is unblemished (5-5) and features Listed, Group 3 and Group 2 wins on British, French and Irish soil; strong claims back down in grade.

quotes.race: Tally-Ho Stud Irish EBF Ballyogan Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Sky Majesty is just really coming back to herself now. It's taken a while to get her back on that comeback trail, but she felt fantastic there and stepped in a lot quicker than I thought she would off a better pace than the last day. She's just really filling back into herself and getting back into gear. Obviously, they'll be looking to get some Group 1 form into her, I'm sure - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Sky Majesty is a lovely filly who enjoyed that bit of cut in the ground and was strongly through the last hundred [metres]. We didn't go overly hard early, I was expecting there to be a little more tempo given the fact the track bias has been so strong and that probably didn't suit her too well but the stiff finish and the slow ground really helped to see her to best effect - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Criterium de Maisons-Laffitte (Group 2) (2yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Christophe said Sky Majesty didn't relish the ground, but she handled it. She did really well and the second filly, whether or not she ran to her best I don't know, but she's got some very good form. I don't think she does a lot [when she gets to the front]. She won a nose in her maiden and then a neck in the Firth of Clyde, so it looks like the better the race, the further she wins - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Firth Of Clyde (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: She's good. She's taken a nice step forward. Sky Majesty picked up great when I asked and showed a great attitude when it mattered - Callum Rodriguez, jockey.

racecards.verdict: The percentage call goes to SKY MAJESTY who is unbeaten on turf when racing below the top grade. Flora Of Bermuda is second pick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Flora Of Bermuda, 7/2 Sky Majesty, 4/1 Sayidah Dariyan, 11/2 Rosy Affair, 9/1 Celandine, 16/1 Hold A Dream, 20/1 Magic Basma,  Rhyme Dust, 50/1 Paris Babe

racecards.race_name: Betfred Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners.comment: Good course form, including a win on this card last year; held twice by Double Rush though
runners.spotlight: Goes well at Newmarket; third to Double Rush at last season's Craven meeting (2lb better off today) before an impressive win in the 3yo handicap on this card; another promising run on his reappearance 17 days ago when finishing third, just over 5l behind Double Rush; has bigger days ahead of him but he may be battling for another minor placing.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Handicap
quotes.quote: We felt Invictus Gold came forward for his last run at Newmarket as he was quite behind in his coat. He is a sprinter, but we have not done much with him. In his demeanour he seemed well and we were quite keen to see him on better ground. He had never run on quick ground and I think that has brought about the improvement today. The day he ran here the last day it rained, but we really wanted to see him on quicker ground. He ran quite well at York in the Rockingham, but I felt he was blunted that day by the heavy ground as he is quite a quick horse. I would say we will look at stakes races now. I think he is worth a try in Listed company, especially if there is a 3yo 6f sprint somewhere. Maybe we could look to go to France as he is quite ground versatile, and he is a very easy horse to ride - Jackie Clover, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At Starsports.Bet Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We liked Invictus Gold a lot going into the first run, so we sort of came away from Yarmouth a little disappointed. He's had a little setback on the gallops so we couldn't get him out any sooner, but he shaped up nicely in his home work, so it was lovely to see him do that on the track - Tom Clover, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won really nicely on the Rowley Mile on Guineas Saturday. It was great to have a nice winner for the syndicate, who are exciting and going places. They've supported us a lot. Hopefully he's still an exciting horse. He's up to 103 now and there's a 6f handicap at York the week before Royal Ascot we could go to, or we might see if he'd sneak into the Wokingham. We could drop him back to 5f for the Palace of Holyroodhouse but I don't think we'll be doing that. He's very quick and I think he's a real summer horse. Hopefully he's got some improvement in him. 14-05-25

runners.comment: Two AW wins this winter but poor latest; 0-11 on turf with best form on slower ground
runners.spotlight: 0-11 on turf with his best efforts coming on slower than good; back up in the weights after a productive AW campaign and he has enough to prove back on turf, all the more so after his tame effort at Newcastle on Good Friday.

runners.comment: Impressive on seasonal return here (5f) but that was an odd race and he may be flattered
runners.spotlight: Often ran well in defeat in top handicaps last year, including two solid efforts at Glorious Goodwood (third in the Stewards' Cup off a 4lb lower mark); returned from a five-month break with an emphatic 5f win (good ground) here at the Craven meeting, one of three to race on the far side of the track; suspicion that effort flatters him slightly and the 5lb penalty asks a stiffer question of him too.

quotes.race: Betway 4 To Win Handicap
quotes.quote: It wasn't the plan to make the running with Jakajaro but Jamie walked the track beforehand and the far side was the place to be. It's nice that he's retained all his old abilities - Robert Cowell, trainer.

quotes.race: La Celia Wines Sprint Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Jakajaro was a horse I thought would win a maiden. This is a good horse. He was still green today and hopefully he will go on. He's in the big sales race here in September and that will be in his target - David Marnane, trainer

runners.comment: Placed in this race in 2023 & 2024; returns to Britain/turf on a fair mark; should go well
runners.spotlight: Stable star who runs in this race for the fourth time, recording best results when second in 2024 and third in 2023; went without a win in 2025 but the ability was still intact, second in the Portland (5.6f, good) and an Ascot Group 3 (6f, soft); faced some stiff tasks in the Middle East this year but his second in a Listed race at Jebel Ali (5f, dirt) was promising, finishing with a flourish for second; fair mark back on grass; should run well.

quotes.race: John Guest Racing Bengough Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Apollo One has been very unlucky, but he's been giving 15lb to improving handicappers. I think at Doncaster he actually thought he'd won. He doesn't really like that ground but there you go. That's him done for the year and he'll go home and rest now - Peter Charalambous, co-trainer.

quotes.race: Howden Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I'm not sure that the rain has helped Apollo One as it just blunts his acceleration. He is not the biggest, but you don't have to be. He has got a heart like his mother Boonga Roogeta, who was as tough as nails. He is just a lovely, lovely horse. I'd say we will probably go off to Epsom now for the valuable six-furlong handicap on Derby Day - Peter Charalambous, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Get Your Ladbrokes Daily Odds Boost Spring Cup Stakes (Listed Race) (AW Championships F-T Qual')
quotes.quote: I would think that Apollo One would drop back to six furlongs for the sprint on all-weather finals day after that - Martin Harley, jockey.

prev_owners.owner: Suman Hedge Bs, Woodside Bs & D Redvers

runners.comment: Seemingly much happier on AW; previous turf efforts need leaving well behind him
runners.spotlight: Enough evidence to point to him being a superior performer on AW but that is reflected in a handicap mark that is 9lb lower on grass; that said, it is still 11lb higher than when twice beaten at the Curragh last September and he'll need to leave his turf form well behind if he is to win.

runners.comment: 2-2 over C&D; left rivals trailing when heavily backed on stable debut here; 8lb well in
runners.spotlight: Promising for Charles Hills as a 3yo, winning a C&D handicap at the Craven meeting before a good third from a tricky draw at York; ended 2025 with a low-key run at Ascot but, having been switched to Andrew Balding's stable, he created a huge impression here 17 days ago, supported as though defeat was out of the question and winning accordingly; 8lb well in and looks a Group horse in waiting; obvious chance for the stable that won this prize in 2021 and 2024.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Handicap
quotes.quote: Oisin came back and said Double Rush was a push button ride. Charlie Hills obviously did a good job with him. We'll treat him like a good horse and maybe look at Royal Ascot  - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: I think Double Rush is going to be a nice, improving horse through the season. Some of our horses just weren't right last season and he had a nice mark. He probably didn't handle the track today and a flatter track would suit him better. There is a nice valuable handicap at York around a week before Royal Ascot which we could aim at. We will see how he improves and take it step by step. We couldn't put a hand on but the horses just weren't last right season. They looked great but just weren't letting themselves go. They seem nice and healthy this year - Charlie Hills, trainer.

runners.comment: Making good progress but he has nearly 5l to find with Double Rush on latest C&D run
runners.spotlight: Upped his game following a gelding operation last summer, winning over C&D in September before making giant strides on AW; returned from a break to do best of the rest behind runaway winner Double Rush over C&D 17 days ago; could have a nice prize in him this year but the 5lb turnaround with Double Rush may be insufficient.

quotes.race: Turners Parks Group Ltd Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Once Coul Angel got the gap he was always going to get there. He likes this ground we may give him a couple more runs and then put him away as he'll be a nice horse for next year - Mick Appleby, trainer.

runners.comment: Inconsistent and latest Newbury eighth didn't suggest he was the answer today
runners.spotlight: Patchy overall record; didn't enjoy the smoothest of passages at Newbury two weeks ago but he was beaten over 5l at the finish; others are stronger.

quotes.race: Chesham Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I'm just delighted with that. Brian was a very cheap horse. He's a lovely horse and tries very hard. We are delighted with how he ran - Liam Keniry, jockey.

runners.comment: Unexposed and progressive; pleasing Newbury return 15 days ago; 2lb well in; solid chance
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo; hugely encouraging seasonal return at Newbury (6f, good; gelded during his absence) a fortnight ago, missing a beat at the start but moving through to lead inside the final furlong before being picked off close home; 2lb well in and this flashy grey appeals as the type to win a major sprint handicap this year; solid contender.

quotes.race: JenningsBet Grey Horse Handicap
quotes.quote: We had this race in mind after Addison Grey ran well at Chepstow last time despite missing the kick and it's a bit of fun for the owners Opulence Racing, who are big supporters of ours - Matt Stanley, trainer's assistant.

runners.comment: Ran well for 6th in this race last year and 6lb lower today; 264-day absence to overcome
runners.spotlight: 6lb lower than for his close sixth in this race 12 months ago; he had the benefit of a pipe-opener before that race, though, and he comes here after a 264-day layoff; should be ending his losing run soon but perhaps not in this field.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It's very exciting, I was really happy with Indian Run. He got a bad trip all the way round on the outside and didn't get any cover but he found and found, which is great. He's in the Dewhurst so we'll probably look there. He's so unfurnished he needs time so we'll give him a nice break - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

quotes.race: Greatwood Charity 25th Anniversary British EBF Crocker Bulteel Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Indian Run is very unfurnished and was quite colty in the paddock, so did pretty much everything wrong before the race, but he did everything right in it. It looked a nice race and Danny said it rode like a nice race. We've thought quite a bit of him for a while and he's not entered in any posh races, but probably will be soon - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's in the Stewards' Cup, along with Solar Aclaim, but he's the opposite in that he wouldn't want it too soft, so they won't both run. He's a talented lad - we've tweaked his wind since his last run at Windsor, where we were a little bit disappointed with his finishing effort. I think he's got a nice race in him. Possibly not at the top level of handicap sprinting, but we know he's decent as he won a Group race as a two-year-old for his previous trainer, so it shows a good level of ability is there. I don't think we've quite worked him out but hopefully that wind operation will give us the extra bit to win a race as he's been running pretty well. 23-07-25

racecards.verdict: 8lb well in and bringing the prospect of further improvement for his new stable, the claims of DOUBLE RUSH are obvious.
racecards.betting_forecast: 10/11 Double Rush, 5/1 Addison Grey, 9/1 Coul Angel, 10/1 Invictus Gold,  Jakajaro, 12/1 Sir Les Patterson, 16/1 Apollo One, 25/1 Brian, 33/1 El Bodon,  Indian Run

racecards.race_name: Betfred Suffolk Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners.comment: Big performances in notable 1m h'caps last April-August; strong contender despite 1m1f
runners.spotlight: Can front-run; 1m wins here last April and in 17-runner race at the York Ebor meeting in August, with his two seconds at Ascot in between including the Royal Hunt Cup; last two outings leave him with a bit to prove, as they were 1m1f, but it's not too hard to excuse them and he is a strong contender.

quotes.race: Clipper Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Bullet Point is going for the Five Diamonds at Rosehill on November 8. It's for five-year-olds only over nine furlongs. We were always looking to do both [entered in the Strensall Stakes]. We'll see how he is on Saturday. That was lovely. Going round a bend probably helped him. He's a very genuine, classy horse and he did that well - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Royal Hunt Cup (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Bullet Point ran great - it feels like gun-point robbery - we did everything the hard way on our side and battled off the other two horses that were with us. But you can't account for what's on the other side, and I could see Silvestre [De Sousa, jockey on winner] there, but he [Bullet Point] put everything in to the run and didn't have a lot more to go on our side - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Japan Racing Association Handicap
quotes.quote: If you win by three and a quarter lengths you're entitled to go for a race at Royal Ascot. Bullet Point won off 89, so he'll be about 97 after this and that would put you in the frame for the Royal Hunt Cup - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.comment: Has a 658-day absence to overcome but his handicap mark has been slashed
runners.spotlight: Excelled in top handicaps at York and Newmarket in 2023, including with a C&D win in the Cambridgeshire (good to firm; 3lb lower today); however, he only once threatened to hit those heights in 2024 and, after wind surgery, missed all of 2025; that leaves him with a 658-day absence to overcome but his handicap mark has been slashed.

quotes.race: bet365 Cambridgeshire (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: We didn't pay a fortune for Astro King, and you always buy hoping you can win races like this. After the John Smith's Cup the race back at York was the obvious target and how he ran there was going to dictate where we went next. William (Buick) said he might get a mile and a half and we considered it, but when we looked at all the options and you looked at this and you thought they will go a massive gallop and you need to get a mile and a quarter and the prizemoney is huge there is only one Cambridgeshire. We will have to go into Stakes company now. He could have run in a Listed race but they are worth fifty or sixty thousand, but this is worth one hundred thousand pounds to the winner. Hopefully he might be rated high enough to go out for the Bahrain International Trophy. It will be fast ground over 10 furlongs and it is a massive prize - Daniel Kubler, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: John Smith's Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: That's pretty tough. We had one beaten not far at Royal Ascot and now this, but fair play to Amy - she's done a great job with that horse. Astro King has been a bridesmaid but I don't think he's been that today - he's put everything on the line. It's one of those things, in another stride we were in front - Daniel Kubler, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He gave us a great day when he won the Cambridgeshire last year and he's run well in valuable races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia since. In hindsight, we might have ridden him for a place in Saudi from a poor draw, but we tried to win the race. He ran in the Earl of Sefton at Newmarket two weeks ago and finished a cracking second, and it showed that's the right level for him. The plan is the Wolferton at Royal Ascot with a run in between, possibly the Suffolk Stakes back at Newmarket on Saturday. I'd like to go back to Bahrain because he was unlucky there and everything else suited. 02-05-24

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Front-running 4th in Lincoln at Doncaster for new yard; concern about good to firm ground
runners.spotlight: He wasn't at his very best last year but took a step back in the right direction when front-running fourth of 21 off this mark in the Lincoln at Doncaster five weeks ago on first run for new yard; no stamina worries but there is a concern about good to firm ground.

quotes.race: Knights Solicitors Handicap
quotes.quote: Botanical was in super nick today. The worry was the drying ground as he was so dominant on quite soft ground at Hamilton, but he showed he copes with it. He was pretty dominant there and while he'll get a bit of a clobbering for that, he's a smart horse - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap
quotes.quote: Botanical won it really well and he should be a nice horse next year. The handicapper will have his say and will know whether it's a strong race but hopefully he's not too hard on us. He seems like a Class 2 horse and we'll see if he can climb the ladder a bit next year. I think ground is quite important to him, he was beaten on a sounder surface at Ascot the time before. I'm not sure if we'd run again this season - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A new horse to us who came from George Boughey. I like him - he's a good, powerful galloper. He ran a great race in the Lincoln as he probably wants further than a mile. He could end up a Cambridgeshire horse on slow ground in the autumn. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Mid-division in the Spring Cup at Newbury but not beaten far and the draw looked a problem
runners.spotlight: 1m winner at Newmarket and York last summer but failed to shine on last two outings, when co-second favourite for the C&D Cambridgeshire on first occasion; only mid-division when 13-2 in the Spring Cup at Newbury two weeks ago but not beaten far and the draw looked a problem; not ruled out.

quotes.race: bet365 Mile Handicap
quotes.quote: It was the plan to play Fifth Column late and Ryan got there just in time. He won his side of the race in the Britannia but not the whole thing. I'm told he could be a a Cambridgeshire type but we'll have to see - John Gosden, joint trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Esher Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Gelding has calmed Fifth Column down and made him a happier horse. Having had a run and won on the all-weather he was fully race fit, which he needed to be as the ground was slow, which is quite correct with there being jumpers here tomorrow. He had been working well at home and I thought if we had a winner today it would be in this race. We'll stay at a mile and aim for the Britannia at Royal Ascot and hope we get drawn on the right side. He could run before if we need to freshen him and can find the right spot; he will tell me - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: We didn't go overly quick and I was trapped a couple of rows further back than ideal. Fifth Column showed a good turn of foot stepping up to the mile for the first time and he hit the line well. A mile is probably his optimal trip and we'll see where he goes from here - Kieren Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Disappointing favourite at Pontefract 11 days ago; connections turn to cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Went close at Glorious Goodwood (1m2f, good) last July but well beaten in C&D Cambridgeshire in September; failed to settle and suffered interference on return, doing pretty well in the circumstances, but disappointing favourite at Pontefract 11 days ago; connections turn to cheekpieces.

quotes.race: Free Bets With BetUK Bet Club Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Marhaba Ghaiyyath was still quite raw. We went round on the wrong lead for a lot of the race and had to do it the hard way in front. I think you'd have seen a better horse if he'd had something to aim at, but he got the job done. He's actually quite weak and I think he could come back to a mile and he could step back up in trip as he gets a bit stronger - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM/EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Marhaba Ghaiyyath was a bit unlucky not to collect on his debut at Wolverhampton so it was nice that he got his head in front. Charlie [Johnston, trainer] thinks he's a nice type and it could well be that he runs again on the all-weather - Bruce Raymond, owner's racing manager.

stable_tour.quote: He put up some big performances last year but I probably shouldn't have run him in the Cambridgeshire because the gelding operation had knocked him for six before that. I thought he ran a lot better than the finishing position suggested in the Rosebery Handicap last month and I'd expect him to step up with that run under his belt at Pontefract on Tuesday. He'll hopefully run in all the ten-furlong handicaps at the summer festivals, and might step up into Listed races when the opportunity presents itself. 21-04-26

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.comment: Easily first home in his group when 4th of 23 in the Cambridgeshire over C&D in September
runners.spotlight: Easily first home in his near-side group when strong-finishing fourth of 23 in the Cambridgeshire over C&D (good to firm) in September; just 1lb higher today and that wasn't his only solid performance in a good handicap last term, so he could be a major each-way player.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race
quotes.quote: Erzindjan ran better at the Curragh than his finishing position suggested. He was very good at Cork last year. The step up to a mile today suited him well and we'll go back up to stakes level with him next time. Maybe a race like the Amethyst at Leopardstown would suit - Kris Weld, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Coolmore Stud Gleneagles Irish EBF Maiden (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Erzindjan handled that ground well and his run the first day put him right - Oisin Orr, rider

runners.comment: Progressive over 7f-8.6f on AW this year; turf mark has been raised in tandem
runners.spotlight: Progressive over 7f-8.6f on AW this year, on last two starts winning the Lincoln Trial at Wolverhampton and close third at the AW Championships at Newcastle; turf mark has been raised in tandem, which leaves him with marked improvement to find in this sphere, but he needs a second look.

quotes.race: BetMGM Lincoln Trial Handicap
quotes.quote: We'll see about the Lincoln  - if it's soft ground, The Lost King will probably go to All-Weather Finals Day (at Newcastle). He'll go to one or the other - Pippa Tuthill, King Power assistant racing manager.

quotes.race: Jenningsbet British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: The Lost King was too green to do himself justice first time but got an easy lead out there today and kept on finding. He'll be a lovely middle-distance horse for next year - David Probert, jockey.

prev_owners.owner: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg

runners.comment: Often held up in rear, with little daylight in Spring Cup (50-1); not the percentage call
runners.spotlight: Often held up in rear, so he saw very little daylight when 50-1 off this career-low mark in the Spring Cup at Newbury two weeks ago; however, he last won in September 2023 and failed to make an impact in all but one of his races in 2025, so he is not the percentage call.

quotes.race: Mint Millions Stakes (Grade 3) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: To be fair, Dr Hay picked this race out even before he purchased Ancient Rome. He's Kentucky-bred so it fitted in well. I think he went well on the [firm] ground today and he's pretty adaptable when it comes to surfaces. He ran in softer conditions a lot of the time in France and last time [at Goodwood] it was soft, but he's a War Front and they go on fast turf - Jamie Spencer, quoted by Bloodhorse.

quotes.race: Coral Chesterfield Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: They did go a good gallop, which was quite tiring in dead ground, and the race fell into his lap in the last furlong. I always thought I was going to be involved; maybe outside the three-furlong pole, he was moving up easily enough and I was following Tom Marquand [on Millebosc], who was kind of dying so we went round him. Ancient Rome is a very lazy horse - you ask him and he'll go for three or four strides, then he's lazy again. Even right at the line he pricked his ears and kind of jammed [the brakes] on, so he's a hard horse to assess. I just planned to drop out, stay on the outside, get cover and come down the outside. Dr Jim said, just ride like Richard Hughes! He's a smart horse and I thought he was a stakes horse, so I'm sure he will be capable of at least Listed company - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had an injury at the backend of last season and has had some time off. He's a big horse who takes a bit of getting ready but he's undoubtedly talented. He's not a certain starter in the Wolferton but if he does take his chance, I think he's well up to that class. 13-06-24

runners.comment: Front-running 1m win here (favourite) 18 days ago; has 5lb penalty (same as revised mark)
runners.spotlight: Down the field when 33-1 in C&D Cambridgeshire last September, before being gelded; however, he was reliable and progressive earlier last season and reappeared with a front-running 1m win here (favourite) 18 days ago; has 5lb penalty (same as his revised mark) but needs plenty of respect.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Handicap
quotes.quote: Mister Winston is a straight forward horse and seems to have stepped forward nicely in recent weeks. He's from a yard in form and did that nicely - Jason Watson, jockey.

runners.comment: Mid-division in his four handicaps, 20-1 off this mark behind Mr Winston here on return
runners.spotlight: Windsor maiden winner for the Gosdens last April, followed by a 1m3f Listed third and big-money sale; only mid-division in his four handicaps since, 20-1 off this mark behind Mr Winston here (1m) on reappearance; back up by a furlong but others have more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Late gains over 7f at Musselburgh latest prompts some hope given today's step up in trip
runners.spotlight: Unraced on firmer than good; won debut on Southwell AW; close fourth on handicap debut there (1m) last October is markedly better than what he's done in three starts since, but he made late gains over 7f at Musselburgh on latest start to prompt some hope given today's step up in trip.

stable_tour.quote: He'd have needed his first race of the season, but I was a bit disappointed with his next at Musselburgh. Perhaps the undulations didn't suit him, and he wasn't drawn all that well, so don't judge him on that because I think he'll make his mark in decent handicaps. I may put some headgear on him next time. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Retains clear potential but he's nothing like as battle-hardened as most of these runners
runners.spotlight: Ran away with a novice at Epsom in September on third start, making all; 11-8 favourite for handicap debut at Redcar (again 1m2f on good) in November but went in snatches and finished only fourth; retains clear potential but he's nothing like as battle-hardened as most of these runners.

quotes.race: Betfred 'Pickyourpunt' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a nice performance. We've always liked Alcarath and it's just nice to see him progress because we thought he was capable of a performance like that. Rossa [Ryan] got off him and said he's still a big baby, he's got plenty to learn, but he's a nice horse and one to follow, I think. We were very much taking it race by race with him.
