I don't know if he'll carry a penalty now or go into a handicap, I haven't discussed it with the boss. We'll see - Robin Smith, trianer's assistant.Alcarath is a big customer. He composed himself well, was still pretty raw for a three-year-old, and he'll have a nice future next year - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

runners.comment: Won at Musselburgh last April and June; non-runner at Redcar on Thursday
runners.spotlight: Won at Musselburgh last April and June; failed to make a serious impact since, albeit fourth of 12 back at Musselburgh three weeks ago; non-runner at Redcar on Thursday.

racecards.verdict: With fast ground a possible problem for Botanical, the vote goes to BULLET POINT ahead of Erzindjan and Mister Winston.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Mister Winston, 9/2 Bullet Point, 13/2 Botanical, 7/1 The Lost King, 8/1 Fifth Column, 9/1 Alcarath, 10/1 Erzindjan, 12/1 Marhaba Ghaiyyath, 16/1 Tycoon, 18/1 Al Arbeed, 25/1 Ancient Rome,  Thunder Wonder, 40/1 Astro King

racecards.race_name: HKJC World Pool Palace House Stakes (Group 3)

runners.comment: Superb Australian 7yo; three Group 1 wins in Europe but expected to improve for the run
runners.spotlight: Superb Australian 7yo who has had a career to be proud of, with multiple wins in home country and Europe, laying down the law in the Group 1 King Charles III at Royal Ascot in 2024 and adding further top-level wins in the Nunthorpe (good to firm) at York and the Abbaye (very soft) at Longchamp in 2025; has stayed in Britain over the winter but connections expect her to improve for the run and that the stiff uphill finish will test her.

quotes.race: Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp Longines (Group 1) (2yo+) (Sprint Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It's just surreal really. We had a couple of little pre-race issues, we had to work through those. We were within a minute and a half of not running - I had an Uber driver on a retainer of 200euros to get the mare's passport here in time. We try to experience new things. I've never been to the races in France and here we are winning a Group 1 on Arc day - Henry Dwyer, trainer of Asfoora.Asfoora was fantastic. The sprint course is a fair bit drier than the round course and she was basically on the bridle throughout. She was fortunate to have a plum [low] draw and I didn't have to ask her much but her condition was the best it's been on the build up to this race. She still has her summer coat and it took some amount of management - Oisin Murphy, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: It seems surreal, silly and it's all been a novelty. I've really been on a holiday with Asfoora the last two years. It was all getting a bit hard before Ascot as we didn't have the transport, and if I'm 100 per cent honest, if I owned her I wouldn't have come back. Akram [El-Fahkri, owner] was very insistent we did and that she deserved another chance. I'd love to see the replay as I was under a scrum of people for the last bit, but that looked very convincing. When you know they're going to win at the two-furlong marker, you're on pretty good terms with yourself. It was an easy watch and really enjoyable. She'll tell us if she doesn't want to be racing any more, but after that you can't say that's the case. She's been a once-in-a-lifetime horse for two years in a row and who knows, maybe three. That'll be a decision for Akram. He's a sportsman and would love to keep her going, why wouldn't you? We can't rule out coming back next year, but she owes us nothing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: Asfoora has run well but she was 6-4 favourite so you like to see those ones win. She didn't so we're probably a little bit disappointed but it's not as though she's run tenth. She's run well but probably not as well as her last couple. I didn't like her last 50 metres, she was there to run second or at least third and she was a little bit plain in that last little bit. Whether she's reached her peak or she's on the way down, or whether she didn't like the track, I'm not sure. We might go to Ireland for the Flying Five but if anything comes out of the run and we're not happy with her she'll be going home - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Asfoora has gone as well as we could have hoped and we're very proud of her. You could just tell about 400 metres after the start she just came off the bridle. She's quick but they were a bit quick for her early. Big Evs controlled his own destiny whereas we were stuck behind a couple and got a bit of a bump which probably cost us the win but she's run well and we're more than happy just to be competing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: We needed a lead-up run at Haydock, so we were always going to come early, but just with the changing of seasons we wanted to be here before it was too cold in Australia and too warm. We came over in the nice interchange period and Asfoora settled in brilliantly. The proof of that was in the pudding today. I've got to have a look at the race conditions again but we'd love to showcase her a bit. Everyone has just been so good to us over here and I'd love to send her down to Goodwood and up to York, but we'll put the horse first - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

runners.comment: Winless since 2yo days; fine 2nd to Asfoora at York last August (first-time cheekpieces)
runners.spotlight: Listed winner at Royal Ascot as a 2yo; out of luck since but he showed what can be done on a good day when chasing home Asfoora in the Group 1 Nunthorpe at York (good to firm; 100-1) last August; no approach to that form since, however, and although Ryan Moore is booked, the absence of cheekpieces raises a query.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: I'm not one to bring horses to make up the numbers. I never have done it and never will. This is not about being proved right, it's having faith in the horse. I told the owners Ain't Nobody was in great form and I said we were going to ride him cold, they're going to go hard here. We'd ride him like when he won at Royal Ascot. It's worked out a treat - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Windsor Castle Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: It panned out perfectly. Obviously it was such a big field you don't know what's going to happen. After going 100 yards, I was following the American horse, getting a good lead and he was always going to bring me as far as I wanted, and Ain't Nobody was tough at the finish. He's a nice horse for the future, he's only a young horse on his second run, so plenty to look forward to - Jamie Spencer, rider.

runners.comment: Improved to win Group 3 (5f, good to soft) in September; this is a tough return
runners.spotlight: Down the field from a poor draw in the Group 1 Abbaye at Longchamp in October but had previously confirmed herself an improving 3yo when beating Shagraan in a Group 3 at Newbury (5f, good to soft; acts well on good); has hopes of doing better as a 4yo but this is a tough start to the year.

quotes.race: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: First Instinct has had a couple of starts this year where she's probably not been the quickest out and I was conscious that she'd have to be here. I gave her a kick out of the gate and within three strides she was rocking, and she actually took me by surprise. She's tough, she's fast, and she appreciated that tiny bit of give in the ground - Tom Marquand, rider.

quotes.race: Goffs Irish EBF Polonia Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Mr Haggas was bullish with First Instinct and thought she had a good chance. She jumped so fast coming out of the gates that I nearly came off, but she got into her stride really quick. Billie (Lee, on Town And Country) was coming quick, but I was pulling out more. I'd be happy at today's distance - Chris Hayes, jockey.

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: First Instinct has been faultless. I was a bit worried that the ground today might just blunt her speed but she fell asleep early - which was key I think - and showed that trademark turn of foot which she showed on her first run. I think she'll be even more effective on better ground - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.owner: MPS Racing Ltd & The Ayrshire Tradesmen
runners.comment: Thoroughly reliable; richly deserved Group 2 win (5f) last August; having first course run
runners.spotlight: Below best from a high draw in the Group 1 Abbaye on final 2025 start; thoroughly reliable previously and he richly deserved his Group 2 win at Goodwood (5f, good to soft; effective on good to firm) last August; versatile track-wise but has never run at Newmarket so there is a query to answer.

quotes.race: King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Sometimes certain races in the sprint division can be winnable and this looked one. When the rain came yesterday it looked like it might inconvenience some, whereas JM Jungle always turns up. If you don't put your hat in the ring, you've no chance, so we said we'd give it a go. He's much stronger this year and looked so calm before the race that I knew he was going to run his race again. They went lickety-split and Jm Jungle loves that. Earlier in the season Jason Hart said the race he'd love to ride him in was the Nunthorpe, simply because of how fast they go and how much he likes York. It looks the natural next step because he's a Group 2 winner now and you want to be going up from there. We put him in the Abbaye earlier this week and that's a similar race. If you get a good draw up against the rail, with his speed he'd be in the van early doors - Sean Quinn, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Aston Martin "Dash" Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: JM Jungle deserved that and he's won a load of consistent races and the handicapper has never missed him for being placed, so it's great he's got his day. I rode him in the three-year-old Dash here a couple of years ago and I got stuck behind a wall of horses and I was never able to get into a rhythm that day. He never handled the track that day but today I was out on a wing and able to keep momentum rolling forward and I think that has helped - Jason Hart, jockey.

quotes.race: Symphony Group Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: When the draw came out and the ground was dry we were delighted. This was the plan all along, but Jm Jungle will roll away in all the big five-furlong handicap sprints for the rest of the year - John Quinn, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: World Pool Handicap
quotes.quote: JM Jungle is in very good form, and up to Haydock he had been running really well and just got touched off at York and Hamilton. Then he won nicely at Haydock. He's got a lot of speed from the gate, so we felt that this track would suit him - John Quinn, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: JM Jungle has been running consistently and I thought he was unlucky to bump into a well-handicapped horse last time. He went to bite the second horse and I had to drag him back off, but he's done it well in the end - Jason Hart, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's another who did well in Bahrain and he arrived back in such good form that we decided to keep going for now, so he'll either head for the Scottish Sprint Cup at Musselburgh or a valuable race at Bath a week later. He gave Jason [Hart] a good feel on his last run in Bahrain and he could still be improving. He's an out-and-out 5f horse. 20-03-24

runners.comment: Front-runs; pure quality on AW (4-4) but had trouble sustaining effort on turf
runners.spotlight: Often leads; he's pure quality on the AW (4-4) but has had trouble sustaining his effort on turf, even allowing for being first home on his side in a Group 2 at Goodwood in August; gelded since last seen but whether he'll appreciate this stiff finish is questionable.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: When everything goes smoothly for him and Night Raider is relaxed in the prelims and at the start, he's a horse with a lot of natural ability - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK Golden Rose Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Night Raider was very comfortable going a good gallop. He beat two decent benchmarks in Wiltshire and Annaf - Oisin Murphy, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Boost Your Acca At BetMGM Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The idea was to go straight to the Guineas with a racecourse gallop at the Craven meeting. Another run is probably the right thing to do, Danny [Tudhope, jockey] said Night Raider could do with another run, he's still green in front but he's obviously a very good horse - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's just come back to us after a little operation. He's a very quick horse who has been gelded, which will help him because he was edgy. He'll be entered in the five-furlong sprints, although I still think he can stay six. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Front-runner; usually seen at 6f-7f but useful 5f run on AW in January; regular hood off
runners.spotlight: Front-runner whose 12 wins include a Group 3 at York (7f, good) last June; he was an excellent third of 19 in the Group 1 Champions Sprint at Ascot (6f) in October; has since run up to his best in a 5f AW race at Newcastle in January and it will be interesting to see how he gets on back at this trip on turf with his regular hood discarded; ran creditably in 6f Group 3 at Newmarket last time.

quotes.race: Dukhan Sprint Cup (Local Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Quinault is an absolute superstar. He's got an amazing will to win and if it's close, he just wants it - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Criterion Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Quinault is a fast horse and on his dam's side, he's definitely bred to go a bit further. Tom [Morley, joint-owner] continually have this argument whether he's best over a stiff six furlongs or an easy seven, but I think it's probably either. He's just a high-class horse who loves to win. Once he gets in front and rolling along at a place like this, he's hard to catch. We'd like to come back here to the Ebor meeting in August as it was a win and you're in race for it. We'll aim for that and be working back from there. He tries very hard and that's the key to it. It's his first Group win and it means a lot. I took him to Dubai in the winter and ran him in a Group 1, as we've always thought he was capable of this sort of thing - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We thought Quinault wouldn't like this ground but he just wants to win - he definitely tries. He's a special horse for a yard the size of ours, especially as he came a long way in such a short space of time last year. He had a little wobble earlier this year and was a little bit ill after we gave him the flu jab, but he's bang in form now. He's such a special horse. There's a chance he improves again next year and I still think he might be better over seven furlongs, so we've got to explore that avenue as well. He'll have a little bit of a break now as he's done his bit for the summer, but we could travel with him. He's a gelding so we'll go where the best prize-money is that he can win. There isn't much point in running him in Group races just for the sake of it - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Jenningsbet Hopeful Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I don't think Quinault was in love with the ground but he just tries very hard - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Liverpool Airport Faster, Easier, Friendlier Queensferry Stakes (Listed)
quotes.quote: I'd love Quinault to go seven furlongs round a bend somewhere if I could find the right race for him - I think that would be ideal. We wouldn't be against travelling him later in the year. We might go abroad somewhere, some of the tighter tracks, maybe in America, somewhere like that might suit him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: What a special horse Quinault has been for everybody this year. He didn't run a bad race the last day but he's back on song today - it's a special day. He's got one way of running in that you let him stride on in front, and he's so genuine he keeps finding for you - Luke Catton, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: We had Sendintank who won ten handicaps in a season, including four in a week twice, but that was at a much lower level than this - this is very different. Quinault is a very tough horse and he's got loads of talent as well. Luke Catton has done a fantastic job settling him and it's such a shame he cannot do the weight. The horse was just a runaway when he arrived, he would just bolt. We trained him on a treadmill for the first two months so he never left the yard, before we slowly started to introduce him to the Heath, so there's a lot of work gone into what you're seeing today. He's always had the talent, it's just been a case of letting the horse know it and letting him use it - he's always been fast, that wasn't the problem! He's bred to get further so as long as we can keep him settled in his races that's a route we'll look to go with him - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Oakmere Homes Supporting Macmillan Sprint Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: This was the biggest occasion Quinault has been to and he got a little bit warm in the preliminaries but he settled nicely in the race and Connor gave him a lovely ride, just managing to get him there on the line. We put him in at Ascot just in case something happened that forced our hand, but my gut feeling is probably not to run. I think he'll get a bit further and I've put him in the Bunbury Cup so that's a possibility - Stuart Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Aspall Suffolk Draught Cyder Handicap
quotes.quote: It was unfortunate Luke Catton couldn't ride Quinault today as he couldn't do the weight. Luke has done a brilliant job settling him at home as he was a tearaway when he came but that is why Godolphin put him in the sale in the first place. He will probably go to York now for the valuable three-year-old six-furlong handicap as long as he comes out of this fine - Stuart Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: Suited by tracks with stiff finishes and won this last year; not to be underestimated
runners.spotlight: Acts on flat tracks but he comes into his own when tackling a stiff test at 5f, as when winning this race last year, taking C&D record to 2-2, and roaring home to win a Group 3 at Sandown (good to firm) in July; cheekpieces worn in October are discarded; yard in form; not to be underestimated.

quotes.race: Coral Charge (Group 3) (Registered As The Sprint Stakes)
quotes.quote: It's fantastic to see Rumstar get his head back in front. Like for any sprinter, everything needs to go just right on the day. I don't think he liked Haydock and at Royal Ascot he got in front a bit too soon. He was also drawn wide and it just didn't work out for him. We made a conscious decision to hang on to him today come through. That is very risky at Sandown as you often don't get that run and meet traffic but Rob [Hornby] found thar gap and rode him to perfection. He knows the horse well and loves him as much as I do. We deliberately didn't entered in the King George at Goodwood as I just though five furlongs there in that Grade might be a bit sharp for him. I am not sure where we will go next. We may have to step up to six furlongs where there are more options although I would prefer to stay at five - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

quotes.race: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We have been very much looking forward to running Rumstar. It seems to have been a long time since last October, waiting for him to get back on the track. He has been in fantastic form and looking great this year. It's great to be back and great to have him back winning in this company. I think we had him where we wanted him today and I think he is a stronger horse this year. I don't weight my horses but he seems heavier than he was last year and the year before - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Rous Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I'm just delighted I've found a race for Rumstar to win because it's been a long time since the Cornwallis. He's not been the luckiest and had a few training issues last year. I was concerned about the ground, but that was obviously a load of rubbish! I'm chuffed for the horse and chuffed for his owner Vincent Ward, who is sitting at home not very well - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Beaten-By-A-Length Free Bet Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Rumstar had been running well in Listed company and I take exception to anyone saying he came up short and was banging his head. He could go back for a Listed race, although there are no firm plans. He's not just a two-year-old - Jonathan Portman, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: At the beginning of the year the Nunthorpe was a race we never had in mind; we thought if we'd go for any Group 1 it would be the Prix de l'Abbaye, which he's entered for. But there are very few options for him at the moment and he seems extremely well, so we're probably going to take a leap of faith and run him at York. Everyone else seems to be doing it, so we thought we'd do it too. I don't think anyone's won a Group 1 staying at home. People say it's a very open year for sprinters and that there's no standout. But, however open they are, Group 1s are still very hard to win and we're under no illusions that dabbling in such company isn't necessarily his gig. 20-08-25

runners.comment: Form spurt later in 2025 with Listed 5f wins (good to firm/soft); may yet progress again
runners.spotlight: In action between May and October last year for Michael Appleby, finding a form spurt late on with a close second to First Instinct in a Group 3 at Newbury sandwiched by Listed 5f wins at Beverley and Ascot (good to firm and soft); more needed back with former trainer but may yet do better.

quotes.race: BetMGM Rous Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Shagraan is improving all the time. He's still growing and filling out and I think he'll be even better next year. We'll put him away now and look to next spring. He loves his racing and hopefully next year he'll be a Group horse. Kieran [Shoemark] gave him a great ride, he's not ridden many for me before but he did exactly as we told him and it was a great job - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Be Friendly Handicap
quotes.quote: Shagraan was drawn on the wrong side and the ground was a bit on the softer side than ideal, but he's done it well. He's still improving and places like Bahrain might suit him, so we'll have a look at where we're going to go - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Anderson Roofing Supplies Ltd 20th Anniversary Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Shagraan has taken a big step forward from his Haydock run and shown a bit of class. We thought he was a horse who could run in a decent grade and he's shown that there. We'll stay at six furlongs for now. Windsor is a nice, sharp track and he was always travelling smoothly and he picked up well. He'll come forward again for that - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a strong and competitive colt by a great sire in Sioux Nation. He made a pleasing second start when an impressive winner at Windsor over 6f, where he travelled strongly throughout. We upped him in class to Listed level last month for the Rose Bowl at Newbury where he stepped up with his performance in finishing a good second. On his homework I think 6f is his strip but he is sharp and ideally he would probably be at his best over 5½f, which leads me to think of the Flying Childers, which we won with Caturra in 2021, who had previously won the Rose Bowl on his way to that Group 2 success. This fellow is definitely going the right way and he runs in the Group 3 Molecomb Stakes at Glorious Goodwood on Wednesday. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Group 3 winner at 6f here in 2024; sole success since came in Listed company; win unlikely
runners.spotlight: Can lead; won 6f Group 3 here in 2024 but a beaten favourite in this race last year and sole success in 2025 came in a Listed York race (5f, good to firm); below best on recent comeback and a win looks unlikely.

quotes.race: Connaught Access Flooring Abernant Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We were looking forward to running Washington Heights today and he is a horse that tries very, very hard in his races. He has run loads of good races for us and probably just been a bit unlucky here and there. He had done well over the winter and we were really looking forward to this year. He was impressive when he won in Sweden last year and we were hoping he'd outrun his odds today. Tom has given him a great ride from the front and got the job done. Kevin is a fantastic trainer of fast horses and it looks like he's bought another nice one for us. He's in the Duke of York and Greenlands in Ireland and we could look at Royal Ascot further down the line. We will see what the boss says - Cosmo Charlton, racing manager for owners Hambleton Racing.

quotes.race: Bro Park Sprint Championship (Listed Race) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: All fairness goes to Simon Turner, who runs Hambleton Racing. They've supported this meeting and had success out here before. He came up with the idea and thankfully it's paid off. Washington Heights is so tough and genuine, he deserved to win one like that. He's been a bit unfortunate this year. He bumped into Shaquille at the start of the year and you've seen what he's gone on to do. He's had his day in the sun today. Thankfully we had a few owners out here as well who enjoyed it. He's been at the top table in these handicaps all year, so I'm sure there's more races in him - Adam Ryan, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Scaleby Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a lovely run at Wetherby and Washington Heights has improved for it as he's quite laid back at home and he's obviously going to come on a lot for that fitness wise too, so we were hoping today that he was going to run a big race again - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a shade unlucky at York as the ground just went against him. If it had been a bit faster, he'd have taken some pegging back. His win in the Abernant proved he was up to Group class and that last run teed him up nicely for the big sprints. 10-06-24

runners.comment: Two terrific runs in Group 1s at 5f in 2025; likes fast ground; form claims if on song
runners.spotlight: A record of two wins from 16 turf starts in no way does justice to the Group 1 form she's capable of, such as a close second in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot and a third to Asfoora in the Nunthorpe at York (both 5f, good to firm); the likely fast ground is a blessing and has good claims if on song.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Frost At Dawn is a star. She's had plenty of seconds and now a third, but how can you complain? I'd just love to find that win at this level - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Women In Racing/British EBF Cecil Frail Listed Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I think Frost At Dawn is better over five and we'll come back to that trip and might go and run in the King's Stand as the owner is very keen to go to Ascot. She ran a good race at Bath behind the winner when they beat the track record and then she probably veered off the line at Newmarket last time. The older she gets the faster she's getting as she's a bull of a horse. She likes that quick ground and since we've put the visor on her she's improved. She's a quick filly and the stiff five at Ascot would be right up her street. If it was fast ground there I think she could run a massive race. She'd be the fastest I've ever had - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Nad Al Sheba Turf Sprint Sponsored By Emirates Skywards (Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I had the luck to have a good draw today, so I just played my card. It's the first time I've ridden Frost At Dawn. She's fast and I think she would travel even better over six furlongs - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

runners.comment: Won 5f Listed race in France as 5yo; no fitness queries but has to raise her game here
runners.spotlight: She divided Washington Heights and Jm Jungle in a York Listed race (5f, good to firm) last July and later won at that level in France but, even allowing for having a fitness edge, she has to raise her game to win today.

quotes.race: Prix du Cercle - Don Juan Cuneo Solari (Listed Race) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Rob Hornby has built up a really good rapport with Miss Attitude and she has to be delivered late as she tends to stop when she gets to the front. We've always thought she was a very smart filly but unfortunately she's had a multitude of issues. Now I've just got to talk the owners into supplementing her for the Nunthorpe. To be honest it's a bit of a no-brainer as we've already seen this year the five-furlong division is wide open. She beat [King George Stakes winner] JM Jungle in a Listed race at York, so why wouldn't you try? - Jack Channon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's rated 92 and wasn't beaten far at Newcastle when fourth last time. The main goal for her this year will be black type. She'll go for the Listed Lansdown Stakes at Bath on April 20 and then she'll be campaigning in stakes races for the rest of the year. 02-04-25

prev_owners.owner: Mrs M Roden & Mrs R Nolan

runners.comment: An improver last May/June but wasn't the same filly after; plenty to find on these terms
runners.spotlight: An improver last May/June, giving First Instinct a fright in a Cork Listed race then winning at Sandown (both about 5f; good and good to firm), but she wasn't the same filly after; has plenty to find this time.

quotes.race: BetMGM Scurry Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Town And Country was keen. I was told at home she can be, but I didn't think she'd be that bad. She ran into a couple of pockets, but she only got out in the last half-furlong and she did well to win. I think when she gets used to sprinting, the quicker they go the better as she can relax, and then we'll see the best of her. I think she can win in Group company - Colin Keane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Drop to 5f suited when beating good rival in C&D Group 3 as 2yo; respected on 2nd run back
runners.spotlight: Has been described as a challenge by connections but he's a talented one and the drop to 5f suited when beating a smart rival (later runner-up at the Breeders' Cup) in a Group 3 over C&D (good; won a novice on good to firm) in October; nothing special on his recent return here but he was eased when his winning chance had gone and the return to 5f can suit; much respected.

quotes.race: Newmarket Academy Godolphin Beacon Project Cornwallis Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Full credit to Tara Murphy who rides Beckford's Folly out and has done since day one. He has been a challenge - he has to be stabled and turned most of the day. He started his career as a full horse. He got beat first time and then won his next two starts at Newmarket. We went to the Sirenia [at Kempton] thinking it would be the right sort of race for him but to be fair Oisin [Murphy] rode him that day and he was a challenge from start to finish. He came out of that race even more of a challenge to be honest. So, needless to say, after that we went to geld him and since then he has done very well. Mentally, it has just taken the steam out of him. He put in a good couple of pieces of work since he was gelded. He put in a good piece of work midweek and there was nothing that could take him off the bridle. Once they jumped out today and were going the clip they were, I could see he was hanging on to their coat tails, and I knew he will finish. Full credit to William and the horse - they got the job done. He might come out to Dubai. He is still a challenge even though he is gelded. He wouldn't be a Breeders' Cup horse or anything like that. The reason he comes to Newmarket is that it is less challenging for him and that is why you see his best performances at Newmarket. If we are lucky enough to be looking at him next year as a potential July Cup horse, at least we know it's only up the road! - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Racecourse Syndicates Association Promoting Shared Ownership EBF Confined Novice (Max 1 Run) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We thought Beckford's Folly may need seven furlongs but William got off and said stick to six for now. We were hopeful of a decent show as he got stuck out in the middle of the track at Lingfield on his debut and we took the hood off him this time - Alex Merriam, assistant to trainer Charlie Appleby.

runners.comment: All runs at 6f; two front-running wins before 4th in Group 1 here in September; tall order
runners.spotlight: All races at 6f, improving on front-running novice (good to firm) and AW Group 3 wins when beaten less than 3l in the Group 1 Middle Park on this course in September; from a yard that's much respected with sprinters but this still asks a lot on the drop to 5f.

quotes.race: Unibet Sirenia Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Five Ways. He shows a lot of ability in his homework and he won well at Salisbury last time, so we just thought it was worth a go. He'll stay further in time, we'll just have to see if we go again this year. He's a lovely horse for the future. We were a bit disappointed first time out, but the ground was a bit loose and he had a bit of wheelspin and probably needed the run - Andrew Balding. trainer.

quotes.race: Michael Brunton Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted, I bred Five Ways, his dam, grandmother and the one before that. Andrew's always thought he was a good horse but I'm surprised by how easy he's won. We hope he's a nice horse but I've been breeding horses for over 50 years so I know not to get too excited. It was a quick time so it's all looking good. I think he'll stay further and it will be time for a reassessment after that - John Hobby, owner-breeder.

racecards.verdict: Asfoora may have better claims later in the year and preference is for BECKFORD'S FOLLY ahead of last year's winner Rumstar.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/1 Rumstar,  Asfoora, 6/1 Frost At Dawn, 8/1 Night Raider,  Quinault, 9/1 Jm Jungle, 10/1 Shagraan, 12/1 Ain't Nobody,  Beckford's Folly, 14/1 First Instinct, 25/1 Washington Heights,  Miss Attitude,  Five Ways, 40/1 Town And Country

racecards.race_name: Betfred 2000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)

runners.comment: Had the run of things in the Greenham to take record to 3-4; another easy lead is unlikely
runners.spotlight: Reversed Dewhurst placings with Zavateri, an absentee from this race due to a setback, in the Greenham at Newbury (7f, good; Group 3) to take his record to 3-4; however, needs further progress, having finished behind several more of these in the Dewhurst, and is far from sure to get another easy lead (dictated the pace last time).

quotes.race: Watership Down Stud Too Darn Hot Greenham Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Alparslan is a high-class horse, and I'm sure he'll turn up in one of the Guineas, but it's a case of which one we go for. We've got time to go to the English and Irish, but it's a nice problem to have and I'm really happy. He's been to Newmarket, and he didn't like the undulations of the track, although that could've been down to two-year-old immaturity. It's a question mark. Whether racing round a bend at Longchamp for the French Guineas would be his cup of tea, I don't know, but the Curragh would suit him well as he's obviously won there. The mile is the question, but when you look at the last 50 yards, he's not stopping. He's going away if anything. I thought we were coming here under the radar. He'd only run three times, and he's entitled to improve off those runs. He's been working very well, and he's got a great mind. He will definitely come on fitness-wise, and I'm sure there's another gear for him - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A smart, strong-travelling horse who progressed nicely last year. He acquitted himself well in the Dewhurst as he didn't handle the undulations at Newmarket. He'll go to Newbury for a trial to see how he gets on with the trip and grade, and then we'll see about one of the Guineas. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Finished nicely for second in the Craven; could pick up some pieces if the pace is strong
runners.spotlight: Two from two last year, both starts over 7f at Doncaster and getting up on the line in Listed grade the second time; finished nicely for 2l second to Oxagon, who dictated the pace, in the Craven over C&D (good) on reappearance having again been held up; open to further progress and could pick up some pieces in this big-field scenario, assuming the gallop is suitably strong.

quotes.race: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Avicenna is learning on the job, was strong through the line and is a horse to look forward to. He's always looked a good horse and we felt he took a good step forward at home since that first run. He'll get a mile, whether this year or next. I think he'll probably be a miler, I don't know whether he's good enough for a Guineas, he's just won a Listed by a nose. He's a nice horse, we don't need to get carried away yet - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He needs more match practice and is likely to run in either the Craven or the Greenham. I've been really happy with him in the last fortnight and we're hopeful that he could be a Guineas candidate of some description. He's in the English, Irish, French and German 2,000 Guineas, and how he runs in Craven week will dictate the next step. I think he'll get a mile well and he's done nothing wrong so far. There's no reason why we can't get excited. 01-04-26

He's a nice horse, he's done nothing wrong and is two from two having won the Flying Scotsman at Doncaster recently. I didn't think he'd won watching it live. I was probably 50 yards short of the finish line and I didn't think he could make up the ground, but he got the head bob. He was very willing under William Buick and we can take a lot away from that. I'm delighted that having received yearlings from the Godolphin team and Sheikh Mohammed for the first time, the first horse that we've got on the track is a tidy performer. That's very satisfying. I'd like to run him again this season but I'm not sure in which race yet. I don't think he's an autumn-ground horse - William thought he just got away with it at Doncaster. He isn't in the Dewhurst or the Lagardere and they're probably unlikely, unless he's supplemented, but he has come out of his last race really well and I don't want to put a line through running him again. I've got to speak to the team, but I might entertain the idea of something like the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf. He's definitely going to stay a mile but I don't think he's ready for an autumn mile. The Autumn Stakes is often won by a middle-distance horse, for example. I think he could stay at 7f or a two-turn American mile on fast ground could suit him, so we'll have that in the back of our minds and see how he progresses over the next fortnight or so. 24-09-25

runners.comment: Has plenty to find in this field and needs to settle better than last time
runners.spotlight: Has plenty to find in this field and needs to settle better to boot, having raced too freely in Listed event last time when bidding for a Newcastle (1m, AW) double; behind Distant Storm on sole turf attempt; unlikely to emulate his sire Night Of Thunder, who landed this prize in 2014.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Already proven over C&D, having won the Royal Lodge to take record to 3-3; much respected
runners.spotlight: Son of 2,000 Guineas winner Night Of Thunder and from the family of Dubawi; three from three last term, all starts over 1m, driven out for 1l success in the Royal Lodge at Newmarket (good to firm; Group 2) the final time; that wasn't necessarily a star performance but he keeps getting the job done and commands major respect, being a progressive colt who has a perfect record and has had a "faultless spring" according to his trainer; furthermore, he's already proven over C&D.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Online Royal Lodge Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Bow Echo got a lovely ride. Billy [Loughnane] allowed him to relax early. I was keen to do it the right way round - we could have been forward and tried to make a test of it, but he has got a turn of foot and it was nice to see it today. He is still a very raw animal but certainly a very good one. He is certainly much the best colt I have trained. We have had some nice fillies but he is head and shoulders above the rest of them. He is a miler at the moment for sure. His pedigree goes back to some ten-furlong horses, but we are pretty confident at a mile at the moment and it was a nice trial for May (the Betfred 2,000 Guineas). The Guineas is very much the plan and I don't think he's a horse that needs to trial. He is a Group Two winner at two and hopefully all being well he will come straight back here next year - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: Betting.Betfair Ascendant Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Bow Echo is a lovely horse who has shown plenty of ability at home, but he's possibly still quite raw. It looked like Publish was coming to win the race, but our horse was waiting for him and outbattled him in the end. I think we'll just see how he comes out of the race. He's very much a horse for next year. Maybe we could step him up in class again this year, but I'd be quite happy to wait and run him in a Guineas trial next spring. He has plenty of pace, he's a Guineas horse and that's what we'll be training him for - George Boughey, trainer.

quotes.race: TPT Fire Supports St Michaels Hospice EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: It was a taking performance. Bow Echo's work had been good at home and I've always liked him. I couldn't believe how well I was going at the two-furlong pole. He's got a long way to go before that [being a credible 2,000 Guineas candidate] and we're not 100 per cent sure what he's beaten, but I'd imagine George [Boughey, trainer] will have options for him. I thought he'd take a lot of beating but he's got to step up to any Classic credentials - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's going straight to the Guineas. He's very clean-winded and has plenty of boot. He stayed a mile at two and he makes my job very easy. It's all systems go for Newmarket and he's undoubtedly the best colt we've trained - it's very exciting. The fact we're not trialling probably opens up the Irish 2,000 Guineas but his next start will determine everything. I'd love to take the typical route of running in the Guineas and the St James's Palace before taking on the older horses. He's showing us all the right signs that he's on track for a big summer. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Impressive in the Tattersalls Stakes prior to running well in the Dewhurst; big player
runners.spotlight: Aptly bred, being by Night Of Thunder and out of a mare by another 2,000 Guineas winner, namely George Washington; 1,900,000euros breeze-up purchase last spring and duly made a big splash in his 2yo races, aside from when pulling too hard in the Acomb; showed smart from at Newmarket (7f, good/good to firm) in the autumn, impressing in the Tattersalls Stakes (Group 3) then running well (one place behind Gstaad) in the Dewhurst; yard has landed this prize three times in the last four years; big player.

quotes.race: Darley Dewhurst Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: After Distant Storm was beaten in the Acomb by today's winner, we thought we'd give him one more run and put him away, and then when he won the Group 3 here last time as he did we were drawn into the Dewhurst. William [Buick] said he rode like a horse who will be better with some time over winter to develop. He felt that the immaturity was coming out in him today, but he's lost nothing in defeat as we see him as a Guineas horse next year. Whether he runs in the Craven Stakes or has a racecourse gallop before that, we'll have to see - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Stakes (Registered As The Somerville Tattersall Stakes) (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It's not the first time I've got one beat in the Acomb but it was my mistake. William was keen to get a pitch on Distant Storm early on and, to do that, he asked him from the gate and the only other time I've seen him be keen was when he was on the lead at home. We were adamant today to drop him in and let the race develop in front of him and in doing so we've seen his acceleration. I think we've seen a nice horse in the making. William was impressed and, with the way this season is stacking up with two-year-olds, my initial impression is to look at the Dewhurst. If it were sound ground conditions I'd be happy to take them on. He's definitely up there - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: Distant Storm is one of the nicest breeze-up horses I've seen with an eye to the future, we always felt this is a horse for next year and we'll give him a bit of time. He's still very unfurnished. He's a nice-looking horse, but still needs to strengthen before you go up a level ? if you pitch them in too soon, you'll go quickly backwards. There will be races in the autumn we can dip our toe in and allow him to progress. If he ticks the next box we can look at the Group 1 target we have pencilled in. He could be an Acomb horse - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

runners.comment: Rock-solid as a 2yo; ran well in the Dewhurst prior to Breeders' Cup win; leading claims
runners.spotlight: Proved rock-solid as a 2yo, readily winning the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f) then posting form figures of 2221 at Group/Grade 1 level, including in the Dewhurst at Newmarket (7f) when doing well considering he was free to post and in the race; ended the campaign by overcoming a wide trip in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf at Del Mar (1m, firm; won with something to spare); supplemented (effectively re-added) into this at a cost of £30,000 having been removed in late March due to a clerical error; leading contender in his bid to end a 2,000 Guineas drought for Aidan O'Brien, who has landed this Classic a record ten times but not since 2019.

quotes.race: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf (Grade 1) (2yo Colts & Geldings) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I didn't do anything really, I think Gstaad is just good. He's been a little bit unlucky in Europe on his last few starts, we should've won one of them. He jumped a bit slow today, but he was travelling very well in the first part of the race. When I saw there was a gap in the back straight to try to go forward and let him sit behind the pace, I made the move and I was cruising the whole way. I knew when I came out of the turn that I'd win. It's very rare to see amazing horses winning a Breeders' Cup hands and heels like that - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.race: Darley Dewhurst Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Next year Gstaad will be older and stronger, but he ran a good race and you have to be very happy with him. I think the race worked out lovely. He would be one for an English or Irish 2,000 Guineas - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Morny (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Gstaad ran a great race, we're delighted. It's a long time since he ran but we're over the moon. We had it in our head he could go back to the National Stakes, so that's where he could go next. He'd have no problem with seven furlongs - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Coventry Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Gstaad looks a very good horse, doesn't he? We've always loved him. He had only had the one run. He has always worked like a good horse. He's big, he's scopey, he has a good stride and is very genuine; he goes with his head down and he has loads of speed. He looks like he will get further than six [furlongs] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Gstaad was very impressive. I thought he travelled beautifully, and we got to the front a long way from home. He's a tall horse and is obviously improving with each run and that was a very good performance - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: He was a little bit babyish going down but Gstaad was a pro in the race. When Wayne (Lordan) kicked he got a bit disorganised but from the furlong pole I always thought I was going to get there. I'll think he'll sharpen up for it, he'll get another furlong - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour.quote: He was always a hardy horse and won the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf on his final start of the season. When he finished second in the Dewhurst, Christophe made the decision to take him back after he jumped, and was caught in the middle of two. When he came back, they all came back and there ended up being no pace. We felt there was more to come from him after that and he went and won in America, coasting around and not doing a lot when he got there. I wouldn't be afraid to let him flow because he isn't a keen horse but has a long stride and a big action. He's being trained for a Guineas. Ryan rode him at the Curragh on Sunday and he had it in his head he could be one for Newmarket. But we'll see how Puerto Rico and Albert Einstein are over the next few weeks. 31-03-26

runners.owner: Mrs D Tabor, Dr P Wilson & R Stanbridge
runners.comment: Mill Reef runner-up; good prospect for Jim Boyle but doesn't seem to be crying out for 1m
runners.spotlight: Showed useful form over 6.5f and 6f at Newbury (good/good to soft) last season, winning a maiden by sizeable margin then clear second in the Mill Reef (Group 2; hung left; collared near the finish); good prospect for Jim Boyle this term but doesn't appear to be crying out for 1m.

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes (Group 2) (In Honour Of Geoff Lewis)
quotes.quote: The winner is a good horse, but Into The Sky has run a hell of a race and he's proved that first-time-out win wasn't a fluke. Hopefully there's loads more to look forward to. We wouldn't have taken this step lightly, but the manner of his victory last time warranted it. They both pulled a long way clear and to do that on his second start, I can only be thrilled, but a little bit gutted too. He's got so much raw ability, and to do that on his second start shows he's pretty special. I won't run him again this season. He's a big frame of a horse, and Pat [Cosgrave, jockey] said, 'God, what a horse he'll be next year'. It's always the way we felt about him; we thought he was next year's horse. What he's done this year has been phenomenal, but we'll speak to all the owners and come up with a plan. We might be thinking about the Greenham because he shows so much speed, but it's far too early to be making any firm plans and we'll put him away and let him strengthen up - Jim Boyle, trainer.

runners.comment: Similar type to his yard's winner of this race in 2024; brings big potential; interesting
runners.spotlight: Son of Sea The Stars, whose stellar 3yo campaign included a success in the 2,000 Guineas; two from two, both outings over 1m on Kempton AW, last time looking value for more than the 1l winning margin in a conditions race that Notable Speech (from same yard) won in 2024 before following up in this contest; deserted by William Buick but the stable landed this Classic with the second string, ridden by James Doyle, in 2022; interesting contender who brings significant potential.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet/British EBF Conditions Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: I've been lucky enough to sit on King's Trail a couple of times at home and he was impressive when he won here the first time. It was a very messy race and he'll have learned plenty from the first couple of furlongs. He's straightforward and has a great mind for a Sea The Stars. I had to wake him up a little to get a position, but you couldn't fault his attitude at all. He's done nothing wrong and I'm sure he'll have a few stiffer targets now - Billy Loughnane, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: Bottom of this pack on bare figures; finished last in the Royal Lodge on sole turf start
runners.spotlight: Campaigned mainly on AW, most recently 5l fourth (ran well but never dangerous) to King's Trail at Kempton on seasonal debut; bottom of this pack on the figures and trailed home last in the Royal Lodge on sole turf attempt; this outsider has plenty to prove and plenty to find.

runners.comment: Ran well in the Greenham; further improvement is plausible upped to 1m; not dismissed
runners.spotlight: Similar to Into The Sky in having raced at Newbury on both starts; did just enough to win 2yo maiden (6.5f, soft) then ran well, about 2l fourth to Alparslan, in the Greenham (7f, good); the way he shaped last time suggests additional improvement is plausible upped further in trip; by 2,000 Guineas winner Night Of Thunder; more interesting than bare ratings suggest.

runners.comment: Very useful but possibly needs to dominate; took well to cheekpieces in the Craven
runners.spotlight: Very useful colt but possibly needs to dominate, having gained both wins from the front, latest when taking well to first-time cheekpieces and comfortably beating Avicenna by 2l in the Craven Stakes over C&D (good; Group 3) on seasonal debut; by no means certain to have his own way in this bigger field and he's held by a couple of today's opponents on Dewhurst running; otherwise may have more to offer in the retained headgear.

quotes.race: Betway Craven Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: After Oxagon won at Sandown last season, we had a high opinion of him. He probably let the race get away from him in Doncaster [when second in the Champagne Stakes] and we'll probably see Puerto Rico [the winner that day] back here in two weeks' time [for the 2,000 Guineas]. I will admit he was a tad disappointing in the Dewhurst as he was one of the last off the bridle and didn't seem to quite finish off up the hill. I then stupidly ran him in heavy ground at Doncaster. Thankfully, the jockey was cleverer than me and pulled him up after two furlongs and let him enjoy his day out. He has trained well this year, and I think the addition of cheekpieces has just focused his mind today. He is one of those horses that things come easily to and he can be a little bit dreamy at home - he is always looking for low-flying seagulls. Oisin feels it's an open Guineas and we should go for it. It would be great to have a runner. Let's enjoy today and hope the horse is in great order. This race today did have a couple of late withdrawals, which didn't help the depth of the field and so we wound up the second favourite. He has run how you hoped he would run. He is a nice horse and deserves to take his chance [in the 2,000 Guineas] - John Gosden, trainer.

runners.comment: Promising colt for his first-season trainer but faces a difficult task on turf debut
runners.spotlight: Unraced at two; AW form this year comprises a win at Southwell (7f) and neck second, doing well having come from difficult position, at Newcastle (1m Listed); promising colt for first-season trainer Charlie Pike but faces a much stiffer task on turf debut; supplemented at a cost of £30,000.

runners.comment: Group 1 winner over 6f as a 2yo; not a guaranteed stayer in this first attempt at 1m
runners.spotlight: Juvenile campaign over sprint distances culminated in Group 1 win at the Curragh (good); held by Gstaad on Coventry running; respectable second to Thesecretadversary, who received 3lb, in 7f Group 3 at Leopardstown on reappearance but doesn't give the strong impression he'll benefit from going up further in trip; indeed, he seems more of a 6f Commonwealth Cup type.

quotes.race: Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: He has got bigger and stronger and Power Blue is improving throughout the year. Every time he turns up he never lets us down. A furlong out I was thinking the filly wasn't going to get to him - Adrian Murray, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Castle Star At Capital Stud Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: It's a bit of a usual thing with Adrian [Murray] and his team winning this race! Power Blue was well prepared and he was the ultimate professional really. He showed a little bit of greenness but he really quickened up the last hundred yards and galloped out all the way to the boards so he'll be getting a bit further than five furlongs, that's for sure. Why not? [when asked whether he could emulate the achievements of previous recent winners of this race]. He won by a wider margin today than Arizona Blaze, who was a Breeders' Cup placed horse and Bucanero Fuerte probably won in similar fashion. He's a nice horse and there's sure to be plenty of improvement - David Egan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's run some very good races, including when second to Albert Einstein last time, and we think he'll go very close in the Coventry. He and Arizona Blaze are probably our best chances. 13-06-25

runners.owner: Cayton Park Stud & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: Irish colt who has built up a solid record; won going away in 7f Group 3 on reappearance
runners.spotlight: Irish colt who has built up a solid record that includes a good effort in Canadian Grade 1 on final 2yo start (sole 1m attempt); won going away from Power Blue, who conceded 3lb, in Group 3 at Leopardstown (7f, good to yielding) on reappearance; could go well but several others bring stronger claims in terms of class and/or potential.

quotes.race: Ballylinch Stud Red Rocks Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: The only bit of a setback we had with Thesecretadversary was at Ayr last year. He was a bit unlucky in Canada last time. He's in everything so we'll see where we go. He stays well. He's been working well. He ran a good race at Ascot last year and won well at Tipperary, where he beat the horse who was second in the Middle Park [Brussels], so it was a fair bit of form. He's in every Guineas bar the Italian, and I entered him in a $1 million race in the US the same day as the English Guineas. We'll talk to the owners - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

quotes.race: Chesham Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Thesecretadversary ran a great race. It's annoying we didn't get there, but he ran a great race. He's been very straightforward, he's always looked a bit above average from the minute we started doing a bit with him. I know he's quite colourful, but he's actually a very good model. Seamie was delighted with him, he said he has the pace of a good horse, he feels he will mature in time - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

runners.comment: Held by some of today's rivals on two pieces of form; first-time headgear needs to help
runners.spotlight: Has finished behind some of today's rivals on two occasions, latest in the Craven when admittedly running well on bare figures; gained sole success (from five attempts) at novice level and looks well short of the required standard in this field; first-time headgear needs to make a difference.

racecards.verdict: The Verdict comprises two unbeaten colts who should continue to improve. BOW ECHO (nap) is first choice ahead of King's Trail.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Gstaad, 7/2 Bow Echo, 4/1 Distant Storm, 7/1 King's Trail, 10/1 Oxagon, 14/1 Avicenna,  Needle Match, 16/1 Alparslan, 20/1 Thesecretadversary, 25/1 Into The Sky, 40/1 Padraig Dawn,  Power Blue, 100/1 Venetian Prince, 150/1 Billecart, 200/1 Lord Britain

racecards.race_name: Turners Handicap

runners.comment: Made giant strides on AW; should be effective on turf too but now high in the weights
runners.spotlight: Developed into a useful performer on AW this winter, reeling off a five-timer (6f) prior to a good third in Listed company (7f); solid efforts in defeat on his last two starts and too soon to pigeonhole him as an AW specialist given his two turf runs were on soft ground and early in his career; likely vulnerable off topweight all the same.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 with a good run and his C&D 2nd last month was even better; 4lb higher today
runners.spotlight: Won twice on AW last year but he took his form to a new level when fourth of 14 in a York sales race last October (7f, good); lumped up 11lb for that but showed there was no fluke about the performance by finishing second in a C&D handicap on his reappearance 16 days ago (behind Sovereign Spell); didn't look in love with the track on that occasion but he is on an upward path and remains unexposed as a sprinter; 4lb rise demands more though.

quotes.race: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: I planned to get a lead but Advertised is very genuine and straightforward and I thought if I could get an easy lead, I know he's got a good turn of foot and I just turned it into a sprint from the three [furlong pole] - Oliver Stammers, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse. We got him beat on his debut by running him over 5f. The winner, who's gone in again, was from the breeze-ups and just caught him out. He won at Newcastle when he hit the front and pricked his ears - he's a very laid-back character. He looked like he wanted seven and he might, but I think a stiff six is going to be great for him. He shows more speed at home than he does at the track and I think there's a lot more to come. He has a sales race entry at the Curragh on September 14 and that's his target. He'd probably have 10lb to find there but I think he can be competitive. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Highly tried at 2yrs following debut win; satisfactory return; respected on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: 5f win on 2yo debut; came up short in Group 2 and Listed company afterwards but still displayed useful ability; sent off favourite for a conditions event at Wolverhampton (6f; tongue-tie added) on last month's return and finished a close third despite hanging to his right; getting back on a straight track should suit and this Commonwealth Cup entrant makes some appeal on his handicap debut.

runners.comment: Handicapped on his Molecomb 4th and that form hasn't worked out; gelded since latest run
runners.spotlight: 6f novice win at Windsor last July before appearing to improve when fourth in the Group 3 Molecomb at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good; form hasn't worked out at all); struggled thereafter and he makes his seasonal/handicap debut off a tough mark; has been gelded since last seen.

runners.comment: 2-2 this year, latterly beating Advertised over C&D last month; 6lb rise may find him out
runners.spotlight: First past the post at Windsor last summer but demoted on a technicality; 2-2 in 2026, winning a Wolverhampton maiden easily before gamely seeing off Advertised over C&D 16 days ago; 6lb rise could be enough to scupper the hat-trick bid.

quotes.race: Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Sovereign Spell found a very good rhythm at the front end and there is a bit of a tailwind which suits front runners. He kept finding and like at Wolverhampton, his last furlong was his best furlong. With a stiff six furlongs here today and being a fitter horse, we thought we'd let him bowl along in front. He relaxed very well and has a good stride. He is a tough horse and will always keep finding, although he'll never win by too far. I think he will keep improving and he could come back here in a couple of weeks - Kevin Philippart de Foy, trainer.

runners.comment: Promising early 2yo but he has rather plateaued since; only midfield over C&D on return
runners.spotlight: Came to hand early last year, winning a York novice on debut before finishing second in the Listed National Stakes at Sandown; only sixth in the C&D handicap won by Sovereign Spell 16 days ago and he needs that run to have brought him on significantly.

quotes.race: Frank Whittle Partnership ebfstallions.com Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: First Legion had breezed very well and was bought with a big reputation. He was a little bit keen in the middle of the race, but he picked up good. He came from a good breeze-up place and he'll improve on good, fast ground - Shane Foley, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big, strong lad and looks like a proper sprinter, but he needs runs to get fit and will come on plenty from his outing at Newmarket last week. He may get seven furlongs in time, but a six-furlong handicap at York will be his next target. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Promise in first two starts before an easy AW win (all 7f); more to come now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Gave trouble in the stalls on his first two runs last year (gelded afterwards) but also showed a good level of ability; made no mistake in a 7f novice at Wolverhampton in December, running out the easy winner of a race that has been subsequently been franked; bred to carry on improving and the drop in trip shouldn't be an issue; leading claims.

runners.comment: Won first two starts before lesser run in Salisbury conditions event; improvement needed
runners.spotlight: Won a Bath maiden (5.7f, good to firm) on debut and followed up in a Salisbury novice (6f, good to soft) four weeks later; last of four in a conditions race back at Salisbury in October; improvement essential now handicapping but it's not out of the question.

stable_tour.quote: He was a very exciting work horse at home as a juvenile and did well on the track, winning his first two starts. His third and final start of last year was in a conditions race at Salisbury and we probably rode him wrong. He's been training well and if he takes everything in his stride he'll be an exciting three-year-old. He heads to Newmarket on Saturday for the three-year-old sprint handicap. 29-04-26

runners.comment: Two 6f wins last year; had wind surgery since last seen; yard in form; not fully exposed
runners.spotlight: Two 6f wins last summer; not at his best at Chester when last seen but he was drawn wide and there were possible trip/ground excuses too (wore cheekpieces which are absent today); has undergone wind surgery over the winter; returns for a stable ticking along nicely; may have more to offer.

runners.comment: Five-race maiden but not short of ability; headgear tried now back to 6f and handicapping
runners.spotlight: 360,000gns breeze-up 2yo; still seeking a first win and he has been expensive to follow thus far; that said, his Goodwood second (6f, good) last summer reads well and when third at Doncaster five weeks ago (7f, good to soft) he travelled through the race like a smart horse; the combination of a drop back in trip and the addition of cheekpieces could see him step forward now handicapping.

stable_tour.quote: I rate him highly and was delighted with his first run at Beverley. If he'd have jumped a bit sharper he'd have probably won, but it was a good start and we've got the option of running in the Coventry Stakes or the Norfolk. At the moment it's looking more like the Norfolk because Wathnan have other options for the Coventry but he'll have an entry in both in case plans change. We won the Norfolk with Shareholder last season but Naval Light is a more laid-back character with a lot of ability.    12-06-25

runners.comment: Rock-solid 2yo form; could progress further this year; stable won this race last year
runners.spotlight: Promise behind useful opposition in his first three starts and his Windsor win in August (6f, good) saw him defeat one who has boosted the form subsequently; gelded before finishing second at Kempton on his handicap debut 206 days ago; 2lb higher for his reappearance but still of interest for last year's winning yard.

stable_tour.quote: He's come out of Ascot [fifth behind Wise Approach] really well and I think it was a particularly strong race. That was a nice performance and he wants 6f at least. There's a restricted novice at York at the end of the month or a race at Windsor in June, both over 6f. I think he's crying out for that trip. Rossa Ryan was taken with him and I think he'll be a lovely horse. Of my juveniles, he's precocious and it nearly came off at Ascot. 14-05-25

runners.comment: 12 runs as a 2yo, winning three; into a deep race on his return and others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Ran 12 times as a 2yo, winning three times; the ground may have been too soft when down the field at Newbury on his final run last year but likely a few of these will have his measure.

quotes.race: PricedUp Daily Sports Boosts Grassroots Series Final Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Kesta is another cheap purchase who Eve [Johnson Houghton, trainer] has done well with. He's not the biggest but he tries exceptionally hard, one day at Windsor he dead heated just because he refused to get beat. He travelled into that very well today and he's extremely genuine. I was very happy to just sit in behind, I was drawn in stall one so I was worried I might get stuck on the wing, but I was able to get a nice run in behind the leaders - Charles Bishop, rider.

racecards.verdict: Handicap debutants Man Of Vision and NAVAL LIGHT appeal most. Headgear and a return to 6f can see the selection break his duck.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Sovereign Spell, 9/2 Advertised,  Man Of Vision, 6/1 Comical Point, 10/1 Naval Light, 12/1 Pilu, 14/1 Rydale Frosty,  Front Line Fury,  Angel Of Anfield, 16/1 First Legion, 20/1 Ten Carat Harry, 33/1 Kesta

racecards.race_name: Boodles Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: This is his first handicap; big chance if springing back to best, as he did here in 2025
runners.spotlight: Seemingly ring-rusty on Group 3 return at Newbury two weeks ago, the same story as in 2025 when he followed that race with a win at this meeting in a four-runner 1m4f Group 2 with first-time cheekpieces; they were kept for two modest efforts last June but have not been called on this season; this is his first handicap and he has a big chance if springing back to his best.

quotes.race: Betfred Jockey Club Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum is a high-class horse and had got some good form from last year. Obviously, the second is a very good horse as well. I am delighted because he was a big disappointment in the John Porter and it's just nice to see him back on track. I think the cheekpieces helped and it was an excellent performance. He has had a hard enough race today and I think we will probably wait for the Hardwicke now. It will nice to have runners with a chance for King Power at the Royal meeting - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: DK Horse Nashville Derby Invitational Stakes (Grade 3) (3yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum absolutely flubbed the start. I was way too far back, but lucky Jamie [Spencer, on pacesetting Navy Seal] was so fast. On the back straight, I was able to make good improvement to get a slot, because I knew he would stay very well. I knew he'd gallop out to the line because he stays a mile and a half - Frankie Dettori, rider.

quotes.race: Betfred Blue Riband Trial (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum showed some promise last year but had a little setback about a month ago. I think he is bound to come on for the run and we thought that whatever happened today, we would go to the Dante Stakes next and see where we are with him. Obviously, I need to talk it over with the owners but if all goes well there then the Derby would be the plan - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts And Geldings)
quotes.quote: Bellum Justum was very professional and it's great to have a winner for King Power. He'll probably have another run this year in something like the Autumn Stakes here next month - Sam Geake, trainer's assistant.

runners.comment: Ran creditably in the Derby and Group 3s on final three starts last term; gelded since
runners.spotlight: 100-1 for the Derby at Epsom but showed improvement in making late headway from the back to finish eighth of 18 runners; similar form later last summer in Group 3s at Newmarket and Newbury; gelded in March and some improvement is needed but he is lightly raced and may be capable of it.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well when eighth in the Derby last season. He showed a similar level of form over longer trips after that. He has a lot of ability and will start off in Listed company, from a mile and a half upwards, and hopefully being gelded will keep his mind on the job. I think he'll be a very nice horse over Cup distances. 21-04-26

runners.comment: 2nd and 3rd places early this year came in small fields and other options look more solid
runners.spotlight: AW Listed winner for the Gosdens in November 2024 but he hasn't been near that form since a Listed second last June; second and third places early this year came in small fields and other options look more solid.

quotes.race: Slate Floodlit Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Military Academy started his career a little later than usual but has progressed with every start and is still learning. He's taken a step forward since Newmarket. He's got plenty of size and scope and hopefully he will mature over the winter for next year. He's run a few races in quick succession, so we'll leave him alone and bring him back next year - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Lightly raced 4yo, gelded since latest start, who surely has more to offer
runners.spotlight: 2-2 as 2yo and progressive last term in his first three handicaps, short-headed by another unexposed sort at Leicester (1m4f) on third occasion; underperformed on heavy going (he won on it as a 2yo) when joint-favourite for the November Handicap at Doncaster on final outing but that's not hard to forgive and this lightly raced 4yo, gelded since latest start, surely has more to offer.

quotes.race: British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hopewell Rock is raw and did well to win on his debut at Newbury. He won that without liking the ground. Billy thought he'd pick up quicker so he'll stay further than a mile, but he did it nicely. He's got a good way of going so is one to look forward to next season. He'll only be a 3yo and we'll see how he gets on and develops. He has a patient owner in Sheikh Mohammed Obaid, who likes his horses to flourish at three - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had little setbacks last spring so we had to be patient. He hated the ground when we thought he'd go well in the November Handicap on his last start. We've earmarked a mile-and-a-half handicap at the Guineas meeting and he could end up in a handicap at Royal Ascot. He's improved since being gelded. 02-04-26

runners.comment: 9lb higher after breezing home in front at Kempton (1m3f); has had just five races
runners.spotlight: Won a maiden at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) on reappearance last term, before failing to go on in his next two starts; however, he was gelded later in the autumn and led 2f out for an impressive 3l win when back in action five weeks ago in useful handicap at Kempton (1m3f, AW); 9lb higher today but likely to stay 1m4f and, after just five races, could still have potential.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Rosebery Handicap (London Middle Distance Series Qualifier) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Gamrai had shown a level of form last year and he's still probably a little bit unfurnished. To come out after being gelded and off a break, then deliver a performance like that against horses who've been running all winter, shows he's got plenty of talent - Rob Hornby, jockey.

runners.owner: A Stennett, G Kennington & C Hodgson
runners.comment: Close, strong-finishing 3rd in valuable C&D handicap (good) in October; gelded soon after
runners.spotlight: Sole win in eight runs was a Chester maiden; best efforts, however, when third in both the 1m6f Melrose at York (good to firm; led over 2f out) and another valuable handicap over C&D (good; finishing strongly) in October; gelded soon afterwards; interesting prospect as 4yo.

runners.comment: Will pop up again at some stage but well held on last year's reappearance at this fixture
runners.spotlight: Scored at the Newmarket July meeting (1m6f) last year but didn't do a lot afterwards; he's back 1lb below that last winning mark, so will pop up in front again at some stage, but he was well held on last year's reappearance at this fixture.

quotes.race: bet365 Trophy (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: It was the perfect set-up for Oneforthegutter with fast ground, a decent gallop and plenty of cover, and when I finally got a gap he was very game - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I never expected Oneforthegutter to get in off his mark, but has run a huge race. He and Joe have just gelled together and ultimately just got outstayed. It was a huge performance and a little bit better than the what we were expecting. Class as much as anything beat him today but we'll look for similar sort of things. He could turn out in the Old Borough Cup at Haydock if it doesn't come around too quickly - Ian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Magnum Classic Ice Cream Handicap
quotes.quote: Oneforthegutter has suffered with his wind in the past and that's his third run back after probably his third wind operation. You couldn't be confident the wind op had worked. As you can imagine [with his breathing] we were worried about the ground but Ben Curtis has given him a great ride and he's stuck at his task and stayed on well. He's always merited winning a prize like that and the new trip today was a good thing. It opens up options for him - Ian Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: 0-9 on turf and he was last seen in this sphere in 2023; fit from AW action
runners.spotlight: Six wins from his 24 AW starts, the latest in February, but 0-9 on turf and he was last seen in this sphere in 2023; fit from AW action (well beaten in hot race last time) but other options seem more likely.

stable_tour.quote: He hasn't run this year because of a tendon injury but we've given him loads of time. The leg feels good and he's training well. He's very much an all-weather horse - he's grown and developed - and he could be a progressive staying handicapper through the winter. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Respectable third of five on turf debut at Thirsk but this race should be a lot harder
runners.spotlight: Consistent 4yo who twice made all over 1m4f on Wolverhampton AW once the visor was enlisted; respectable third of five on turf debut at Thirsk (1m4f, good; hung left) three weeks ago but this race should be a lot harder.
