stable_tour.quote: The application of a visor seems to have focused his mind and he's won comfortably twice on the all-weather this spring. The handicapper hit him hard for the second of those wins and forced my hand to run him back quickly at Thirsk, where he was third. He takes his races fairly hard and typically would need longer between them. He'll probably go for a mile-and-a-half handicap at the Guineas meeting next. 21-04-26

racecards.verdict: Gamrai is the recent winner and Bellum Justum won at this meeting in 2025 but watch out for HOPEWELL ROCK and Daiquiri Bay.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Gamrai, 9/2 Hopewell Rock, 5/1 Daiquiri Bay, 7/1 Bellum Justum, 15/2 Nightime Dancer, 9/1 Pride Of Donegal, 20/1 Military Academy,  Oneforthegutter, 25/1 Nolton Cross

racecards.race_name: Air Charter Services "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Which Have Won No More Than One Race)

runners.breeder: R Kent & Executors Of Lady Lonsdale
runners.comment: Came up short in Listed race on final 2yo start; lightly raced and in good hands
runners.spotlight: Confirmed debut promise when winning at York (6f, good) last October before coming up short in Listed race here three weeks later; personal best needed on her first go in a handicap but she's lightly raced and in good hands.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thaluna is still learning and it was only her second run. She'd improved but she learned a lot today, she had to squeeze through a gap and she'll probably be better on faster ground - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.comment: Pleasing reappearance/handicap debut over C&D; may improve for the outing; respected
runners.spotlight: Catterick winner last October; made a pleasing reappearance/handicap debut over C&D (good ground) 18 days ago, always prominent and finishing fourth; Ryan Moore keeps the ride; may improve for the outing; respected.

quotes.race: EBF 'Confined' Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C And D With No More Than Three Runs) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sierra Sands won nicely and he has plenty of scope, so we'll put him away for next year after that - Ed Dunlop, trainer.

runners.comment: Third over C&D at the Craven meeting; going the right way and in the mix again
runners.spotlight: Finished a place ahead of Sierra Sands when third over C&D (good) at the Craven meeting, racing freely and in the firing line throughout; going the right way and should be in the thick of things again.

runners.comment: Good third at Naas in March and unsuited by drop back in distance next time; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Comes into the reckoning on his third at Naas (7f, soft) in March and he was probably unsuited by the drop back to 6f at Newcastle on Good Friday; still relatively lightly raced and not ruled out in first-time headgear.

quotes.race: Take Time Out During ~SGWeek25! EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Obviously it was a good pot down there (Chelmsford). Cotai Lights was working like a horse that wanted a mile but after he'd ran, he sharpened up quite a bit. It was the right decision to come back to six (furlongs) - Barry McHugh, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Nearly sprang 40-1 surprise over C&D; interesting on handicap debut after winter break
runners.spotlight: Didn't show much on her first two (AW) starts but she nearly sprang a 40-1 surprise over C&D (good) last autumn, making most of the running; unexposed and interesting on handicap debut after her winter break.

runners.comment: Made frame twice over 6f last summer; bred to be suited by 7f+ and could be unexposed
runners.spotlight: Made the frame twice over 6f last summer; missed next intended outing due to lameness; bred to be suited by 7f+ and may well have more to offer now tackling a handicap over this trip after nearly ten months off.

runners.comment: Progressive filly; justified favouritism at Kempton four weeks ago; high on the list
runners.spotlight: Has improved with each of her four runs, justifying favouritism at Kempton (7f) four weeks ago despite racing freely and wide; shaped well over 1m here (good) last autumn; open to further progress and high on the list.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Nanoscience has done it nicely and Oisin [Murphy, jockey] was very pleased with her. She's a lovely filly, well bred and I'm delighted for Kirsten [Rausing, owner] - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

runners.comment: Well held at 33-1 over C&D on stable debut; others make much more appeal
runners.spotlight: Well held at 33-1 over C&D on stable debut 18 days ago; only 2lb lower here and others make much more appeal.

quotes.race: EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Try Storm Cat has run well in defeat on both [previous] occasions and he deserved to get his head in front. We'll see what the handicapper does and what kind of mark but I think he will go another furlong and the seven-furlong nursery at Goodwood could be an option- Charlie Johnston, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Has blown hot and cold since Lingfield AW win; ran poorly there on Monday; enough to prove
runners.spotlight: Has blown hot and cold since winning at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February, and he ran poorly over the same C&D on Monday; enough to prove.

prev_owners.owner: Mps Racing Ltd, Roger Thompson & Partner
Mps Racing Ltd, Roger Thompson & Partner
Mps Racing Ltd, Roger Thompson & Partner

runners.comment: Shaped nicely when never-nearer fourth over 5f at Catterick; return to 7f looks a big plus
runners.spotlight: Just one win from 12 attempts, but she hasn't been long with her current yard and she seemed unsuited by the drop back to 5f when a never-nearer fourth of eight at Catterick ten days ago; looks well handicapped and the return to 7f should be right up her street.

runners.owner: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
runners.comment: Made frame on all three 2yo outings; pedigree suggests she can do better this season
runners.spotlight: Made the frame on all three outings (7f/6f) as a 2yo; has a modest opening handicap mark and her pedigree suggests she can do better this season; not without hope.

racecards.verdict: Paroda Diva is interesting back up in trip but the vote goes to NANOSCIENCE who can follow up her recent Kempton AW win.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Stellar Vision, 4/1 Nanoscience, 9/2 Sierra Sands, 5/1 Thaluna, 7/1 Lohoobb, 12/1 Cotai Lights,  Velvet Rhythm, 14/1 Splash, 20/1 Paroda Diva, 25/1 King Of Chaos, 33/1 Try Storm Cat

racecards.race_name: National Stud Handicap

runners.comment: Returned to Britain and won at Redcar 12 days ago; only 2lb higher and in the mix again
runners.spotlight: Campaigned in Qatar and France in 2025; went off joint-favourite on return to Britain and won nine-runner race at Redcar (1m, good to firm) 12 days ago, digging deep; only 2lb higher and should be in the thick of things again.

stable_tour.quote: He is a horse that is certainly worth a mention in this stable tour. He is a lovely colt by Calyx, whose progeny seem to be doing very well. I would not expect him out until later in the season when he will start off over 7f. 06-07-23

runners.comment: Below par since winning 2024 Lincoln; below last winning mark but would prefer soft ground
runners.spotlight: Had his favoured soft ground when winning the Lincoln in 2024; below par since, last seen finishing in midfield at Newcastle last June; back below his last winning mark but may find conditions too quick.

quotes.race: William Hill Lincoln (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: It was a great performance, Mr Professor travelled supremely well through the race and loved the ground. David was frightened about kicking too soon but when he asked him he quickened nicely and he kept going. If it's soft at Newbury, you'd have to have a look at the Spring Cup. But will it be as testing? Who knows - Dominic Ffrench Davis, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Silver Tankard Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Mr Professor has kept on improving this year. The straight track at Newmarket is where he's let us down but he just didn't settle there. He comes out of his races so well, we weigh ours every Monday and he'd put 8kg on since his last run. The ground was an unknown today but he battled to the line, though he wasn't doing an awful lot in front. He's in the sales next week and he is going to go, we'll see what money there is for him - Alice Haynes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been running well. He probably prefers time between his races and we may have made the mistake of running him too quickly at Goodwood the other day. Owen Lewis gets on very well with him at home, felt the ground was a bit soft and he didn't really like it. We'll freshen him up and he'll be out again in about a fortnight. 21-09-23

runners.comment: On a roll when last seen, winning twice; big chance if ready to roll after winter break
runners.spotlight: On a roll when last seen, winning at Sandown (1m, soft) and on this course (1m1f, good to firm) in second half of last season; that form looks solid and he's been nudged up only 3lb for the second success; leading claims if ready to roll after seven months off.

stable_tour.quote: I was glad he won a couple at the end as it was getting a little frustrating last year. He could go for the Suffolk Stakes and I'm hoping he'll end up in the Royal Hunt Cup, and maybe in the Cambridgeshire as well. He should be really competitive in those types of races and should pop up in one as he likes that style of racing. 27-04-26

runners.comment: Raced mostly on AW; below par last time; something to prove on rare encounter with turf
runners.spotlight: Mostly in good form on the AW during the winter, winning at Wolverhampton (8.6f) and Kempton (1m); however, he was below par back at Wolverhampton six weeks ago and has something to prove on a rare encounter with turf.

quotes.race: Best Odds Guaranteed At BetMGM Handicap
quotes.quote: Advancing has done really well today. The draw was a bit of a concern and there wasn't much pace on paper but we tried to put a bit of speed into the race and it suited him really well - Marco Ghiani, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Two winter AW wins but seems to have gone off the boil; questions to answer back on turf
runners.spotlight: Won twice on the AW over the winter but he seems to have gone off the boil, well beaten at Newcastle on Good Friday; not so effective yet on turf; others make more appeal.

runners.comment: Never better than midfield in Spring Cup at Newbury two weeks ago and only 1lb lower today
runners.spotlight: Consistent of late on the AW, runner-up at Kempton in October and March, but his turf efforts have been more up and down; never better than midfield in Spring Cup at Newbury two weeks ago and only 1lb lower today.

quotes.race: R & M Electrical EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Cogitate is a beautiful looking horse, he has the size and scope and looks to have a big future ahead of him. He qualifies now for the Acomb and that could be a good step. We've won that a couple of times before with Dutch Connection and Phoenix Of Spain so that might be the route he takes.

stable_tour.quote: He wants fast ground and conditions will be key to his chance. I think a stiff mile will really suit him and he already has some decent form in the book. We were looking to get another run into him before the Britannia, but 93 is a good mark and we've decided to keep our powder dry. He bumped into a good horse in Night Raider on his comeback at Southwell but still ran well and wasn't 100 per cent wound up for that. He's done a couple of nice pieces of work recently and there should be good improvement in him. He's a horse who runs well fresh and I hope he's a Group horse. 13-06-24

He's a lovely, big colt we bought last year. He has a very good attitude and does everything we ask of him at home. He'll be a lovely horse next year but before then he should be okay as a juvenile as everything he has done on the bridle makes me think he's a useful colt. 21-06-23

runners.comment: Lightly raced; cannot be dismissed on handicap debut/first start since leaving the Gosdens
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo, previously trained by the Gosdens (changed hands for 30,000gns in October); 0-4 but made the frame on each outing, second in 1m2f maiden at Windsor on final one last summer; has joined a useful stable and cannot be dismissed on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Recent runs underwhelming; needs to be revived by the presence of Ryan Moore in the saddle
runners.spotlight: Fine stable servant with 11 wins to his name, although recent efforts have been underwhelming; only seventh of ten at the Craven meeting here and he needs to be revived by the presence of Ryan Moore in the saddle.

quotes.race: Watch On Racing TV Handicap
quotes.quote: We played the same cards as last time here and although the ground is a bit softer today, Sterling Knight has absolutely thrived on it. I started to make a move at the three pole and the only place to go was the inside. Luckily, he had plenty in the tank to get through the gaps. When he hit the front he idled and waited for something to come upsides him again. He's done it well -- Rhys Clutterbuck, jockey.

quotes.race: Hascombe & Valiant Stud Handicap
quotes.quote: Sterling Knight is tough and durable and was entitled to run his race. It was a good performance at Windsor and he was going up 7lb, so we ran him with the penalty and 3lb off with Rhys, but he's definitely improving. He's strengthening and the handicapper can stop anything, but we hope this isn't the end of him. He's won over seven on the all-weather, but we just felt he wasn't seeing it out and he has a load of toe, so a stiff six here has really suited him. There's a good programme for three-year-old sprint handicappers and he'll have to follow it - Robin Trevor-Jones, travelling head lad.

stable_tour.quote: He's won ten times for us. We gave him a bit of a winter campaign and he ran very well twice and then we ran him in a decent race at Lingfield on Good Friday - he got a terrible draw, got stuck out the back and didn't like that. We'll now go back to turf racing more than likely. He likes some cut in the ground and is the type to pop up and win a decent handicap somewhere. 30-04-25

runners.owner: J Morley D Reynolds C Watkins & Partner
runners.comment: On a long losing run but knocking firmly at the door; makes plenty of each-way appeal
runners.spotlight: On a lengthy losing run but he's knocking firmly at the door, just edged out in a first-time tongue-strap at Lingfield (1m) four weeks ago; goes well at Newmarket and makes plenty of each-way appeal.

quotes.race: Mary Lofthouse Supporting Spinal Research Juvenile Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Juvenile Qual')(GBB)
quotes.quote: I Still Have Faith is a big baby. His biggest problem is he's full of speed and ability. We brought him to Wetherby today because I'd like to run him in the Wensleydale Hurdle here and if we take him to the track once and then bring him back a second time, he'll think he knows exactly what he's doing.  He learned plenty the whole way round. Jack said he jumped the first two then he didn't know if he got a fright or he lost concentration but he started knocking them out of the ground. His best jumps were his last three. As much as you school them at home, they'll always learn more at the races - Ben Brookhouse, trainer.

quotes.race: Turners Amateur Jockeys' Cambridgeshire (Special Rider Conditions) (Handicap)
quotes.quote: The Doncaster Legends race was the one we wanted to win with I Still Have Faith so this is just a bonus. Fern gave him a great ride and he ran on again when he got some company - Ben Brookhouse, trainer

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV 'Confined' Handicap (For Horses With No More Than One Win)
quotes.quote: I told Stefano to ride I Still Have Faith like that as he doesn't do much in front. He broke his whip a furlong out so did it well. He will go jumping and has already schooled over a fence - Ben Brookhouse, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He didn't get the trip on softer ground and a stiffer track at Cheltenham in the Triumph Hurdle trial, having won on his hurdling debut at Wetherby. We were intending to run him in the Wensleydale at Wetherby before Cheltenham but the meeting was abandoned. He's decent and loves good jumping ground. He'll have a break now and come back in the spring when we can hopefully find some good opportunities for him and rack up two or three wins. 30-11-23

runners.comment: Seems more effective on AW (3-4) than turf (1-9) and was down the field in the Spring Mile
runners.spotlight: Seems more effective on AW (3-4) than turf (1-9) and finished down the field in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (14-1) five weeks ago; now has cheekpieces to accompany the usual tongue-strap.

stable_tour.quote: It didn't quite work for him in Dubai this winter, so we brought him back earlier than planned and he was able to get his head back in front at Newcastle. He hated the ground in the Spring Mile, so you can put a line through that as he's still progressive. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Lightly raced 5yo; encouraging sixth at Newbury; may still have untapped potential
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo; made all for narrow win at Newbury (7f, good) last June and shaped encouragingly upped to 1m2f on same course on reappearance, racing freely but keeping on into sixth; today's intermediate trip could be ideal and he may still have untapped potential.

quotes.race: Grosvenor Sport Win Rewards Everyday Handicap
quotes.quote: Twisting Physics ran very well and probably needs to be stepped up to a mile. He ground it out and we'll probably aim for the Golden Mile at Goodwood before going to the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket - Oliver Cole, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Signed off 2025 with a low-key effort but previous two runs give him definite claims
runners.spotlight: Signed off 2025 with a low-key effort but he'd previously won convincingly at Haydock (good to firm) and run well when third at Kempton (AW), both over 1m; not ruled out if cherry ripe after 192 days off.

runners.comment: Good third here on final 4yo start; shaped well on return; looks ready to strike
runners.spotlight: Ended last season with a good third to Man Of La Mancha over 1m1f on this course (good to firm); shaped as if retaining all his ability when seventh of 22 in the Spring Mile at Doncaster, short of room closing stages; should be spot-on with that run behind him and looks ready to strike.

quotes.race: Ice Co Supporting Macmillan Handicap
quotes.quote: Classic Encounter would have been a very unlucky loser. We didn't want to get there too soon but I didn't want to time it as late as that. We were just in a pocket and nothing improved in front of us. Hopefully he can build on this as it was his first time over the trip - William Buick, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He was a multiple winner last year but his work has always been better than his mark and he's from a family that gets better with age. He'll be more effective on fast ground. 02-04-26

runners.comment: 1-1 on turf; has flattered to deceive last two AW starts; this drop in trip could help
runners.spotlight: Sole turf run resulted in a win here (1m2f, good) last spring; has flattered to deceive on his last two AW runs (1m4f/9.4f), fading after racing freely; today's drop back to 1m looks well worth a try and he may still be unexposed.

quotes.race: bet365 EBF "Confined" Novice Stakes (Have Run No More Than Once) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Spanish Voice likes to do things his way. He's in the Dante but we'll have to chat to Andrew about plans - Philip Robinson, owner's racing manager.

runners.comment: All four wins on AW; mark has risen steeply since his last go on turf
runners.spotlight: Four wins at Kempton between October and March but he could finish only sixth of nine there when a warm favourite four weeks ago; will need a personal best to regain the winning thread and his mark has risen steeply since his last go on turf.

runners.comment: Disappointing upped to 1m at Kempton final 3yo start but he's bred to stay;  lightly raced
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) last summer and ran well on handicap debut at Newbury (7f, good) next time; disappointing when upped to 1m at Kempton but he's certainly bred to stay; still lightly raced.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for CLASSIC ENCOUNTER who should be firing on all cylinders after a pleasing return in the Spring Mile at Doncaster.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/1 Skipper, 11/2 Man Of La Mancha,  Twisting Physics, 13/2 Spanish Voice, 7/1 Classic Encounter, 12/1 Mr Professor, 14/1 Advancing,  I Still Have Faith, 16/1 Zryan,  Cogitate,  Earl Of Rochester,  Carron,  Footwork, 18/1 Sterling Knight, 20/1 Final Night,  Slipper Time

racecards.race_name: Steve Poskitt's 60th Birthday Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C and D) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.comment: 42,000euros half-brother to winner in Malaysia; dam 5f winner; yard's first 2yo went close
runners.spotlight: April foal; 42,000euros yearling; third foal; half-brother to Malaysian 6f winner Red Warrior; dam 5f winner (RPR 84); stable's first 2yo runner of the year went close at Southwell on Wednesday.

runners.comment: Torrid run through final 2f on debut and still only beaten 2l into 4th; sets the standard
runners.spotlight: Weak 9-1 shot for his Musselburgh debut six days ago (5f, good) but he shaped with considerable promise in fourth, travelling well but having nowhere to go through the final 2f, finishing off with running left in him; should be hard to beat with that experience behind him.

runners.comment: 12,500euros half-brother to stable's useful sprinter Master Of My Fate; betting to guide
runners.spotlight: March foal; 12,500euros yearling; second foal; Soldier's Call half-brother to multiple 5f winner Master Of My Fate (including 2yo/AW; RPR 91); betting should guide as regards expectation levels.

runners.comment: £18,000 half-brother to winner in Italy; yard had two well-backed newcomers win this year
runners.spotlight: February foal; £18,000 yearling; Kodi Bear half-brother to Italian 1m 2yo winner Eternity King; dam unplaced 7f-1m2f (RPR 64); stable, who won this race with a newcomer in 2024, are 2-5 with 2yos this season and both winners were well supported; appealing newcomer.

runners.comment: Lope Y Fernandez half-brother to 6f winner Maynora (RPR 58); market instructive
runners.spotlight: April foal; third foal; Lope Y Fernandez half-brother to 6f winner Maynora (RPR 58); dam unplaced 5f-1m2f in France, half-sister to French winners Princesse De Saba (Group-placed 5f 2yo) and Aniyla (1m1f); betting to guide.

runners.comment: 50-1 and always behind on her Redcar debut 12 days ago (5f, good to firm); hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: 50-1 and always behind on her Redcar debut 12 days ago (5f, good to firm); hard to fancy.

runners.comment: 1,000gns sister to 5f AW winner Angel's Call (RPR 75); yard won both divisions last year
runners.spotlight: February foal; 1,000gns foal; sister to 5f AW winner Angel's Call (RPR 75); dam 5f 2yo winner (89), closely related to Italian 7.5f 2yo winner Lethal Kiss; stable won both divisions of the corresponding race last year but those winners had a run behind them.

runners.comment: Green and ran better than her distance beaten suggests on debut; likely improver
runners.spotlight: 28-1, green and weakened into ninth of the 11 runners on her Beverley debut 17 days ago, shaping with more encouragement than the distance beaten might suggest; stable won both divisions of this race 12 months ago, including with a filly who had been well held in the corresponding Beverley race; can do better.

racecards.verdict: Kodiak Breeze is an interesting newcomer but TAMAM STAR can gain compensation for his luckless debut run on Sunday.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/5 Tamam Star, 4/1 Kodiak Breeze, 6/1 Waiting For Archie, 7/1 Arapaho Gold, 10/1 Black Velvet Boy, 20/1 Celestial Noir, 33/1 Call Nicki, 100/1 Bea Kindly

racecards.race_name: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Hooded for 6f Salisbury debut last July when forcing a late dead-heat; off since
runners.spotlight: Hooded for Salisbury debut (6f, good to firm) last July where she raced with her head on one side virtually throughout but showed spunk to force a dead-heat; off since and it's hard to judge the merit of that muddling race but the new trip shouldn't be a problem; can give it a good shot.

quotes.race: Hot To Trot Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: When I had to get after Distant Shore, she was very brave to go for a not-so-big gap. She's got a funny old head carriage. She's not a very big filly either but she's tough - Aidan Keeley, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: She's not the biggest but is quite talented. We'd love to get some black type with her and I think we'll start back over seven furlongs. If her size doesn't hold her back, she could be quite good, but she's an unknown quantity at this stage. 01-04-26

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Signs of ability on 6f debut in September; should achieve more now upped to 7f
runners.spotlight: Out of a 1m Listed winner who was runner-up in the 1,000 Guineas; signs of ability in a valuable Haydock event on debut (6f, good; 5-1) in September, albeit just running on at one pace in the closing stages; lacks a recent run but no surprise if she does better over 7f.

runners.owner: A E Oppenheimer And Ms Emily Oppenheimer
runners.comment: Modest form in two juvenile runs (6f); this trip should suit better; market can guide
runners.spotlight: Modest form in two juvenile runs over 6f (good and heavy) but she went off shortish prices each time and her 3yo career could be more fruitful, especially over a trip that should suit; market can guide on comeback.

runners.owner: Julie & David Martin, Dan Hall & Partner
runners.comment: No impact in sole juvenile start (6f); promising 5th over 7f on AW in April; can progress
runners.spotlight: No impact at Haydock in October but she looked more of a prospect on Southwell AW (7f) last month when doing some steady late work; might find this test on the sharp side but another step forward is possible.

runners.comment: 160,000euros yearling; kept up the chase on 6f debut when 2nd to previous winner; improve
runners.spotlight: 160,000euros yearling; pedigree is a mixture of stamina and speed; unraced as 2yo but she kept up the chase against a previous winner, at Pontefract (6f, good; 7-2) last week, and looks likely to benefit from the experience and the extra furlong; good claims.

racecards.verdict: Salisbury winner Distant Shore has been off a long time and preference is for TOWN QUEEN who made a good start at Pontefract.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Town Queen, 5/2 Distant Shore, 13/2 Perfect Ruler,  Porth Eilian, 8/1 Karvala

racecards.race_name: Sky Bet Thirsk Hunt Cup Handicap

runners.comment: Good win on AW in January but three lesser runs since; last turf win was back in 2023
runners.spotlight: Newcastle win in January shows he's still capable of smart performances but three lesser runs have followed (all AW; behind some of these latest); last turf win was in 2023 so others arrive with more pressing claims.

quotes.race: BetVictor Hungerford Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I was intending to run Witch Hunter in the Great St Wilfrid but I put him in this as well as with the rain coming I thought I might not run Chindit and it might open up for him. I ran Chindit and it still opened up for him so I'm delighted.  He was unlucky not to win at the All-Weather Championships at Lingfield which I thought was his Derby. He's improved all year - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.race: Buckingham Palace Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted for William (Stobart, owner) - he rang me one day and said he'd like to buy a horse to go to Royal Ascot; we got here, 100/1, no chance, and he looked like he had no chance, sitting last, and he's gone and won. It does happen to nice people sometimes. Jamie's given him a lovely ride - I hate the way he rides, why does he keep doing that to us?! He gave Witch Hunter a super ride and the horse kind of enjoyed that. When he passes one he gets his momentum. And when they pass him, sometimes he just goes, sod it, I'll go another day. He's a very good horse on his day and I don't care what price he is - Richard Hannon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran very well at Newcastle this month, finishing on the bridle with nowhere to go. That's the way he has to be ridden, because he misses the kick, but he has so much ability that I'm sure he's going to win a big one this season, although picking the day when he'll hit the bullseye is very hard. I'd say one of those top handicaps at Royal Ascot would be his aim. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Smart at his best and back in Britain after spell in Australia; has had wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Smart at his best for William Haggas, winning a Listed race at Sandown (1m2f, good) in July 2024; campaigned solely in Australia in 2025 and well beaten on his last two starts; potentially well handicapped back in Britain for a new yard after wind surgery, but he carries obvious risks.

quotes.race: Ranvet Stakes (Group 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Al Mubhir just did too much on the way around. He just never let go - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Visit racingtv.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Everything went really smoothly and the soft ground was always going to help coming back to a mile. Al Mubhir\ relaxed well and surprised me how well he did it in the end. He's clearly a talented horse and if we keep getting things right, he's got a big future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: MansionBet Beaten By A Head Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Al Mubhir did that nicely. The jockey liked him but said he knew nothing so we might have to run him again but he was a bit spicy after the race so we'll have to see - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.comment: Progressive course winner; excellent second in strong AW handicap on Good Friday; player
runners.spotlight: 7f course winner on good to firm last summer and has done little but progress since, winning over 1m at Southwell on New Year's Day; excellent second of 14 at Newcastle (1m again) since, with reopposing Flight Plan and Apiarist in behind; should continue the good work back on turf; top of the list.

quotes.race: Always Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Handicap
quotes.quote: Blue Rc has improved with every race, really. He was such a baby as a young horse but he's growing up mentally and physically and we're really pleased with his progress. He's qualified for the All-Weather finals so we could give him a mini-break and get him ready for around that time and equally be ready on the grass - James Tate, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.Blue Rc relaxed well. Luckily there was a reasonable gallop on for what looked like it could have been a tactical affair. I was a bit stranded out in the middle and had to commit him a touch earlier than he perhaps likes - he doesn't do much in front - Rob [Hornby] was able to get on what is the most ideal part of the track but once my horse had to battle, he pulled out extra. He's progressing nicely and he'll be a better horse when he gets a proper gallop to aim at - Hector Crouch, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's won three of his five starts. He was very immature mentally and physically - he started by being upset in the stalls and was withdrawn - and then we started off by running in a hood over 6f round a bend. Gradually we've increased his trip from 6f to a mile and removed the hood as he's grown up mentally. He's grown up physically at the same time and I'd expect another step forward. His new mark of 92 demands a step forward but I'd like to think there's more in him. 09-07-25

runners.comment: Started year in good form on AW but lesser run latest; others preferred back on turf
runners.spotlight: Three fine efforts on AW to start the year but his run of good form came to a halt when well behind Blue Rc at Newcastle over Easter; acts on turf but has a much better strike-rate on AW; drawn widest.

quotes.race: Win £1M With BetMGM's Golden Goals Handicap
quotes.quote: We've always liked Apiarist and he's thriving. He's picked up a couple of nice prizes and he's progressive. He's maturing with every run and the drop back to seven furlongs today suited him as he's raced keenly in the past. I thought Rab Havlin gave him a fantastic ride. He settled nicely and he has the stamina to stay out this trip. I think he won nicely in the end. This opens up options moving forward for him. The Lincoln could be the starting place for his turf season and those big handicaps are run at a good gallop, so they should suit him - Adam Ryan, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: British EBF £100,000 Final (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Apiarist. Last time he went too quick and we took our time today. He's a big, raw horse and he's going to be a lovely three-year-old. He could be a very progressive horse - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a lovely big horse and anything he did last year was a bonus. He's grown again through the winter but has really strengthened up. I might start him off in a 7f conditions race at the Craven meeting, just in case he runs a bit fresh, and then step him up to a mile. I'm sure there are going to be some big days with him. 04-04-24

runners.comment: Two wins in 2025; fair sixth on return and could resume progression in refitted headgear
runners.spotlight: Won a Nottingham maiden (1m, good) and a Yarmouth handicap (1m1f, soft) last year; respectable sixth (Mirsky third) of 12 in 1m1f Musselburgh handicap on reappearance three weeks ago; wandered around a little under pressure there and now refitted with the cheekpieces he wore once last season; could resume his progression and much respected from a handy inside stall.

runners.owner: Fine Clarets Racing, Tp Watson & C Wood

prev_owners.owner: Fine Claret Racing,Mrs Burke & C Wood

runners.comment: 8lb lower than when winning this last year; revival isn't ruled out in new tongue-tie
runners.spotlight: Failed to build on a decent fourth at Lingfield (1m2f) in February when behind Blue Rc at Newcastle (1m) on Good Friday but the fact he made all in this race off 8lb lower last year means a revival can't be discounted, particularly as he's well drawn to attack again; tongue-tied first time.

stable_tour.quote: His season fell apart last term but he's had an operation to remove one of his testicles and is moving much better as a result. He's definitely working like he's back to his best and I'm confident he can bounce back. If the ground is decent, he'll probably go to Thirsk on Saturday for a seven-furlong conditions race and then maybe something like the Royal Hunt Cup. 11-04-25

He's a lovely colt who won on the second of his two runs last year at Newcastle in November. He strengthened up nicely over the winter and I was happy enough with his run back, again at Gosforth Park when a neck second a Listed race over a mile. He goes to the 2,000 Guineas on Saturday where the bare form is not good enough. However, he will step forward hugely for having that run under his belt as he lost 15kg last time out which is a big amount for any race. He worked very well under Danny Tudhope last week and he will go well. 07-05-23

prev_owners.owner: Julie Martin & David R Martin & Partner

runners.comment: Golden Mile winner last year; fair reappearance but ideally wants slower ground
runners.spotlight: Last year's Golden Mile win at Goodwood (strong record there) shows he's still smart on his day; respectable return to action when fifth in good conditions race over 7f here three weeks ago but he's gained the vast majority of his ten career wins on slower ground than he's likely to encounter this afternoon.

quotes.race: Coral Golden Mile (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I imagine they might not have bothered running the first day if they'd realised it was going to be so wet yesterday, but it didn't do Rhoscolyn any harm. He's a real old Goodwood specialist and this is probably the biggest race he could win down here. It's nice to see he's won it for the Horse Watchers. I think there's another handicap here for him at the end of August worth 100,000GBP over seven furlongs, so he'll probably come back for that - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap
quotes.quote: Rhoscolyn lost his mojo a bit, but he likes Goodwood and likes that ground - Dominic McFadden, part-owner.

quotes.race: World Pool Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought it went perfectly. We'd had a bit of a look at the race earlier and thought that you would want him a little bit handier round here normally, but there looked to be a good bit of pace on. I think it's really important that Rhoscolyn gets a well-run race and he got one today. David has always been adamant that you get him in a good rhythm and more often than not, that is sitting a little bit further back, because he is a bit too keen and strong in his races. But today, he has relaxed. He jumped better than he did at Beverley when the blindfold came off a bit late, but he's a lot better if the blindfold is off before the last horse goes in. And that was my fault for not reminding the jockey last time out, to be honest. It went to plan today and I couldn't be happier - Chris Dixon, of The Horse Watchers.

quotes.race: Bet At racingtv.com EBF Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Rhoscolyn is very smart to do that from stall ten. He's got a good temperament, he's laid back and you would imagine there would be more to come from him next year - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He bounced back last year, having paid the price for a good first year with us. Soft ground and seven furlongs brings out the best in him, particularly at Goodwood. He won three races from August onwards, so again he'll be starting this year with his mark right up there. He'll start back in a conditions race at Thirsk on Saturday. 19-04-24

He's been a flagbearer for us over the last three years. We bought him for a cutdown 23,000gns during Covid and he's been a revelation. He's won big races at Epsom twice, has a great record at Goodwood and has been placed at Royal Ascot. He's a top-end handicapper. Nowadays, soft ground is imperative to him having a good chance. He hasn't been running so well on ground that's been too quick for him, but he's shown time and again he can come back and win another race. He goes to Goodwood on Wednesday, provided the ground is on the soft side. He won the race last year and he's still got all his ability. 26-09-24

runners.comment: C&D win last May; creditable third of 12 on reappearance; likely to be in the mix
runners.spotlight: Hit a hot spell at the beginning of last summer, winning over C&D (good to firm) before following up at the Epsom Derby meeting (8.5f, good to soft); creditable third (Sea Force sixth) of 12 on Musselburgh reappearance (1m1f, good) three weeks ago; likely to be competitive again.

quotes.race: TrustATrader Handicap
quotes.quote: Mirsky ran well a few times last year without winning, but we always felt he had something like this in him. It maybe took us a while to get the hang of him, but he's won his last two now, which is great. The Hunt Cup would be a possibility now - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap
quotes.quote: Mirsky was second in the Clipper Logistics at the Ebor meeting last year but that's his first win for us. It was a long enough last furlong, he's a strong traveller and seems best ridden prominently - David O'Meara, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran some good races last year without winning and will do all the same races again. On his work at home, he looks like he'll take a step forward. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Has odd quirk but done well on AW in recent starts; one of two solid contenders for yard
runners.spotlight: Has looked quirky on occasions but he produced a decidedly useful effort when coming with a strong run to get up late in 8.6f Wolverhampton handicap in November; matched that form when a close third there on reappearance six weeks ago; won a fast-ground novice on turf last year (also second here on debut); one of two solid contenders for James Tate.

stable_tour.quote: He's a really nice horse and is growing up and developing all the time. It was a rough race at Sandown on Saturday when he finished sixth but I'm sure he'll  put that run behind him and show the running to be wrong. He's running over 7f at the moment but I wouldn't rule out a mile. 09-07-25

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

runners.comment: Two wins in Ireland last year but well held on recent first run for Declan Carroll
runners.spotlight: Pair of 1m wins on good ground in Ireland last summer, namely a Naas maiden (wore cheekpieces) and Curragh handicap (visored); low-mileage new recruit for Declan Carroll but he'll need to leave last month's Newmarket reappearance with a tongue-tie added (retained) well behind to play a leading role here.

quotes.race: Kwiff: Supercharged Betting Experience Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Esherann was a bit idle with me the last day in a very, very slowly run race but that was very slow as well today but the visor just helped him to concentrate a little bit - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to RacingTV.

runners.comment: In the form of life with two Musselburgh wins last month; can't discount in current mood
runners.spotlight: Last four wins at Musselburgh, including two last month, latterly producing a career-best performance to see off ten rivals over 1m on good; also went close at this course last year; a further 4lb rise demands even more but can't rule out in her current mood.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Silver Arrow Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought she'd run well. She's a C&D winner and Bellarchi likes it round here, it's her perfect set-up. She likes a bit of cut in the ground and first day back two weeks ago we went to Wolverhampton and she needed the run but she ran really well - Grant Tuer, trainer.

quotes.race: Champagne Pommery Brut Royal Gold Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Bellarchi is tough. She's in the form of her life and she felt even better going to the start than she did [at Chester] on Sunday. She's a jockey's dream - the more you get after her, the more she keeps finding - Oliver Stammers, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bellarchi has really deserved to win a race as she's been good from day one. I was disappointed she didn't win on debut at Thirsk, but she jumps and runs and has a great mind. She does her job but she's bumped into one or two along the way. She pretty much runs to her mark every time, the only time she didn't was in the Marygate and we don't know why - Grant Tuer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We keep buying her back at the sales and she keeps on winning. She's won eight times from 36 starts and earned more than £100,000, but the studs obviously think she's too small to breed off. She wears her heart on her sleeve and goes on any ground. She stays a mile but I think she's better at 7f. 04-09-25

runners.owner: C H McGie & Northumbria Leisure Ltd
runners.comment: Second off 1lb higher last May but off since a lesser run the following month; gelded
runners.spotlight: Just second outing for Geoff Harker when runner-up off 1lb higher at Haydock (1m, good) last May but never involved when dropped to 7f at York the following month and not seen since (gelded); this is a tough race to return in.

stable_tour.quote: He's a progressive three-year-old and appreciated stepping up to a mile at Haydock on Saturday when he won well. We'll see how he comes out of the race but that win should get him into the Britannia, which is a race that should suit him well. He might prefer a bit of ease in the ground. 9-06-24

runners.comment: Lightly raced new recruit for Tim Easterby but drawn wide and perhaps best watched
runners.spotlight: Off the mark in a Windsor novice (1m, good) last June; far from disgraced despite only beating one home when fifth on his handicap debut at Ascot (good to firm) last July and perhaps unsuited by soft ground when well held there in September; sold for 23,000gns in November and gelded ahead of this return for a new stable; drawn wide and probably best watched this time.

runners.comment: Only nudged up 3lb for recently Beverley success but this is a much stronger race
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who was having only his second start for this yard when clinging on over the extended 7f at Beverley (good to firm) nine days ago; only raised 3lb but this is a step up from that Class 4 and his draw isn't ideal for one who usually races close to the pace.

stable_tour.quote: He looks progressive. He bumped into one at Hamilton on his handicap debut and first run after being gelded, and then won well at Beverley last week, despite the ground and the draw - you can mark that performance up and he's a talented horse. He's quite a strong traveller and I haven't quite worked out his best trip yet. 02-07-25

prev_owners.owner: Dianne Sayer Anna Noble Arnie Flower

runners.comment: Won this in 2022 (also fourth in 2024) but recent reappearance was poor
runners.spotlight: Sprung a 66-1 surprise in this on good to firm in 2022 (also fourth in 2024); added career win number 17, as an 11yo, at Ayr (1m, good to soft) last September but arrives with something to prove after finishing tailed off behind a couple of these on his Musselburgh reappearance.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Best Odds Daily Handicap
quotes.quote: Redarna is a wonderful little horse who tries his heart out, which he certainly did there. He's just fabulous. It's quite strange that he's now winning over seven [furlongs] when it always used to be eight ? he's gone the opposite way to most horses.  There's no race for him at the final meeting at Ayr, so he'll probably go to the grass now and we'll be back to give it another go next year - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

quotes.race: Blackwell Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Redarna has run some good races here. I thought he needed soft ground so he's proved me wrong. The cheekpieces have helped him come out of the stalls as that was the best he has broke - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

quotes.race: Wemyss Bay Holiday Park Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Redarna has run some good races at five and six furlongs so I wouldn't say he was necessarily any better at this trip. The ground was probably too quick for him last time and he was just that bit sharper today - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

quotes.race: Wemyss Bay Holiday Park Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Redarna stayed on well over a stiff five furlongs at Carlisle last time and we thought bringing him here and trying him over seven furlongs we could learn a bit more about him. This is probably the right trip for him but the cut in the ground was also a help. It would be nice if we could find a suitable amateurs' race for him now, so that I can ride him! - Emma Sayer, trainer's daughter.

racecards.verdict: Steadily progressive course winner BLUE RC (nap) is preferred to last year's winner Flight Plan in a typically competitive renewal.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Sea Force, 9/2 Blue Rc, 11/2 City Of Poets, 13/2 Flight Plan, 8/1 Mirsky, 12/1 Bellarchi,  A War Eagle, 14/1 Rhoscolyn,  Dashing Darcey, 16/1 Al Mubhir, 20/1 Apiarist, 25/1 Esherann,  Accentuate, 66/1 Redarna

racecards.race_name: Sky Bet Sunday At Thirsk 31 May Book Now Handicap

runners.comment: Well on top at Newcastle latest and this consistent sort is the one to beat back on turf
runners.spotlight: 4yo who has finished out of the first two only once in eight handicap starts, gaining compensation for a pair of near-misses this year when well on top over an extended 1m4f at Newcastle 12 days ago; just as effective at 1m6f and on turf; the one to beat.

runners.comment: Good 2025, winning twice and runner-up five times, including reappearance
runners.spotlight: Had a good 2025, winning over 1m7f at Ayr (good to firm) and 2m at Chester (good); also runner-up on five other occasions, including his reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: He's a grand little staying horse. He goes on quick ground and progressed well last year. He's tough and the idea is that he could go for the Chester Cup reserve race. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Lost his way way badly over hurdles in Ireland last year and plenty to prove back on Flat
runners.spotlight: Dual Flat winner at up to 2m for Keith Dalgleish in early summer 2023; consistent in handicap hurdles in Ireland in 2024, including a 2m6f win, but lost his way badly there last year; back on the Flat for a new yard after 196 days off with a fair bit to prove.

runners.comment: Underwhelming over hurdles but ran better back on Flat latest, with form boosted
runners.spotlight: Touch disappointing over hurdles for this yard but fared better back on the Flat when fifth of 12 over 1m4f at Pontefract (good to soft) 25 days ago and three subsequent winners have emerged from that race; swaps the first-time cheekpieces he wore last time for blinkers he tried once over hurdles; his best RPR on the Flat was achieved over this trip.

runners.comment: Came good over 1m6f on AW last time and should remain competitive off 4lb higher
runners.spotlight: Positive start to his time with Bernard Llewellyn, getting off the mark in 1m6f Soutthwell handicap 17 days ago; showed promise on turf for previous yard and should remain competitive off 4lb higher.

racecards.verdict: Sir Mark Prescott's ANALOGICAL continues to make steady progress and can defy a 4lb rise for Newcastle.
racecards.betting_forecast: Evs Analogical, 4/1 Marbuzet,  Shipshape, 5/1 Ashdown Forest, 20/1 Scottish Dancer

racecards.race_name: Alison And Andrew Richardson Ruby Anniversary Handicap

prev_owners.owner: A Bintouq, C Fahy & R & S Marchant

runners.comment: Winning start for new yard over 7f here this 6f winner is only 2lb higher today
runners.spotlight: Better than ever when making a winning start for the Michael Dods stable over 7f here (good) a fortnight ago; 6f winner for previous yard last autumn so the return to sprinting shouldn't be an issue; respected off just 2lb higher.

runners.comment: 9yo who took advantage of reduced mark at Catterick last week; only up 1lb
runners.spotlight: Retains a large portion of his ability despite his advanced years and took advantage of a reduced mark at Cattterick (6f, good) ten days ago; only nudged up 1lb for that narrow success.

quotes.race: William Hill Farewell Flat Handicap
quotes.quote: Aberama Gold seems to enjoy those conditions and we're lucky to have got him really. He ended up in Goodwood on this sort of ground, he won at York before that on better ground, but these are his sort of conditions by the looks of it. I don't know if we'll run him again this year. I'm not sure he's up to Listed class. He's a very good sprint handicapper and he's had a great year. I can't imagine he's going into next year well handicapped, but on these conditions, if you handle them it's probably worth a stone. We'll probably look for valuable sprint handicaps on bottomless ground - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Stewards' Cup (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Owner Evan Sutherland said Aberama Gold would handle the ground better than most and he was right. It was very straightforward, he travelled well, the last half a furlong felt like a long way but the loose horse might have been a help. I have inherited a very good horse off Keith Dalgleish. It is his third start for me now, I can't take a great deal of credit for him. The Ayr Gold Cup will be a good target and between now and then I am not certain as there is a bit of time. He is not just a mudlark but he probably wouldn't want it rattling fast - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: That was very nice. We've not really done anything with Aberama Gold since he arrived. He ran at Ayr very quickly after coming from Keith's and even now I hardly know the horse yet. He's in the Stewards' Cup next Saturday and if he gets in, why not run? - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: Heed Your Hunch At Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Aberama Gold keeps improving and who knows when we will get to the bottom of him. He doesn't do a whole lot when he gets there but he's a nice horse. I always thought a bit of him and he probably just went a bit weak between two and three. He's versatile with ground and track - Shane Gray, jockey.

quotes.race: Shadwell Stallions Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: We had been disappointed with Aberama Gold but giving him time and a strong pace at six furlongs has paid off - Keith Dalgleish, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a great year in 2023, but not so much last year. He runs himself in and out of form and hopefully this is an 'in' year. If it is, he's well handicapped. He likes dig in the ground and won the Stewards' Cup two years ago on almost unraceable ground. 14-04-25

runners.comment: C&D win one of five in 2025; better than result at Ripon latest (second home in group)
runners.spotlight: Enthusiastic front-runner who shone for Ruth Carr in 2025, winning five 6f handicaps (including here on good to firm); encouraging seasonal return at Catterick (6f, good) last month and likely remains in better form than his subsequent Ripon ninth might suggest as he was second home on his side.

stable_tour.quote: He's a front-runner who wears his heart on his sleeve. He's really straightforward and a pleasure to have at the yard. He was a good second at Catterick on his reappearance last week. He's declared at Ripon on Thursday and we'll see what the handicapper does about the Catterick run. I don't really like to back them up too quickly on the back of a break, but he might run if the handicapper forces me to and he seems okay. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Seemed rusty on reappearance but well handicapped again if staging a revival
runners.spotlight: Started 2025 with three wins but didn't seem as forward for this year's reappearance, never threatening at Ripon 16 days ago; he'll need to have come on a bit but is nicely handicapped again if staging a revival.

runners.comment: Progressive in AW novices but well held on C&D handicap debut; hood added now
runners.spotlight: Advanced his RPR with each start in sprint novices on AW, culminating with a 6f win at Wolverhampton in February; his run of progressive form came to an abrupt halt on his C&D handicap debut (good) a fortnight ago but it's too soon to suggest he won't prove effective on turf; wears a first-time hood now.

runners.breeder: Ecurie Des Monceaux & Skymarc Farm Inc

prev_owners.owner: Dan Maltby Bloodstock Ltd & B Smart

runners.comment: Pleasing return on AW in March and excuses on turf since
runners.spotlight: Two 6f wins on fast ground last season; made a pleasing return to action at Newcastle (6f) in March and raced away from the main action when well held back on turf at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) since; not discounted.

stable_tour.quote: He's won twice this year and there's a slight suspicion he's better in a smaller field, where he can boss them. He ran well at York but it was probably too competitive for him. He's probably better at 6f than 5f, he travels a little better. 14-08-25

runners.comment: On a losing run but well handicapped as a result and should be sharper for reappearance
runners.spotlight: Hold-up sprinter and on a losing run of 21; well handicapped as a consequence and should be sharper for his Ripon reappearance 16 days ago.

runners.owner: Hard Held Partnership And Angus Racing

prev_owners.owner: Angus Racing Club & P D Niven

runners.comment: Four wins in good 2025 but no great record fresh so possibly best watched here
runners.spotlight: Four wins last year, including 6f on good to firm; mark went up as a result but showed he can still be very competitive when runner-up on AW on his penultimate outing of 2025; no great record fresh so it might be best to look elsewhere this time.

runners.comment: Six-time 5f winner but off since August 2024
runners.spotlight: All six wins over 5f; also second over 5f here (good) in August of 2024 but hasn't been seen since a poor run at Beverley later that month; previously trained by his owner; can only really watch after such a long time off.

racecards.verdict: There was an excuse (raced on the wrong side) for KATS BOB when a beaten favourite at Ripon last time and he's taken to bounce back.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Kosometsuke, 7/2 Aberama Gold, 5/1 Rock Opera, 11/2 Kats Bob, 10/1 Emperor Caradoc, 11/1 Mister Sox, 12/1 Mr Dreamseller,  Sugar Baby, 25/1 Khabib

racecards.race_name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap

prev_owners.owner: Pall Mall Partners And Sue Hopgood

runners.comment: Ended 2025 in fine form but paid the price with the handicapper; yet to get going in 2026
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 in top form, winning twice at Beverley (5f, soft) before a close fourth in Listed company at Ascot; that did her handicap mark no good and she has made no impact in two runs this year; others appeal more.

quotes.race: Eddie And Violet Smith Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's massive really. Elegant Erin is honest, genuine and loves soft ground. Everything on paper was going to set up perfectly. I entered and then declared her because there weren't many runners. The handicapper then put her up 5lb this morning and I thought, we've probably got to run and I'm glad we did. We'll try to find some black type for her next. You'd love the Beverley Bullet to have been next week, but it's not, so we'll look elsewhere. She's very sound and I don't see why she shouldn't unless a silly offer comes for her - Paul Midgley, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's an absolute sweetheart, I love her to bits. She's very honest and genuine and she's easy to train. The lack of early pace got her beaten at Pontefract last time and she has run well all year without winning, which is quite frustrating. She needs a proper end-to-end gallop over a stiff 5f. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Well handicapped on 2024 form but down the field in both runs last year; enough to prove
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; well handicapped on his 2024 form but he was only seen twice last year and finished down the field on both occasions; enough to prove back from a break.

quotes.race: Aston Martin 3YO "Dash" Handicap
quotes.quote: We thought Tatterstall had a nice chance. He hung when winning on his first run at Wolverhampton, and then at York he was only beaten about two and three-quarter lengths. This was the obvious race to come for, he likes the ground and Connor said he battled back - Chloe Dods, trainer's daughter.

stable_tour.quote: He won a 5f handicap at Glorious Goodwood on the opening day. We only had two runners there and he won. He likes a quick 5f and has won at Wolverhampton, Catterick and Epsom as well as at Goodwood. He doesn't like it soft, so our hands are tied slightly about where we could go with him, but at the moment he'll run on Thursday at Southwell in the Racing League over 5f. 28-08-24

runners.owner: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi
runners.comment: Modest strike-rate but talented for B Meehan; sold 22,000gns; interesting on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Poor strike-rate for one of his ability when trained by Brian Meehan but he can go well fresh and is starting out for David O'Meara (sold 22,000gns last October) off a dangerous mark, some 6lb lower than when third in a hot 5f handicap at York's Dante meeting last May; possible he'll have one eye on that prize but still more interesting than many.

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Toca Madera had done everything right first time, and was a little bit unlucky, but he did that well. We'll see how he comes out of it. He didn't like the ground but Kieran was very complimentary, saying he'll be better on much better ground. With rain round the corner Royal Ascot is a possibility - Brian Meehan, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Musselburgh win was decisive but on soft ground; high in weights now
runners.spotlight: Easily saw off 11 rivals at Musselburgh last month (5f, soft), form that has received some boosts since; not well drawn when down the field at Newbury two weeks ago (6f, good); mark left alone and perhaps vulnerable over 5f on a quick surface.

stable_tour.quote: The handicapper put him up 8lb for winning at Musselburgh, which I thought at the time was an overreaction to form on soft ground that he handles a lot better than most. The fact he was sent off at 14-1 at Newbury last week suggests everybody else knows his new mark is wrong, and that was how the race panned out. We'll have to look at big handicaps - perhaps he'll be better over five furlongs, because he's got loads of speed - but it will be tough for him. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Newcastle win in January (5f); not so good twice since and blinkers now added
runners.spotlight: Good handicap form as a 3yo; drew a blank last year but back to winning ways at Newcastle in January (5f; 3lb lower mark than today); two runs since haven't been so encouraging and connections now turn to blinkers.

quotes.race: Midnite Ain't Your Grandad's Bookie Handicap
quotes.quote: Vantheman is a good horse. It was his first run for a while and he did have a blow so he should come on a lot for that. He is a big boy who is probably better with a lead for a bit longer but he showed a great attitude - Shane Gray, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Well handicapped and his Beverley return was encouraging; contender back on better ground
runners.spotlight: Well handicapped on last season's best, including a York win off 4lb higher (5f, good); only midfield at Beverley on his reappearance 17 days ago (5f, good to soft) but the ground would have been slower than ideal and he travelled strongly before plugging on past a few tiring rivals in the final furlong; better expected back on a quicker surface.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: With the second winning at Epsom, it swapped the weights around a bit and it's brilliant to win at our local track. Squealer has only got one run of 100 yards and I'm not sure where we'll go next. We'll see what the handicapper does - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

quotes.race: Custom Chairs By KC Sofas Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't quite think Squealer would pick up like he did, he hit a little bit of a flat spot then he picked up very well in the end. He's got an electric turn of foot when you can get him to switch off in the first half of the race. He wants top-of-the-ground. He's been a bit unlucky a few times but now he's got his head in front I think he'll grow in confidence. He's a nice sprinter going forward - Rowan Scott, jockey.

quotes.race: Ire Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Squealer is a lovely colt who has done little wrong in his career so far. It was a good place to win today. He'll go to the Cornwallis Stakes next as there aren't many other races left this season for horses like him - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: His win at York in June meant a lot to us as it's our local course and the owners have an apartment in the old Terry's Chocolate factory, which overlooks the track. He beat Jm Jungle that day and that form looks even better now. The handicapper has got his measure a bit and he's been unlucky with his draws in recent races. He'll go back to York for the final meeting there but he needs quick ground. He won't go to Bahrain this time as he didn't travel well there last year. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Two big-field wins last summer; on a fair mark if a wind op has the desired effect
runners.spotlight: Narrowly landed big-field events at York and Goodwood last July, both for Warren Fentiman; ended the year quietly but he has had a wind op since last seen and is only 1lb higher than for the Goodwood win.

quotes.race: Coral Golden Rewards Shaker Handicap
quotes.quote: It means the absolute world, especially on Brazen Bolt, he's a really nice horse. I won on him last time at York, came here today and I thought we had a really nice chance. When the rain started coming I got a little bit worried but he showed what he can do and he's won lovely - Warren Fentiman, jockey.

quotes.race: Great Prices On bresbet.com Handicap
quotes.quote: It was fairly easy, I just jumped out of the stalls and sat with him. Brazen Bolt was happy there and we didn't complicate it. He's an older horse and knows what he's doing - Gianluca Sanna, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: His owners would like to go for the Dash at Epsom on Derby day, but in the last couple of years he might not have got in off his current handicap mark, so maybe he'll have to win or run well before then to make the cut - that'll be the plan of action. I don't see why we don't go to Goodwood again with him in the summer. He's a straightforward sprinter. He's just the sort of horse we like here, being a good horse who just needed a change of scenery, a change of regime and a bit of tender loving care. 15-04-26

runners.comment: AW win in March and two sound efforts since; others perhaps better handicapped though
runners.spotlight: A wind op last spring had a positive effect; back to winning ways with a ready Southwell win in March; both runs since have been respectable but others in the field look better handicapped.

stable_tour.quote: I think he's a Group sprinter in the making. He won his last two races on the all-weather very well and will go to Bath for a £45,000 three-year-old handicap on Sunday. If it comes up very soft he'll wait for a 0-90 at Thirsk, then he'll go for the Westow at York. 03-04-24

runners.comment: Closely matched with Equity Law on two C&D runs last summer; should give his running
runners.spotlight: Beat Equity Law over C&D last June but the tables were turned when the pair repposed here in August; two solid efforts on AW in March; should give his running.

stable_tour.quote: We paid a few quid for him and I like him. It's been a bit trial and error - he ran really well over 6f first time but he's since won well over 5f at Thirsk and ran another great race over that course and distance last week. If the winner had attacked nearer him, I think we'd have beaten him. He'll benefit from another winter on his back - when he strengthens and matures, he'll be a lot better than his handicap mark. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Two good runs for Ruth Carr this spring; up in class but should make another bold bid
runners.spotlight: Two good runs since joining Ruth Carr, fourth of 12 at Newcastle in March and third of 17 at Musselburgh three weeks ago; up in class but should give it another good go.

stable_tour.quote: He came from Des Donovan's yard and ran really well for us first time up at Newcastle and again when third at Musselburgh on Sunday. He's slightly quirky and a little bit highly strung, but he's a proper fast sprinter. 15-04-26

runners.comment: C&D winner; arrives on the back of a good Ripon third last week; more appealing than many
runners.spotlight: Conditions to suit and back to his last winning mark; two good runs this year, third of eight at Ripon last week (5f, good), and he's more appealing than many.

quotes.race: ROA Supporting Racing To School's Milestone Handicap
quotes.quote: Equity Law was down in grade but he jumped [off] the best of them all. I can't fault him. He had horses running all over him from all over the place in the final furlong, but quickened nicely, so full credit to him - Sean Kirrane, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: Equity Law was quick out of the stalls from his wide draw which was helpful and it was an easy race to ride on paper. He's obviously improved for his comeback run on soft ground at Bath - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

racecards.verdict: Toca Madera is intriguing on his stable debut but the well-handicapped SQUEALER can build on his promising return at Beverley.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/2 Kinetic Force, 6/1 American Bay, 7/1 Toca Madera,  Wheels Of Fire,  Equity Law, 8/1 Tatterstall,  Vantheman,  Squealer, 10/1 Sports Coach, 16/1 Brazen Bolt, 20/1 Elegant Erin

racecards.race_name: Sky Bet Irish Day Saturday 16th May Book Now Handicap

runners.comment: Unexposed 4yo; encouraging run at Nottingham on handicap debut; can take a step forward
runners.spotlight: Promise in three 2yo runs and again on his handicap debut at Nottingham two weeks ago, shaping as though the run might bring him on; still has potential and that wouldn't apply to many of these.

runners.comment: Back on the up since December, winning four times; shouldn't be far away if ground is okay
runners.spotlight: He had dropped a long way in the weights prior to his Wolverhampton win on Boxing Day; added further wins at Wolverhampton (twice) and Bath (1m, good) since; similar form when fourth at Nottingham two weeks ago (1m2f, good); shouldn't be far away if the ground is deemed suitable (untried on faster than good).

quotes.race: Make The Move To Midnite Handicap
quotes.quote: Law Supreme was always doing enough. Since he stepped up to a mile and a quarter he seems to find it that bit easier and Ian's horses are in great nick - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

runners.comment: Can be given a pass for latest AW run and earlier Doncaster win was a good effort
runners.spotlight: Too good for 21 rivals at Doncaster in March (1m, good to soft) in March; last of 13 at Southwell under a penalty soon after but he didn't see a lot of daylight and he can be given a pass; revival on the cards.

runners.comment: 0-8 but has C&D form and can go well fresh; one to consider off a dangerous mark
runners.spotlight: Eight-race maiden but runner-up on three occasions, including both seasonal debuts; ran well when second over C&D last July too and he needs serious respect back from 176 days off.

stable_tour.quote: He's quite a nice colt by Lightning Spear out of a Galileo mare and I've given him time. He's had quite a few entries but we weren't keen to run him on very firm ground. That's why he went to Hamilton for his debut when it was soft. You never know whether horses will like coming down the hill there, and he did get a bit lost, but then he met the rising ground and stayed on well to finish second behind Top Juggler. It was an excellent run for his first race and the winner's n ow rated 79. He's owned by the Denton Hall Racing syndicate - that and our racing club are a good way of getting people into racing without a great outlay and they enjoy it. 28-08-24

runners.comment: Two 1m wins at Ripon last summer; returns from six months off; stable run three here
runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer, both over 1m at Ripon (good and good to firm); ended that campaign with two lesser efforts; betting useful back from six months off with his trainer running three.

runners.comment: Gained 4th Beverley success nine days ago; 4lb higher in a better race but can't discount
runners.spotlight: Four of his five wins have come at Beverley, the latest nine days ago (8.5f, good to firm); 4lb higher in a stronger race but as the only last-time-out winner in the field he has to come right into the reckoning.

prev_owners.owner: Ms J Bianco, D Barker, G Wood

runners.comment: Better on AW and not at best in that sphere on last two starts; new trip today
runners.spotlight: He has won on fast turf (7f) but he is a better horse on AW; not at his best on his last two starts and now tries 1m for the first time on his 26th start.

runners.comment: On a fair mark and looks to be running herself into form; each-way shout
runners.spotlight: Only 1lb higher than for her Beverley win (8.5f, soft) last September; running herself back into form, fifth of ten at Ripon last week having fluffed the start; not out of it.

runners.owner: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor
runners.comment: 0-11 and inconsistent; likely best watched back from a break; stable run three here
runners.spotlight: 11-race maiden; ran well at Newmarket (1m1f, good) last October before a lesser effort on the AW at Southwell (1m3f) one month later; one of three runners for Tim Easterby.

racecards.verdict: Lightning Galaxy and PENSION POT could be the pair to focus on. The selection can build on his promising seasonal/handicap debut.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Law Supreme, 9/2 Sunny Orange, 6/1 Rising Force,  Lightning Galaxy,  Kiss Me My Love, 7/1 Pension Pot, 10/1 Front Gunner, 14/1 Thats My Boy Luke, 20/1 Off Spin

racecards.race_name: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Last seen when beaten 22l in a Bangor novice in November; handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Landed a 2m Worcester novice last June before winning four on the Flat between 1m2f-1m3f; last seen when beaten 22l in a Bangor novice (2m, soft) in November; has scope for further improvement in this sphere and an interesting contender on his handicap debut.

runners.comment: Bumped into an improver when second at Hereford last month.
runners.spotlight: No joy in four goes over fences and made a winning return on his handicap debut in this sphere at Plumpton (2m, good to soft) in March; bumped into an improver when second at Hereford (2m, good) last month and should be on the premises.

quotes.race: Mayo Wynne Baxter Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Desert Halo's been a bit frustrating in some respects as he's had a few niggles and isn't the easiest to train, but he's a seriously tough horse. I love him to bits because he has such a will and determination to work and to try. He'll work with anything at home and it's brilliant for him and for his owner, Joanna [Jenson], who's been so patient and understanding with him, to get the win today. - Richard Bandey, trainer.

runners.comment: Both wins over hurdles have been over C&D, the latest in September off 6lb lower.
runners.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles have been over C&D, the latest in September off 6lb lower; will have benefited from his recent pipe-opener when fourth at Market Rasen (2m,good) and should run well.

runners.comment: Got off the mark over hurdles at Warwick last May off 6lb lower.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark over hurdles at Warwick (2m, good) last May off 6lb lower; may need the run following 11 months off.

quotes.race: Logicor Warwickshire Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I thought Iolaos Du Mou was home and didn't think the second horse would finish as quick. But luck fell our way to win by a nose - he really deserved it. He had a problem with his hind feet and was feeling pain, which is why he kept having breaks. We've got it sorted now and he's been training really well. We always knew he had the ability. Tabitha [Worsley] gave him a fantastic ride. She was on him when he was second last time and that's what made us realise he can run from the front. He loved every minute of it - Stella Barclay, trainer.

quotes.race: British Horse Society Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Iolaos Du Mou will come on a lot for that. He'll go hurdling and we were worried about the ground, but everyone was - John Jarvis, part-owner.

stable_tour.quote: For a start, we all call him Pablo and he was second at Fontwell recently, but I think that will turn out to be a pretty good race and he should be winning over hurdles soon. 30-10-23

runners.owner: A Baxter, S, Sowray, K Ward
runners.comment: No joy in three runs over hurdles for Alan King; handicap/stable debut.
runners.spotlight: Sole success on the Flat came in a Sandown maiden in 2023 when trained by Alan King; no joy in three runs over hurdles; sold for 10,000gns to join new yard in October; makes handicap debut and probably best watched for now.

quotes.race: Darley British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were looking at the 1m1f handicap on this card for Westerton but we thought we'd be brave and go for this race where the prize-money is excellent. I left it to Ryan Moore and it worked out great. That's my 2,000th winner and it's great to do it for wonderful owners who have flown down from Aberdeen this morning. They're a delight to train for - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was initially disappointed by his hurdles debut at Stratford, but Tom Cannon said he blew up. He murders everything at home so we can't really stretch him and he'll come on plenty for that run. He loves jumping and I hope he'll progress well, probably kept to the sharper tracks for the time being. 25-10-24
I was very disappointed with his effort at Huntington when he didn't look keen under pressure. He may switch back to the Flat for the time being. 07-11-24

runners.breeder: Yeomanstown Ls Ltd T Coyle Flaxmanstable
runners.comment: Doubled his tally over hurdles when winning at Market Rasen in February.
runners.spotlight: Doubled his tally over hurdles when winning at Market Rasen (2m, soft) in February; has held his form in three runs since and holds place claims at least.

runners.comment: Landed a Worcester maiden last June but has been beaten in four handicaps since.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark in a Worcester maiden (2m, good) last June but has been beaten in four handicaps since; his mark continues to drop but he doesn't look ready to take advantage.

runners.comment: Won three around this time last year, latest over C&D.
runners.spotlight: Won three around this time last year, latest over C&D (good to soft); beaten four times since, the last two over fences; switches back to hurdles and worth a look in the betting.

runners.comment: Sole success came when trained in France in 2023; has had plenty of chances since.
runners.spotlight: Sole success came when trained in France in 2023; has had plenty of chances since and his mark continues to drop; blinkers replace cheekpieces and not one to have faith in.

runners.comment: Has shown little in three runs, latest when last at Catterick in January.
runners.spotlight: Has shown little in three runs, latest when last of five at Catterick (1m7f, soft) in January on handicap debut; should be capable of better however, and he's in the hands of the newly-crowned champion NH trainer.

runners.comment: Dual purpose sort who hasn't stood much racing since winning here in July 2024.
runners.spotlight: Dual purpose sort who hasn't stood much racing since winning here (2m4f, soft) in July 2024; first run in this sphere since when a faller at Hereford in December; may need further and softer conditions to be at his best.

runners.comment: 0-10 over hurdles and continues to drop in the weights.
runners.spotlight: 0-10 over hurdles and continues to drop in the weights; doesn't look ready to take advantage.

runners.comment: Sole success came at Huntingdon last May when trained by Chris Gordon.
runners.spotlight: Sole success came at Huntingdon (2m, good) last May when trained by Chris Gordon; hasn't shown anywhere near the same form since.
