stable_tour.quote: She got beaten a head at Plumpton last week when she got collared on the line by one of Anthony Honeyball's with a 10lb claimer. She made a bad mistake at the last down the back, which probably cost her the race. That was painful but it was good to see her back in form. I want to find her an ideal race, a 0-100 handicap over 2m on better ground, and fingers crossed she should be thereabouts. 26-02-25

runners.comment: Yet to score over hurdles but has finished runner-up on his last two starts.
runners.spotlight: Yet to score over hurdles but has finished runner-up on his last two starts, the latest over C&D (good to soft) in March; needs to brush up his jumping but should run well.

runners.comment: Finished last on stable debut at Stratford in March.
runners.spotlight: Landed a juvenile hurdle for Sam England last October; sold to join new yard for 1,400gns in February but finished last of ten to complete on stable debut at Stratford (2m, good) in March; hard to fancy.

stable_tour.quote: He was cheap and likes his jumping, although he was fortunate when he won at Wetherby last time. He's still got some learning to do. He's quite keen, so we put a tongue-tie on him there and he didn't jump very well - he'd jumped a lot better without it at Sedgefield, where he was allowed to make the running. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Yet to be placed from nine starts over hurdles; easy to dismiss.
runners.spotlight: Yet to be placed from nine starts over hurdles; easy to dismiss.

racecards.verdict: The one that may take all the beating here is dual C&D winner DIESEL LINE (nap). He has most to fear from Desert Halo.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/1 Saccary, 11/2 Diesel Line, 6/1 Desert Halo,  Kalkaroo, 8/1 Westerton,  Playful Fox,  Portcammon, 12/1 Spartan Times,  Auntie Maggie, 16/1 Iolaos Du Mou,  Raffles Nobu, 20/1 Ten Ten Twenty, 25/1 Crown Of India, 40/1 Genbu, 50/1 Little Soiree,  Now Then Wendy

racecards.race_name: Support The Stoke City Foundation "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)

runners.comment: Seventh on his first run for 12 months in March; step down in trip not certain to suit.
runners.spotlight: Made a promising debut in this sphere when second here (2m7f, good) in March 2025; beaten 25l when seventh of nine on his first run since back here (2m4f, soft) in March; step down in trip not certain to suit.

stable_tour.quote: A nice youngster who's waiting to go over fences. He had an issue with his hock after finishing second at Uttoxeter, which meant he was off for nearly a year. He's had his run back and is a nice horse for the future. 08-04-26

runners.breeder: Bertwood Stables & Mrs H De Soultrait
runners.comment: Novicey jumping on his hurdles debut in a Grade 2 at Kempton when eighth in February.
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in three Irish bumpers last year; sold to join current yard for £105,000 in November; novicey jumping, in at the deep end, on his hurdles debut in a Grade 2 at Kempton (2m, good to soft) when eighth of ten finishers in February; sure to have been well schooled since and could be a different proposition here.

runners.comment: His two efforts in this sphere in March leave a lot to be desired.
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in the point-to-point sphere in 2023 but his two efforts over hurdles in March leave a lot to be desired.

runners.comment: Showed up well until fading from two out on the second of two starts over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Showed up well until fading from two out on the second of two starts over hurdles; holds place claims.

runners.comment: Down the field in a couple of bumpers for Michael Keady at the end of last year.
runners.spotlight: Down the field in a couple of bumpers for Michael Keady at the end of last year; this looks to be a tall order on his hurdles/stable debut.

runners.comment: Has shown poor form in three bumpers; massive improvement required on this hurdles debut.
runners.spotlight: Has shown poor form in three bumpers; massive improvement required on this hurdles debut.

runners.comment: Won bumper at Worcester and second in a couple of similar contests; hurdles debut.
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut in a Worcester bumper in September and ran with credit when runner-up in similar events at Sedgefield and Chepstow; sure to have been well-schooled and should take plenty of beating on this first start over hurdles.

stable_tour.quote: A home-bred, he won his bumper for us at Worcester in September. We've always liked him at home and he'd done plenty in the spring, but he hadn't been away before that debut so we were a bit taken aback when he won. That was great, a real bonus, because I think he has plenty of improvement in him. He'll run under a penalty in a bumper and hopefully continue on an upward curve. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Showed little in four bumpers but may show improvement on this hurdles debut.
runners.spotlight: Showed little in four bumpers but no surprise were he to show improvement on this hurdles debut for good yard.

runners.comment: Well beaten in a couple of Ffos Las maidens over hurdles last month.
runners.spotlight: Won a small-field Irish point last February (heavy ground) but well beaten in a couple of Ffos Las maidens over hurdles last month.

racecards.verdict: This looks to be an ideal starting point over hurdles for bumper winner TRIGG from the Skelton yard. Next best is Lexington Wood.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Lexington Wood, 11/8 Trigg, 6/1 Not At That Price, 8/1 Barry Fife, 33/1 Pic N Mix,  Maestrow, 50/1 Pappariche, 66/1 Noble Don,  Pretty Darn Quick

racecards.race_name: Support The Stoke City Foundation "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)

runners.comment: Placed in two Irish points but soundly beaten on both hurdling starts
runners.spotlight: Placed in two slow-ground Irish points during the winter but soundly beaten in two hurdles races (2m3f/2m) towards end of last season; needs to take a big step forward.

runners.comment: Half-brother to smart jumper Tea Clipper and useful jumper Rathlin Rose; makes debut here
runners.spotlight: 35,000euros 3yo; tenth foal; half-brother to six winners including smart jumper Tea Clipper and useful jumper Rathlin Rose; dam useful Italian jumper; entitled to learn from this debut outing but still worth a glance in the betting.

runners.comment: Placed in Irish point debut and has also shown promise in bumper; hurdle debut today
runners.spotlight: Placed on Irish point debut in April 2025 and also showed promise in all three bumpers last season; should have a future over hurdles; considered each-way.

stable_tour.quote: He ran last week at Huntingdon and came fifth. He's running in bumpers at the moment but his point-to-point form is very strong and I'm looking forward to getting him over hurdles next season. He has a big engine but wasn't quite ready to go over hurdles this season. 12-02-26

runners.breeder: D P Topping & Miss A Argerich
runners.comment: Won maiden point on debut in March; now makes his rules debut
runners.spotlight: Won five-runner maiden point (2m4f, good to soft) by 5l debut in March; has much more on his plate on this rules debut but good market support will make him of interest.

runners.comment: Beaten favourite on both hurdling starts but probably has a big role to play here
runners.spotlight: Found shock 300-1 winner too strong on hurdle debut at Exeter (2m, heavy) in December and again a beaten favourite when only fifth of 16 over that C&D (good to soft) in March; however, he was well clear of the others on the first occasion and had excuses last time; has tongue-tie fitted today; can still do better.

runners.comment: Second in a bumper last summer but well held on both hurdling starts this year
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in good-ground Perth bumper for an Irish stable last summer but did not get seriously competitive in two novice hurdles for Stuart Edmonds towards end of last season; significant improvement required.

runners.comment: Second on both hurdling starts, albeit beaten at skinny odds last time; big player
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who made promising rules debut when close second at Wincanton (1m7f, good to soft) in February; raced too freely and was turned over and skinny odds at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) last month but drops back in trip with a hood fitted here; remains of strong interest.

runners.comment: Struggled when 25-1 for last month's rules debut at Bangor; remains best watched
runners.spotlight: Came to grief on Irish point debut in March and struggled when 25-1 for last month's rules debut at Bangor (2m, good); remains best watched.

runners.comment: Showed nothing more than minor promise on first two hurdling starts
runners.spotlight: With a top stable but showed nothing more than minor promise in two Cheptstow hurdle races (both 2m, good to soft) towards end of last season.

racecards.verdict: Olly Murphy's TAP TAP SHAMIE has a point to prove after last month's short-odds reverse but he's still the one to beat.
racecards.betting_forecast: 1/2 Tap Tap Shamie, 3/1 On The Bayou, 12/1 Chedworth Boy,  Final Surprise,  Kingofthefrontier, 25/1 Evening Tess, 33/1 Saxon Cross,  Anxious Moments, 66/1 Annual Invitation

racecards.race_name: Staffordshire Chamber Of Commerce Staffordshire Plate Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: High-class chaser in his prime but pulled up in veterans' race on stable debut
runners.spotlight: High-class chaser for Willie Mullins when on song but became inconsistent for him and, following a one-year absence, was pulled up in veterans' race for new stable in February; current ability hard to gauge.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Cotswold Chase (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Capodanno has probably (been a bit disappointing) because he showed as a novice that he was going to be a big force to be reckoned with. I don't think they got the clearest of runs with him, but they seem to be able to train him now and keep going with him. It was a good performance. It was very straightforward. It was a small field and I was going to ride my horse to suit him and luckily it worked out. He was very close with Gerri Colombe the other day and I suppose if he was here he would have been very short. If you took that look at it beforehand he was probably just overlooked a little bit - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: Dooley Insurance Group Champion Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Capodanno is a good horse and he could progress. We didn't do things right at Cheltenham, we changed tactics today and it worked. He could be a Gold Cup horse - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Get A Run For Your Money With BetVictor Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Capodanno put up a tremendous performance after that mistake at the second last. It seems he will be a much better chaser than hurdler - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Conway Piling Handicap Hurdle (Grade B)
quotes.quote: Capodanno was impressive. He's a fine big horse and looks a real chaser in the making. I think a bit of nicer ground has made a huge difference to him. He's one I think we'll be looking forward to over fences - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Monroe Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: The ground is testing and I got my own way in front, setting my own fractions. Capodanno jumped great and travelled great, I'm delighted with him. Patrick [Mullins] rode him the last day and said he'd benefit from a tongue-tie, it seemed to work - Mark Walsh, rider

stable_tour.quote: It was probably too big of an ask for him in the Betfair Chase on his first start of the season. But, look, we had a go and it didn't work out. There's no harm done, and there are plenty of other races to look forward to with him. 25-11-24

He had finished second to Bob Olinger at Punchestown prior to falling in the Grade 1 Ladbrokes Novice Chase last month. That was so uncharacteristic for him and he came home with a badly bruised shoulder, but thankfully he is fine again. He's likely to go for the Brown Advisory. 09-03-22

runners.comment: Still on workable mark after last month's Aintree fifth; player if aided by cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Took big step back in right direction when fifth at Aintree (3m1f, good to soft) three weeks ago, in race he won the previous two seasons; still on a workable mark and has a fighting chance here if first-time cheekpieces have any positive effect.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted to be able to get Cruz Control back on track - he'd completely lost his way. He ran ok in Punchestown, and Stan [Sheppard, jockey] just said to me afterwards, 'He's proper tired', and it's taken until now to get him really back on song. We mixed it up at home - took him to the beach, jumped the Aintree fences at Lambourn with him, and I'm so delighted for the owners, who are great supporters of mine. We've sweetened him up - did more slow work, gave him some away days, and the sun on his back - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control missed the ditch in the home straight the second time but otherwise he jumped pretty economically, fast and effectively. It was a good performance. He was unlucky to lose at Doncaster and he got chinned at Newcastle on another occasion but otherwise he's not done a lot wrong this season. He appears to be slow but he's such a big, long-striding horse he's covering ground - he's taking one stride to other horses' two. I've been reluctant to step him up to three miles because although he's seven he's still a frame. We've given him time to mature and I think he'll just get better and better, hopefully - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: Sportvision Stadia & Event Branding Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Cruz Control jumped much better compared to how he jumped at Ascot, where he was just running into fences. We did a load of schooling with him at home over some poles and he's tucking his front end up so much better. He's a horse that's still to do some maturing - he's got such a big frame and has been such a hollow horse - and hopefully he can go on from here. If he can jump with accuracy he could go up in trip - Tom Lacey, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control is a fine horse. Two-and-a-half miles around Cheltenham just didn't suit him and he jumped okay today, but I got a free lead. It's a cliche but we'll see the best of him over a fence - Stan Sheppard, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big, tall, angular type who has done nothing wrong, winning his bumper and scoring twice over hurdles. However, he's always been a real chaser in the making and got off the mark on his third attempt over fences at Newcastle, where I was much happier with his jumping following plenty of schooling. He followed that up with a good second at Doncaster on Saturday and the result might have been different had he been a little bit quicker over the last few fences. He'll get better in time, is constantly filling his frame and seems to handle most ground. I think he's progressive. 20-12-23

prev_owners.owner: Scea De La Vallee De L'Orne

runners.comment: Second over 2m4f here last May but returns here with quite a bit to prove; cheekpieces on
runners.spotlight: Now 5lb lower than when second for Micheal Keady here (2m4f, good) just under a year ago but both subsequent runs for Sara Bradstock were disappointing and he was well beaten in Cheltenham Festival cross-country chase on stable debut in March; now sports cheekpieces; needs to get career back on track.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: If you're not in you can't win. I'm delighted with Horantzau D'Airy and he'll continue chasing until the summer - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Punchestown's Fittest Club Sunday June 11th Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Horantzau D'airy had the experience and he handled the nicer ground. He's a fine, big horse and he will jump a fence - Paul Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: I got him last autumn after he'd broken a blood vessel or two. We ran him in the Cross Country Chase at Cheltenham as we thought it would be easier on his system and he ran okay. He made a few mistakes but the plan is the Topham. If we don't get in, he'll go to a good race at Uttoxeter shortly afterwards. He didn't quite get the trip in the National last year, but the Topham might not be far enough, so he might fall between two stalls. 01-04-26

prev_owners.owner: Rectory Road Holdings Limited & J McCauley

runners.comment: Appreciated eased in grade at Bangor six weeks ago, winning readily by 10l
runners.spotlight: Appreciated eased in grade at Bangor (3m, good to soft) six weeks ago, winning readily by 10l; contests deeper race here but probably still on workable mark after 5lb rise, and quicker ground also suits.

quotes.race: Fingal Ravens Raceday Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Joyeux Machin was one horse that got held up at the wrong time. We always thought he was a good horse and he loves nice ground. We'll see about Christmas or about Naas in January, we have to step up in grade now - James Nolan, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Slane (Pro/Am) Flat Race
quotes.quote: Barry said normally good horses get you out of trouble. The horse Joyeux Machin was tracking didn't stop and then he was locked in a little bit and he said a couple of doors closed. He said he's a good horse to get him out of trouble and he put it to bed in 100 yards. He's built on his first run, I hope. He didn't stop in Leopardstown, he was just beaten by a very good horse on the day and they were miles clear of the third. Hopefully he seems to be decent. He wouldn't show you a savage amount at home but when he went away to gallop on grass he improved every time he went away. This fella is a very relaxed, very easy individual, nothing bothers him. We'll have a talk now with the owners. He'll get an entry at Cheltenham and we'll see where we go from there - Paul Nolan, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A very consistent horse for us last term and after last month's run in the Silver Trophy at Chepstow he should go well at Haydock on November 22, when stepped up to three miles, which I think is very much his trip. I don't see why he can't run consistently well again this season. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Well held at Cheltenham Festival but big player if judged on Newbury win in December
runners.spotlight: Below form in Kim Muir at Cheltenham in March but showed career-best form when winning at Newbury (3m2f, good) just after Christmas and will be a danger to all here if back at that level in first-time cheekpieces.

quotes.race: BetVictor A Run For Your Money Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: King's Threshold had the tongue-tie on for the first time at Huntingdon and it made a big difference, so it's stayed on and helps him. The other thing is he is growing up. He's massive and it's taken him a long time to reach maturity. He's definitely going the right way and he stayed that trip well today. I wouldn't be looking to go further yet and he likes goodish, but not quick, ground - Emma Lavelle, trainer.

quotes.race: Join The 20 Club At Huntingdon Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I thought King's Threshold would keep the race. The bump happened just after the last and he's won by over a length but he hasn't helped himself, he just drifted to the right and made it harder work than he needed to. Trip has always been a question mark but I do think there's an element that he just thinks about it as well. It wouldn't surprise me if we ended up in headgear and 2m6f is probably his ideal trip - Emma Lavelle, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: A big, backwards horse who Barry [Fenton, husband and assistant] has always loved. Little by little we're getting there and I was really pleased with the way he jumped at Kempton on his chase debut. The tight track probably didn't suit but he travelled well. On slower ground and a more galloping track I think he'll win his races. 22-11-23

He had a great season last term and I was pleased with his comeback at Cheltenham. I'm not truly convinced he gets 3m1f yet and he travelled well through the race and just made a couple of small errors. I've always had the 2m6f chase at the Coral Gold Cup meeting at Newbury in mind for him and he'll head there, having come down 2lb in the handicap. 05-11-25

runners.comment: Below form during light campaign last season but not written off just yet
runners.spotlight: Early faller in February, after one-year layoff, and safely held in two major handicaps since (2m4f/2m5f); has more to prove than some of these but will be suited by the forecast good ground and is not written off just yet.

quotes.race: mallardjewellers.com Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Peaky Boy might just still be a big baby. He was ridden down on the paint, covering him up and not seeing a lot of his fences but his jumping was superb. I'm surprised he didn't travel a bit more comfortably but Nico said it was fine. I think there's an awful lot of improvement in this horse, I don't think we've seen half of him yet. He could be a good horse. I'm sure he'll get three [miles] but I don't think he needs to yet - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Citipost Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Peaky Boy is a nice horse who has a future over fences. His first run here took a bit out of him and he is a bit like that. He'll strengthen up and toughen up but will be lovely to go chasing with next season - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Favourite From The Sun Now Daily Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When we started with Peaky Boy he needed his wind tending to, but he's lovely and very laidback. Michael Scudamore went up to Scotland, so Olly (Harris, owner) kindly sent him to us. It looked like he handled the ground and I'm sure he's going to stay well. He'll stay at two and half miles for the time being and you'd like another run before we go for anything deeper. He's a horse with a big future, especially over fences - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He wasn't quite right when we first got him in the spring and we had a setback with him in the autumn, but his form tells you he's not a bad horse. He's not ready to run yet, but he has a good record around Cheltenham and we can look at three-mile handicaps when the time comes. We think he prefers better ground. 18-11-25

He won his only start in points at Borris House last March. He enjoyed a nice summer break and I gave him his rules debut in a bumper at Bangor last month when he ran a lovely race to be second of nine over 2m½f. We bumped into a very smart one on that occasion (Realisation) and had he not been there we would all be very excited as he would have been a nine-and-a-half-length winner. We will stick to bumpers this season as he is still only four and has lots of filling out to do and is not the biggest. This lovely young horse does everything we ask at home and he has a bright future judged on his pointing and bumper form. 21-11-22

runners.comment: Placed in Summer Plate last year but pulled up twice since; others are much less risky
runners.spotlight: Seemingly boosted by first-time cheekpieces when placed in Summer Plate at Market Rasen (2m5f, good) last year but looked out of sorts when pulled up twice in November and it's hard to predict whether this will be a going day.

quotes.race: Ascot Underwriting Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was good. A good start. I've never been convinced about bringing novices here the first time but Nico gave Bhaloo a wonderful, educational ride and by the time they got racing the horse's confidence was up. There's more to come and we love him - Nicky Henderson, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Visit Sri Lanka "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bhaloo was very professional and appreciated the better ground. This looks his trip. Nico De Bonville, winning jockey.

quotes.race: kcsofas.co.uk British EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bhaloo was impressive. The 2m4f was ideal as 2m was a bit sharp last time - James Bowen, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's been running in the summer because he's a top-of-the-ground horse. He finished third at Market Rasen in the Summer Plate and those are his races. We thought about going to America for the Grand National but he needed a couple of weeks off and it's done him the world of good. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Low-mileage 7yo who is 2-2 over fences; probably still has more improvement to come
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who is 2-2 over fences, the latter win gained at Sandown (3m, soft) in March; withdrawn twice with good ground deemed unsuitable since but his first two wins (one over hurdles) were gained on good; probably still has more improvement to come; must be considered.

stable_tour.quote: He's another to go chasing. He had a good season last term, winning at Doncaster in February, before being pulled up at Ayr at the end of the season. He's ready to go over fences. 21-10-25

runners.comment: 4-9 over fences after last month's small-field win; unexposed over this sort of trip
runners.spotlight: Won four-runner mares' chase at Hereford (2m5f, good) last month and is now 4-9 over fences; this race is much more competitive but she could have untapped potential over 3m.

stable_tour.quote: She has an entry in the Mares' Chase at Cheltenham, but it's about trying to give ourselves options off a mark of 124. It's quite difficult to find races off that rating. She's in at Ludlow on Wednesday in a 0-130 2m4f handicap chase,  although I suspect that wouldn't be her ideal track. I think she really wants 3m and good ground, but we're poking around trying to find something we can run in. She's also entered at Exeter on Friday in a Listed mares' chase, but we're definitely struggling with things ground-wise. I'd always thought she wanted soft or heavy going and that it wouldn't be a problem, but I was wrong - it wasn't the first time and I dare say it won't be the last. She patently couldn't handle the really deep ground last time at Sandown over 3m. 18-02-26

runners.comment: Ran quite well at Chepstow last month but competes from 6lb out of the weights here
runners.spotlight: Ex-French 8yo who was 0-5 in Britain last season; unexposed over 3m and ran quite well when fifth of six in first-time visor at Chepstow (2m3f, good to soft) last month but is effectively 2lb higher from further out of the weights here; cheekpieces refitted.

racecards.verdict: He didn't fire at the Cheltenham Festival but KING'S THRESHOLD gets the vote in the hope he can replicate his earlier Newbury form.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Calimystic, 9/2 Joyeux Machin, 11/2 Cruz Control, 7/1 Party Vibes, 8/1 King's Threshold, 14/1 Peaky Boy,  Bhaloo, 16/1 Miralago, 20/1 Capodanno,  Horantzau d'Airy

racecards.race_name: Lord Thomas Playdough Ryan Novices' Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Safely held in all three handicap hurdles then pulled up on chasing debut; tongue-tie on
runners.spotlight: Still unexposed after only nine races but he was safely held in all three handicap hurdles (2m-2m4f) then pulled up when upped to 2m7f for last month's chasing debut; needs new tongue-tie to make a big difference.

stable_tour.quote: He was first of the unraced horses in what looked a good Chepstow bumper. We'll find him something similar and make him into the best horse he can be long term. 12-11-24

runners.comment: Low-key stable debut in October; beaten when falling in December; quite a bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; made low-key stable debut in October (breathing issue reported) then looked beaten when falling on latest outing in December; returns with quite a bit to prove.

runners.comment: Unexposed over 3m but 0-6 and generally very disappointing since switched to fences
runners.spotlight: Won over hurdles on rules debut in February 2025 but disappointing since switched to chasing in the autumn (six attempts); still unexposed over this sort of trip but was beaten 40l+ over about 2m4f on both outings in March and needs to turn things around.

quotes.race: Grace And Dotty Fedora's And Feathers Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Rule Me In came highly recommended from Pat Collins and will make up into your typical Christian Williams staying chaser in time. Looking at the way he jumped you'd have to say he's going to be even nicer over a fence - Christian Williams, trainer.

runners.breeder: S C E A De Maulepaire
runners.comment: Struck form over hurdles this year and has pointing experience to call upon on chase debut
runners.spotlight: Battled well to win over hurdles at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in January and also ran well when clear second to next-time-out winner at Southwell (2m4f, good; first-time cheekpieces) in March; moves back up in trip for this chasing debut and has Irish pointing experience to call upon; high on the list.

quotes.race: Mini Golf At High Gosforth Park Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Cher Monsieur is still learning his job but he's very tough and genuine. We've got racing turning in and I've winged three out and two out but I got the last wrong. He had to fiddle and it's given the second horse half a length advantage and I think the loose horse coming to me has helped my fella go by him - Conor O'Farrell, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He was always running well, always being competitive and always being beaten single-length distances before he won last time at Newcastle. I think he's still improving. He was lucky at Newcastle as he had that loose horse to help him, but he's a horse who on nice ground, mentally and physically, is improving. He'll be out soon but wants a sound surface and that's why we went to Newcastle. We ran him three runs ago back at Ffos Las and, although he was beaten only eight lengths, at the same time we felt he was better than that, so wherever we go there'll be nice ground. 04-02-26

runners.comment: Second on chase debut in 2024 but out of form last season, after a layoff
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on chase debut in summer 2024 but returned from long absence with two disappointing hurdle runs towards end of last year and was also well beaten when back over fences in March (2m5f; first run after wind op); upped to 3m for first time under rules; needs to prove his ability remains.

runners.breeder: J D'Argentre, G D'Artentre Et Al
runners.comment: Ran quite well on chasing debut last May but out of form when last seen in winter
runners.spotlight: Won 2m4f hurdle at start of 2025 and made a fairly encouraging chase debut when third of six at Newton Abbot (2m, good) just under a year ago; returned from break with three disappointing runs in November-January, though, and has questions to answer on first attempt at 3m; hood refitted.

runners.comment: Well beaten when 33-1 for chasing debut in March; headgear switched here
runners.spotlight: Unplaced all six hurdle runs; might improve over fences at some stage but was well beaten when 33-1 for chasing debut at Bangor (3m, good) in March and could be considered only if much stronger in the betting here; swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers.

runners.breeder: Mrs Catherine Bodin & Mr Joel Bodin
runners.comment: Ran big race when third on chase/handicap debut at Fontwell in March; respected
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 6yo who ran big race when close third of five on chase/handicap debut at Fontwell (2m5f, good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) in March; moves up in trip here and his promising Irish point debut in 2024 suggests the forecast faster ground will suit; respected.

prev_owners.owner: The Boundary Stables Partnership ( C R Barber)

runners.comment: Didn't run badly over hurdles in March but was safely held in both previous chases
runners.spotlight: 0-11 under rules; didn't run badly when back over hurdles in March but was safely held in both chases last season (2m7f/3m) and has become disappointing.

runners.comment: Well treated on last spring's form but well beaten last time and now 0-24 under rules
runners.spotlight: Quite well handicapped on last spring's form but was well beaten when back on good ground at Hereford in March and is now 0-24 under rules.

runners.comment: 14-race maiden who has no worthwhile form over jumps
runners.spotlight: 14-race maiden who has no worthwhile form over jumps and was pulled up on his last two appearances; can't be recommended from out of the weights.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for CHER MONSIEUR, who ran well in his last two hurdle races and could have more improvement to come over fences.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Cher Monsieur,  Tom Desjy, 7/1 Choice Runner, 8/1 Rule Me In,  Crac De Megaudais, 14/1 New Invention, 16/1 Warner's Cross,  Jo Arengeot Bey AA,  Ultra Viers, 25/1 Butchers Bill, 50/1 Stonegate

racecards.race_name: Pirtek UK & Ireland Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Grand servant to yard but it's hard to see him being able to give weight away to these.
runners.spotlight: Grand servant to the yard with five wins in this sphere, the latest at Ascot (2m5f, soft) in December off 2lb lower; well held since and it's hard to see him being able to give weight away to these younger rivals.

quotes.race: Alpha Aggregates Handicap Hurdle (For Female Amateur Jockeys)
quotes.quote: I couldn't ask for a better horse to have my first (rules) winner on. I've looked after Whatsupwithyou ever since I started at Ben's so it's quite special really. This is my fifth season so I've looked after him for four years. It's quite nice to ride him, let alone win on him - Megan Fox, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: eventmasters.co.uk Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Whatsupwithyou is always on the go and always wants to get on with things, that's why he was ridden with a bit of patience today but he jumped his way there. David (Bass) said he knew he had plenty of horse turning in to go and win - Tom David, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse who rounded off last season with a battling win at Uttoxeter over hurdles. Prior to that he had finished second at Cheltenham, as well as other good, placed efforts. He is still on a good handicap mark (122 ) and hopefully he can go on from there. I'd like to think he will progress over hurdles. 26-10-22

runners.comment: Has shown little in four runs for current yard and needs to come further down the weights.
runners.spotlight: Both hurdles wins when trained by Willie Mullins; has shown little in four starts for current yard and needs to come further down the weights.

quotes.race: Listowel Races Supporters Club Lartigue Hurdle In Memory Of John Molyneaux (Listed Handicap)
quotes.quote: The cheekpieces helped to sharpen up Last Kingdom's jumping and helped him to travel through the race. I felt we were a little bit at sea without them at Galway. I thought they might just help to bring out a bit of improvement, and they did. He jumped much better and travelled sweeter. I committed him plenty early, but I was confident of him staying on that ground, and he did. He saw it out nicely - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Farmhouse Foods Novice Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh, jockey] said Last Kingdom has grown up a little bit since the last day. He said he jumped well and missed the last but still would have managed to win and he travelled away smoothly. He's happy on that ground and he might make into something like a Lartigue horse, he's only four - David Casey, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: Cheekpieces brought about improvement when he won the Lartigue at Listowel. That was a big step back in the right direction. 17-11-25

prev_owners.owner: T A Rahman, S Siddiqui, R Gray & Partner

runners.comment: Four-timer on his first four starts in this sphere at around 2m; 40-1 when he tried 2m4f
runners.spotlight: Completed a four-timer on his first four starts in this sphere at around 2m; held his form in defeat until weakening right out of it when 40-1 at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft) last month; the same distance is being persevered with but he's down in class and not out of this.

quotes.race: #WearAHatDay Supporting Brain Tumour Awareness Month Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was pleasantly surprised by Sir Galahad. He wasn't a bad Flat horse. When I bought him off James Ferguson he said he was a lot better than he'd been showing. He's enjoyed his jumping. He tried hard, considering he was a maiden on the Flat. He might be an above-average summer horse - Olly Murphy, trainer.

runners.comment: Continues to fall in the weights without showing any sign of taking advantage.
runners.spotlight: Continues to fall in the weights without showing any sign of taking advantage; first-time cheekpieces (retained) failed to spark him back to life when fifth of eight at Wincanton (2m4f, good) in March.

stable_tour.quote: He picked up an injury after his first run of last season at Chepstow, which put him on the back foot. He's not always been the most fluent of jumpers over fences, which is why we started him back over hurdles at Aintree, but we're hoping a clear run can help him this season. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Four of her five wins over hurdles have been been at this track.
runners.spotlight: Four of her five wins over hurdles have been at this track (three over today's distance); must overcome a lengthy absence and is 7lb higher than for her last success but she cannot he dismissed around here.

quotes.race: TCS Recruitment Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think Miss Maverick just handled the ground better than the majority in this race. She's a keen-running sort and, to be honest, I didn't have a lot left in the tank but she had the race won from a long way out and hopefully she can progress from this - James Davies, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: A cracking little mare. She was due to go to Cheltenham this month but the race has been transferred to Haydock, so she'll start back there. She'll then go on to her beloved Uttoxeter and Hexham. We tried her over fences but it didn't work out, so we'll stick to hurdles. 08-04-26

runners.owner: Feilim O' Muiri And Brendan Barrett
runners.comment: Won twice over hurdles but pulled up on his last two runs.
runners.spotlight: Made a good start over hurdles when winning twice after finishing second on his debut; the wheels have fallen off this year and he pulled up on his last two runs, latest in first-time cheekpieces (retained); a hood is now on for the first time; steps back in trip and has questions to answer.

quotes.race: Gredley Charitable Trust Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm really happy with that. El Galactico has been second, first and now first from just three runs and he's going the right way. He's getting bigger and stronger, he's a nice stamp of horse with a good temperament to go forward with. James Taylor, my head lad, rides him out every day and he's delighted with him. He's improving all the time. He could do anything, he'll get three miles with time and the trip today was fine, he travelled well and jumped well but wouldn't want any less than two and a half - Neil Mulholland, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had two runs and been second and first so he's done nothing wrong. He'll go handicapping over hurdles and will run wherever the ground is right. He's working well. He lacks experience but you'd hope his mark is okay. 12-11-25

He's had four runs, winning twice and finishing second on another occasion. He finished fifth, not beaten far, on his handicap debut last time out at Ascot, where he was stepping up in trip as well. He's a nice improving horse going forward. He's still a novice and is one of the nicer ones coming through. 04-02-26

runners.breeder: Saleh Al Homaizi & Imad Al Sagar
runners.comment: Has made the frame several times since his last win in September 2023.
runners.spotlight: Has made the frame several times since his last win in September 2023; returns from a winter break on a career-low mark and not out of this if he is ready to roll.

prev_owners.owner: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg

runners.comment: Ran poorly when eighth of nine finishers at Chepstow last month.
runners.spotlight: All five wins over hurdles have been at 2m; hasn't won since his return to action in October and ran poorly when eighth of nine finishers at Chepstow (2m3f, good to soft) last month; handicapper is at last relenting but his best chance of success in the short-term may be back at 2m.

quotes.race: PH Betts (Holdings) Ltd Silver Cup Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We might run Bluegrass in some nice handicaps on the Flat in the summer. He's fairly straightforward, he's very lazy at home. He's had a few wind operations and he runs in a tongue-tie for a reason - Stuart Edmunds, trainer.

quotes.race: Robert Case Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bluegrass has a bit of class about him but I don't know if the track really suited him. It's great that he's got his head in front and he was rated high enough to be competitive in a maiden hurdle. We'll go back handicapping after that - Stuart Edmunds, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Bluegrass never really got into his stride last day but he can improve a bit more. He's a very relaxed horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's one of those Galileo colts with a lot of speed on the dam's side. She won the Commonwealth Cup and the Sprint Cup at Haydock, but he's got the Galileo stamina. He was still green when he ran in the Zetland and you'll see a more mature horse this year. He could go to the Derrinstown, and we'll take it from there. 19-04-22

The handicapper has probably got the best of him. I'm going to step him up in trip to give him a bit of a chance as I feel we're permanently trying to chase him along over 2m. There's a race at Chepstow over 2m4f next month that he could go for. He's extremely well bred but has five screws in one fetlock joint, so he's done pretty well. I took him to run at Goodwood on the Flat last year but the ground was too quick, and he's still rated nearly 100, so there aren't really any options for him. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Below form in two runs for current yard; needs to show more.
runners.spotlight: Fair form when reaching the frame in a bumper and two maiden hurdles (all 2m) in Ireland for Gavin Cromwell last year but below that form in two runs for current yard; needs to show more.

runners.breeder: Aston Mullins Stud & S Barrow Esq
runners.comment: Won two of his first three starts over hurdles but no wins since.
runners.spotlight: Got off to a flyer when winning two of his first three starts over hurdles in 2024 but has been unable to get his head in front since; his mark continues to drop and cheekpieces are back on replacing a visor; best watched.

runners.comment: Lowly rated these days on the Flat and has shown little in three runs over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Lowly rated these days on the Flat and has shown little in three runs over hurdles; makes handicap hurdle debut up in trip and needs to show significant improvement.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Handicap
quotes.quote: Corsican Caper loves this type of ground, so he'll probably keep going through the autumn. He's not hard on himself and hopefully there's a bit of improvement in him. He'll cope with a bigger track as well and anything from a mile-six to two miles will suit him - Kevin Frost, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Another chance is given to SIR GALAHAD after a no-show in a better race at Aintree last month. The main danger is Miss Maverick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Liverpool Knight,  Sir Galahad, 6/1 Miss Maverick, 7/1 El Galactico, 8/1 Bluegrass, 9/1 Top Coeur, 10/1 Whatsupwithyou,  Crebilly, 12/1 Torrent, 14/1 Corsican Caper, 25/1 Last Kingdom

racecards.race_name: Pirtek Stoke Classic Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Would have finished closer but for being badly hampered last time when third at Fakenham.
runners.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but would have finished closer but for being badly hampered last time when third at Fakenham (2m4f, good); the step up in trip should suit and she has good claims.

runners.comment: Needs more stepping up in trip on this handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Landed three-runner Irish bumper last May; has shown ability in three runs over hurdles but needs more stepping up in trip on this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Ran his best race when beaten a short head at Bangor two weeks ago on handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: The penny is slowly starting to drop and he ran his best race when beaten a short head at Bangor (2m3f, good) two weeks ago on his handicap debut; should go close, at the least, if stepping up in trip has a positive effect; Sean Bowen rides for the first time.

stable_tour.quote: He could be a very nice horse in time. He's really quite keen and he pulled too hard in bumpers, but the hurdles have helped him settle and he's starting to grow up. He'll go to Bangor at the end of next week and we're pleased with him. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Runner-up at Stratford in October; below that form when fifth at Exeter later that month.
runners.spotlight: Showed fair form on his third hurdles start when runner-up at Stratford in October; below that form when fifth of seven at Exeter (2m7f, good to firm) on his handicap debut later that month; still early days and may show more here.

quotes.race: Athlone Handicap
quotes.quote: Cinnodin didn't do much wrong at Wetherby, he was just a bit unfortunate in the circumstances. We thought this race might cut up and we had it as a plan a month ago. I don't normally like going a mile and three quarters with a three-year-old this early on but he would get two miles tomorrow as he is an out-and-out stayer - Richard Hughes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's probably his own worst enemy. He keeps running so well and it's hard to find a four-year-old 0-80 2m race, but he'll go and win once he gets one of them with a bit of pace. 18-09-24

runners.comment: Runner-up when well backed on his handicap debut at Chepstow three weeks ago.
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in a bumper on his rules debut in November 2024 and filled the same position when well backed on his handicap debut at Chepstow (2m3f, good to soft; 6-5) three weeks ago; runs off the same mark and should go close on this step up in distance.

stable_tour.quote: He finished second in a bumper at Chepstow, then went to Fontwell and things just didn't click for him that day. It took him a while to get over that, but he's back going well and showed with that good first run that he's got the ability. He's a big horse who'll probably go straight hurdling - he knows how to gallop and jump. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Got off the mark at the sixth attempt over hurdles, at Taunton in March.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark at the sixth attempt over hurdles, at Taunton (3m, good) in March; unable to match that effort when fourth of six finishers at Wincanton (3m, good) last month off 7lb higher but should not be far away.

runners.comment: He is not progressing and made it 0-5 over hurdles when pulled up at Huntingdon in March.
runners.spotlight: He is not progressing and made it 0-5 over hurdles when pulled up at Huntingdon (3m1f, good) in March in first-time cheekpieces (retained); needs to show more.

runners.comment: Modest form in four starts over hurdles, latest when pulled up at Huntingdon.
runners.spotlight: Modest form in four starts over hurdles, latest when pulled up at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March on handicap debut; first-time tongue-tie is now fitted on this step up in trip; hard to fancy.

runners.comment: In the money but well beaten in his last three starts; cheekpieces are now applied.
runners.spotlight: In the money but well beaten in his last three starts; cheekpieces are now applied and they need to have a significant impact for him to be successful.

runners.breeder: Earl De Cordelles & Mr Robert Brard
runners.comment: Seventh of 11 finishers at Chepstow on his return three weeks ago from 12 months off.
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent 11-race maiden who finished seventh of 11 finishers at Chepstow on his return three weeks ago from 12 months off.

runners.comment: Showed much more when fourth of nine finishers up in trip at Stratford 13 days ago.
runners.spotlight: Showed much more when fourth of nine finishers up in trip at Stratford (3m2f, good) 13 days ago on his handicap debut following wind surgery; has place claims if he can repeat the dose.

runners.breeder: Patrice Vagne & Haras De Saint Voir
runners.comment: Has failed to show any notable form in four runs over hurdles, handicap debut on latest
runners.spotlight: Has failed to show any notable form in four runs over hurdles, handicap debut on latest; takes a big step up in trip but hard to fancy.

racecards.verdict: The eye is drawn to the booking of Sean Bowen who rides GOOD BOY GRIFF for the first time. Hillwalk is second choice.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Hillwalk, 7/2 Good Boy Griff, 4/1 Coolkatie, 5/1 Walkinthepresent, 9/1 Cinnodin, 14/1 Shinealight,  Donttellyamumjack,  The Kings Soldier, 25/1 Saint Vic, 33/1 Jaja Jimmy,  Inca, 50/1 Golly Gosh

racecards.race_name: QuinnBet Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Has shown solid form in at least three of his four races over fences without winning.
runners.spotlight: Has shown solid form in at least three of his four races over fences without winning; the handicapper has given him a chance on this return from a three-month break; both first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces go on and any improvement should see him go close.

stable_tour.quote: He was third in a beginners' chase at Worcester over two and a half miles last month, which was a career best and better than anything he showed over hurdles. Hopefully, he can go on and improve after a bit of a stop-start campaign last season. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Has four wins over hurdles but is still looking for his first chase success.
runners.spotlight: Has four wins over hurdles but is still looking for first chase success; has gone close on last two starts when placed; this drop back in trip may not suit as he looks a stayer in the making but he's not out of this.

quotes.race: Blood-Stock.com Full Circle Series Final Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was watching Montregard throughout the race but I kept casting my eye back to Tune In A Box and I saw him travelling everywhere. I thought Montregard would be the horse to beat and would close him down, but he didn't and the winner is a horse who keeps surprising us - Tom Lacey, trainer.

runners.comment: Got off the mark on the return to fences when a convincing winner at Southwell last month.
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner and has three wins over hurdles; got off the mark on the return to fences when a convincing winner at Southwell (2m4f, good) last month; up 7lb but looks sure to give another bold account.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Trial Novices' Hurdle (Registered As The Sharp Novices' Hurdle) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ukantango ran very well, that was a step up in grade and he ran a funny race really ? I thought he was going nowhere at the top of the hill and he was in front at the bottom of it! I don't know what we'll do next as he's had a very hard race but we're very happy - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had an issue at the end of last season and will be seen a little bit later than first anticipated. He's well handicapped over fences but wants nice ground. 24-10-24

He's hopefully going to improve for a fence and will make his start in the next few weeks on what I think is a nice mark. He jumps really well and he is one I've always been looking forward to going chasing with, so this is an exciting season for him. 01-11-23

runners.comment: Has three wins over fences but was beaten 28l when fourth at Newton Abbot four weeks ago.
runners.spotlight: Has three wins over fences but was beaten 28l when fourth of five finishers at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) four weeks ago on his return from a winter break; still 6lb higher than for his last success and others look better handicapped.

quotes.race: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You can't fault Nickelforce. It is not like he has been shirking the issue, but he has just been coming up against well-handicapped horses and stuff like that. We thought the race, and the track here, would suit him. I was half wondering if we should have gone to Sandown Park tomorrow as that race cut up, but it is good prize money here. He deserved that, and he will now probably go and have a winter holiday now as he has to have good ground and he has been busy all summer. I've always thought there could be a good handicap in him. One of my owners, who is away on holiday, wants to go to Galway with him, but he would need to go up a few pounds for that. If he could get into the Summer Plate at Market Rasen that sort of race would suit him and that would be a good target for him - Ben Case, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing To School Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Nickelforce is such a good jumper. With amateur races it's tricky but Charlie [Case, jockey] knew the horse, so that was an added bonus. He's something to look forward to - Linda Lovell, part-owner.

runners.breeder: Exors Of The Late Michael Lysaght
runners.comment: He has been pulled up on three of his last four starts; hard to fancy.
runners.spotlight: Won four times for the Skeltons but, following a good second on his stable debut here (2m4f, heavy) in December, he has been pulled up on three of his last four starts; hard to fancy.

stable_tour.quote: He ran very acceptably at Newton Abbot first time up last month over a trip that was plenty far enough. It was the first chance I'd had to get a run into him, given the ground, and I think he could be winning again soon over a slightly shorter distance. 12-11-24

He was second on his first run for us at Uttoxeter in December but he's been quite disappointing since. He's bled a couple of times and we're just trying to work him out. He ran well at Bangor last week and hopefully that's a step forward. 08-04-26

prev_owners.owner: Vincent Le Roy, L Viel & Jerome Guiheneuf

runners.comment: Ex-French where all his winning was on heavy ground; market helpful on British debut
runners.spotlight: Ex-French where all his winning was on heavy ground; difficult to assess on his British debut and the betting is probably the best guide to his chance.

runners.owner: Noel Fehily Racing Syndicate - Ski Lodge
runners.comment: Yet to get off the mark over fences in five starts; is getting expensive to follow.
runners.spotlight: Yet to get off the mark over fences in five starts; cheekpieces worn last time are retained; steps back in trip but is getting expensive to follow.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big, fine horse who won a bumper at Chepstow and was going to run again in the spring but scoped badly and then the ground went against him. He's schooled well and will go straight over hurdles. He'll probably start at two and a half miles but will get three. He could be a decent novice. 25-10-24

He was disappointing on his hurdling debut at Ffos Las but won nicely at Haydock. He picked up a little injury, which meant he missed the middle part of the season, but he was back ready to run at the start of March. The ground dried up, though, so we didn't get a chance to run him again. He's an unexposed type who is going chasing. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Steps up in trip on his chasing debut and should run well.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark over hurdles in a maiden at Exeter (2m2f, good to firm) in October and ran well when third at Ascot the following month; steps up in trip on his chasing debut and should run well.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs B Fuller, Mrs E Worth, Mrs S Rober
Mrs Fuller Mr&mrs Worth Mr&mrs Roberts

runners.comment: Won twice over fences last summer, including over C&D; won a couple of points last month.
runners.spotlight: Won twice over fences last summer, including over C&D; won a couple of points last month and looks reasonably treated on this return to fences; not out of this.

stable_tour.quote: He ran once in an Irish point-to-point, and the third has come out and won since. He should be out shortly, whether it's in a bumper or over hurdles, I'm not yet sure. We had him at the backend of last season and he goes nicely at home. He'll probably want a trip. 21-11-22

racecards.verdict: The safest option here is UKANTANGO who got off the mark over fences last time. Start Again is the main danger.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Ukantango, 4/1 Tune In A Box, 6/1 Pony Soprano,  Start Again, 7/1 Ski Lodge,  Jet Smart, 8/1 Grand Clermont, 10/1 Nickelforce, 20/1 Doyouknowwhatimean

racecards.race_name: Howden Cross Country Chase

runners.comment: Tuesday's Ladies Cup winner in excellent fettle and big shout
runners.spotlight: Prolific points' winner extended his excellent record around this course when running away with Ladies' Cup over this trip on Tuesday; stiffer task now conceding weight all-round, but in excellent fettle and big shout.

quotes.race: Kildare Hunt Club Cross Country Chase for the Ladies Perpetual Cup
quotes.quote: It was the plan all season to come here and it has worked out. I didn't think Fountain House would do it that easy, but he's a proper horse and we've had great fun with him - Ian McCarthy, trainer.

runners.comment: Second experience of the banks here, having never counted in this race last year
runners.spotlight: Gained a second chase success with a good display over 2m2f at Thurles in February (soft); well held twice since (blinkered last time) and second experience of the banks here, having never counted in this race last year.

runners.breeder: G A E C Devauzelle De Vauzelle
runners.owner: J P Lane & Emma Downey & P J Rothwell

prev_owners.owner: J P Lane & Emma Downey & P J Rothwell

runners.comment: Recent comeback run for this yard early this month was poor; plenty to find
runners.spotlight: Last win on the track came in 3m Listowel handicap chase in 2024, more recently won Tinahely open point-to-point in November; recent comeback run for this yard early this month was poor; plenty to find.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It was very heavy ground the second-last day in Fairyhouse and Galon De Vauzelle just didn't handle it. Hence he was out so wide today. I went to Cheltenham and I thought he was doing a half-speed down to the third-last and he just switched in and made a mistake at the wrong time. He did nothing wrong that day, I thought he was running a blinder. Last year Seddon beat us 10 lengths and look at what he went on to do. He was 4lb higher this year and we fitted blinkers for the first time, not because he is un-genuine, but just to sharpen him up. Going around the parade ring beforehand, he was on his 'A' game. I was very confident of a very big run. I'd love to bring him back to the UK and try him on good ground over further. It is something I have in my head. I'd love to drop him in over three and a-half miles on good ground in a good chase over there - Philip Rothwell, trainer.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Philip (Rothwell) said Galon de Vauzelle needs to be ridden half-cold and leave it as late as you can. I thought jumping the third-last he was starting to roll a bit too soon under me but he jumped super, and in fairness, he was tough to the line. The cheekpieces fired him there when I needed him - Jack Foley, jockey

runners.comment: In good form of late over conventional fences but previous banks runs poor
runners.spotlight: Veteran gained his second win over fences, and fifth in all, in 2m4f handicap at Down Royal's Christmas meeting and most recently finished a good third in 3m4f Ulster National at Downpatrick; previous two runs over this course have been poor (pulled up in this last year).

quotes.race: equuip - A Leg Up For Thoroughbred People Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: I A Connect pecked a bit at the back of second-last but he stays and probably wants further than that. I sent him on early as all he does is stay and to be fair to him he stuck his head out and battled - Jack Kennedy, rider.

quotes.race: William Hill Ireland Best Odds Guaranteed Hurdle
quotes.quote: I A Connect picked up again when the other horse came to him. He will be better over 2m4f - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was running a big race at Punchestown in a hot handicap hurdle when he got rid of Adrian Heskin at the second-last. There could be a nice race in him this season off his mark in the low 130s. 18-10-22

runners.comment: Decent Topham run latest; type who could go well here if taking to the banks
runners.spotlight: Decent sort at his best, career-best performance when close second in last season's 2m5f Topham at Aintree; very lightly raced this season, most recently running well for long way in same event before fading from last; type who could go well here if taking to the banks (won only point-to-point).

quotes.race: Randox Supporting Prostate Cancer UK Topham Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It cost me a bit of momentum I suppose [being hampered by the loose horse on the run-in], but when we got to the Elbow he ran straight and I'd say we were just beaten by a class horse. Lisnamult Lad has given me a hell of a spin. It just took me a couple of fences to trust him and to know his limits, but he was very accurate at the take offs and landings and very measured. At the last I thought we had it, but it's a long way to the line. I'm gutted that it didn't come off, but he can come back here again - Johnny Burke, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Top Price Guarantee Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lisnamult Lad is not a big horse but he's tough. I was delighted with his mark in Ireland, we were 124 but 10lb higher here. I rang the English handicapper and gave it out to him but it worked out well - Ian Donoghue, trainer.

quotes.race: Lake Isle Of Innisfree Opportunity Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lisnamult Lad is an odd sort of horse that seems to get lit up in his races. I got a nice breather into him and he hit the line hard. We will have to teach him to settle better and maybe a big track is what he wants - Ben Harvey, rider

stable_tour.quote: We knew about him in the spring; Adrian Murray had told me he was good and I'd seen him work. He won well for Adrian in a point-to-point last month and we bought him afterwards. He'll go for a bumper before maybe going hurdling straight after. 21-11-22

runners.comment: Kim Muir debut effort for new yard encouraging; can't be ruled out on banks' debut
runners.spotlight: Decent performer at his best for Willie Mullins, winning 2m4f Naas beginners' chase last season and ran well for a long way in 4m Scottish National; struggled back hurdling earlier this season before let go for 16,000gns in January; surpassed expectations (125-1) on yard debut in 3m Kim Muir at Cheltenham when beaten under 10l in first-time cheekpieces; can't be ruled out on banks' debut.

runners.comment: Below best this season and needs to be revitalised by this switch to the banks
runners.spotlight: Both chase wins have been in quite valuable 2m1f handicaps (yielding), most recently at Fairyhouse in November 2024; below best this season, however, and needs to be revitalised by this switch to the banks; ground should suit.

quotes.race: EasyFix Equine Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: The Folkes Tiara had lost his form a little but great to see him back. His jumping was unreal. Brian thought he was beaten coming to the last but he just winged it. He was brilliant - Henry de Bromhead, trainer

quotes.race: New Smart View Racecards By Racing Post Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The Folkes Tiara jumped super. Rachael was in front a lot sooner than I thought she would be but he actually jumped his way to the front so she just sat against him and took him back. He toughed it out really well. He got under the last a bit but picked up again and when the other horse came to him, he went away. This ground is key to him as he likes a bit of nice ground. He was second in this race last year and it's great to go one better. We could probably look at the two-mile handicap at the Dublin Racing Festival as he runs well here. That would be the first thing that springs to mind - Robbie Power, stable representative

stable_tour.quote: He's been a bit disappointing recently; his form has tailed off, but we'll try to rediscover it. 11-11-25

runners.comment: Just denied in recent Fairyhouse handicap; claims on earlier C&D fifth in stronger company
runners.spotlight: Off the mark chasing in 2m6f Fairyhouse handicap in November (yielding-to-soft) and better again when just denied over same C&D early this month on similar ground; in between wasn't discredited in strong renewal of PP Hogan Memorial over today's C&D (fifth to Vanillier); definite claims.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Ladies Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: He jumped like a buck. Vaureal ran well for me here last season in the Ladies National and Ian (Donoghue) said we would try this and it's worked out brilliant. It's lovely to get my first winner over fences, especially at Fairyhouse with its history, I only grew up down the road - Caragh Monaghan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Last year's winner hasn't had the ideal prep this time and likely vulnerable
runners.spotlight: Standing dish around this course and his three wins here include this race last year when beating some higher-rated rivals on good ground; light prep this season, pulled up over C&D in November and, following month, brought down before halfway in 3m6f Cheltenham cross-country contest; well beaten here on Thursday.

prev_owners.owner: Exors of the Late W S Acham

runners.comment: Tailed off on comeback run in early March in Newcastle handicap hurdle; hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Most recent of three wins came in 3m Perth handicap hurdle last summer; tailed off on comeback run in early March in Newcastle handicap hurdle; hard to fancy.

quotes.race: Brenda Anderson Memorial Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Broken Ice has been banging on the door and was entitled to win there with his chase mark. He stays well and will definitely stay further, and may even prefer slower ground - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was only sixth at Sligo the other day but was a really consistent servant prior to that and we'll mix and match it between hurdles and fences with him this season. 27-10-22

runners.comment: Some okay runs in point-to-points for new yard this season but seems an unlikely one
runners.spotlight: Won 3m Navan handicap chase on heavy ground in 2022 for Barry Connell, his sole win; some okay runs in point-to-points for new yard this season, but seems an unlikely one.

runners.comment: Classy at his best but so far unconvincing in this discipline; fifth last year
runners.spotlight: Very smart as a novice and some good runs in the Galway Plate and Munster National in 2024; generally ineffective in cross-country races since then however, reportedly burst blood vessels when fifth in this race last year, most recently (after two point-to-point wins) pulled up after never counting in 3m1f Fairyhouse hunter-chase at Easter; questions remain.

quotes.race: Jim Wilson Memorial Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Chemical Energy wants better ground and Davy [Russell] said the further he went the more he warmed up. You couldn't knock him. That's [National Hunt Chase] the type of race he'll go for, the further he goes the better he'll be. He won't have a run until then. We'll mind him and freshen him up -Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Christmas Party Race Day December 11th Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: I didn't think there was much between the two but Davy (Russell) said the ground was too good for Rodaniche. But Chemical Energy handles that ground and he jumped well. He's a grand, honest horse and runs his race every day. I think that's Shane's first ride for me. We wanted to claim off him and it's worked out well - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing "Double The Odds First Goalscorer Special" Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Chemical Energy is not a bad horse. I wasn't sure about him staying but it definitely looked like he stayed. He had a little blow so he'll definitely come on from that. We'll try and find a novice hurdle for him now. The owners are from England so I wouldn't be shocked if he ended up going over there for something. I'd say he doesn't want heavy ground - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Rainbow Communications INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Chemical Energy has a great attitude and he's the sort of horse we might just leave off for the spring. He's a real stayer too and a faster pace will suit him - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's Red Mills INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He's a nice horse and we were hoping he'd do that on his work but he will improve a lot from here - trainer Gordon Elliott.

stable_tour.quote: He got his head back in front in an open point-to-point last week. That will have done wonders for his confidence and he's going down the hunter chase route. He likes nice ground. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Cheltenham third gives prospects, may want it softer
runners.spotlight: Hasn't won since Thurles beginners' chase win in 2020 for Gordon Elliott; some okay cross-country form in recent seasons, standout run this term when third in 3m6f Cheltenham handicap in January, tame enough Exeter effort latest when ground may have been on the quick side; others preferred.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: He put in a great round of jumping, he's a nice horse and hopefully he can keep progressing from that. He ran well at Fairyhouse last time over two miles and five furlongs and the step up to three miles really suited him - Jack Kennedy, rider of Escaria Ten

quotes.race: MansionBet Faller Insurance Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Escaria Ten is a nice big horse, he's a big chaser. Whatever he does this year will be a bonus. He's still raw and Adrian said if he had winged the last he would have won easily - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's not been getting home over longer trips so we're going to try something different and bring him back to two miles five for the Plate. That's a race which could really suit him. He's got a touch of class. 19-02-23

He's a lovely old horse. He didn't win last season but he ran some big races, especially when he was fourth in the cross-country race at Cheltenham in December. The cross-country at the November meeting was his target but now it's been abandoned - it's too firm - he'll either run in the staying amateur chase at Cheltenham or in the veterans' chase they've put on instead. He's had a wind operation since his last run because he came there with every chance down the hill before stopping quite quickly. The handicapper has given him a chance now. I'd be disappointed if he couldn't win again. The cross-country race has now been moved to Trials day in January, so we can also run there. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Four-time Grade 1 chase winner seems well off the form of those days; hard to assess
runners.spotlight: Four-time Grade 1 chase winner (peaked at 167) for Joseph O'Brien but left yard after a disappointing cross-country debut in December 2024; just okay efforts back on cross-country circuit this term, most recently poor effort back over conventional fences at Wexford last month; hard to assess right now.

quotes.race: Marsh Chase (Registered As The Melling Chase) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fakir D'oudairies came home very well and we're delighted with the run. He was beaten by a good horse. You're always a bit frustrated when they don't win, but he ran very well and we're delighted with his performance. We'll see how he comes out of the race and I'll discuss it with JP and Frank [Berry, racing manager], but I don't think there's a lot for him now this season.

quotes.race: Marsh Chase (Registered As The Melling Chase) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Mark had Fakir D'Oudairies in the perfect spot throughout and he's a special horse. There was a moment when I thought the horse on his outside [Hitman] was going well but we got a good jump at the last and that sealed it for us. We'll take it race by race but he looks like he's pretty good at two and a half miles. When there's a suitable opportunity at that level and at that grade then we'll let him take our chance. I wouldn't rule out changing things but we'll see - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Ascot Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: They went a proper gallop on the ground and Fakir D'oudairies didn't travel early. He made a mess of the second last but he's very tough, there's a strong headwind up there and he stuck his head down and battled up the hill - Mark Walsh, rider.

quotes.race: Marsh Chase (Registered As The Melling Chase) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fakir D'Oudairies would have won regardless of the scrimmaging elsewhere and he deserves his day in the sun. He's been running great all season so I'm delighted he got his head in front. He had a hard race at Cheltenham in the Ryanair as they went a right good gallop and Joseph [O'Brien] has done a good job of freshening him up - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: very happy, he jumped very well. He had been schooling nicely at home and I thought he'd come on a bit for the run but down the back I was very impressed with his jumping and he toughed it out well to the line. He's very exciting - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Finesse)
quotes.quote: We didn't hang around but Fakir D'Oudairies travelled very comfortably and jumped very well. He has a good cruising speed and I didn't realise I'd won quite as far. I'd say he's probably better with a bit of juice but it's a long way from being winter ground out there and he handled it fine, so back here in the spring I'm sure he'd be fine - J J Slevin, jockey.

quotes.race: Buy Tickets Online Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Fakir D'Oudairies is hardy and a good solid horse for a race like that and he'll go further and will appreciate it softer as well - J.J. Slevin, rider

stable_tour.quote: He's been a star for us over the years and he's in great form at the moment. He is set to start his season at Cheltenham in the December Gold Cup on December 16. He seems to be well and we're looking forward to the season with him. 27-11-23

He's been a grand servant with nine wins so far, two of them have been in the Marsh Chase and he goes for a hat-trick in the race this week. His first run of the season was a good second to Galopin Des Champs, before adding another Grade 2 to his record at Thurles in January. His last run when third to Shishkin in the Grade 1 Ascot Chase was a below-par effort, but I am happy with where he is now. He's in good shape and we are looking forward to Aintree as I think he is as good as he was 12 months ago. 12-04-23

runners.breeder: Agb Agency, A Gronfier Et Al
runners.comment: Burst blood vessels on yard debut over C&D in November; plenty of time off since
runners.spotlight: Regular in cross-country races in France, though no success since September 2022; joined Peter Maher after finishing sixth in the Velka Pardubicka in October and reportedly found with blood in nostrils on yard debut when soundly beaten over C&D following month; has had plenty of time off since.

runners.breeder: Mrs M Pallot & Mr J C Pallot
runners.comment: Good point-to-point form of late; not one to rule out on return to the track
runners.spotlight: Decent novice hurdler for Willie Mullins (suited by a sound surface) but still a maiden chaser; however, comes here on the back of three point-to-point wins for Michael Mangan, having earlier chased home Fountain House over the banks at Lingstown; not one to rule out on return to the track.

quotes.race: KilbegganRaces.com Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: What Path is a big horse for around here. He loved the trip and loved the ground. He will be better when he gets a fence in front of him - Paul Townend, rider

quotes.race: Tipperary Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: What Path was lairy in front. He was entitled to win and was fresh today, he probably won snug enough at the death. He'll jump a fence - Paul Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well at Cork the other day on ground that wouldn't have been suitable. He'll be a better horse on better ground than that. 13-11-23

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Haras Des Marais
runners.comment: Dual C&D winner; big player here if getting a run; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; 2023 Grand National runner-up who has proved a good operator in the cross-country discipline in recent seasons, winning last two runnings of P P Hogan Memorial over C&D, this year beating The Goffer; subsequent third in Glenfarclas at Cheltenham was another solid run; withdrawn here on Thursday, big player here if getting a run.

quotes.race: Glenfarclas Cross Country Chase (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Full revs all the way. Credit to Vanillier. I've got [hold of] the bit in his mouth as long as I can, and he hasn't jumped as fluently as he can do, but that's down to the ground. He's 11, he's been here five times, I think, and he's only been out of here [the winner's enclosure] once - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes P.P. Hogan Memorial Cross Country Chase
quotes.quote: Vanillier has really sharpened up of late. The blinkers helped. He really enjoyed that. He's entered in the National and he has the option of the Cross Country at Cheltenham - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Randox Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was really nice. I probably found myself too far back, but Vanillier is a really strong stayer and he stayed on all the way to the line - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: Liam & Valerie Brennan Florida Pearl Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: On the whole Vanillier jumped very well. I would have liked it if something had joined him earlier in the race just to force a bit more pace into it, but he's just a dour stayer. I walked the track beforehand and it's nice, safe ground. Hopefully he'll be okay in the morning. He's a big, lazy type of horse who wants to get his toe in. There's the two staying novice chases at Leopardstown and Limerick this Christmas. He'll get an entry for both and, ground depending, a decision will be made closer to the time. He's a big horse and we want to mind him in terms of the ground - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Registered as The Spa Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
