quotes.quote: I watched the race with Jonathan (Moore, injured regular rider) and he said the last day he couldn't even get him to line up at Leopardstown and here he had his ears pricked and he bounced out the gate. It's tough for Johnny, but the good thing is he'll be back on these horses and they're young horses so hopefully they have a bright future. Vanillier is a proper staying chaser in the making, to what level he can go I'm not sure but he's a lovely big horse - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He's a three mile chaser for next season. I didn't think he'd be able to win a maiden hurdle up until recently but he's improved a lot. He's entitled to step up in grade after that - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He took to cross-country chases well last season, finishing third behind Stumptown at the festival, and the plan is to run in the cross-country race at Cheltenham's November meeting. He'll be aimed at the festival again in March. He's been a great horse for us and has been unlucky in big races on occasions. 04-11-25
He has an entry in the cross-country at Cheltenham on Friday and we're going to give that a shot. Hopefully that will spark him up. I wouldn't rule out going back to the Grand National. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Thursday's La Touche winner, massive respect if turning out again; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; five-time chase winner for Joseph O'Brien, including the La Touche over this course last year (4m1f); prepped recently over hurdles before repeating La Touche win here on Thursday where he had The Goffer back in third (beaten 1.25l); unlikely to make a quick return but massive respect if doing so.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications La Touche Cup Cross Country Chase
quotes.quote: Joseph [O'Brien, former trainer] and his team had everything done with Busselton. We didn't have to do any schooling with him. If you gave me money to go out and get a La Touche winner, Busselton wouldn't be one of them. He's only about 15.3, but then Darragh [O'Keeffe] sits into him so well and they're a great combination. We'll try to do it all again next year. I think there's still more in him. He's still only nine - Enda Bolger, trainer.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications La Touche Cup Cross Country Chase
quotes.quote: The La Touche is a special race and we're delighted to win it. It was our first runner in it and even just to have a horse for the banks is special. JJ [Slevin] gave Busselton a fantastic ride. I think the top of the ground is the key to him. He has won under all codes and will win again under most hopefully, but today is really the special day - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Guinness Kerry National Handicap Chase (Grade A)
quotes.quote: Busselton is as hard as nails. He jumps, stays, seems to go on any ground and he would have kept battling. It looked like a great performance. He has been on the go for over a year but he's a very honest horse - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Ireland Home Of The Acca Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Busselton is as tough as nails. He was flat out the whole way and he was very genuine, he has picked up and galloped home. He's just not very quick - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Irish EBF Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Busselton is a great, likeable horse. He was having a bit of a look around in front but it was a good performance and he jumped well in the main barring being slow at one. Taking a lead would have been a help but I wanted a good, honest test for him because he's a stayer. He might be okay over a strongly-run 2m2f as well. The 10lb allowance as a 4yo is a big help and we're delighted to get another win out of him - JJ Slevin, rider

stable_tour.quote: He returned from six months off when fourth in the Lismullen Hurdle last weekend and I was very happy with the run. He came out of it in good shape. We will look at something like the Paddy Power Chase at Leopardstown for him now and he'll go down that staying handicap chase route. 27-11-23

He's a grand campaigner who has six wins to his name including the Kerry National at Listowel in the autumn. He ran in the Irish National earlier this week where the ground went against him and he was subsequently pulled up. He is better on spring ground and anything too heavy doesn't see him at his best. He's not one to give up on when granted better ground. 12-04-23

runners.comment: Third to Busselton in Thursday's la Touche, big player if turning out again; reserve
runners.spotlight: Third reserve; second to Vanillier in P P Hogan Memorial over C&D in February and most recently a close third (beaten 1.25l) to Busselton in 4m1f La Touche here on Thursday; big player if turning out again.

quotes.race: Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Goffer keeps on galloping as he showed there and with that in mind the obvious place to go with him will be the Irish National at Fairyhouse over the Easter holiday as long as he comes out of this race in good heart - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bulmers Leopardstown Handicap Chase (Grade A)
quotes.quote: We thought The Goffer had a chance on the drying ground. He probably wants a bit further but he jumped great and galloped the whole way to the line. We're very happy. Davy was great on him. I told him to go out and take every chance, don't leave the paint. In those big handicaps that's what you have to do. We'll look at all those long distance races and he could be an Irish National horse - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Markaye Contracts Ltd Michael Purcell Memorial Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: The Goffer found plenty and if something was alongside him it might have brought him on a bit more but he did it well here off a nice gallop. He's a big horse and he will improve - Jordan Gainford, rider.

quotes.race: Kilberry Pub & Kitchen Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: The Goffer had been working well. He's an improving horse and he jumped great - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I was thrilled with his run behind Vanillier the other day at Punchestown and that'll set him up nicely for a crack at the Cross Country Chase at Cheltenham.  09-02-26

racecards.verdict: Tuesday's winner Fountain House has to be respected, but a chance is taken on LISNAMULT LAD taking to this discipline
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Fountain House, 9/2 Chemical Energy, 11/2 Lisnamult Lad, 8/1 What Path, 10/1 Vaureal, 12/1 Olympic Man,  Fakir d'Oudairies, 14/1 The Folkes Tiara,  Escaria Ten, 16/1 Quornofamonday,  I A Connect,  Gentleman De Reve, 20/1 Vital Island, 25/1 Galon De Vauzelle, 33/1 Call The Tune, 50/1 Broken Ice

racecards.race_name: DAR Golf Handicap Chase

runners.comment: Fairyhouse specialist but no trace of form this season; hard to be confident in
runners.spotlight: All three chase wins have been at Fairyhouse, notably the 2024 Irish National; well below best this season however, most recently at same venue in Grade 3 Bobbyjo Chase in February; hard to be confident in and wants softer ground.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Irish Grand National Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: It's a massive race to win and that was a good performance. It's unbelievable really. I thought they didn't go quick and I was comfortable where I was, we were just pottering away. I gave the fourth-last a right belt and I thought that'd knock the stuffing out of Intense Raffles. He stuck out his head and galloped all the way to the line - J J Slevin, rider. I'm buzzing. That's every bit as much as a thrill [as 2012] for different reasons. He came here as second favourite and we had huge confidence in him. He ran just like we expected he would. It's a very satisfying feeling - Thomas Gibney, trainer.

quotes.race: Book Your Advanced Tickets Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: It's easy to get carried away in a three-runner race. Good Time Jonny is probably much better dropped out in a big field and Henry's mare hadn't been in great form. If we didn't win it we would have been very disappointed but, at the same time, we couldn't have been happier with the way Intense Raffles did it. We could have gone for the novice race tomorrow in Naas, but we decided to come here today to test out the distance. We wanted to see if he'd stay and today it looks like he'd get every bit of it, so there is a good chance he'll come back on Easter Monday (for the Irish National) - Thomas Gibney, trainer.

runners.comment: 2024 Thyestes winner hard to fancy on evidence of comeback run; wants it softer too
runners.spotlight: Thyestes winner of 2024 for Henry de Bromhead (off 144) went on to finish decent sixth in Grand National but long absent until faller at the last after never featuring on yard debut in 3m bet365 Premier Chase at Kelso in February; best form on heavy so obvious ground concerns.

quotes.race: Goffs Thyestes Handicap Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: The stewards have just asked me for the reason for Ain't That A Shame's improvement in form, but we genuinely we didn't know (at Navan) and were very disappointed - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Holden Fleet Management Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Ain't That A Shame deserved to win. It was a good performance and I couldn't be happier. He handles those conditions and it was a perfect race for him - Rachael Blackmore, rider.

quotes.race: I.N.H. Stallion Owners EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Ain't That A Shame jumps and stays well, is a scopey big horse who has taken time but it is nice to see him come to himself. We'll look at the festivals and the three mile options, maybe the handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse. I'm looking forward to getting him over a fence next year - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a bit disappointing in the Troytown for whatever reason. We'll get him checked out and see if anything shows up. That wasn't his true form. 20-11-23

He has run two big races in defeat this season with a head second in the Munster National and a good fourth to Real Steel in a big handicap at the Leopardstown's Christmas meeting. His big target this season is the Grand National, which I think should suit him as he stays 3m well and gives the impression he'll get further. He could have a run beforehand but it wouldn't be a problem if he went straight to Aintree. 01-03-23

runners.comment: Irish National also-ran; drops back in grade but ground could prove on the lively side
runners.spotlight: Better than ever this season, recording back-to-back wins at Fairyhouse, including 3m6f Porterstown Chase, before narrowly denied a hat-trick in 3m Thyestes at Gowran; has disappointed both starts since however, pulled up after never counting in 3m5f Irish National last time; drops back in grade here but ground could prove on the lively side.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Porterstown Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Jumping the last I was confident, but the horse must have been idle because when he got to him Better Times Ahead picked up again. It was great to get a pot like that with him because he's been a bit fragile. He was hampered at the third-last and was shuffled back a bit. There was a good strong gallop all the way and it helped. It would be nice to think he could go for the Irish National he's after winning here twice now, so he seems to handle the course - Robert Tyner, trainer.

quotes.race: Christmas Party Jackpot Jingle At Fairyhouse 13th December Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Better Times Ahead is a grand old horse and loves that ground. He got a good ride from Mark and stayed on well. He's rated a bit lower over hurdles and he'll tip away between both codes. He enjoys the ground and that's the main thing - Frank Berry, racing manager

runners.comment: Ulster National winner for whom Irish National probably came too soon; respected
runners.spotlight: Much improved since going handicapping, just denied at Down Royal before decisive 3m5f success in Ulster National at Downpatrick in late March, winning going away; didn't count just eight days later when tough ask in 3m5f Irish National but don't rule out back in grade here and handles this quicker ground.

quotes.race: Randox Ulster National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: He jumped brilliantly, Born Braver is a typical Court Cave as he probably doesn't want good ground, he just wants a bit of an ease in it. He had perfect conditions today and the trip suited. I had a good run around, had the perfect position and knew when I jumped the last and asked him he would respond. I just didn't want to get stuck into him too soon. We had been hoping to scrape in at the bottom of the Irish National weights and while that didn't work out, thankfully he got this - Keith Donoghue, jockey

runners.comment: Kim Muir also-ran has a bit to prove right now but rider's claim a positive
runners.spotlight: Career highlight when winning last season's Kim Muir at Cheltenham (3m2f, good-to-soft); two prep runs over hurdles this season before attempting repeat Cheltenham bid but none too fluent and never landed a blow on quicker ground; bit to prove right now but rider's claim a positive.

quotes.race: Fulke Walwyn Kim Muir Challenge Cup Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Spon By Thames Materials) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Daily Present is a stayer, but he was too free in the race last year. The ride that chap gave him was great as he never left the inside. He just had to try and keep on filling him. He was brilliant on him. I definitely thought Johnnywho was coming back, but I knew my lad would stay, however when I saw Derek (O'Connor) rallying I thought we were done. In fairness to this lad the last race he won at Down Royal he looked like he was going to be fourth, but he stayed on as if he wanted four miles. We are just so delighted. That was the lad's first ride in England. He is a super rider that is loaded with talent, and what a pair of hands he has. I just thought he was super on him - Paul Nolan, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Daily Present looks a fair horse, Sean thinks he's a proper one and I hope he's right. We'll take a look at Fairyhouse and Punchestown. He's only five and strengthening, and he'll probably get one more run - Paul Nolan, trainer

quotes.race: Fairyhouse Supporting Treo Eile Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Daily Present had a lovely run at Naas where he galloped through the line. Sean said he had loads left today. He's a light-framed horse so we won't run too often. He'll have to step up now - Paul Nolan, trainer

runners.comment: Respectable effort over wholly inadequate trip latest; new trip today
runners.spotlight: Won here over 2m4f last season (soft) and touched off at Fairyhouse over 3m1f; unable to exploit much lower hurdles mark this term before respectable fourth back chasing on latest over an inadequate 2m at Gowran; tries a new trip here.

quotes.race: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Folly Master is a lovely horse, very straightforward and genuine. He wants proper soft ground and maybe another mile. He could be one for a bigger day in the spring - Tom Dreaper, trainer.

quotes.race: Leugh Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Folly Master is a lovely horse and is getting better for racing. He is a staying chaser for the future - Tom Dreaper, trainer.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie La Grugerie
runners.comment: Progressive handicapper; could be open to more improvement at this extreme trip
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in 3m1f handicap on this card last season and progressing well this season, recording third handicap win when scoring over 3m2f at Doncaster with runaway success in valuable 3-finisher contest in late February in first-time cheekpieces; plausible he could be open to more improvement at this extreme trip.

quotes.race: DJB Cleaning Handicap Chase (For The Harwell Trophy)
quotes.quote: We always thought Jasmin De Grugy would be a three-mile chaser but it's just been about finding the right opportunities for him. The ground was probably soft enough for him here but he won quite well in the end. This might be his ceiling but it's hard to know and he's eligible to run in better races now. It's worth having a go at a nice valuable novice handicap - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

quotes.race: Southwell Golf Club Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: When we had schooled Jasmin De Grugy over fences he was a little bit sticky to start, but to be fair to Anthony and his team they've done a super job getting him jumping well and that's paid off today - Richie McLernon, rider.

quotes.race: Peter Bowen Racing Club Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It's the perfect scenario really because the handicapper can't quite get to grips with Jasmin De Grugy. Being one of JPs, he was a nice, expensive store horse. Things didn't really click for him as a young horse, but he's improved with racing. He was a bit of a goon jumping hurdles early on, but he's improved with every run and was so smooth there. Every time he's got near the front he's lugged across a bit, so hopefully he can keep ahead of the assessor. I think we'll put him away and ideally work towards novice handicap chasing over three miles in the autumn - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He really improved last season and won three times in May. He'll go chasing and very much shapes like a three-miler. He should still have scope off his mark and could be a smart staying chaser. 14-11-24

runners.comment: No show on comeback run in Irish National; hard to be confident in although ground to suit
runners.spotlight: Sole win over fences came in 3m Mayo National in 2024 on good ground; good second in Galway Plate that summer but last year's form was poor; pulled up after never counting on return from long absence in Irish National; hard to be confident in although has ground to suit.

quotes.race: McHale Mayo National Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Duffle Coat has finished second a lot lately, so it's great for him to win a big pot. I've been reeled in on him before when I've sent him for home, so I waited as long as I could and the better ground helped him to see it out well this time - Sam Ewing, jockey.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Registered As The Prestbury Juvenile Hurdle) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was flat to the boards the whole way. To be fair Duffle Coat is really tenacious and a little terrier. From the top of the hill I gave him a little squeeze and he picked up underneath me. I wasn't overly concerned as I thought we had gone quick on genuine soft ground. His stamina is his forte - Robbie Power, jockey.

quotes.race: gowranpark.ie 3YO Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jack said it turned into a bit of a sprint and it didn't suit him. A faster gallop would have suited him. He won well at the line and he keeps winning so that's all that matters. There's a winners' of two at Down Royal and Punchestown and there's a Listed race at Wetherby as well - Gordon Elliott, trainer

quotes.race: Sanctuary Synthetics 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Duffle Coat had never been on grass and it's the first time he has worked properly. He was good. He has to be smart because he had nothing done. Keith said he'll improve stones - Gordon Elliott, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's run some huge races in big handicaps over the years but has just lost his way a little of late, so he's going to go down the cross-country route this season. 26-10-25

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Cap Orne & Yannick Fouin
runners.comment: Largely struggled in big handicaps this season; opposable
runners.spotlight: Dual chase winner last term and good third to Daily Present in 3m2f Kim Muir at Cheltenham; has struggled in big handicaps this season, exception a never-nearer remote third in Leinster National; never really recovered from bad early blunder when pulled up in Irish National on latest; others look more reliable.

stable_tour.quote: Hopefully he can pick up a nice handicap at some stage this season. He ran well enough in the Kim Muir last season and some of those big handicap chases will be on his agenda over the next few months. Hopefully there's more to come as he's had only 12 runs. 17-11-25

runners.comment: 0-7 chasing and seemingly tough task here upped in trip
runners.spotlight: Three-time hurdles winner is 0-7 chasing, pick of this season's form when placed in 3m1f Carlisle handicap in February; didn't get home on softer ground  at Uttoxeter on latest; tough task here upped in trip.

quotes.race: Racing UK Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Saint Davy has been a bit unfortunate, he's been off for a long time and we couldn't run in a novice handicap chase so we've had to stay hurdling. He wasn't good enough in the Grade 1 at Aintree but he's a grand horse. He's a chaser in the making really and he doesn't mind the soft ground. I'm not sure what we'll do with him next - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Bet Bundles Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a nice performance and Saint Davy lost a shoe over the far side. We all dream about big things, if you don't then there's no point training racehorses. We think he's a nice horse, he's done nothing wrong so far - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing Again Thursday 20th October Open National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1) (Go North Jodami Qual) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Saint Davy is probably not really a bumper horse and it didn't help that they went slow. It was nearly a year since he ran [in a point-to-point] and it was all about giving him confidence - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, rider.

stable_tour.quote: His first run last season in the Grade 2 won by Handstands at Sandown was a good one and we thought he'd improve massively for the run, but he got a shocker of a fall at Ffos Las next time and I don't think you saw the real Saint Davy after that. He's still a novice, so we'll probably take a similar route. Soft ground is what he really needs and he's an out-and-out galloper. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Last year's winner hasn't hit form this season; still 7lb above last year's mark
runners.spotlight: Came good over fences in this race last year with 15l win (raised 14lb) on yielding; four runs this term in admittedly hot handicaps have been disappointing, including remote fourth in Leinster National, most recently pulled up after racing prominently for long way in Irish National; handicapper relenting but still 7lb above last year's mark.

quotes.race: Oaklodgelandscapes.ie Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Shanbally Kid is a bit like his owner, he likes to be on his own. He gets a bit upset when he's near horses. I said to Danny keep him on his own as much as you can but I didn't realise Danny had that plan in mind. He's probably a National horse for the future. He's a novice in England for next season as well because the English season ended last week - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was in his comfort zone the whole way when he stepped up in trip in a handicap chase [3m7½f] at Punchestown at the end of last season. Danny [Mullins] gave him a good ride, took his time and kept him wide. There is more to come this season now he's got his jumping together, and all the staying handicap chases will be on his radar. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Porterstown second was good but major improvement needed on recent efforts
runners.spotlight: Bumper and two-time hurdle winner; 0-15 chasing but has run well in defeat at times, most notably over 3m6f at the Cheltenham Festival in 2025 and when a neck second to Better Times Ahead in the Porterstown at Fairyhouse in November (yielding); out of sorts in four runs since however so big upturn in performance required but 13lb better off with Better Times Ahead now, plus rider's claim.

quotes.race: BetVictor Proud To Support Irish Racing Irish EBF Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Will Do is better the further he goes and that ground is probably as good as he wants it - Jack Kennedy, rider.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Will Do is a good stayer. He loves galloping and he showed that when he won his bumper at Cork and although he looked beaten a few times there, he still managed to win it. He's a nice horse going forward and hopefully he will win plenty of races - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Jim Ryan Racecourse Services (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: It's nice to get one under the belt in bumpers. He is a good staying type and would strike you more as a staying chaser in time. John Gleeson - winning rider.

stable_tour.quote: You'd imagine something like the Troytown at Navan will be on his radar now. He'll come on plenty from his run in the Munster National and all he does is gallop and stay. He could do with slickening up his jumping. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Hasn't convinced since January return over both hurdles and fences
runners.spotlight: Six-time chase winner (including here) but not since May 2024; missed 2025 entirely and hasn't convinced since January return over both hurdles and fences (dropped 6lbs).

quotes.race: Tote Killarney National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Brideswell Lad travelled well throughout, J.J. was very pleased with him and gave him a brilliant ride. That was nice to get at the start of the new season but it might be the end for him for a while. He has been on the go a while so might get a break and the Kerry National would be in mind - Seamus Neville, trainer.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Brideswell Lad got a very heavy fall at Listowel and took a long time to get over it, but we felt we were getting there. He is ground dependent and will keep going for the summer - Seamus Neville, trainer.

runners.comment: Ulster National faller; others possibly better handicapped and trip remains an unknown
runners.spotlight: Maiden hurdle win over 2m4f; 0-6 chasing this term, decent handicap debut run at Leopardstown (2m6f), most recently halfway faller in 3m5f Ulster National; others possibly better handicapped and trip remains an unknown.

quotes.race: Jump Into January Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Fishery Lane is a strong stayer I would say. He will improve on the job regarding his jumping, and I would see him going up in trip rather than dropping back - Paul Townend.

stable_tour.quote: Given the work he did at home here last season, he's one I hope will be able to hold his own at the top level in novice hurdles this season. We'll try to find a maiden hurdle for him shortly and I'm looking forward to getting him out and getting him jumping. He's got lots of potential. 25-11-24

runners.comment: Tougher task than at Kelso last time although not one to rule out
runners.spotlight: Began this campaign with 3m1f Aintree handicap win in December (good-to-soft) but hasn't repeated that sort of form in three runs since, including treated for post-race heat stress after Eider Chase fifth; most recently never nearer fourth under top-weight in lesser 3m2f Kelso contest; more needed but not one to rule out.

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fortunate Man has done it well because he was lacking a run against the others. He had a good season last year and he's only a 6yo and could be the type for the regional Nationals - Jonjo O'Neill Jr, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Committed To Top Prices Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Fortunate Man can be a bit frustrating as he's good when he's good and awful when he's awful. He'll be a grand long-distance staying chaser - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'd like to think he could improve a bit more with another year under his belt. I'm not sure where he'll start off yet, but he's better on soft ground and could be one for the regional nationals. 18-11-25

runners.owner: Patrick Corbett & Michael Corbett & J J Corbett & W Clancy
runners.comment: Ulster National second is now 5lb better off with winner Born Braver for 5l defeat
runners.spotlight: Bumper/hurdles winner is 0-8 chasing but has being going close in handicaps, notably second in 3m4f National Trial here in February and when chasing home 5l winner Born Braver in 3m5f Ulster National at Downpatrick last time; 5lb better off with that rival here.

quotes.race: Dairygold Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Uncle Pat is progressing away. He jumps great and he's maturing away. I think he'll keep improving - Paul Townend, rider.

runners.comment: Made respiratory noise when pulled up in Midlands National; caution advised but nice mark
runners.spotlight: Two of his five chase wins in France were on cross-country courses (very soft/heavy) and good second on first two runs for current trainer in 3m6f Cheltenham cross-country contests over the winter; favourite, reportedly made respiratory noise when pulled up in Midlands National at Uttoxeter on latest so caution advised, albeit he looks on a workable mark.

runners.comment: Maiden not really progressing in handicaps; remains opposable
runners.spotlight: Maiden went close to landing breakthrough win at Leopardstown (3m1f, yielding) in December but hasn't backed that up, most recently never counting when modest enough fourth at Fairyhouse; remains opposable.

stable_tour.quote: He was entered at Naas on Sunday but we didn't declare him because of the ground. He's a chaser in the making. He'll start off over hurdles and has summered nicely. 12-11-24
He was entered at Naas on Sunday but we didn't declare him because of the ground. He's a chaser in the making. He'll start off over hurdles and has summered nicely. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Needs to jump better than at Navan but definite claims on National Trial third here
runners.spotlight: No wins since two hurdle successes two seasons ago; much improved to take third in the 3m4f Grand National Trial here in February (neck off runner-up Uncle Pat) and every chance when unseating at the last in Leinster National; bad mistake ended his chances at Navan last time but given a clear round could go well and yard having a good week.

quotes.race: Punchestown Members Club From 215 Euros Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was delighted when I saw we were going to get Limerick ground again. Built By Ballymore just handles the muck so well. He might not quicken up in it but he keeps going in it. I thought his rating was high enough, but he just handles that ground better than most - Martin Brassil, trainer.

quotes.race: CUBE Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Built By Ballymore is a big raw horse and will take a while to come to himself. I was happy enough where I was sitting, I kicked on two out and he will have learned loads from that - Conor Brassil, rider.

runners.comment: Former Irish National winner races off much reduced mark now for a reason
runners.spotlight: Without a win since landing the 2022 Irish Grand National; much reduced mark nowadays is for a reason; visor replaces cheekpieces but remains opposable.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Irish Grand National Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Grade A)
quotes.quote: Our plan was to jump Lord Lariat out, but I was a bit concerned about getting the trip. We wanted to utilise his jumping as he is a good jumper. Paddy said he got plenty of breathers into him and it all worked out well - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer.

quotes.race: Tote Jackpot Is Back Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Lord Lariat surprised me as I was a bit anxious carrying top-weight on that ground. He's won on proper good ground before. It's probably looser than we thought and he kept galloping. He's improving and maybe he's a bit stronger now to handle that ground - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer.

quotes.race: Fairyhouse Ladies Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Lord Lariat stayed at it well and the girl used her head. He's been thereabouts for a while and deserved to get over the line. He likes that ground and there might be something for him at Leopardstown - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: He's a big baby and he's going on his holidays now. He's only five and he'll grow into himself. He jumped super - Karl Thornton, trainer of Lord Lariat

quotes.race: Junction Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: He's just a big, raw horse and probably won't be a horse until next year. He's by Golden Lariat, a show jumping stallion who doesn't have many horses but everything he has is okay. He's a grand, fun horse. He'll come back here on Wednesday. He probably wants that nicer ground as well - Karl Thornton, trainer of Lord Lariat

stable_tour.quote: I think he'll go for the Porterstown Handicap Chase at Fairyhouse next month. He could have one run in the new year before we give him a break and it'll be all systems go for the Grand National at Aintree. He didn't run badly on his comeback at Punchestown ? it was a nice starting point in a small field. 20-11-22

runners.comment: Came good on better ground at Down Royal; much more on his plate here
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at 19th attempt chasing last month when forcing tactics adopted in 3m2f Down Royal handicap, ready success on good ground; 7lb rise leaves him just 1lb out of the handicap which is negated by rider's claim; interesting if ground continues to dry out.

prev_owners.owner: Munster Van Centre/Seven Plus One Syndicate
Munster Van Centre/Seven Plus One Syndicate
Munster Van Centre/G Cromwell Racing/Seven Plus One Synd'
Munster Van Centre & Gavin Cromwell Racing Limited

runners.comment: Hard to fancy on balance of recent form and really wants testing conditions
runners.spotlight: Two chase wins on heavy in the 2023/24 season; sole piece of form this season came when second to an improver over 3m at Navan in similar ground, well held the last twice at 3m4f including in National Trial here; 6lb wrong.

quotes.race: Fairyhouse Members 2024 Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Evies Vladimir loves that ground. He jumped brilliant after a mistake at the first and it was very straightforward. We'll see what the handicapper does - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Very open, a tentative vote going to BORN BRAVER, whose Irish National run could have come too soon after his Ulster National success
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/1 Jasmin De Grugy, 15/2 Uncle Pat, 8/1 Built By Ballymore,  J'Arrive de L'Est, 9/1 Born Braver, 10/1 Will Do,  Fortunate Man, 12/1 Brucejack,  Shanbally Kid, 14/1 Better Times Ahead,  Daily Present, 16/1 Union Station,  Saint Davy,  Fishery Lane, 20/1 Intense Raffles,  Sa Majeste,  Duffle Coat,  Folly Master, 25/1 Brideswell Lad,  Ain't That A Shame,  Evies Vladimir, 33/1 Lord Lariat

racecards.race_name: Palmerstown House Estate Pat Taaffe Handicap Chase (Listed Race)

runners.breeder: Mr & Mrs D Futter & Peel Bloodstock
runners.owner: Sullivan Group Limited & P Crowley & Neill Hughes

prev_owners.owner: Sullivan Group Limited & P Crowley & Neill Hughes
Sullivan Bloodstock Limited & Neill Hughes & P Crowley

runners.comment: Tendency to jump left a negative but top-weight could go well if putting it all together
runners.spotlight: Sole chase win came in 2m7f beginners' here last season but some fine runs in competitive handicaps, fourth in last season's bet365 Gold Cup and this term when second in 2m6f handicap here and most notably chasing clear leader when blundering last in 4m2f Aintree National and weakening late on when fifth of 16 finishers (good-to-soft); tendency to jump left is a negative but could go well if putting it all together here (in-form rider's claim a positive).

quotes.race: QuinnBet Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: High Class Hero did it nicely. The ground was quite testing as they had a lot of rain before racing. He's in the Brown Advisory and he would look like that type of an animal. We'll probably head that direction. Loughglynn will probably stay at home and we'll find something for him. Overall, I'm very happy with them - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Stamina is his strong suit. The further he goes the better he seems to be and he ran a cracker to finish third in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown at the end of last season. I'd imagine he'll be an ideal type for the Grand National this season. That's what's in my head. 17-11-25

runners.owner: Vincent Caldwell & Angela Shamoon & Mrs A Shamoon Ibgi

prev_owners.owner: Vincent Caldwell & Angela Shamoon & Mrs A Shamoon Ibgi

runners.comment: Last season's Scottish National winner but jumping letting him down of late
runners.spotlight: Last season's 4m Scottish National winner but mixed bag this term however, including early faller in Thyestes and most recently mistakes before unseating four out in Aintree National; hard to be confident in and handicapper not relenting.

quotes.race: Coral Scottish Grand National Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I just wanted to get Captain Cody settled early and creep him into the race. I followed him at Cheltenham last time and he was too free. He probably unshipped Danny Mullins because he was going so well, he was overracing, so the plan was to get his head dropped early. As soon as he did that he got into a lovely rhythm. I wanted to go wide because he hasn't had that many runs over fences and I wanted to let him see his fences. It couldn't have gone all the better all the way round. I didn't want to get there too soon. I knew I was going to beat Johnny. Even at the last I thought let's just get him over it, and away he went - Harry Cobden, jockey.

quotes.race: Paddy Kehoe Suspended Ceilings Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Jody was very good. She minded her own business and kept Captain Cody balanced and jumping. She's always there riding winners all the time for us. When you consider how light she is, she must have to carry a stone and a half of lead every day - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Ladies Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Captain Cody had a top-class run at Cheltenham last year. His jumping was a bit rusty at times but he was very good at the last two when it counted - Patrick Mullins, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Auction (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Captain Cody has definitely improved. I know Patrick thought his horse would come on for the run at Punchestown but I knew my fellow would too - Jody Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: A thorough stayer who would gallop all day long. He showed his stamina when he won the Scottish National at Ayr and I'd imagine he'll have the Grand National on his radar this season. The Irish equivalent might be an option, too, as he's a winner around Fairyhouse over hurdles. 17-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Ms Kiva O'Brien & Mrs J M Walker

runners.comment: Unseated at Aintree when no threat; fresh horse so could improve
runners.spotlight: Won major 3m handicaps at Leopardstown last season over fences and hurdles; light campaign this term with Aintree in mind but never counted before unseating four out in National last month; fresher horse than most of these so could improve but certainly needs to.

quotes.race: Race And Stay At Leopardstown Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois was very nimble over hurdles. I thought coming here he's a better chaser than he is a hurdler but he was good there. He's in the Grand National so we'll have to consider it - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: Paddy Power Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Perceval Legallois got me out of trouble! It didn't go to plan. I didn't want to be as far back as I was. They kicked on down the back straight and I was a good bit back, further than I wanted to be, but I weaved my way through and he winged the last. I thought coming down to the second-last I had a chance if he kept going the way he was going. I got a great kick out of that because the horse deserved it. He's been unlucky on his last few runs. I knew the ability was there but nothing went right on his last few runs - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: P.J. Foley Memorial INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: That was great from Percival Legallois. We've liked him and I was fairly confident he'd handle conditions. Obviously we were very afraid of Willie's horse coming here but I'm not one bit surprised because he has shown us plenty at home - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He did well last season, winning the Paddy Power at Leopardstown over Christmas and then going back there to win over hurdles at the Dublin Racing Festival. He has an entry in the Coral Gold Cup. There's nothing set in stone - he could also go back over hurdles at some stage. 04-11-25

He's been a bit frustrating and the handicapper keeps pushing him up a little bit despite him not winning. He might just not be well handicapped anymore but hopefully he'll have a good chance in one of those staying handicap chases if things fall his way. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Recent Ludlow winner likes decent ground going right-handed; one to consider
runners.spotlight: Most of five chase wins have come on decent ground, including last time when taking 3m Ludlow handicap (just 2 finishers) having been dropped in grade following some good runs in better-class handicaps; seems suited by going right-handed; respected.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Your Darling likes going right-handed and we were a bit worried about the tighter track but he's done it well. There's a chase at Punchestown that might suit him - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Clarke Chase (A Handicap Chase) (For The Sir Stanley And Lady Clarke Challenge Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That's two wins out of his last three starts, so I think it's a record for Your Darling. We're chuffed to pieces because I thought the ground was against him, but he looked to enjoy it. He travelled and jumped well and had to battle at the end.   It's all about his headspace - there's nothing ever wrong with him. I knew halfway round he was going to run well today. You enjoy every day as they come and hopefully he can go back to Ascot in November - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: S.A.F.E. Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Your Darling is the most frustrating horse I'll ever train - if only he turned up every time. He's probably one of the most talented horses I've trained for a long time and when he wants to do it, he's electric. When he got in deep to one there, he still landed 15 yards out the other side of it but he doesn't want to do it, he flops through it. It's quite clear the rating doesn't overly matter to him, it's whether he wants to do it or not. He'll probably go up another 6lb for that and get thumped because he doesn't want to know. So we'll put him away now and go straight to the Topham Chase  - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Premier Food Courts Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race
quotes.quote: We knew Your Darling was very good and when you get one as good you hope they go and do it on the course. He's handled that ground, but wouldn't want it. We wanted to go hurdling, but because the yard was under a cloud we came down the bumper route and will stay here for the rest of the season. We'll see about the Champion Bumper and are not in a rush, but he'll run somewhere before the summer. He's got plenty of speed and we'll stick to two miles when he goes hurdling, but that was a nice start. He's one of the best horses we've had - he's got everything in his life. He's not stupid, he takes it all in his stride, his very healthy and sound and is a lovely horse to go forward with - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was in the Grand Sefton but we thought we'd look towards the race he's won twice at Ascot this month instead. He's a legend and he seems as good as ever, and I'm pleased with where we are. He goes well fresh, so we'd like to pick a target that might pay his way for the season straight off the bat. 07-11-25

He is possibly the biggest head scratcher in the yard as he is so talented on his day. That said, he has won two of his last three races so he has not been doing too much wrong. He ran a perfectly respectable race last time at Aintree when coming home fifth. I've learned he is very good fresh so I am now going to run him rarely, but when he does he will be ready to do a job. He will not be out again until Christmas at the earliest. 30-11-21

runners.comment: Novice made mistakes when a remote fourth in 3m5f Irish National; needs to jump better
runners.spotlight: Made amends for a fall on his chasing debut with wins in a beginners' event at Punchestown and Naas Grade 3  (extended 3m, heavy); struggled in the Brown Advisory and didn't land a blow (mistakes) when remote fourth in 3m5f Irish National last time; jumping still needs attention.

quotes.race: Finlay Ford At Naas Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Paul said Argento Boy enjoys those extreme distances and the ground wasn't an issue. He said he travels better, and attacks his fences better than he did hurdles. He'll probably be entered in all the chases at Cheltenham. The Irish National could be a race for him too, but we'll see. - David Casey, assistant to Willie Mullins.

quotes.race: Celebrating 175 Years At Punchestown Tote Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: It's nice to see Danny picking up the pieces again on Argento Boy who was running a cracker here the last day when he slipped up. I was very happy that he was able to do that over that trip. He jumped a lot better. He was green enough at times, especially coming to the last. We put cheekpieces on him over hurdles and might do the same over fences - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes "Best Odds Guaranteed On Racing" Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Argento Boy felt much better today through the race. The further they went the better he felt. Ideally, he is a 3m chaser - David Casey, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: He travelled well for a long way at Punchestown on Sunday and the lack of a run probably just caught him out. I was delighted with how he ran, though, and that will set him up nicely for the rest of the season. We'll try to find another maiden hurdle for him somewhere next. 25-11-24

runners.comment: Stiff tasks of late; cheekpieces added now and has a bit to prove off this mark
runners.spotlight: Much improved to win 3m Navan beginners' in January on testing ground; stiff tasks since, too keen and didn't get home in Brown Advisory and never counted when pulled up in Irish National; cheekpieces added now and has a bit to prove off this mark.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: I got a lovely time in front, Joystick jumped from fence to fence, and got an easy enough time of it. When Darragh (O'Keeffe) came past me at the second-last, I thought maybe he had me but I kept picking up and picking up and he was a good winner at the line - Brian Hayes, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He never looked like a hurdler and always gave the impression he would do better over fences. He'll go down the staying novice chase route, that looks his bag. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Strong Kempton form on good ground makes him a player
runners.spotlight: Better chaser than hurdler, third win coming in 3m Kempton handicap in January (good); better again when second in better-class contest over same C&D following month, disappointingly never counted in Ultima at Cheltenham latest; possibly best going right-handed so could go well here, especially if ground continues to dry out.

stable_tour.quote: He's a horse we like. We haven't over-raced him but he's won a bumper and a couple of hurdle races. He's an Irish point-to-point winner and we'd been happy with his schooling before his chase debut at Market Rasen, where he made a pleasing start in third. We've generally kept him to right-handed tracks because he's shown a tendency to go a bit to his right, but I hope he'll be more adaptable down the line. 25-10-24

He's a horse we like, an Irish point-to-point winner who's been successful since in a bumper and a couple of hurdle races. We were happy with his schooling before his chasing debut at Market Rasen and he made a pleasing start in third. We've generally kept him to right-handed tracks because he's shown a tendency to go a bit to his right but I hope he'll be more adaptable down the line. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Didn't stay in Irish National but definite contender back in trip if handling ground
runners.spotlight: Improver in Naas handicaps over the winter on testing ground, winning 2m4f novice contest and only caught late  in 3m1f Leinster National off 132 (clear of remainder); didn't appear to stay 3m5f of Irish National latest but definite contender back in trip here if handling quicker conditions.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Nas Na Riogh Novice Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He got the job done. Goraibhmaithagat made a few silly mistakes on the way, but he was tough and handled the ground well. Mark gave him a good ride. He finished off very well the last day. He had to fight and he did. Today was the plan, so we'll see where he goes from here. He handles that ground well. I'd say he needs the slow side of good anyway - Frank Berry, owners representative.

runners.comment: Last year's winner needs to jump better than in Topham; respected
runners.spotlight: 10yo won this last year off 126 (yielding); mixed bag this term, undergoing wind surgery after third start and good comeback run when second in 3m Kelso handicap in February; mistakes when pulled up in Topham at Aintree but remains of interest.

quotes.race: Randox Supports Race Against Dementia Topham Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bill Baxter was the horse that was probably coming out to put our name on the map. I ride him every day. I had a plan a while back with Scott who helps me enter the horses. Then he fell at Hereford but it wasn't his fault. This was the race that was going to suit him as long as the rain came. Last night I rang the owner and I said if it is like this we won't run. Someone is looking down as it has rained all day. He would suit this type of race as he travels and jumps and he got him in a great rhythm. I thought this horse had a solid chance as long the ground was soft. He never lets you down and he will go on to bigger and better things - Warren Greatrex, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Cyril Alexander Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I love Bill Baxter, he's a star and very tough. He was unlucky to fall last time as there was a bit of uneven ground on landing. To come back and jump like that and stay on so well was really good. I'm thinking of the Topham Chase for him, or something else at Aintree. He travels very well, he's won three of his last four and I think he'd have won at Hereford so he deserves a go at a big pot now. Warren Greatrex, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He gave us a great day when winning at Punchestown in May, and I thought it was a great comeback over hurdles when putting it up to Haiti Couleurs. That was a prep run for the Becher and that will be the plan this side of Christmas. He's won over the fences before, stays very well now and if the ground became really testing it wouldn't hinder him. If he went and won the Becher, all roads would lead to the Grand National. He's full of confidence off the back of last season and seems to be getting better with age. 23-11-25

A yard favourite. He won a Listed handicap chase at Punchestown in May on soft ground and returned in November to come second behind Haiti Couleurs in a Pertemps hurdle qualifier at Newbury. Last month he reverted to chasing for the Becher and finished a staying-on sixth. I'm now thinking about the Great Yorkshire Chase and the Topham, which he won in 2023. He has an appetite for the game and I'm sure there's another big race in him. 07-01-26

runners.comment: Paddy Power 3rd; return to better ground and first-time cheekpieces could see improvement
runners.spotlight: Winning hurdler and 0-8 but better chaser, standout run on seasonal return when third of 28 in 3m1f Paddy Power Handicap at Leopardstown over Christmas (yielding); hasn't backed that up however on softer ground, well held in both Leopardstown handicap and Leinster National; return to better ground and first-time cheekpieces could see an improved showing.

runners.comment: Thrived on good ground at Ascot this season at 3m; potentially big player
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to top-class Protektorat; surprise withdrawal from last weekend's bet365 Gold Cup due to ground, having made notable progress before that on similar good ground in 3m Ascot handicaps, winning twice including latest in premier handicap in February; potentially a big player.

quotes.race: Full Circle Series At Punchestown Festival Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was really disappointed with Montregard at Newcastle but I think the cheekpieces have helped him here and he's toughed it out well - Tom Lacey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse of JP McManus's who won his maiden at the second attempt over hurdles when last seen at Warwick in April. I was really pleased with him that day; he was green but toughed it out and stayed on nicely. I'd say he's progressed through the summer and is set to return in a 0-105 handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter on Friday. He'll ultimately jump a fence too. A nice prospect. 20-12-23

runners.comment: Solid first handicap effort at Fairyhouse but this trip stretches him so stamina concerns
runners.spotlight: Three-time hurdles winner made winning chase debut in 2m5f Fairyhouse beginners' in October (yielding) but hasn't really progressed, albeit solid first handicap effort when third over 3m1f at same venue last month; 3m tends to stretch him so stamina concerns.

quotes.race: Punchestown's Fittest Club Sunday June 11th Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Barry Lyndon is a lovely horse. He loved that ground but his jumping let him down. He hit the line strong and if his jumping gets better he can improve - Conor Maxwell, rider.

runners.comment: Easy task latest; back in handicap company with likely more to offer
runners.spotlight: Has taken well to chasing this term, winning 2m4f Wexford beginners' and acquitted herself well in stronger company, notably third in 2m7f Grade 2 Limerick mares' novice, most recently landing odds in weaker four-runner 3m1f Grade 3 novice at same track in late March, making most from halfway; those runs came in testing conditions but handles better ground; likely has more to offer.

quotes.race: Hugh McMahon Memorial Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Uhavemeinstitches was tough and Mark said she won cosily enough. It was a nice pot to win and is more black type for the mare. We were waiting for the weights for the Irish National, but I don't think she'll get a run as she's too far down. It might have been a tough ask for a first-season novice so I was glad to come here. - James Motherway, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh] gave Uhavemeinstitches a lovely ride. They went very quickly in front. Mark said they went nearly too fast, he thought and it fell apart a bit. She's a nice mare going forward. She is still a bit babyish; she made one or two novice mistakes, which I didn't think she would, but I suppose it's the speed as well. It was her first time racing at that speed over fences. I am not sure where she will slot in. That was for horses rated 120 or less over hurdles, so a lot of the higher-class horses were ruled out of it. We will have to see where she fits into the rankings as the season goes on, but she is a nice filly to have. We went a real strong gallop and I always thought Liam [Quinlan] was going to come back which he did - James Motherway, trainer.Uhavemeinstitches was good bar the first but she learned and jump brilliant after that. It was only her fifth lifetime start so you would have to be happy with her. I'd be hoping she would stay well and do something like her mother - Mark Wash, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Earl Of Harrington Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Uhavemeinstitches is a lovely filly who we've liked from day one. She jumped so well early on that she was jumping into the back of one or two of them, but she was really good at the last two. She had a little look when she got to the front, but Simon [Torrens, jockey] said she found plenty when he got after her. She really filled out her frame during the summer and when she came back to us in the autumn, I was really delighted with her. I knew I had a mare to train then. She's only four rising five, so hopefully there's plenty to come. Stamina will probably be her forte down the line - James Motherway, trainer.

runners.comment: Progressive until no show last time; had a break since and could bounce back
runners.spotlight: Tongue-tie brought about improvement with wins over the winter in handicaps at Lingfield and valuable 3m Great Yorkshire Chase at Doncaster (soft); reportedly never travelled when unseating at latter venue in February however and given time off since; can't rule out.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Great Yorkshire Chase (Premier Handicap Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was flat out the whole way, we went a good, strong gallop for the first mile and a half and I couldn't really go with them even if I'd wanted to. Then we slowed up and I got passing a few. Dartmoor Pirate is relatively unexposed over fences. He missed the odd one here or there but he jumped well when I needed him to and ended up in front with the luxury of a bit of time on our hands - Rex Dingle, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's one we're excited about. He was fourth in the EBF Final and will go novice chasing. He jumps really nicely and we hope he'll make up into a Graded-class horse. We're working back from the new novice handicap chase at the Cheltenham Festival which could be a great race for him if he does well. 14-11-24

He ran in the Newbury sales bumper and Rex Dingle got trapped a little out wide on him. I'm really pleased with him and he's working smartly. He's got a lovely pedigree - he's a half-brother to Barizan, who was second in the Triumph. We'll really fancy him when he runs in a bumper, then we'll probably go hurdling. 12-10-23

runners.comment: Creditable Cheltenham hurdles run in circumstances; unexposed over fences at this trip
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdles winner is 0-4 chasing, good second in 2m4f Gowran handicap and most recently did well after being hampered in finishing fifth of 24 in BetMGM Handicap Hurdle at Cheltenham; remains unexposed as a chaser (7lb lower than hurdles) and upped in trip here.

stable_tour.quote: He was reported to have an atrial fibrillation after his run at Naas on Sunday, so while we were a bit disappointed, there was obviously a reason for it. We'll have to check that out now. 11-11-25

runners.comment: Just denied on comeback run at Leopardstown in March; should go well
runners.spotlight: Sole chase win came in 3m1f Kilbeggan handicap in 2024 but career-best on latest when just failing to get up in 2m6f Leopardstown handicap in March (yielding-to-soft), his first run since August; should go well.

quotes.race: Tayto Group Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: That was a nice performance from Invictus Machin. He worked well at home and we weren't sure coming here with Gordon's horse being so fancied. I would have been very disappointed if he didn't run a good solid race. He's a Coastal Path and a fine stamp of a horse, and will be a lovely horse next year - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

runners.comment: Non-stayer in National Hunt Chase;  interesting contender back in trip with ground to suit
runners.spotlight: Made winning return in 2m5f Cork handicap in November (yielding) and given winter off until not looking to stay 3m6f in National Hunt Chase at Cheltenham in March; interesting contender back in trip here with ground to suit.

quotes.race: Kevin McManus Bookmaker Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I thought I was beat and I thought I would finish fourth or fifth, but Iceberg Theory really got rolling up the straight and winged them all and galloped all the way to the line. I think three miles is his trip, he could be a nice staying horse - Conor Stone-Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Wesco Electrical Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We put cheekpieces on Iceberg Theory today as we were worried the last day that he might be a bit of a devil, so we put them on today to make him concentrate. We were a bit worried with the way he was carrying on here in the parade ring, but Sean said he was only acting the maggot. He did it well and maybe we'll give him a stab at the auction final in Punchestown - Paul Nolan, trainer.

runners.comment: Novice progressing well in handicaps; due to run here on Friday
runners.spotlight: Point/hurdle/bumper winner was beaten favourite in two beginners' chases before making immediate impact on handicap chase debut at Leopardstown (3m1f, yielding) and better again when runner-up over 3m at Navan last time; due to run here on Friday (5.25).

stable_tour.quote: You'd have to say he was a bit disappointing at Galway on Saturday. We think he's better than that and we will look for a similar sort of maiden hurdle for him next time. 28-10-24

runners.comment: Progressive of late on soft; potentially still well-handicapped
runners.spotlight: Improved for going chasing this season, winning 3m Newbury handicap and better again when clear second at Uttoxeter over same trip, both on soft ground; potentially still well-handicapped and could go well if handling better ground.

quotes.race: 500 Logistics Decade Of Delivery Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That track helps As The Fella Says, and I wanted to come here. James [Bowen] was pretty cool, and his clock is very good. He gets it right more often than not. He's still growing up, but he's got a future. He's only a novice, but he's getting there - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's still a maiden over hurdles and his mark of 114 is workable, but I'd imagine he'll go over fences. He was a point-to-point horse and he's big, but he wouldn't want the ground as soft as we thought he did. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Below best this season but 7lb lower than when third in this last year so don't dismiss
runners.spotlight: Last win came in 3m Kempton handicap in Christmas of 2024; third to Bill Baxter in this race last year but not at best this season, chasing home a clear winner at Ludlow last time (only two finishers); 7lb lower than last year so don't rule out.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Get Rewarded With Ladbucks Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The blinkers definitely helped Beachcomber out. He jumped very well. Rich got him in a lovely rhythm from quite early on, he was able to dictate as he wanted to, and I think going right-handed definitely helped as well -  AJ O'Neill, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Pertemps Network Handicap Hurdle (Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beachcomber is a bit in and out and didn't like going left handed at Catterick last time. This was better for him and he's won here before. He'll jump a fence one day - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

quotes.race: Discover Whats Trending At Rhino.Bet Casino Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beachcomber made things easy for me as he settled nicely in front. He's been a bit quirky in the past but he's growing up now - Richie McLernon, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He missed the first fence coming out of Swinley Bottom on his comeback at Ascot and things didn't really go for him, but he's better than that. He ran well at the Punchestown festival and is best going right-handed. Kempton suits him particularly well and there's a three-mile handicap chase there on Monday to consider, before perhaps looking to the same race he won at Kempton last Christmas. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Bit to find on recent efforts but talented rider's claim a positive
runners.spotlight: Won 3m handicap chase at Down Royal (yielding-to-soft) in first-time cheekpieces in January, beating subsequent Ulster National winner Born Braver; in rear in the Grand National Trial here next time and ordinary run in Ladies National at Fairyhouse last time; bit to find but talented rider's claim a positive.

quotes.race: SBK Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lucky Lyreen stays strong, idled in front but when something came to him he went on again. He lets you down a small bit with his jumping but I think he just loses concentration a little bit at a hurdle - Jack Kennedy, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's probably gone as far as he can go over hurdles, so we'll go novice chasing with him and see where that takes us. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Hasn't progressed from his novice season; looks to have a good bit to find
runners.spotlight: Now 0-10 chasing and hasn't progressed from his novice season; looks to have a good bit to find.

stable_tour.quote: We'd be leaning towards the National Hunt Chase as long as he gets in. He ran well at Musselburgh last time at a track which wouldn't have suited on ground that was plenty quick. He's definitely going the right way and we think there's more to come. 20-2-25

runners.comment: Fairyhouse winner raised 12lb for that but still 12lb out of handicap here
runners.spotlight: Not a great strike rate but on song on latest when readily landing 3m1f Fairyhouse handicap last month in first-time blinkers; raised 12lb for that but still 12lb out of handicap here so plenty on his plate.

quotes.race: Tote, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Clonmeen put in a tough performance, he gave a stone to the second. A good handicap off a low weight might be what I'm thinking about, maybe the National Trial here - Willie Murphy, trainer.

racecards.verdict: INVICTUS MACHIN was eating up the ground on his return to action at Leopardstown and gets the vote in a wide open handicap
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/1 As The Fella Says, 15/2 Invictus Machin, 10/1 High Class Hero,  Montregard,  Uhavemeinstitches, 12/1 Your Darling,  The Doyen Chief,  Bill Baxter, 14/1 Iceberg Theory,  Beachcomber,  Goraibhmaithagat,  Kish Bank,  Dartmoor Pirate,  Beckett Rock, 16/1 Captain Cody, 20/1 Lucky Lyreen,  Barry Lyndon,  Kinturk Kalanisi,  Joystick,  Argento Boy,  Perceval Legallois, 25/1 No Time To Wait, 33/1 Clonmeen

racecards.race_name: SBK Irish EBF Mares Champion Hurdle (Grade 1)

runners.comment: C&D maiden winner but recent form leave her with lots to find
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner got off the mark at the third attempt over hurdles in 2m4f maiden here in January (soft-to-heavy); two runs since in much better company suggest she'll struggle again here.

quotes.race: Matchbook 50:50 Graduation Series Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was kind of messy with Paul's horse (Poetisa) jumping left but I was happy enough where I was. Ill Raise A Glass is a smallish filly but when Bambino Fever came out we thought we'd have a good each-way chance at least. She did it well and should stay further in time - Darragh O'Keeffe, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie La Grugerie
runners.comment: Last year's winner; beaten 1l by Wodhooh at Cheltenham; cheekpieces now fitted
runners.spotlight: Last year's winner took well to fences this season, finishing second in Limerick Grade 2 over Christmas before going one better in similar company at Thurles (2m5f, yielding) in January; right at her best back hurdling in Grade 1 Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham when a clear staying-on second to Wodhooh (beaten 1l) having allowed winner first run (good); cheekpieces now fitted for the rematch.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Mares' Hurdle (Registered As The David Nicholson Mares' Hurdle) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: She's run a blinder and just got beat by a proper horse. We just hit the crossbar but Jade De Grugy ran right up to her best. I thought at one point she might get up but the winner pulled out more. She was a bit better than us on the day but I'm very proud of her - Kenny Alexander, owner.

quotes.race: Carey Glass Irish EBF Mares Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: It was straightforward. Jade De Grugy jumped like a buck and settled well. She was just two grades above them, probably. We were disappointed with her in Cork the first day. [Was it fitness?] I'd say so. She's raw, and Kala Konti came out and won again since. I'd say she was just outstayed by a good mare, then when running into that calibre again at Limerick. With the benefit of those two runs, it was much more straightforward here. I'd say the run in Limerick was as good as today. I'd say the one who beat her is a fair sort. She'll be fine, she'll jump fences and if they want, she can go back hurdling. [Is she better over fences?] She has a fair level over hurdles; she's 150, so she'd have a lot to do to get to that level. [Cheltenham target?] Thurles was all I heard - Paul Townend, Jockey.

quotes.race: SBK Irish EBF Mares Champion Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Jade De Grugy has been improving all year. Nicer ground was a big help and tactically Paul was brilliant. We're delighted to be able to win a Grade 1 race with a filly like this. Brighterdaysahead probably just had a very hard race at Christmas and she never really recovered from it. She could [jump a fence] but it wouldn't be what we'd be looking forward to at this stage, we'd rather keep her hurdling. I'd say we'll probably train her for the Mares' Hurdle next year -  Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Quevega Mares Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Annie Power won this race before winning the Champion Hurdle and it has been won in the past [Black Tears] before winning the Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham. It was a nice comeback on Jade De Grugy's first run of the season. She had worked nicely at home and I was very happy with her coming here. She showed me today what she had showed me at home. I think she'll improve a fair bit for the race, which leaves us in a good position going to Cheltenham. Carrying the weight she carried today against nice opposition, I think is a good sign - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Honeysuckle Mares' Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Jade De Grugy showed how good and how tough she is, and it was a great run from the runner-up as well. She does look like a two-and-half mile mare, coming back from Cheltenham, to put in a run like that. A lot of the Cheltenham horses haven't featured at this meeting and I think it's a tough ask on that ground. It'll be Punchestown next I'd imagine. We didn't find out or look for anything at home since Cheltenham, it's a Grade 1, so you have to take your chance. This is the race you want to win rather than Cheltenham because it's a Grade 1. You always want to win Grade 1 rather than a Grade 2 - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: SBK Solerina Mares Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Jade De Grugy was very impressive. She did things right all the way and she jumps brilliant. She travelled and quickened up in the straight. Brian was very happy with her. She's a very sensible mare and always did everything right. We're delighted with her. She has the race at Cheltenham and the Grade 1 back here as well afterwards. There is a short gap between them, but I'd imagine they will be the two targets - David Casey, assistant to Willie Mullins.

quotes.race: Savills Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jade De Grugy is exciting. She did it nicely. I thought we built up down the back the second time and she stayed going well. She obviously stays well, the ground is testing, and she has a lovely attitude. She jumped well and did everything nicely - Paul Townend, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: A fine, big strong mare who put together three really good runs last season. She chased home Lossiemouth in the Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham and then won very well at Punchestown in the Grade 1 race there. She has the option of going over fences, but we could keep her over hurdles. She will do the opposite to Kargese. If one goes over fences, the other won't. The Mares' Hurdle would be her obvious target again should she stay over hurdles. 17-11-25

runners.breeder: S A S Ecurie X & Mr Yannick Fouin
runners.comment: Running well in graded company of late but meets two superior rivals here
runners.spotlight: Second-season hurdler has twice landed odds in ordinary company this term and has progressed well in Graded company, notably third in Grade 2 Ryanair Mares' Novice at Cheltenham and most recently Grade 1 Honeysuckle Mares' Novice at Fairyhouse when second to Zanoosh under a positive ride; meets two superior rivals here however so seems booked for third.

quotes.race: Fred Kenny Memorial Mares Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jack [Kennedy] said it was straightforward, Place De La Nation jumped well and quickened well. He said it was pretty simple, it looked that way beforehand so thankfully there was no drama. The Solerina Mares Novice Hurdle is back here in a month so we might have a look at that - David Casey, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Place De La Nation was jumping so well early, but I didn't want to use that because I didn't want to let her on and end up giving her a grueller. There's plenty of improvement in her. She jumps like a buck, and I wasn't able to use my ace card today - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: She wasn't beaten far in the Triumph Hurdle when fifth to Poniros and she's still a novice for this season, which is an added bonus. She has invaluable experience of Cheltenham, so I imagine she'll be a live one for the Mares' Novices' Hurdle at the festival in March. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Beat Jade De Grugy 1l at Cheltenham, could be pushed even closer this time
runners.spotlight: Has won 10 of her 11 hurdle starts, including this term in Grade 2 Ascot Hurdle, Grade 3 mares' contest at Leopardstown over Christmas and 2m5f Grade 1 Close Brothers Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham, getting first run on Jade De Grugy going to the last when beating that rival 1l (good); first run here since winning as a 3yo and deserved favourite but could be pushed very close by Jade De Grugy.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Mares' Hurdle (Registered As The David Nicholson Mares' Hurdle) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I don't think I was ever quite in the wilderness - it's hard to get winners here and we just weren't bouncing, but we're on the board now. The race worked out great; Jack gave Wodhooh a peach [of a ride]. She idled a bit halfway up the straight but picked up again - she's something else. It's hard to know just how good she is, because to be fair to her she doesn't do anything fancy at home, but we're lucky to have her. My own feeling is that she needs two and a half miles, but you never know. We'll enjoy today. Ted Durcan sourced her for us. We knew today was our best chances - we've a winner on the board now and three seconds. I'm just delighted, for myself number one, but for all the staff and owners and all the team at home. She could go to Aintree - she went well there last year, and we've Ireland as well, we'll see - Gordon Elliott, trainer.  It's been a frustrating couple of days, but when you have a mare like Wodhooh that you are waiting on you are I suppose hopeful or even quietly confident that you are going to get one on the board. Obviously I had no winner here last year so to get that is brilliant and thankfully Gordon and all of the team haven't had to wait as long as last year. A massive thanks to them for all the hard work they put in. It's brilliant. I was very happy the whole way. She just hit a bit of a flat spot coming down the hill, which she can do, and I probably gave her a bit of a squeeze a bit early and got there plenty soon enough on her but she's so honest nothing was going to get by her in the straight. - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Kerrymount Mares Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Wodhooh doesn't do anything fancy at home. She's very laid-back, but she knows how to win. She's so unassuming. I think we went for the right race. We were toying with going for the Grade 1 over two miles, but that could have been a bit sharp around there for her today. This turned into a bit of a sprint, and she nearly got caught napping for a couple of strides, but she picked up and galloped. Two miles around Cheltenham could be a bit sharp for her, so I'd say she'll go for the Mares' Hurdle. She's shown again how tough she is. I doubt she'll run again before Cheltenham - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Ascot Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Ascot Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Danny Gilligan said Wodhooh was a little bit rusty but when he gave her a squeeze she was straight on it. It's hard to know what's there because she only ever does what she has to. Everyone will have their opinion and we'll all sit down and make a plan, but I don't think we'll be coming back too much in trip and maybe stepping out further. We'll pick and choose our three or four races for the season, but there's no plan beyond today. The owners are a great craic and we're very lucky to have her - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Martin Pipe Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I won on Wodhooh here in December. Since then, it's been the plan to come here. Gordon [Elliott, trainer] told me going out, 'Ride her with plenty of balls'. I didn't think I would be in front as soon as I was, thankfully she stayed galloping all the way to the line. I think she's getting better with every run, and she's unbeaten. So she's well entitled to step up into graded company - Danny Gilligan, jockey.

quotes.race: SBK Fillies' Juvenile Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Wodhooh has done nothing wrong so far. She's a big scopey filly so who knows where she'll take us? Sir Gino looked awesome at Cheltenham so we'll get her home, see what Gordon Elliott says and take it from there - Ian Murphy, owner.

quotes.race: 'Bet In-Race' With Coral Fillies' Juvenile Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've not had many runners here. Wodhooh will have to improve to be a Triumph Hurdle filly, but there's plenty of prize-money to win and this race has been the plan for a while. It's an amazing pot with £25,000 to the winner, so it's great to be here - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Lisburn And Castlereagh City Council 3-Y-O Hurdle
quotes.quote: Wodhooh is tough. She would have been suited by a quicker gallop early on. She probably learned more than she did last day. She might go to Newbury now for a Listed hurdle next month - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power 3-Y-O Hurdle
quotes.quote: We knew Wodhooh had come on from the run in Listowel but I think on softer ground there is another half-stone in her. She's a very honest filly. Jack said it was like she only jumped in at the third-last. She was flat out for the first half of the race and then the further she went the better she was. We'd like to get a bit of black type over hurdles with her now. There is a race in Newbury the first week in December that she could go for - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Kerry Group 3-Y-O Hurdle
