quotes.quote: It was a tricky situation but the stewards had to do their job. Wodhooh is a filly you could see maybe going for that juvenile fillies' race at Aintree. I think she'll pay her way and will be black type over hurdles. Jordan said she was a bit deliberate at one hurdle and jumped a couple of others a bit big, but we'd done a lot of work with her at home - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's some bit of stuff, although she doesn't do anything fancy at home. She's very laid-back, but she knows how to win and she just keeps on winning. I was thinking of having a crack at the Grade 1 against Brighterdaysahead and Lossiemouth over Christmas, but in the end we stuck to mares' company and I think we made the right decision. It turned into a sprint but she still won well. I was keen to go straight to the Mares' Hurdle after that, so that's what we're doing. She's won at the track and she ticks almost every box. She's one of our best chances of the week. She never lets us down. 09-02-96

racecards.verdict: A fascinating rematch between WODHOOH and Jade De Grugy, the former only marginally preferred
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/6 Wodhooh, 6/4 Jade De Grugy, 12/1 Place De La Nation, 100/1 Ill Raise A Glass

racecards.race_name: Ballymore Champion Four Year Old Hurdle (Grade 1)

runners.comment: Shock winner of Triumph on stable debut, obvious chance and preferred by Paul Townend
runners.spotlight: French recruit failed to win in two runs for Yannick Fouin (6l behind Proactif on his second start at Auteuil); sent off at 50-1 on his first start for Willie Mullins in the Triumph Hurdle (2m1f, soft) but belied those odds to win by 1.5l; obvious chance of following up, and the forecast rain won't be an issue for him; preferred by Townend.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't give Patrick [Mullins] any instructions going out, I just said that we thought the start would be a circus. It was actually a very good start, thankfully. He just rode to his own instructions, so that was easy enough. I said Apolon De Charnie was going to win before the last, then after the last he had to get down and win the race for a second time. Once he got to that front he still didn't stop. A lot of horses put their heads up when they hear that Cheltenham roar, but he didn't - Willie Mullins, trainer.Apolon De Charnie was fantastic. He's not very big, I don't normally watch the juveniles at home, but he just caught my eye. I got a dream run everywhere - Patrick Mullins, jockey.

runners.breeder: Mrs F S Williams & Newsells Park Stud
runners.comment: Bolted up in second start over timber at Cork, well-regarded, unexposed, rain a worry
runners.spotlight: Minor promise in three runs on the Flat (rated 76); nice run on hurdles debut at Leopardstown in December; built on that to land a Cork maiden (yielding) under a positive ride in a first-time tongue tie (retained), beating a 121 rated horse by 10l; this is harder but he's well-regarded and unexposed; could go well, though the forecast rain is a concern.

quotes.race: Dermot Casey Tree Care Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We liked Bartholomew but I'd say he is still a bit immature. He is a stronger horse now though and has improved a bit. We'll enter him in the (Grade 1) four-year-old hurdle at Punchestown as he has beaten a horse rated 121 by ten lengths today, so we hope he is getting to that type of area. We were waiting for nice ground and he jumped well and was more professional today. We'll see how he is after his Punchestown race and he could come back for a late-summer, autumn campaign. On the Flat, he would want further than 1m4f but he'll have to have a break at some stage this summer too - Martin Brassil, trainer.

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage De Pierrepont

prev_owners.owner: Mme Marc Boudot, M Seror Et Al

runners.comment: AW winner, impressive on hurdles debut but poor twice since, others preferred
runners.spotlight: French Flat AW winner; won a Limerick maiden hurdle (2m, heavy) in dominant fashion on his Irish debut; not so good since, pulled up in a Grade 1 Juvenile Hurdle at the DRF and beaten 28l when down the field in the Fred Winter at Cheltenham; others have more appealing profiles.

quotes.race: Aqua Process Solutions @ Limerick 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bertutea had a bit of hurdling experience in France, and he jumped really well today. He's a lovely horse and a great ride. He's only doing what he has to. I only had to wake him up down the straight and he picked up nicely. I think he might be better on a bit of nicer ground, but he's a nice horse with ability, so he was able to handle it well today - Sean O'Keefe, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He could be one for the Triumph Hurdle, or else we'll go down the Fred Winter route with him. He didn't manage to win in France, but he ran well in defeat twice over hurdles and can hopefully continue to progress. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Naas maiden hurdle winner, well beaten upped in class twice since, can only watch now
runners.spotlight: Won over 7.5f on the Flat in France (soft); beat Saratoga when landing a 4yo maiden hurdle at Naas in January (2m, heavy) but has seemingly had his limitations exposed in the Triumph at Cheltenham (pulled up) and a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse (unseated when beaten); can only be watched after those two efforts.

quotes.race: Nursery Of Champions Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Kai Lung did it well. It wasn't the plan to make it but it looked like there was no pace and he can be a little bit keen so Danny thought he'd settle a bit in front. Even at that, he was a bit gassy, but he jumped well. Obviously the second had had a couple of runs and the third was a decent Flat horse as well. He had a good few runs on the Flat himself so he had plenty of experience. He kept galloping away well, after being keen, which was good - David Casey, assistant trainer to Willie Mullins.

prev_owners.owner: Ecurie Des Poilus & Haras De Saint-Voir

runners.comment: PU in the Triumph, back to form in Fairyhouse Grade 2 latest, in the mix with a repeat
runners.spotlight: Impressive winner at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft) on debut for Gabriel  Leenders in October; beaten favourite behind Proactif on first start for Willie Mullins in a 4yo hurdle at Fairyhouse (2m, yielding); pulled up after a bad mistake at the fourth in the Triumph; back on track when beaten a neck by Proactif in Grade 2 at Fairyhouse (2m, yld-sft); in the mix with a repeat of that.

stable_tour.quote: I'd like to think he's one of our Triumph Hurdle juveniles. I thought he got the job done very nicely at Auteuil for Gabriel Leenders. I've given him a little break with a view to reappearing in the New Year before we look towards Cheltenham. I'd say he's very smart. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Gowran maiden winner on heavy, well beaten in Fred Winter, forecast rain a plus
runners.spotlight: Placed on sole start in France for Damien Mele at Auteuil (1m7f, very soft) last May; beaten at skinny odds over this C&D (sft-hvy) on Irish debut in January; made amends despite racing keenly at Gowran (2m, heavy), making most to score by 2.75l; never involved when beaten 23l in the Fred Winter at Cheltenham (16.5f, gd-sft); needs to leave that behind but the forecast rain is at least in his favour.

quotes.race: Sea Moon & Silverwave At Burgage Stud Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was lairy and as we were going so slow it gave Madness D'Elle too much time to think. When I got him down and started racing, he jumped fine and his experience helped. It was a falsely run race, it was a dash for two furlongs and still the last furlong was hard work. It was a hard race to get a handle on, but he is a grand horse - Paul Townend, jockey

stable_tour.quote: Shaped with plenty of promise in a hurdle race at Auteuil for Daniela Mele over the summer and it'll be interesting to see how he progresses. Hopefully he's a Triumph Hurdle horse. 17-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Simon Munir, Haras De Saint-Voir & Isaac Souede

runners.comment: 2/3 in France inc' Gr' 3 at Auteuil, very exciting prospect, go well on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Won two of three starts in France; bolted up by 13l on debut in a 3yo hurdle at Auteuil; runner up in 17.5f Grade 3 (very soft) back there last May; went one place better in another Auteuil Grade 3 (2m2f, very soft) when last seen in September (subsequent Grade 3 winner 8.5l behind); lacks a recent outing but he's an exciting prospect and no surprise to see a big run on his first start for Henry De Bromhead.

stable_tour.quote: We're very excited to get him after he won a Grade 3 juvenile hurdle in France for Francois Nicolle. He's currently on a break at home and hopefully he'll join us in the next few weeks. 11-11-25

runners.comment: French AQPS and Navan maiden hurdle winner, outclassed in Gr 2 latest, tough task
runners.spotlight: French AQPS winner; well-beaten on Irish debut at Naas (2m, heavy) in January; justified short odds on next start when winning by 13l at Navan (2m, heavy) a  month later; last of seven finishers when behind a couple of these in Fairyhouse Grade 2 latest; rated 123 and looks to be up against it in this company.

quotes.race: Navan Racecourse Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It wasn't the strongest of races and Moulin Labbe improved from his first run for us in Naas. He did plenty wrong but he's a nice horse. He settled okay but would want to settle a little bit better, although in a better race he'll be fine. He was having a little look in front as well, so I was trying to keep the revs up on him. He's a nice horse for the future and is still a bit raw. He'll make a fine chaser - Paul Townend, jockey.

runners.comment: British raider, won first four hurdles, limitations exposed last twice, much more needed
runners.spotlight: British raider from yard that had a Grade 1 winner here earlier this week; won first four starts over hurdles on varying ground; fine run when 2l behind Maestro Conti in Cheltenham Grade 2 in January (2m1f, soft); beaten 13l when runner up in another Grade 2 at Kempton; beaten 26l in the Triumph on latest; much more needed.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Registered As The Prestbury Juvenile Hurdle) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: One Horse Town is  a proper juvenile. We've had easy pickings in the last few races but we said he deserved his chance in a bigger race. We didn't need to complicate things, Paul O'Brien is brilliant from the front. It's great and that was extremely satisfying. He's probably going to go to Trials day and then, well I don't want to say it, [the Triumph Hurdle]. Mum and Dad own a bit of him as well as Jonathan Gregory, who's a big supporter of the yard. That is a proper result for us - Harry Derham, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I think he deserves his place in the Triumph having had such a good season, and he's come out of the race on Trials day particularly well. I think the nature of the Triumph will suit him and I'm very sure he'll run his race. Will that be enough to win? Probably not because I think Narciso Has is near enough banker material, but he'll do us proud. 19-02-26

runners.breeder: Alban Chevalier Du Fau & Emmanuel Cheval
runners.comment: 3-4 over hurdles, sole defeat in Triumph, bounced back at Fairyhouse, obvious chance
runners.spotlight: Won sole start in France, beating Apolon De Charnie by 6l at Auteuil (2m2f, very soft); took the scalp of Macho Man on Irish debut at Fairyhouse (2m, yielding); disappointed when 7-2 favourite for the Triumph (2m, soft); back on song to beat Macho Man and Majolique in Fairyhouse Grade 2 latest (2m, yld-sft); obvious chance.

quotes.race: O'Driscoll's Irish Whiskey Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh] said Proactif let himself down on that ground, there was a nice dig in it. He didn't let himself down at all last time. It's nice to have one like him. He's a fine, big horse who can go jumping fences, and the same goes for the second, although I could see Majolique staying over hurdles. He will have a good long rest in the summer, so we'll keep him working from now until Punchestown - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Hurdle
quotes.quote: Proactif is a grand, big horse. Mark [Walsh] said he jumped well and was still a little bit green in front, but he galloped and jumped. Knowing Willie, the DRF might come a little bit soon but he's had a run in France. He stays and jumps and looks the ideal type [for the Triumph]. Touch wood, he stays in one piece. I thought they were going to get to him going to the last but he got to the line well - Frank Berry, owner's racing manager.He did it easy, Proactif is a real nice horse. He jumped and travelled great. We would hope there would be a nice bit of improvement in him and he's one to look forward with - Mark Walsh, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: JP said to make sure we enter him in the Supreme. I always like to have a reserve, as you never know what might happen, but I think there's a huge difference between what those other Supreme contenders have shown. 12-02-26

runners.breeder: Lynch Bages Ltd & Camas Park Stud

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

runners.comment: Won the Fred Winter on latest off 130, very much respected in first Grade 1
runners.spotlight: Flat winner for Aidan O'Brien; hinted there was a bigger performance in him when placed in first three maiden hurdles, one over this C&D (yielding) and twice at Naas on softer ground; duly delivered the goods on handicap debut, winning the Fred Winter at Cheltenham (2m, gd-sft) by 2.25l off 130; steps into Grade 1 company for the first time and very much respected.

quotes.race: McCoy Contractors Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (Registered As The Fred Winter) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I got a great run and a great start. I was upsides Sam Twiston-Davies [on Bibe Mus] the whole way around and we went a good gallop. I didn't think the two in front were going to lead us the whole way so I moved up and winged the second last. Saratoga did it very easy - Mark Walsh, jockey. I met Michael O'Leary today, he wished me a happy birthday and said, 'Only the good die young ! Every winner at Cheltenham is very, very special. That one I go back a long way with Padraig's father Christy. I owned the horse's [half] brother a couple of years ago, Brazil. They were praying that the ground would be fast, as he bounces off it. They were worried the ground might be a bit too soft for him a couple of weeks ago, but every day it was drying out. We are very happy with the horse. We've had a lot of fun. We've had some great days here. Everybody leans towards coming to Cheltenham and it means so much to so many. I'm delighted that one has won for Padraig - JP McManus, owner.

stable_tour.quote: We were delighted to get a horse like him, given his rating on the Flat. His jumping has been improving the whole time. He's taken a step forward every time he's run. We were delighted with him at Naas last time. There'll have to be more improvement in him if he's going to go to Cheltenham and win, but we're hopeful there is. 19-02-26

runners.breeder: S A R L Haras De Saint Faust Et Al

prev_owners.owner: A S & D Allard & Bg Racing Service

runners.comment: Thurles maiden hurdle winner, respectable runs up in class last twice, more needed
runners.spotlight: Placed on sole start in France; easy winner on debut for this yard at Thurles in January (2m, heavy); respectable efforts twice since, 3.5l fourth of 22 in mares' Grade 2 at Cheltenham; 9.25l third of 11 behind Zanoosh in mares' Grade 1 at Fairyhouse; needs to find a bit more to win this.

quotes.race: Thurles Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Charme De Faust handled the ground well and will improve as she had a couple of blows. She jumped brilliantly. I liked how she did it and she has developing to do to fill into her frame. I think she'll have a nice future and when she strengthens up. She'll be a fine mare - Paul Townend, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: A brand new addition to the yard who we're hoping might make up into a Triumph Hurdle contender. She was second at Auteuil in September for Gabriel Leenders in what looked a decent race with plenty of runners. She could be quite smart. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Listed hurdle win on Irish debut, not far behind two of these at Fairyhouse, rain a plus
runners.spotlight: French Flat winner; won a 4yo Listed hurdle at Naas (15.5f, heavy) on Irish and stable debut; found just Proactif and Macho Man too good in Grade 2 Juvenile at Fairyhouse (2m, yld-sft) on latest when a 2.25l third; if the forecast rain arrives she could get much closer to those two rivals but has to be viewed as a negative that Paul Townend has jumped ship.

quotes.race: Download The William Hill App Juvenile Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't expecting that. I didn't think she'd be ready enough to do that today. I thought she'd need the run. She's a filly that came at the start of the season that we liked and then got injured and came back late. If she'd finished in the first three today we'd have been delighted. Majolique put up a good performance. I suppose the fact they went so slow helped her, it turned a mile and seven furlong race into a mile and five race. It's great to win, she obviously has ability. I think she'll improve hugely for it. She's in the Triumph. Cheltenham might come a bit quick. It's only a fortnight away. The owner won the Grade 1 in Aintree last year with Murcia, maybe she might be one for that. I don't know, Willie will make a plan for her when she gets home. She hasn't done a whole pile of work since she came back. She must have plenty of ability to do what she did - David Casey, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won a three-year-old fillies' Flat race at Longchamp in May and will hopefully be in our Triumph team come March. 17-11-25

racecards.verdict: The French recruit MATIN MIDI ET SOIR looks an exciting prospect and he beat a subsequent Gr' 3 winner by 8.5l last time out
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Apolon De Charnie, 5/1 Saratoga, 11/2 Proactif, 13/2 Matin Midi Et Soir, 15/2 Majolique, 10/1 Macho Man, 11/1 Bartholomew, 25/1 Charme De Faust, 33/1 Bertutea,  One Horse Town, 40/1 Kai Lung,  Madness d'Elle,  Moulin Labbe

racecards.race_name: Lawlor's Of Naas Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)

runners.breeder: S & G Kinast & Haras De La Rousseliere
runners.comment: Consistent, smart graded and h'cap form this season, rain and rider's claim positives
runners.spotlight: Consistent sort with plenty of smart form in the book; won first two starts this season, a 2m4f hurdle at Limerick (heavy) and the Grade 3 Red Mills at Gowran; respectable third in BetMGM Cup at Cheltenham off 151; 7.75l third of 10 in Fairyhouse Grade 2 latest; rider's claim a big plus and forecast rain in his favour; should go well.

quotes.race: Red Mills Trial Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: It was a tough performance. I didn't know how well I was going for much of the race, to be honest. When I got Storm Heart out and set about him, he stuck it out really well and he got a good jump at the last when he needed it. He's now starting to fulfil what I thought he might do as a novice because as a juvenile I stick with him a few times. It's nice for him to get his head in front. He seems versatile ground-wise and he handles that testing ground - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Goggin Buckley Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was coming here off a layoff and the others had race fitness on their side, but class kicked in late on and it was a good performance. There was a bit of tactics at the start, nobody wanted to go, so I said I would follow the pace setter and it developed as the race went on. A few good jumps down the straight and a bit of speed got Storm Heart there nicely. Probably even on today he has run a good few pounds below where his peak can be, so it will be interesting where Willie and the team in Gigginstown want to go but it's nice to have him winning again - Danny Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: Tote.ie 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Storm Heart was very good. I didn't expect that and he is more than alright looking at that performance. His attitude was great and he loves jumping. I think there could be huge improvement in him - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a huge race in the big handicap hurdle at the Dublin Racing Festival when second, but missed Cheltenham with a small setback afterwards. Hopefully we can get a clear run with him this season as he's talented. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Grade 1 Juvenile winner, back to form at Fairyhouse latest, stamina to prove for this trip
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 1 Juvenile at the DRF last season; below best first three starts this season but better effort when a 7.5l third of 18 in Listed handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse latest (2m, yld-sft); same mark here but stamina to prove for this longer trip.

quotes.race: Gannon's City Recovery & Recycling Services Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Hello Neighbour is a proper one. We've brought him along along slowly. He's answered every call and hopefully he can improve again. We have always liked him. We put the hood on him and he was still a little bit keen but I think he'll learn every day - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

quotes.race: O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: That was great. It was a brave call to come here on his first start and thankfully Hello Neighbour hung on. He was keen in snatches in the race and because of that he didn't jump as well as he can do. I think when he learns to settle better in races he'll be better again. We'll look at the Dublin Racing Festival now - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Roscommon Rated Race
quotes.quote: We're going to go hurdling with Hello Neighbour now and hopefully he's a good horse - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Enjoy Hospitality At Navan Racecourse Maiden
quotes.quote: Hello Neighbour has a great mind and I was very surprised that he was keen early. He pulled for probably a mile or more and still finished. He did well as he probably got there plenty soon enough and then he idled - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He'll go for the County. He's a Grade 1 winner back in a handicap and he's going to have plenty of weight. He may not be well handicapped but should have the pace for it. It's always a tough time for them after their juvenile season. But it can be done ? look at Espoir D'Allen winning the Champion Hurdle as a five-year-old. 19-02-26

He's a lovely horse who ran to a good level when winning his two starts on the Flat for us at Navan and Roscommon. We gave him a three-week break after his win at Roscommon and he's just started back now with a view to Leopardstown at Christmas. He has a nice pedigree, jumps well and we like him. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Back to form with easy win in Lanzarote, beaten off 8lb higher at Cheltenham, tough mark
runners.spotlight: Ground versatile sort is 4-15 over hurdles; back to form in fine style when landing the Lanzarote at Kempton in January (2m5f, good) off 136; hiked up 8lb and came up short in the BetMGM Cup at Cheltenham, though did meet trouble in running; dropped 1lb but may need more help from the handicapper.

quotes.race: Coral Lanzarote Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wanted to settle Iberico Lord out the back and he was a bit cold in the early stages, which was perfect. They went a good gallop and turning in I felt I had loads left. I probably drove him on a bit early, but he kept it up so it worked out well. The trip has definitely helped him and the whole complexion of the race suited me as well. He's dropped to a nice weight too - James Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: "Book Christmas Festival Hospitality Now" Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Iberico Lord started that race looking like a hurdler and finished it looking like a steeplechaser, and that's what it's all about. It's got to be education, education, education. He was always on the short list for this, which has always been a good race for us, and his schooling's been very good at home. It was never a question of whether we should go chasing. I'd love to run him under a penalty but you're not allowed to these days, they force you upstairs. The Wayward Lad round here wouldn't be the worst thing but I wouldn't be in a rush to go to Ascot or Cheltenham, I think he needs to learn a bit more - Nicky Henderson, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Betfair Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'd say the ground just went against him last time but we made amends for it today. Iberico Lord has seen it out really well on this ground, which is really hard work - Nico de Boinville, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Under Control, who is going for the Gerry Feilden at Newbury, beat him at Sandown fair and square and there was no fluke about it. I thought Iberico Lord was very good to start with then he fell on his second start for us, then his wind didn't work in his next one and then everything went wrong - Nicky Henderson, trainer. He was great today. It got a bit rough at the top of the hill but I was able just to take a pull and give him and a breath of air. I knew Luccia was going to take me all the way to the last and to be fair she did. The way he ran at Sandown last time he was staying on all the way and I knew he'd love the hill and that ground today - Nico de Boinville, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He went novice chasing and won at Kempton, but he fell at Ascot next time, got in a muddle and we had to go back over hurdles. We're in the middle of loose schooling now but he ought to be going over fences, although he's rated 142 and that won't make things easy. He's a sharp horse, and a good one when we get it together. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Standout effort at Aintree last year, hard to fancy on what he has done this season
runners.spotlight: Highly touted French recruit has yet to win in four starts for Willie Mullins; flopped when favourite for the 2025 Martin Pipe on stable debut; narrowly denied in premier handicap at Aintree; tailed off when falling on seasonal reappearance in a Navan beginners' chase; midfield in BetMGM Cup latest; 3lb drop not enough to tempt.

stable_tour.quote: He's always worked well and I think switching to fences might bring out what we see from him on the gallops. He went close at Aintree in a handicap hurdle on his final start of last season and is another who you haven't seen the best of yet. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Grade 2 Juvenile winner, decent efforts last two h'cap hurdles, not discounted
runners.spotlight: Fruitful novice campaign included a Grade 2 win at Kempton (2m, gd-sft); best run this season a 2.75l second in an Ascot handicap (19.5f, soft) in cheekpieces which return now; not a bad effort when a keeping on 7l seventh in the County Hurdle (2m1f, soft); modest run on the Flat latest; not discounted back up in trip over timber.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Dovecote Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tripoli Flyer has got a huge engine. Johnny said you can put him where you want in a race, he's got an explosive bit of speed about him. He thought he could have waited a bit longer maybe but he got the job done and we were here to win this. I think he's genuinely better going right-handed and he does jump a bit right, but if it's nice ground I think he's earned his chance to go to the Supreme. He's won plenty now and definitely deserves a go - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.  We'll have a coffee on Monday morning and see where we go. I feel like Aintree owes us one after Tripoli Flyer got beat there last year although I have to be careful what I say as we were beaten by the stable's other runner! - Ismail El Magdoub, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He's entered for Cheltenham, but we're going to go to Southwell first for the mile-and-a-half novice on Friday and see how that goes. He's got good two-mile form and stays a bit further. 19-02-26

runners.comment: Back to form with fine effort in Martin Pipe latest, chance but forecast rain a concern
runners.spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner; beaten 3l when runner up behind Salvator Mundi in Grade 2 novice at this track (2m1f, soft) in January 2025; no show in two heavy ground Grade 3s on first two runs this term; fine effort in Martin Pipe off 137 on latest and effectively 6lb lower here with rider's claim; chance but forecast rain a concern.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Club Moscow Flyer Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Kel Histoire ran well. He learned a fair bit from the last day and hopefully he will learn a bit more from this. They went no gallop and it developed into a bit of a sprint but we're very happy with the run - Frank Berry, owner's racing manager.

quotes.race: Mallow Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Kel Histoire was very sticky over the first three but you wouldn't mind that on his first run over hurdles and he warmed into it. The further he went, the better he jumped. He was fine on that ground and I'd say he'll go on slower ground too - Mark Walsh, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Arrives here on the back of a good win on the Flat in France, but looks a real hurdling type being by Masked Marvel. He should stay well. 25-11-24

prev_owners.owner: A S & D Allard, Jacques Bisson & Palmyr Racing

runners.comment: Yet to win for Willie Mullins, stayed on well over 2m latest, rain a plus, interesting
runners.spotlight: Two-time winner on heavy in France is 0-7 for Willie Mullins; below best first two runs this season but more like it at Fairyhouse on latest when staying on for a 7.5l fourth over 2m (yld-sft); same mark here, forecast rain a positive and this trip should suit; interesting.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Compiegne and looks a real sharp type, so hopefully he can continue to progress and make into a Triumph type. 25-11-24

runners.comment: Excellent third last time in Martin Pipe, just 2lb higher now, Townend up now, claims
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; won two handicaps last season, over 19.5f (soft) at Naas off 114 and then off 14lb higher at Sandown (2m4f, good); excellent 3.25l third despite trouble in running on seasonal reappearance in the Martin Pipe (20.5f, soft) when sent off at just 8-1 and 2lb higher now; Paul Townend now takes over; leading claims.

runners.comment: Thurles maiden winner on soft, beaten in Turners latest, can't discount on h'cap bow
runners.spotlight: Placed on heavy sole start in France; runner up on stable debut in 4yo maiden at Limerick (2m, heavy); went one place better at Thurles (2m, soft) in February, winning by 13l; midfield in the Turners at Cheltenham latest (2m5f, gd-sft); not discounted on handicap debut with forecast rain in his favour.

runners.comment: Two-time Fairyhouse handicap winner, up 9lb for easy win latest, forecast rain a negative
runners.spotlight: Two-time winner, both at Fairyhouse; won a 2m (soft) novice handicap off 109 there in December; added a 21.5f handicap (yld-sft) off 122 last month, scoring by 5.5l; 9lb rise for that seems fair; should be competitive again but wouldn't want to see too much rain (well beaten in four previous starts on soft to heavy).

quotes.race: Fairyhouse Steel Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was worried Fierce Handay was slightly overracing but he's obviously a horse who has improved from his last run and he's going the right way- Harry Cobden, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Won the Brown Lad in November, solid run in Pertemps latest, drop in trip a plus
runners.spotlight: Won the Brown Lad at Naas (2m4f, sft-hvy) in November off 119; 3.25l runner up in Pertemps qualifier at Carlisle (3m1f, soft) off revised mark in December; soundly beaten in Naas Grade 1 but bounced back with a respectable 7.25l fourth in the Pertemps at Cheltenham (3m, good), not quite getting home; could go well back in trip returned to softer ground.

quotes.race: SIS Brown Lad Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I said to the owner before the race that Letos has to win this to be the real one, which I believe he is. He's only five, he's a huge horse and he might bring us to where we dream of going. He could go for the Coral Cup or the Pertemps Final route but we'll have to discuss that. I ride him out myself at home and he feels like a horse who wants three miles. We're just hoping to get something nice along the way, but our eventual plan is chasing and that's where I'd have the real big dreams - Tony Mullins, trainer.

runners.comment: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner, opening mark not overly generous, likely best watched
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; off the mark at the fourth attempt over hurdles in a Limerick maiden (2m3f, soft) in March, winning by 8.5l; that form has taken some knocks since and opening mark doesn't look overly generous; probably best watched in first handicap.

quotes.race: Private Suites @ Limerick INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He was very keen and I thought that it would affect Dani Donadoni at the end but I let him catch his breath coming down the hill. I thought I was beaten but once he caught his second wind, he has flown. With the experience under his belt there could be a lot of improvement. It is great for his owner/breeder Kevin McCarthy who has had horses with us for decades, going back to Dani California who won an Irish Cesarewitch - Patrick Mullins, jockey.

runners.comment: Won off 7lb lower at Leopardstown in Dec', 3m too far latest, drops in trip; tongue tied
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; off the mark at the eighth attempt over hurdles in a maiden here in November (2m6f, sft-hvy); followed up in a Listed handicap hurdle at Leopardstown (20.5f, gd-yld) in December; raised 7lb and pulled up in Listed handicap at the DRF on latest but 3m on heavy may have stretched him; could rebound dropped in trip; tongue tie added.

runners.comment: No win since Dec' 2024, pulled up and beaten 23l last twice, cheekpieces tried
runners.spotlight: Has come up dry since winning a maiden at Leopardstown in December 2024; hasn't threatened in five runs this term and has a lot to find with Champagne Kid on their meeting at Leopardstown in December; pulled up and beaten 23l on last two starts; cheekpieces need to transform.

stable_tour.quote: I thought he ran better than his finishing position [seventh of eight] suggests in the Grade 1 at Leopardstown. He probably made his move a bit early in the race and got tired. He's the sort of juvenile I could see running well in the Fred Winter.  19-2-25

runners.comment: Maiden hurdle winner, runner up in Grade 2 in Dec', poor last twice, needs to revive
runners.spotlight: Navan maiden hurdle winner in September (2m3f, yielding); runner up in a novice handicap here (2m1f, sft-hvy) in November and beaten a head in a Grade 2 Novice at Limerick the following month; pulled up (coughing post-race) and soundly beaten in handicaps the last twice though so a revival is needed.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I don't know how strong the race was, but County Final  jumped well and won well. He ran well in fifth at Punchestown and is definitely learning as he goes along. There are no big plans for him. It was a restricted maiden hurdle for horses who hadn't been in the first four, and he had the bit of experience which helped - Frank Berry, racing manager to owner JP McManus.

runners.comment: Raised 11lb for easy Fairyhouse win, 2m too sharp latest, rain would enhance claims
runners.spotlight: 4-17 over hurdles, the latest win coming by 24l on his penultimate start at Fairyhouse in February (2m4f, heavy); hit with an 11lb rise for that and beaten 11l at Wexford last time but 2m would have been too sharp; could do better stepped back up in distance and rain would further enhance chance.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Tommy Carberry Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I thought it was a good performance. It's a great race to win, because Tommy Carberry was my hero when I was a young fella growing up. One Big Boum looked to be in control and he stretched out well to the line. He's an improving horse and the blinkers certainly make a difference to him. He's effective on that ground and it looks very necessary. He could go to Punchestown but it depends on the ground - Phillip Fenton, trainer.

quotes.race: Ardmulchan Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: First-time blinkers were a big help. One Big Boum is big enough to jump a fence, so I'm sure we will end up over fences maybe sooner rather than later. His jumping was immaculate today, so we are very pleased. He ran at Christmas, so I'm sure it will be three to four weeks before we will ask him to go again - Philip Fenton, trainer.

runners.comment: Won two of last three inc' here, looks progressive, forecast rain no inconvenience
runners.spotlight: Has won two of his last three starts, a 19.5f handicap here (sft-hvy) off 107 in January and a 2m3f handicap at Naas (sft-hvy) on latest in March; career high mark now but he looks progressive and the forecast rain won't inconvenience him; 1lb wrong.

runners.comment: Won auction final here last year, fine effort at Leopardstown in Dec', needs rain to miss
runners.spotlight: Three-time winner over timber; career highlight a 1.25l win in Red Mills Auction Final at this meeting last year (19.5f, yielding); excellent effort when a 3.5l second behind Champagne Kid on last start over hurdles at Leopardstown in December (20.5f, gd-yld); fit from a spin on the Flat last month but very soft ground would not be ideal; 1lb wrong.

quotes.race: Coors Mares Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Thisistheway is a lovely mare. She had the form to go and do that. She probably wants 2m4f and that good strong gallop suited. She will improve again - Cian Quirke, rider

runners.comment: On long losing run, better effort latest but unproven at this trip, hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Smart form as a younger horse but on losing run since Grade 2 success at Limerick in December 2022; a step in the right direction in a 2m Cork conditions hurdle on latest but he's unproven at this trip; 4lb wrong and hard to fancy.

quotes.race: Coolmore NH Sires Kew Gardens Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I'm surprised but it's brilliant. No Looking Back was a bit of an unknown after winning in Thurles. He's a horse that Oliver and the team have loved. Johnny Barry has always thought lots of him and he proved him right today. When I quickened him he picked up over the last, and hopefully he can progress again. He landed running and galloped to the line. You'd have to be surprised going from a maiden to open company - Phillip Enright, jockey

quotes.race: Thurles Racecourse Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: No Looking Back won his bumper in similar fashion here. He didn't do a pile when he hit the front but he had to get there. His jumping was okay but he will be sharper the next day - Oliver McKiernan, trainer.

quotes.race: www.thurlesraces.ie (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: No Looking Back surprised me, because when I walked the track I didn't think it was soft enough. He'll be heading to Fairyhouse for the big sales bumper there. I wasn't expecting him to win there but delighted he did - Oliver McKiernan, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to LETOS (nap) who should be suited by the drop back to this trip after a good effort in the Pertemps Final

runners.spotlight: Promise in both starts in point-to-points at Damma House and Nenagh for Colin Bowe; dam a bumper winner; in good hands and interesting on Rules' debut.

runners.spotlight: Had a subsequent bumper winner behind when third in a Dromahane point on debut for Luke Murphy in November 2024; absent since pulling up at Borris House the following month; probably best watched after such a long absence.

runners.comment: The Irish Rover gelding, half-brother to bumper winner but likely best watched
runners.spotlight: The Irish Rover gelding; E1,000 yearling; half-brother to bumper winner King Ulanda; dam maiden on Flat/over hurdles, half-sister to two hurdle/chase winners; best watched.

runners.comment: Authorized mare, dam half-sister to Big Buck's, top yard, of obvious interest on debut
runners.spotlight: Authorized mare; E68,000 yearling; half-sister to winners Rickety Bridge (point/2m4f hurdle) and Raffles Capital (French 2m1f hurdle/2m2f chase); dam half-sister to multiple Stayers' Hurdle winner Big Buck's; top yard and of obvious interest on debut.

runners.comment: Point winner for Pat Doyle, Maxios gelding respected on Rules' bow for top yard
runners.spotlight: Maxios gelding; off the mark at the second attempt in point-to-points at Ballygogue House in February for Pat Doyle; that form doesn't look overly special but he's in good hands and has to be respected on Rules' debut.

runners.comment: E60,000 Getaway mare, half-sister to top class Monkfish, check the market
runners.spotlight: Getaway mare; E60,000 3yo; half-sister to Monkfish (high-class 2m5f-3m hurdle/chase); dam placed bumper/2m-2m6f hurdles; well-bred and yard can ready one; tongue tied; check the market.

runners.comment: Mount Nelson mare, half-sister to top bumper performer Blackbow, interesting
runners.spotlight: Home-bred Mount Nelson mare; half-sister to winners Blackbow (high-class bumper and 2m1f/2m4f chase) and Banntown Girl (useful bumper/2m hurdle); dam unraced; yard has had success in this sphere; interesting on paper.

runners.comment: Soldier Of Fortune mare, dam unraced, bred to need further than this in time
runners.spotlight: Soldier Of Fortune mare; half-sister to winners Whatdoyawanttoknow (2m3f hurdle) and Judge John Deed (point); dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m3f-3m1f hurdle/chase winner Tullymurry Toff; bred to need further than this in time.

runners.comment: Vadamos filly, half-sister to two bumper winners, good claimer booked, check betting
runners.spotlight: Vadamos filly; sister to 1m7f/2m hurdle winner Star Of Guiting, half-sister to winners Petrossian (bumper) and Realistic Optimism (bumper/2m2f hurdle); dam unraced half-sister to useful On Raglan Road; good claimer booked; check the betting.

stable_tour.quote: He won his maiden hurdle at Galway quite emphatically, but never went a yard at Tramore. He's better than that and hopefully we'll get him back on track soon. 28-10-24

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Chase (Div I)
quotes.quote: I just had a phone call from Pride Of Place's previous trainer, Michael Hourigan, and he told me how to train him and stuff like that. He got a lovely ride from Charlie and goes on the good ground. That was a 0-110 and he's rated 101 so hopefully he might still be in the same bracket so we'll follow them around. Charlie's riding well, he rode a nice winner for us at Roscommon as well - Enda Bolger, trainer.

runners.owner: Paul M Butler & James Patrick Byrne

stable_tour.quote: He ran nicely at Aintree and for quite a while I've had the £100,000 long-distance hurdle in mind for him at Haydock on Saturday. The time has come to go up in trip to 3m. He was second in the EBF Final at Sandown last season and that's always a good race. 16-11-21

runners.comment: Two-time Flat winner rated 71, won this last year, yard form a plus, should go well
runners.spotlight: Two-time Flat winner rated 71, won this last year, yard form a plus, should go well.

quotes.race: Packie Downey Memorial Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Dark Note is a great servant and has won now on the Flat, over hurdles and fences. He gives the owners a good day out every day he runs so he's a right little horse. You can be sure he'll be in Killarney and Galway and will keep mixing it. Cian was very happy with him today and thought the extra trip was a big plus to him which will open up a few more options. He was slower than the other horse at the last but had the Flat speed to quicken up well - Brian Slattery, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Killyhevlin Lakeside Hotel & Lodges Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Dark Note had a very good run last time. I knew Jack was under pressure when he came alongside me. He probably got a head in front of me but me fellow ran all the way to the line - Cian Quirke, rider.

quotes.race: John Madden & Sons Apprentice Claiming Race
quotes.quote: I was happy enough. Dark Note got a lovely position all the way around in the box seat. I got a lovely split but I probably went too early. He got very lairy when he got to the front, I could've covered him up for a bit longer.  But look he got the job done and he done it well - Jake Coen, jockey.

quotes.race: Matt Hampson Foundation Silver Trophy Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm relieved to finally get his head in front. In Excelsis  Deo has been running well and stayed consistent without having the luck in running. Johnny [Burke] has given him a lovely ride, nursing him into it and we thought at the bottom of the hill this was the closest he'd been all season so we just hoped he'd come up the hill as he had done on a few runs previously. We'll see what happens from here but enjoy this first. We've been in various spots in this winner's enclosure so it's good to have finally won - Harry Fry, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He took us by surprise with how he won on his chasing debut at Hereford and then got found out against more experienced horses after a hike in the handicap. His last run was over two miles and I think that's where he'll start his campaign. I hope there's more to come. 04-10-23

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (Handicap)
quotes.quote: Jungle Cove is a star. He's basically my lead horse at home. Emma-Jayne gave him a fabulous ride and said she knew he was going to win a furlong out; that she had so much horse underneath. I knew he'd pick up. He goes on any ground - Jessica Harrington, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF "Nasrullah" Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Jungle Cove is a brilliant horse. He's my lead horse at home and works like a Group horse. Dylan gave him a great ride, full of confidence and stuck to the inside. He doesn't interfere with the horse. More senior jockeys get on him and kind of bully him, which he hates. He just loves tooling around and feeling as if he's in charge - that's him. It's a fantastic pot to win. It's brilliant for Dylan on his first ride - Jessica Harrington, trainer.

quotes.race: Borris Handicap

quotes.race: Hollywoodbets Racing & Sports Betting Maiden
quotes.quote: Jungle Cove travelled through the race well, he won well. He's going to have a busy summer, he's a very good work horse so he'll be leading all them good ones at home - Shane Foley, jockey.

quotes.race: Lincoln Aviator (Conditions) (Dirt)
quotes.quote: Six Speed has been training really well but he fluffed the start in his first race - he jumped in the air and he had to use him up a little bit - and he ran out of gas. This time he was well schooled and we were expecting quite a lot of him. His homework was so good and, although he ran third first time out, he did disappoint as he should have run better. He's put it to bed this time with more experience behind him. I'm not sure how far he'll go and he's got plenty of speed but I hope his stamina can carry him for the Guineas' distance - Bhupat Seemar, trainer, speaking to Racing Dubai.
